items.title: NASA Stennis Space Center Honors Employees and Teams
items.summary: NASA's Stennis Space Center in Mississippi recently hosted its annual Honor Awards ceremony to recognize staff contributions to agency missions and commercial space programs. Center Director Christine Powell and Artemis Program Manager Jeremy Parsons presented the honors on November 18. Several individuals received accolades for leadership, engineering excellence, customer service, and innovation, including Stephen Rawls, Bradley Tyree, Anna Lizana, Daniel Jones, Peyton Pinson, Joseph Schuyler, Michael McDaniel, Amer Arshad, and Claire O’Shaughnessy. Additionally, the Liquid Oxygen/Liquid Methane Assessment Confined by Missile Test Team received the Space Flight Awareness Team Award for critical safety testing. The event also acknowledged numerous civil service employees celebrating major career milestones ranging from 25 to 40 years of service.

items.title: Mathematical Modeling Tracks Infant and Toddler Sleep Development
items.summary: Researchers applied a mathematical model of adult sleep regulation to understand how sleep mechanisms mature from age one month to five years. Using a Bayesian approach to analyze parameter distributions, the study found that a decreasing rate of sleep homeostatic pressure accumulation explains shorter sleep durations as children grow. Meanwhile, a longer time scale in homeostatic drive accounts for the consolidation of sleep into fewer daily bouts. The analysis also revealed greater parameter variation among infants under six months compared to older children, establishing population-level trajectories for early childhood sleep maturation.
items.author: Lachlan Webb, Andrew J. K. Phillips, James A. Roberts
items.original_title: Inferring population-level physiologically based model parameters for sleep in infancy and young childhood
items.original_summary: by Lachlan Webb, Andrew J. K. Phillips, James A. Roberts The sleep patterns of infants and young children differ from adult sleep patterns, with longer duration and multiple bouts per 24 hours. There is also considerable heterogeneity in infant sleep, both between individuals and within individuals across development. While mathematical models have been used to understand the mechanisms that regulate adult sleep, the development of sleep from infancy through early childhood has remained largely unexplored. Here we used an established mathematical model for adult sleep regulation to investigate how the underlying mechanisms of sleep mature from ages 1 month to 5 years, and identify a basis for inter-individual differences at each age.

items.title: Simulations Help Guide Exetendon Designs to Lower Running Costs
items.summary: Scientists developed a muscle-driven simulation framework to predict how passive foot devices called exotendons affect the energetic cost of running at higher speeds. The model correctly anticipated that an exotendon design reducing energy use at moderate speeds would also lower costs at a faster, untested speed of 4 meters per second, while other tested configurations would not yield significant savings. Although predictions for maximum savings did not translate directly to experimental results, a 5-kilometer time trial using the most effective exotendon showed participants experienced a lower average heart rate and increased cadence. The findings indicate that predictive simulations offer a reliable way to guide the design of assistive wearable devices for running.
items.author: Jon Stingel, Nicholas Bianco, Carmichael Ong et al.
items.original_title: Simulation-guided design of exotendons to reduce the energetic cost of running
items.original_summary: by Jon Stingel, Nicholas Bianco, Carmichael Ong, Steve Collins, Scott Delp, Jennifer Hicks A passive device that attaches to the feet, called an exotendon, can reduce the energetic cost of running at moderate speeds, but its efficacy and optimal design parameters at higher speeds are unknown. Identifying optimal parameters at new speeds experimentally would require many experimental trials with different exotendon designs, which is challenging for participants at higher running speeds. We developed a muscle-driven simulation framework to predict the effect of various exotendon designs on the energetic cost of running at an experimentally untested speed (4 m/s). We used these predictions to select four designs, which we evaluated experimentally as users ran at this speed.

items.title: Pupil Dynamics Reveal How the Brain Processes Uncertainty During Learning
items.summary: A recent study investigated how human arousal systems manage uncertainty during probability learning tasks. Researchers combined pupillometry with an experiment where participants tracked hidden, frequently changing probabilities. Using a Bayesian model, the team measured trial-by-trial learning rates alongside change point probability and prior uncertainty. The results showed that participants adjusted their learning rates based on prior uncertainty in a rational manner. Furthermore, pupil measurements reflected distinct neural signals: phasic dilations tracked change point probabilities, while tonic dilations represented prior uncertainty. High tonic arousal also weakened the link between phasic responses and sudden change detection, influencing how individuals update their beliefs in changing environments.
items.author: Aaron Greenhouse-Tucknott, Cedric Foucault, Anne Buot et al.
items.original_title: Pupil dynamics reflect uncertainty-driven adjustments of probability learning
items.original_summary: by Aaron Greenhouse-Tucknott, Cedric Foucault, Anne Buot, Florent Meyniel Adaptive learning in dynamic environments depends on the brain’s ability to represent and respond to uncertainty. Changes in arousal-mediated pupil diameter provide insight into the neural basis of this process. Prior work has focused on magnitude-based inference tasks and revealed that learning is primarily influenced by the detection of change points and the corresponding modulation of arousal. In comparison, the role of arousal systems in learning contexts where changes are harder to detect, such as in probability learning, remains poorly understood. Here, we combined pupillometry with a probability learning task in which human participants estimated a hidden generative probability of stimuli that changed abruptly and unpredictably.

items.title: Investigating Immune Evasion Strategies in Mucorales Fungi
items.summary: Mucormycosis is a severe fungal infection driven by Mucorales species that employ various species- and stage-specific tactics to bypass host immune defenses. Research shows that resting spores of Rhizopus can survive inside macrophages because the immune cells restrict germination without fully killing the spores. As these fungi germinate, cell-wall remodeling increases exposure to beta-glucan, though immune responses vary by species. For example, Rhizopus spores remain dormant and block phagosome maturation, whereas Mucor circinelloides germinates using stress-response pathways. Additionally, certain species resist neutrophil damage or suppress nitric oxide production in macrophages. Rhizopus also triggers specific dendritic-cell activation and T-cell responses that can damage hyphae. Mapping these immune evasion mechanisms could aid the creation of targeted therapies.
items.author: Rajesh Palanisamy, Maldonado Gabriela, Soo Chan Lee
items.original_title: Immune evasion in Mucorales species: From stealth spores to angioinvasive hyphae
items.original_summary: by Rajesh Palanisamy, Maldonado Gabriela, Soo Chan Lee Mucormycosis is an invasive fungal infection caused by members of the order Mucorales, which employ stage- and species-specific mechanisms to evade host immunity. Resting spores of experimentally studied Rhizopus species can persist after macrophage uptake because macrophages restrict germination but do not efficiently kill all internalized resting spores. Germination is accompanied by cell-wall remodeling and increased β-glucan exposure in several experimentally examined Mucorales species; however, functional Dectin-1-dependent responses have been demonstrated most clearly in Rhizopus and its conservation across species and isolates remains incompletely defined. Studies predominantly in Rhizopus delemar identify fungal CotH proteins as ligands for host GRP78 or integrin α3β1, linking invasion to tissue-specific host pathways.

items.title: New Antiviral Leads Target Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever Protein
items.summary: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus lacks approved vaccines or treatments, posing a significant public health threat. The viral nucleocapsid protein is critical for viral replication and translation through its interaction with messenger RNA. Researchers designed a high-throughput assay to monitor this protein-RNA binding and screened nearly 109,000 small molecules. They identified and validated several promising inhibitors that noncompetitively block the nucleocapsid interaction without harming host cellular translation. Tested against a lower-safety-level surrogate virus, the prioritized compounds showed low cytotoxicity and strong antiviral activity, significantly reducing the production of infectious viral particles. These compounds offer promising starting points for developing desperately needed CCHFV therapeutics.
items.author: Hoangvi Le, Anuradha Roy, Ethan Mir et al.
items.original_title: A new therapeutic opportunity in Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever: Targeting the stalk domain of viral nucleocapsid protein for therapeutic intervention
items.original_summary: by Hoangvi Le, Anuradha Roy, Ethan Mir, Xin Li, Saima Ali, Austin Royster, Songyang Ren, Yongcheng Song, Sheema Mir, Mohammad Mir Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) is a high-consequence pathogen for which no approved antivirals or vaccines exist. The viral nucleocapsid protein (N protein) is central to the Nairovirus life cycle, coordinating genomic RNA encapsidation and selective enhancement of viral mRNA translation through its interaction with the panhandle-like hairpin structure in the S-segment mRNA 5′ untranslated region (UTR). Here, we developed a robust fluorescence polarization anisotropy (FPA) based high-throughput assay capable of quantitatively monitoring the interaction between purified N protein and the viral 5′UTR hairpin.

items.title: Analysis of VYD222 Antibody Neutralization Against SARS-CoV-2 Variants
items.summary: Extensive mutations in the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein have rendered many therapeutic monoclonal antibodies ineffective, but the re-engineered human monoclonal antibody VYD222 (pemivibart) maintains strong neutralization capabilities against emerging variants. VYD222 received FDA Emergency Use Authorization for pre-exposure prophylaxis of COVID-19 in specific immunocompromised populations. Structural analysis reveals how VYD222 adapts to mutations that typically allow viruses to escape older treatments. Deep mutational scanning shows that the virus's ability to evade VYD222 is limited by structural constraints and the requirement to preserve receptor binding, offering crucial guidance for tracking variant risks.
items.author: Meng Yuan, Brandyn R. West, William B. Foreman et al.
items.original_title: Structural and functional analysis of VYD222: A broadly neutralizing antibody against SARS-CoV-2 variants
items.original_summary: by Meng Yuan, Brandyn R. West, William B. Foreman, Colin Powers, Ziqi Feng, Ashley L. Taylor, Xinye Yu, Grace Wang, Laura Walker, Tyler N. Starr, Robert Allen, Ian A. Wilson Extensive mutations in SARS-CoV-2 spike protein have rendered most therapeutic monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) ineffective. However, here we describe how VYD222 (pemivibart), a human mAb re-engineered from ADG20 (adintrevimab) exhibits substantially improved neutralization potency and breadth against SARS-CoV-2 variants despite substantial virus evolution. VYD222 received FDA Emergency Use Authorization for pre-exposure prophylaxis of COVID-19 in certain immunocompromised adults and adolescents. Here we show potent neutralization of this antibody against a broad range of emerging variants, including the recently dominant XFG.

items.title: New Narrative Comprehension Assessment Developed for Indian Children
items.summary: A study details the development and preliminary psychometric evaluation of the Narrative Comprehension Assessment (NCA), designed to measure English-language narrative skills in Indian children aged four to eight. Due to a scarcity of culturally relevant English narrative assessments in India, researchers created a picture-based tool consisting of literal and inferential comprehension questions. The evaluation utilized two wordless picture narratives split into four sequential tasks: Picture Walk, Retelling, Prompted Comprehension, and Guided Story Narration. Testing across 80 typically developing children showed high content validity, internal consistency, and test-retest reliability, alongside significant differences across age groups. These findings suggest the NCA is a stable and valid tool, though larger and more diverse samples are needed for future normative use.
items.author: Ramandeep Kaur, Darryl Jeethesh Dsouza, Dency Davis et al.
items.original_title: Development and preliminary psychometric evaluation of a Narrative Comprehension Assessment (NCA) for Indian children
items.original_summary: by Ramandeep Kaur, Darryl Jeethesh Dsouza, Dency Davis, Melicia Shainy Dsouza Narrative comprehension requires children to understand explicitly presented information and integrate events to derive implicit meanings. Despite its developmental and educational importance, English-language narrative assessments developed within the Indian cultural context remain limited. This study developed and conducted a preliminary psychometric evaluation of the Narrative Comprehension Assessment (NCA), a picture-based assessment for Indian children aged 4–8 years. The NCA was developed across three phases. An initial set of 27 comprehension questions was refined through expert review to 20 items comprising 9 literal and 11 inferential questions. The final assessment used two wordless picture narratives and four sequential components: Picture Walk, Retelling, Prompted Comprehension, and Guided Story Narration.

items.title: Study Examines Biosignals to Predict AI Health Recommendation Choices
items.summary: A cross-sectional laboratory study investigated whether facial-expression probabilities and galvanic skin response (GSR) features can predict a person's binary choice between AI-labeled and doctor-labeled health recommendations in a simulated assessment. Evaluating 60 participants using cross-validation and stacking meta-learners, researchers found that multimodal stacking did not significantly improve prediction compared to individual modalities, with early-window facial expressions outperforming the stacking model in certain comparisons. The authors emphasize that these exploratory findings do not establish direct trust detection or support clinical deployment, and they call for larger studies with independent measures and external validation.
items.author: Hamid Shamszare, Avishek Choudhury
items.original_title: Prediction of a task-specific AI-reliance choice from facial expression and galvanic skin response signals
items.original_summary: by Hamid Shamszare, Avishek Choudhury Background Reliance on AI-supported health recommendations is consequential, but a single behavioral source-selection decision is not equivalent to multidimensional psychological trust. Biosignals may contain predictive information before a choice, although small-sample multimodal models require leakage-free evaluation and cautious interpretation. Purpose This study evaluated whether facial-expression probabilities and galvanic skin response (GSR) features predict a task-specific binary choice of an AI-labeled rather than doctor-labeled recommendation in a simulated ADHD assessment. The outcome is treated as a behavioral indicator of reliance rather than a direct measure of psychological trust. Method: This cross-sectional laboratory analysis included a cohort of 60 participants (40 AI-labeled and 20 doctor-labeled choices).

items.title: Evaluating Single-Camera Pose Estimation for Gait Analysis Compared to Multi-Camera Systems
items.summary: A study compared a single iPad camera pose estimation method with an eight-camera markerless motion capture reference system to evaluate spatiotemporal gait parameters in thirty-six healthy adults. Participants completed walking trials under usual, bag-carrying, and phone-use conditions across four visits. While mean differences were small, proportional bias was present across all gait variables, and test-retest reliability varied by parameter and condition, with gait speed demonstrating the best reliability. The findings indicate that single-camera systems can offer an accessible approach for selected outcomes like gait speed, but the two methods are not interchangeable when comprehensive spatial and temporal characterization is required.
items.author: Bethany Weber, Brandon Schoenwether, Tyler Booth et al.
items.original_title: Comparative evaluation of single and multiple camera-based pose estimation methods for gait spatiotemporal parameter estimation
items.original_summary: by Bethany Weber, Brandon Schoenwether, Tyler Booth, Megan McFarland, Jennifer Britton, Moataz Eltoukhy Single-camera pose estimation may provide a more accessible approach to measure a person’s walking patterns (i.e., gait analysis) than multi-camera markerless motion capture (MMC), but its validity and test-retest reliability remain unclear. This study evaluated spatiotemporal gait parameters from a single iPad camera against an eight-camera MMC reference system across four visits, two weeks apart. Thirty-six healthy adults (18.7 ± 1.7, ranging 18‒27 years) completed usual-gait, bag-carrying, and phone-use walking conditions. Validity analyses included 458 paired trials from Visit 1 and used repeated-measures and mixed-effects methods. Reliability analyses included 33 participants with complete four-visit data and evaluated absolute agreement of single visit-level measurements.

items.title: Qualitative Study Identifies Barriers to Preventing Perioperative Hypothermia in Elderly Orthopedic Patients
items.summary: Elderly patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty frequently experience perioperative hypothermia due to anesthetic suppression and diminished thermoregulation, leading to potential poor outcomes. To identify practical barriers to hypothermia prevention, researchers conducted a qualitative study using semi-structured face-to-face interviews with fifteen medical professionals, including anesthesiologists, anesthesia nurses, and operating room nurses, at a hospital in China. Content analysis revealed three primary levels of barriers: system and process issues regarding warm chain management and resource allocation, human resources and team atmosphere concerns involving staffing and organizational culture, and inadequacies in multidisciplinary collaboration and continuous improvement systems. The findings suggest that hospital managers should target these specific areas to enhance temperature management strategies for elderly surgical patients.
items.author: Cuicui Dou, Yi Sun, Keke Dai et al.
items.original_title: Analysis of factors hindering the prevention of perioperative hypothermia in elderly patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty: A qualitative study
items.original_summary: by Cuicui Dou, Yi Sun, Keke Dai, Man Wei, Jiawen Li, Kaili Qu, Qiongyan Hu, Huiyan Zhang Background Elderly patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) have a high incidence of perioperative hypothermia due to anesthetic suppression of thermoregulation, prolonged surgical duration, and diminished endogenous thermoregulatory function, which can lead to poor outcomes. Effective prevention of hypothermia is a critical clinical issue; however, previous studies have lacked in-depth analysis of comprehensive continuous management and practical barriers. Objective This study aimed to identify barriers to the prevention of perioperative hypothermia in elderly THA patients. Methods A qualitative study design was employed, conducted from January to February 2026 at a Grade III Level A hospital in the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
items.ai_title: Qualitative Study Identifies Barriers to Preventing Perioperative Hypothermia in Elderly Orthopedic Patients
items.ai_summary: Elderly patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty frequently experience perioperative hypothermia due to anesthetic suppression and diminished thermoregulation, leading to potential poor outcomes. To identify practical barriers to hypothermia prevention, researchers conducted a qualitative study using semi-structured face-to-face interviews with fifteen medical professionals, including anesthesiologists, anesthesia nurses, and operating room nurses, at a hospital in China. Content analysis revealed three primary levels of barriers: system and process issues regarding warm chain management and resource allocation, human resources and team atmosphere concerns involving staffing and organizational culture, and inadequacies in multidisciplinary collaboration and continuous improvement systems. The findings suggest that hospital managers should target these specific areas to enhance temperature management strategies for elderly surgical patients.
flow: Select participants including anesthesiologists, anesthesia nurses, and operating room nurses via purposive sampling
Conduct semi-structured face-to-face interviews regarding hypothermia prevention barriers
Analyze interview data using content analysis software to extract recurring themes
Categorize findings into system processes, human resources, and multidisciplinary collaboration dimensions

items.title: Exploring barriers and facilitators to Hepatitis C virus treatment access in Los Angeles County: A mixed-methods study
items.summary: by Shikha Handa, Nathan Sudeep, Larisa Albers, Monica Pattarroyo, Juan Vasquez, Roberto E. Montgomerie, Ryan M. Nguyen, Kendall Dimson, Deena Afana, Chrysovalantis Stafylis, Jeffrey D. Klausner, Daniel Soto Diagnosed but untreated chronic Hepatitis C virus infection remains an important public health problem in Los Angeles County, particularly affecting underserved and minority groups. This mixed-methods study (October 2024-January 2025) aimed to identify and describe the barriers and facilitators to accessing Hepatitis C virus treatment among Los Angeles County residents. The study used de-identified programmatic data from 344 case-residents in a linkage-to-cure program and conducted thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with ten participants (seven untreated, three treated) from the linkage-to-cure program.
items.author: Shikha Handa, Nathan Sudeep, Larisa Albers et al.

items.title: Association between cognitive function and depressive symptoms among Chinese older adults: A cross-sectional analysis of CLHLS 2017-2018
items.summary: by Lunan Gao Background Prior studies have yielded inconsistent findings regarding the interplay between cognitive function, depression, self-care ability, and sleep quality in older adults, necessitating deeper exploration to elucidate these complex associations. Objectives This study aimed to examine whether self-care ability mediates the association between cognitive function and depressive symptoms, and whether sleep quality moderates this relationship in Chinese older adults. Methods We analyzed data from 7,580 older adults (aged ≥65 years) participating in a nationwide longitudinal survey in China (CLHLS, 2017−2018 wave). Depressive symptoms were assessed using the 10-item Center for Epidemiological Studies Depression Scale (CES-D-10). Self-care ability was measured by physical activities of daily living (PADL) and instrumental activities of daily living (IADL).
items.author: Lunan Gao

items.title: High blood pressure among children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus in Uganda: A multicenter cross-sectional study
items.summary: by Charles Mwendwa Mutisya, Martin Nduwimana, Dickson Kajoba, Grace Ndeezi Background The coexistence of diabetes mellitus (DM) and hypertension (HTN) worsens the clinical outcomes of children with diabetes concerning both microvascular and macrovascular disease. It increases mortality risk by 5 times, with a higher risk of death in developing countries. Therefore, comprehensive care for patients with diabetes, including hypertension screening, must be provided. Methods This multicenter health facility-based cross-sectional study included 150 children and adolescents aged from 6 months to 18 years with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) who were treated at Jinja Regional Referral Hospital (JRRH), Mbale Regional Referral Hospital (MRRH) and Lira Regional Referral Hospital (LRRH).
items.author: Charles Mwendwa Mutisya, Martin Nduwimana, Dickson Kajoba et al.

items.title: Alginate hydrogel co-loaded with phellodendron bark extract and HucMSC-exosomes for combined antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and pro-repair acne effects
items.summary: by Yu He, Yu Wang, Yaofeng Zhi, Minxian Li, Meimei Wu, Yanyang Mai, Jiadi He, Jiaqin Chen, KwanNin To, Meigong Zhong, Xiaohong Ruan, Wanli Zuo, Yanming Huang, Liping Liang, MengDie Ou, Guohua Cheng, Xin Zhang Acne vulgaris is a common inflammatory skin disorder involving follicular hyperkeratosis, Cutibacterium acnes proliferation, and aberrant inflammation, often leading to scarring. Current antibiotic treatments face resistance and limited repair capacity. Here, we developed an alginate-based hydrogel co-loaded with Phellodendron bark extract (PBE) and human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (HucMSC-Exo) (PE gel). Antibacterial activity of PBE was evaluated against C. acnes , S. aureus , and E.
items.author: Yu He, Yu Wang, Yaofeng Zhi et al.

items.title: Association between surgery-oriented standardized clinical pathways and postoperative delirium in geriatric hip fracture patients: A retrospective cohort study
items.summary: by Zixing Zhao, Jinsheng Yu, Yubin Lan, Baitao Yang, Qi Tan, Zaoxiong Wen, Yitao Yao, Cuitian He, Xinyu Fang Background Elderly hip fracture patients are at high risk of postoperative delirium (POD). The association between surgery-oriented standardized clinical pathways and POD incidence remains poorly clarified. This study aimed to explore the association between surgery-oriented standardized clinical pathways, internal fixation clinical pathway(IFCP), versus arthroplasty clinical pathway(ARCP), and POD occurrence in elderly hip fracture patients. Methods This retrospective cohort study examined the medical records of patients aged 65 years and older who underwent hip fracture surgery at a tertiary medical facility from January 2022 to December 2025.
items.author: Zixing Zhao, Jinsheng Yu, Yubin Lan et al.

items.title: Intelligent chemical production mode occupational health risk identification, assessment and intervention study
items.summary: by Yin Fei Shen, Jian Qing Xu The intelligent transformation of the chemical industry has reshaped petrochemical production workflows and altered occupational-health risk landscapes. This paper delineates four typical operating scenarios for intelligent chemical manufacturing and develops a four-tier hierarchical risk indicator system covering objectives, criteria, factors, and measurable indicators. A hybrid entropy-weighted Bayesian-network evaluation model is established, where entropy weights calibrate prior probabilities of root-node inputs while conditional-probability tables are retained to characterize risk-coupling behaviors. Model performance is validated via time-series partitioning, multi-model benchmark comparisons, and cross-validation using Monte-Carlo simulations. An entropy-weighted TOPSIS multi-criteria decision-making method is adopted to rank intervention-target priorities, and discrete time-series analysis quantifies outcomes from a six-month closed-loop intervention program.
items.author: Yin Fei Shen, Jian Qing Xu

items.title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus in women from northern provinces of Lao People’s Democratic Republic, 2018–2019
items.summary: by Vilaysone Khounvisith, Bounthome Samountry, Janko van Beek, Aurélie Sausy, Regina Brunnhoefer, Bounta Vongphachanh, Khamtim Samountry, Maude Pauly, Joel Mossong, Jessica Tapp, Claude P. Muller, Antony P. Black, Judith M. Hübschen Background Cervical cancer is a frequent cause of morbidity and mortality in women worldwide and strongly linked to the presence of high-risk (HR) human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes. The present study aimed to determine HPV prevalence and genotypes and their relationship with cytology results in Lao women. Methods Between October 2018 and February 2019, a total of 1302 asymptomatic women (mean age 37.4 years, range 18–76) from Xiengkhouang, Luangprabang, Oudomxay and Huaphan provinces were invited to answer a questionnaire, and cervical cells were collected for cytology and a swab for PCR and Anyplex TM II HPV-HR detection.

items.title: Civic and community engagement among health profession students and professionals compared to the general population: A systematic review and meta-analysis protocol
items.summary: by Aria Ghasedi, Ramin Vahidi Background Physicians, nurses, and other health professionals encounter poverty, inequality, and the structural roots of ill health as a routine part of clinical work — an exposure that differs from that of most other occupations. The World Health Organization, the Global Consensus for Social Accountability of Medical Schools, and many professional bodies describe civic and community engagement as a professional responsibility. Whether health profession students and practitioners show higher, lower, or comparable levels of civic engagement relative to the broader public in non-crisis conditions has not been systematically reviewed. The existing literature is fragmented, limited to single professions, focused largely on pandemic volunteerism, and more concerned with attitudes than with behaviour.
items.author: Aria Ghasedi, Ramin Vahidi

items.title: Puncturable registered attribute-based keyword search for secure cloud data sharing
items.summary: by Zeyang Song, Yuyan Guo, Mingming Jiang, Zhiyao Yang Cloud data sharing requires methods that protect sensitive files while allowing authorized users to find and access them. Centralized key generation creates a risk of key escrow, while exposed user keys may compromise previously shared data. We develop a scheme that combines encrypted keyword search with selective restriction of decryption keys in a registered framework. Users generate their own secret keys, and a key curator verifies and aggregates public registration information. Owners attach descriptive keywords and tags to encrypted files. Search compares combined keyword representations, and each new index excludes users according to the owner’s current list.
items.author: Zeyang Song, Yuyan Guo, Mingming Jiang et al.

items.title: Elevated blood lead levels among pregnant women in Amran, Yemen: Socio-demographic correlates and associations with a history of spontaneous abortion
items.summary: by Lina Qasem, Abdulsalam Al-Shami, Tawfeek A. A. Yahya, Lutfi AS. Al-Maktari, Mohammed Al-Maqhafi, Akram Al-Marqasi Background Lead exposure in pregnant women is a critical public health concern, particularly in resource-limited settings where environmental regulations are less stringent. Prenatal lead exposure (Pb) is associated with various adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. Therefore, this study aimed to assess blood lead levels (BLLs) among pregnant women in Amran, Yemen, and to identify health risks associated with environmental, behavioral, and socio-demographic factors. Methods A cross-sectional multi-center study was conducted between August and November 2024, involving a sample of 150 pregnant women (aged 20–41 years) recruited across public and private healthcare facilities in Amran.
items.author: Lina Qasem, Abdulsalam Al-Shami, Tawfeek A. A. Yahya et al.

items.title: Visuo-spatial perception deficit in ophthalmological disorders: Visual field extent matters
items.summary: by Hind Drissi, Marie Jauze, Eloise Perrier, Kenza Takani, Anne Céline Blanc, Armelle Laurens, Amandine Plaza, Jacqueline Jourdan, Julie Ferrotin, Elise Miclo, Lucie Loria, Florence De Saint-Etienne, Carole Malet, Laure Pisella Objectives Persons with Visual Impairment (VI) are more at risk to be without academic qualification. This is classically attributed to limited access to visual information, considered difficult due to reduced visual acuity. However, in some cases, visual acuity is preserved but visual field is reduced. Given the importance of visuo-spatial skills in learning, we assessed the accuracy of perceptual visuo-spatial judgements relative to visual field extent and visual acuity to question their respective contribution to the functional repercussions in VI.
items.author: Hind Drissi, Marie Jauze, Eloise Perrier et al.

items.title: Gender representation in highly cited endodontic research: A multivariate analysis
items.summary: by Esra Arılı Öztürk, Ceren Turan Gökduman, Şule Aktaş, Burhan Can Çanakçi To evaluate the representation of women as first, last, and corresponding authors in highly cited endodontic articles and investigate factors related to female authorship. The 200 most-cited endodontic articles published between 2015 and 2024 were identified in the Web of Science Core Collection. Authors’ genders were determined using an automated database and manually verified. Associations between female authorship and journal features, geographic origin, funding, collaboration patterns, and citation performance were analyzed using multivariable regression models. Among 1,262 authors, 31% were women. Women represented 36% of first authors, 24.5% of last authors, and 33.5% of corresponding authors; 77.5% of articles included at least one woman.
items.author: Esra Arılı Öztürk, Ceren Turan Gökduman, Şule Aktaş et al.

items.title: Calreticulin modulates the infection process and nodule organogenesis in the Phaseolus vulgaris-Rhizobium symbiosis
items.summary: by Yolanda Ortega-Ortega, Janet Carrasco-Castilla, Marco A. Juárez-Verdayes, Noreide Nava, Jorge Solis-Miranda, Ronal Pacheco, Carmen Quinto Calreticulin (CRT) is an endoplasmic-reticulum Ca 2 ⁺ -binding chaperone with established roles in Ca 2 ⁺ homeostasis and protein quality control, but its contribution to legume-rhizobium symbiosis is poorly understood. Here, we identified the CRT family of Phaseolus vulgaris and investigated the role of PvCRT08 during symbiosis with Rhizobium tropici CIAT 899. PvCRT08 showed dynamic transcript accumulation during the symbiosis; moreover, promoter activity was detected in root hairs, cortical cells, nodule primordia, and infected cells of mature nodules. RNAi-mediated downregulation of PvCRT08 increased the number of infection threads reaching cortical cells, whereas overexpression increased infection threads retained in root hairs and reduced those reaching the cortex.
items.author: Yolanda Ortega-Ortega, Janet Carrasco-Castilla, Marco A. Juárez-Verdayes et al.

items.title: A boundary-sensitive and structure-adaptive lightweight network for medical image segmentation
items.summary: by Yaodong Guo, Yuzhu Liu, Sai Ma Reliable medical image segmentation remains challenging in weak-contrast boundary regions, ambiguous anatomical transitions, and structurally heterogeneous areas. In addition, many high-performing models improve overlap-based metrics by introducing increasingly complex architectures, making it difficult to balance segmentation accuracy, boundary fidelity, and model compactness. To address these issues, this paper presents a boundary-sensitive and structure-adaptive lightweight framework for CT liver segmentation. The proposed method integrates three task-oriented components in a U-shaped architecture: Boundary-Sensitive Semantic Recalibration Attention (BSRA), Structure-Adaptive Scale Selection Fusion (SASF), and a Detail-Compensated Residual Lightweight Block (DCRB). Experiments were conducted on the CT subset of the CHAOS dataset under a patient-level five-fold cross-validation protocol.
items.author: Yaodong Guo, Yuzhu Liu, Sai Ma

items.title: Heterogeneous mixture-of-experts for long-horizon vessel trajectory prediction across regional datasets
items.summary: by Yuxiang Tan, Yingqiang Cai, Kuan Fan, Xiaowen Li, Guangyu Qiu Long-horizon vessel trajectory prediction for maritime traffic monitoring and route planning requires both a prompt response to manoeuvres and control of error accumulation. UnifiedInternalMoE combines a motion-prior residual expert with four temporal predictors in a separate checkpoint for each region and seed. Convex weights are fitted to validation predictions at 5, 10, and 60 min and interpolated to produce the complete future trajectory. A ten-seed comparison across four regions, together with capacity controls, learned gating, and internal ablations, evaluates the benefit of the heterogeneous combination and its sources. In a five-seed evaluation on an independent Finnish AIS subset, the fusion has the lowest mean average displacement error (ADE) at all six horizons, with ADE@60 of 1719.53±25.80 m; it does not consistently lead in long-horizon final displacement error (FDE) or frozen source-to-target transfer.
items.author: Yuxiang Tan, Yingqiang Cai, Kuan Fan et al.

items.title: Sleep hygiene, caffeine use, and academic performance among university students: A cross-sectional study
items.summary: by Razi Alshaikh, Wadea Jebriel, Mohammad Shahrouri, Tartil Zarura, Hasan Khouli Background Caffeine use is common among university students, but its associations with sleep hygiene and academic performance remain uncertain. This study examined these associations among Palestinian university students. Methods A cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted from March 21 to May 28, 2026. Among 379 participants, continuous grade point average (GPA) was available for 354. Measures included estimated caffeine intake, caffeine timing, Sleep Hygiene Index (SHI) score, sleep duration, sleep regularity, and study hours. Associations were assessed using analysis of variance, correlation, and multivariable linear regression. Caffeine intake was entered into the regression model as ln(mg/day + 1).
items.author: Razi Alshaikh, Wadea Jebriel, Mohammad Shahrouri et al.

items.title: Motor imagery-based brain-computer interface training for upper-limb rehabilitation after subacute stroke: A randomized sham-controlled trial
items.summary: by Qifeng Tong, Jianing Wu, Pengcheng Fan, Sunyue Cai, Minzhe Wang, Jianqiu Gong, Fangchao Wu Objective To determine whether motor imagery (MI) based brain-computer interface (BCI) training improves upper-limb motor function in patients with subacute stroke compared with a high-fidelity sham-BCI control, and to explore accompanying structural and resting-state functional MRI changes. Method In this participant-blinded randomized controlled trial, 32 patients with subacute stroke were randomized to a MI-based BCI group or a high-fidelity BCI sham-control group (n = 16 each). Both groups received dose-matched training (30 min/session, 5 sessions/week for 4 weeks) in addition to standard rehabilitation. Upper-limb motor outcomes were assessed using the Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity (FMA-UE; primary outcome), Wolf Motor Function Test (WMFT), Motor Assessment Scale (MAS), and Modified Barthel Index (MBI).
items.author: Qifeng Tong, Jianing Wu, Pengcheng Fan et al.

items.title: Impact of MRI sequence heterogeneity on deep learning–based segmentation of brain metastases
items.summary: by Dong-Won Shin, Chang Hyun Lee, Hyun Ju Kim, Kihoon Sung, Young Jae Kim, Kwang Gi Kim, Gi Taek Yee Brain metastases (BMs) require accurate delineation for treatment planning, yet magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) acquisition protocols vary substantially in clinical practice. Such protocol-level heterogeneity may affect the generalizability of deep learning-based segmentation models. This study evaluated the impact of heterogeneous T1-weighted MRI protocols on BM segmentation performance using two three-dimensional architectures, 3D Attention U-Net and DUCK-Net 3D. A retrospective dataset of 925 contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI studies from 720 patients was analyzed. Models were trained under six sequence configurations, including multi-sequence, Black-Blood (BB), Non-Black-Blood (Non-BB), and three single-sequence cohorts.
items.author: Dong-Won Shin, Chang Hyun Lee, Hyun Ju Kim et al.

items.title: Forest proximity and habitat heterogeneity support insectivorous birds and arthropods in California vineyards
items.summary: by Eleanor K. MacDonald, Daniel S. Karp, Autumn Turner, Breanna L. Martinico, Houston Wilson, Erin E. Wilson-Rankin, Matthew D. Johnson Agricultural intensification often simplifies habitat structure, reshaping multi-trophic communities by altering arthropod prey and the insectivorous birds that depend on them throughout the year, particularly during breeding. In vineyards, insectivorous birds may also contribute to pest suppression, creating opportunities to link biodiversity conservation with agroecosystem function. We paired point count bird surveys with concurrent sticky trap arthropod sampling across 20 organic or near-organic vineyards in Napa Valley, California, USA, to test whether the same habitat features predict variation in insectivorous bird guilds and arthropod communities.
items.author: Eleanor K. MacDonald, Daniel S. Karp, Autumn Turner et al.

items.title: CogD-ML: Cognitive determinants of social commerce purchase intention in Bangladesh using machine learning and explainable AI
items.summary: by Saikat Barua, Raiyan Rahman, Abul Kalam Al Azad, Sifat Momen Cognitive factors are associated with online purchase intentions in developing economies, and the linear models conventionally used to study them can miss non-linear patterns. We report an applied integration of the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) with machine learning and explainable AI (XAI) to predict social media-driven e-commerce purchase intentions in Bangladesh. Survey data from 352 young, student-dominated consumers captured attitudes, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and purchase behavior on validated Likert scale items. After reliability-based labeling and feature selection, we ran an ablation across seven classical classifiers and one multilayer perceptron, with stratified five-fold cross-validation, threshold sensitivity analysis, and a cross-domain check.
items.author: Saikat Barua, Raiyan Rahman, Abul Kalam Al Azad et al.

items.title: Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day Distance Milestone
items.summary: Spaceflight enthusiasts marked the Voyager 1 spacecraft reaching a distance of one light-day on November 18, 2026, nearly fifty years after its 1977 launch. To commemorate the event, stargazers at the Emirates Astronomical Observatory flashed a Morse code message reading 'V-G-R' into the night sky. Traveling at the speed of light, it takes one full day for a signal to reach humanity's most distant interstellar spacecraft, currently located roughly 26 billion kilometers from Earth.

items.title: Severe Tropical Cyclone Xavier Stirs the Southwest Pacific
items.summary: A slow-moving tropical disturbance northeast of Samoa and the Cook Islands rapidly intensified into Tropical Cyclone Xavier, marking an unusually powerful start to the region's storm season. Fuelled by high sea surface temperatures and El Niño conditions, Xavier achieved peak winds of 220 kilometers per hour, making it the strongest November tropical cyclone on record east of the international date line. The storm damaged local homes and disrupted power supplies before weakening as it encountered dry air and moved westward. Meteorological services expect additional storms later in the season.

items.title: Stunning Astrophotography Captures Iconic Cosmic Nebulae
items.summary: Recent astrophotography data reveals a colorful cosmic landscape featuring the famous Horsehead Nebula, a towering dust and gas structure located roughly 1,500 light-years away. The scene also highlights the triple star system Alnitak, the hydrogen-illuminated Flame Nebula, and the active star-forming region NGC 2023. The underlying data was gathered over nearly six hours at the Utah Desert Remote Observatories, utilizing equipment operated remotely by an astrophotographer located more than 2,000 kilometers away in Illinois.
items.author: NASA APOD
items.original_title: NASA Science
items.original_summary: On November 17, fans of interstellar spaceflight around planet Earth were invited to shine a message into the night sky. Traced by a flashlight beam switched on and off, the dashes and dots of a Morse code message captured in this time exposure from the Emirates Astronomical Observatory, are read V-G-R. That's a call sign for the Voyager 1 spacecraft currently in interstellar space some 26 billion kilometers away. How long did it take the message to reach humanity's most distant interstellar spacecraft? Traveling at the speed of light, the answer is one day. In fact, the Voyager 1 spacecraft was confirmed to reach its one light-day distance milestone on November 18, at 10:16:07 UTC, nearly 50 years after launch in 1977.

items.title: Entropy Products and Black Hole Horizons in Scalar Theory
items.summary: Researchers analyzing regular black hole horizons in Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory demonstrate that entropy products are not strictly fixed by charges and couplings. By constructing asymptotically flat branches, the study shows that horizon products can vary above or below squared extremal entropy while remaining constant as mass changes.
items.author: Kevin Goldstein, Vishnu Jejjala, Suresh Nampuri
items.original_title: Entropy Products and the Extremal Limit That Never Comes
items.original_summary: Two regular black hole horizons need not have an entropy product fixed by the charges and couplings. In Einstein--Maxwell--scalar theory, we construct asymptotically flat branches with products above or below the squared extremal entropy. Regularity selects their horizon scalar values, and different branches can share the charges, couplings, and asymptotic scalar. Each product stays constant as mass and asymptotic scalar vary. The horizon areas stay apart and no extremal limit is reached: the temperature vanishes only where the mass diverges. We prove local existence.

items.title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. Because capabilities such as rendering requested text or composing multiple objects are inherently prompt-dependent, a natural hypothesis is that improving them requires learning complex, input-dependent transformations. To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model. On SD3.5-M, these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M). We fit them to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints, with no reward in the objective.
items.author: Tuna Han Salih Meral, Kaan Oktay, Alec Helbling et al.

items.title: High-temperature Gibbs states are uniformly Markovian and trivial
items.summary: We prove that, above a constant temperature threshold, Gibbs states of local noncommuting qudit Hamiltonians exhibit exponential decay of mutual information and conditional mutual information (CMI). Specifically, we prove exponential decay of the CMI for arbitrary spatial tripartitions $A \sqcup B \sqcup C$ which need not comprise the entire system, thereby establishing a \textit{uniform Markov property} for high-temperature Gibbs states. A central obstruction to proving such bounds is that conventional cluster expansions for the logarithm of reduced Gibbs states can fail to converge due to noncommutativity. Our main insight is to construct a classical representation of the Gibbs state using an overcomplete basis.
items.author: Andrew D. Kim, Tai Hsuan Yang, Jong Yeon Lee

items.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
items.summary: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections.
items.author: Weihao Cheng

items.title: Little Red Dots from Primordial Vacuum Bubbles
items.summary: Quantum tunneling transverse to the inflaton trajectory can produce $10^6$--$10^8M_\odot$ primordial black holes at the abundance of JWST's little red dots, without the enhanced curvature perturbations excluded by limits on CMB spectral distortions. Rare vacuum bubbles nucleate during a brief interval of inflation and later form black holes, with adjustable mass and abundance and a narrow mass spectrum of percent-level width. The leading constraint, from accretion, is satisfied for a population matching the bright little red dots even if all the emitted radiation escapes as hard X-rays.
items.author: Miguel Barroso Varela, Katherine Freese, Matthew Kleban et al.

items.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
items.summary: Hybrid architectures have become mainstream among open-weight language models. Their global-attention and bounded-state layers maintain heterogeneous caches whose demands vary with context length and concurrency. We present TideCache, a serving system on CPU--GPU superchips with three components for allocating GPU memory among caches and managing their residency across GPU and host memory. The Transparent Cache Pool redistributes physical pages among cache components behind fixed virtual addresses, preserving cache layouts and backend interfaces. The Cache Streamer uses computation intervals provided by bounded-state layers to prefetch the next global-attention layer's prefix into GPU slots shared across global-attention layers, reducing GPU residency while overlapping layer-wise transfers with computation.
items.author: Jinbin Luo, Xiaozhe Yao, Shang Yang et al.

items.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
items.summary: Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. Latent action learning recovers such supervision from visual transitions, yet often learns the underlying dynamics largely from scratch. We ask whether a pretrained video generator can instead provide the prior for both inverse and forward dynamics. We introduce O$^{2}$LaF, built on a simple principle: one prior, two dynamics. We initialize both models from the same pretrained video DiT and adapt them to their distinct roles: a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries for inverse dynamics, and a causal, action-conditioned video generator for forward dynamics. By controlling information access and optimizing both dynamics end-to-end through a compact bottleneck, O$^{2}$LaF learns transferable actions from unlabeled videos.
items.author: Yuxin Jiang, Wenqiang Sun, Jiaqi Li et al.

items.title: Fractional Charge at Dislocations from Band-Inversion Cancellation
items.summary: Band inversions with opposite Chern numbers cancel in the Hall response and yield counterpropagating boundary modes that can gap out. However, a bulk probe of the topology that survives such a cancellation is lacking. We here show that dislocations in inversion-symmetric two-band crystals with cancelling band inversions bind a half-integer charge, which reveals the quantized bulk polarization of the bond-centered obstructed atomic limit realized by such crystals. To demonstrate this, we continuously deform a broad class of two-band lattice models into decoupled chains, without closing the bulk gap or breaking the inversion symmetry, where the dislocation charge follows from a count of occupied bonds.
items.author: Vladimir Juričić, Rodrigo Soto-Garrido

items.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
items.summary: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail. In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent. Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic grounding across diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation without task-specific adaptation.
items.author: Yiyang Du, Yuxuan Kuang, Qitao Zhao et al.

items.title: Field theory and the biquadratic spin-1 chain
items.summary: The antiferromagnetic biquadratic spin-1 chain is gapped, $SU(3)$ symmetric, and integrable. Standard arguments suggest that its low-energy physics is described by the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ nonlinear sigma model at $θ=π$. Using the Bethe ansatz, we show that its low-energy excitations can be interpreted as deconfined domain walls, just as in the sigma model. However, the lattice model is integrable, whereas the field theory is generally believed not to be. We propose a solution to this mystery by finding an integrable field theory with the same low-energy limit but which is not Lorentz invariant. The integrability-preserving scaling limit is obtained by adding a higher conserved charge and tuning the chain to criticality.
items.author: Luisa Eck, Paul Fendley

items.title: Local velocimetry for atomic superfluids: from Riemann rarefaction waves to quantized vortices
items.summary: We demonstrate local velocimetry for atomic superfluids in two dimensions (2D). Using matter-wave interferometry based on Raman--Bragg beam splitters, we map the local gradient of the phase of the superfluid's wavefunction onto displacement of the interference fringes and reconstruct the 2D velocity field. We illustrate the capabilities of this technique by applying it to two canonical problems. First, we directly observe the self-similar evolution of the velocity field in 1D Riemann rarefaction flows. Second, we map out the full 2D velocity field around quantized vortices, explicitly demonstrating the quantization of velocity circulation.
items.author: Yansheng Zhang, Yi Jiang, Feiyang Wang et al.

items.title: Bio-PM-Guided Synthetic IMU Generation
items.summary: Collecting and labeling inertial measurement unit (IMU) data for human activity recognition (HAR) is expensive, and models trained on one group of subjects often fail to generalize to unseen individuals. Even with balanced data, classifiers struggle to distinguish dynamically similar activity classes and benefit from targeted augmentation. We explore whether synthetic IMU data generated in the representation space of a pretrained biosignal encoder, Bio-PM \cite{b1}, can serve as a practical augmentation source. Rather than synthesizing raw signals, we leverage Bio-PM's frozen encoder to convert 10-second IMU windows into token embedding sequences and train class-conditional decoders in this space: (1) an autoregressive transformer decoder that predicts tokens sequentially, and (2) a diffusion decoder that learns the token distribution through a denoising objective.
items.author: Deepali Singh, Deepesh Parpani, Aviral Gupta

items.title: Query-Optimal Quantum Minimum Finding from Numerical Estimators
items.summary: We propose a quantum minimum-finding algorithm for objectives accessed via numerical estimators that avoids the logarithmic query overhead of amplifying the confidence of estimates before the search. A coherent estimator that is $\varepsilon$-accurate with probability at least $2/3$ on each of $N$ labels suffices to find a $2\varepsilon$-optimal label using $O(\sqrt N)$ base-estimator queries at constant confidence. The query bound and the additive-error constant are separately worst-case optimal. More generally, suppose a preparation assigns probability mass at least a known $p$ to objective values at most $a$. Without knowing $a$ or the prepared distribution, our algorithm returns a candidate and an estimate $v$ such that, jointly with constant probability, $v$ is $\varepsilon$-accurate for the candidate and $v\le a+\varepsilon$.
items.author: Egil Bae

items.title: Fast, in-place, and ancilla-free quantum algorithms for integer multiplication and inversion
items.summary: Arithmetic operations are a fundamental building block in the design of quantum algorithms, with their implementation cost expected to have a significant impact on the viability of a wide variety of quantum applications. In this work, we present novel algorithms for a number of in-place quantum arithmetic operations that are highly efficient in terms of their space and gate count overheads compared to the current state-of-the-art. We show that in-place modular multiplication of integers, modulo a power of two, can be performed with either a classical or quantum odd multiplier using $O(n^{1+ε})$ gates and no ancilla qubits, for any $ε>0$.
items.author: David Halpenny, Adithya Sireesh, Petros Wallden

items.title: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermions with Neural Gaussian Tensor Networks
items.summary: Accurate simulations of strongly correlated electrons remain a central challenge in computational physics. We introduce neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states (NN-GPEPS), which exploit the locally-entangled subspace of Gaussian states to give an architecture more compatible with modern neural networks and an exact contraction cost of $O(N^{3/2})$ on two-dimensional lattices. For the Hubbard model at $U/t=8$ and $1/8$ hole doping, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies in large lattices of up to 1024 sites. These results demonstrate an accurate approach to strongly correlated fermions by connecting neural networks with Gaussian tensor networks.
items.author: Runze Chi, Ao Chen, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan

items.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
items.summary: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming prior work in all of these dimensions. We release a family of models that define a new Pareto frontier in terms of metric accuracy, sharpness, temporal consistency, and runtime.
items.author: Peiyun Hu, Marko Mihajlovic, Lyndon Duong et al.

items.title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
items.summary: LLM-based agents are becoming increasingly capable at discovering, validating and patching vulnerabilities in real software, and vendors and researchers report that this is already changing how vulnerabilities are found and fixed. These claims, however, are scattered across papers, vendor reports and disclosures and are rarely comparable. We introduce a framework that rates these capabilities on an autonomy scale modeled on the levels of driving automation, and qualifies each claim by its correctness, its availability and the strength of its evidence. We use this framework to systematize the published evidence on LLM capability in vulnerability research. We find that agents discovered, validated, and patched vulnerabilities in real-world software without human intervention before the restricted frontier models of 2026, and that open-weight models subsequently attained comparable autonomy for discovery and validation.
items.author: Amine Lbath, Manan Suri, Aurelien Delaitre et al.

items.title: A Tutorial on Complementarity-Based Contact Models for Robotics
items.summary: Simulating rigid-body dynamics with contact is fundamental to robotics, from motion synthesis and control to mechanism design. Many widely used simulators rely on cone complementarity formulations, whose physical assumptions and numerical solution require substantial background. While excellent surveys, monographs, and course notes exist, they mostly address computational mechanics or computer graphics or document a single simulator. To the best of our knowledge, a self-contained pedagogical treatment for robotics, bringing these formulations and their solvers together with complete derivations and a unified notation, does not yet exist. This tutorial addresses this gap by connecting rigid-body dynamics, conic optimization, and frictional contact.
items.author: Onur Beker, A. René Geist, Michael Posa et al.

items.title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
items.summary: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) addresses this by learning a policy that decides, per instance, which features to acquire under a budget. Existing AFA methods train this policy by optimizing a self-constructed utility target rather than distilling an explicit teacher. We construct this teacher explicitly. At training time the label and the unobserved feature values are available, and together they determine the teacher in closed form: an oracle that ranks every candidate by its effect on the downstream predictor's error.
items.author: Yang Meng, Zixin Ding, Robert L. Grossman et al.

items.title: Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
items.summary: The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms. Our construction of these so-called equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for $Γ(2)$ and $Γ_0(2)$ proceeds at the level of generating series that take values in an infinite-dimensional (pro-unipotent) Lie group and closely follow Brown's analogous construction in the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ case.
items.author: Emiel Claasen, Mehregan Doroudiani, Claude Duhr et al.

items.title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model. We propose Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework that offloads temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components, allowing the VLA to focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. PGX decomposes long-horizon loco-manipulation into three layers: (i) a predicate-based state machine governs task progression, using physical predicates to gate phase transitions, trigger recovery, and coordinate navigation and waiting. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demonstration segmentation, online execution, and stage-wise evaluation; (ii) VLA skills operate within active manipulation phases, with flat or stage-trained models concentrating on task-relevant actions; and (iii) world-coordinate locking (WCL) maintains spatial consistency through base station keeping, object-relative positioning, and world-anchored contact targets.
items.author: Kai Lu, Chenyang Ma, Ioannis Havoutis

items.title: UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation
items.summary: A question of fundamental interest is whether parity is violated on large scales in the Universe. This possibility has been motivated by recent analyses of the four-point matter correlation function. It has also been suggested that detectable parity violation could be generated during inflation by the dynamical Chern-Simons operator, a leading effective field theory correction to general relativity. In this work, we examine this possibility in realistic UV completions, including fermionic and string-theoretic examples. We show that existing bounds on the tensor-scalar-scalar (TSS) bispectrum strongly constrain the possibility of generating a detectable parity-odd trispectrum. For tensor-to-scalar ratios near current observational limits, detectability is incompatible with, or pushes against, the regime of validity of these UV completions.
items.author: Alexander Cassem, Mark P. Hertzberg

items.title: Star-forming disc galaxies align tangentially with the cosmic tidal field
items.summary: The alignments of galaxy shapes, with one another and with the large-scale structure of the Universe, have been a topic of considerable investigation within cosmology and extragalactic astrophysics for the last 60 years. Galaxy alignments are a major systematic for weak gravitational lensing and help us learn about the processes of galaxy formation. Red early-type galaxies are known to show strong radial alignments around other galaxies; however, blue star-forming galaxies have shown little evidence of alignment. We combine SPHEREx spectrophotometry with DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys to build a full-sky catalogue of 71 million galaxies with precise redshifts. With this catalogue we are able to measure alignment signals by splitting galaxies into colour and morphological samples.
items.author: Calum Murray, Roman Paviot, Martin Kilbinger et al.

items.title: Realized versus Population Reliability: Anytime-Valid Self-Consistency Certification under Correlated Reasoning
items.summary: Self-consistency certification treats repeated sampling from a language model as sequential evidence accumulation and stops when an anytime-valid e-process crosses a threshold, guaranteeing finite-sample Type I error control by Ville's inequality. Prior constructions assume sampled rollouts are conditionally independent. We show this assumption fails in practice: reasoning streams are positively correlated through shared reasoning prefixes or across-prompt heterogeneity, changing not merely certificate efficiency but the hypothesis certified. Modeling dependence via a per-unit latent state (the random-effects / intraclass-correlation structure) induces exchangeable, equi-correlated increments with correlation $ρ$. Correlation splits the single null into a realized null about the drawn belief and a population null about average model behavior, which coincide only when $ρ=0$.
items.author: Terence D. Agbeyegbe, Toneukarin G. Agbeyegbe

items.title: Which black hole modes ring freely? Horizon regularity, the forced ringdown transient, and GW250114
items.summary: The quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a black hole are defined by keeping only ingoing waves at the horizon. We ask what horizon regularity requires of the outgoing waves this condition discards. For a scalar-like perturbation, bounded first derivatives in a frame regular at the future horizon rule out outgoing waves that decay more slowly than the surface gravity $κ$, and smoothness singles out a ladder of frequencies, $ω=mΩ_{\rm H}-ijκ$ with $j=1,2,\dots$ and $Ω_{\rm H}$ the horizon angular velocity. We call these the horizon modes. For Schwarzschild black holes and the dominant $\ell=m=2$ Kerr modes, only the fundamental QNM decays more slowly than $κ$.
items.author: Jahed Abedi, Niayesh Afshordi

items.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. We introduce the Multimodal Concept Lens (MC-Lens), a multimodal Jacobian lens, to study these functions in VLM concept processing. Its vision encoder and language decoder lenses map intermediate states to a shared semantic space defined by the decoder's output vocabulary to compare concept accessibility across modalities. MC-Lens supports internal concept interventions to examine the role of accessed concepts in downstream computation.
items.author: Jiahao Huang, Jun Wang

items.title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards
items.summary: A passing UVM regression shows the design agrees with the reference model on what the scoreboard checks, not that it meets the specification. Bugs that pass every test yet violate the specification, termed scoreboard escapes, survive mature testbenches. We present Verify the Verifier, to our knowledge the first framework whose LLM-based Anomaly Cross-Checker examines a passing regression's traces against the specification. Of 564 bugs inserted into four OpenTitan IPs, 68 are candidate scoreboard escapes: non-equivalent, exercised by the tests, yet passing. The framework confirmed 41 as scoreboard escapes with assertions failing on the buggy design and proven on the original.
items.author: Ana E. Sanchez Villalobos, Michael D. Quinn, Aakash Tyagi et al.

items.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
items.summary: Neural-network quantum states (NQSs) exhibit a disparity in converging to the ground state during energy minimization: while the energy converges quadratically with the error in the variational wave function, other observables converge only linearly, which limits the accuracy of physical predictions. Here we show how to close this gap by introducing a new algorithm that improves the accuracy of NQSs. Our method, termed dynamical averaging, estimates expectation values by averaging over a state (or observable) evolved in real-time. Using insights from quantum information, we prove an up-to-quadratic suppression of error in arbitrary ground state observables, thus matching the fast convergence of the energy.
items.author: John M. Martyn, Rod Rofougaran, Samuel Stein et al.

items.title: Relativistic Kinetic Theory of Collisionless Particles with Variable Mass and Frame Transformations
items.summary: In this work, we present the relativistic kinetic theory of a gas of collisionless point particles with non-constant mass, which can also be understood as being subject to a scalar force. Our results hold in an arbitrary conformal frame, and we explicitly derive how they transform between frames. The mathematical construction relies on a tilted Sasaki metric, whose associated phase-space geometry is adapted to particles of variable mass, as well as on the one-particle distribution function, from which macroscopic observables are derived. Finally, we show that the one-particle distribution function can always be taken to be gauge- and frame-invariant, and the corresponding generalisation of the Liouville (or collisionless Boltzmann) equation is satisfied in each frame.
items.author: Adrián Casado-Turrión, Paulo B. Ferraz, Mindaugas Karčiauskas et al.

items.title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm for Differential Equations: Application to Simulating a Biomolecular System
items.summary: Quantum algorithms for differential equations have the potential for substantial algorithmic speedups over classical methods. However, they rely on certain assumptions and abstract oracle specifications that leave their practical feasibility and computational advantages for realistic applications unclear. Here we formalize the concept of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for differential equations as one that accepts classical inputs and returns classical outputs, and provide implementations for algorithmic primitives in constructing such algorithms. We present a tailored end-to-end quantum algorithm for the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann (LPB) equation, a partial differential equation (PDE) with variable coefficients widely used in simulating a biomolecular system. We explicitly implement all aspects of the algorithm, from preparing an initial state to generating a quantum solution and estimating properties of the system.
items.author: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Daniyaal Farooqi, Gavin K. Brennen et al.

items.title: Classically Trained Quantum Generative Models with Shared Training and Fine Tuning for Quantum Matter
items.summary: Ground-state measurement statistics characterize quantum matter. Selected correlations can guide the classical training of a quantum sampler even when sampling the full distribution is difficult. We ask whether training across related ground-state distributions helps the sampler reproduce their correlations more accurately. We train a hypernetwork to map Hamiltonian parameters to circuit angles, sharing information across the phase diagram before local fine-tuning with additional reference data for quantum deployment. For classical training, we derive an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator of Fourier coefficients for circuits built from general Pauli rotations, with a cost that depends on the circuit generators. We also introduce a CDF-KL loss for comparing selected marginals.
items.author: Mario Herrero-Gonzalez, Elham Kashefi, Mina Doosti
