items.title: PhyDEX: A Benchmark for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models via Dynamic Extrinsic Dexterity
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have advanced rapidly in language-conditioned robotic manipulation, yet existing benchmarks mainly evaluate gripper--object contact and largely ignore how objects interact with the environment through gravity, friction, inertia, and mass distribution. As a result, it remains unclear whether current policies truly understand physics or merely interpolate from their training data. We address this gap through the lens of dynamic extrinsic dexterity and introduce PhyDEX, a throwing benchmark in which a robot must infer an object's mass, center of mass, and friction to send it to a destination beyond its kinematic workspace. PhyDEX contains 35K trajectories (143 hours) across nine tasks and 100 scenes, covering uniform, irregular, and dynamic-mass objects with static, multiple, and moving destinations.
items.author: Hao Vo, Taisei Hanyu, Yuki Ikebe et al.

items.title: Twisting Spinning Particles with Superghost Backgrounds
items.summary: We construct twists of spinning particles in the classical BV formalism by giving constant backgrounds to the bosonic ghosts of local worldline supersymmetry, in analogy with Costello and Li's twist of supergravity, which gives a nonzero background to the ghost of local spacetime supersymmetry. We represent the superghosts on polynomial states and gauge selected worldline R symmetries, imposing the shifted R constraints absolutely and the unshifted ones relatively. On flat targets, the N=2 particle, its N=4 extension on a complex target and an N=8 particle with two fermion flavors give the de Rham, Dolbeault and polynomial linear BCOV complexes. The last two are the linearized field content of the open and closed B-model target-space theories.
items.author: Erik Fink, Jingqian Gou, Niklas Holbach et al.

items.title: Refractive Neutrino Mass: Effects of Fluctuations of the Dark Matter Field
items.summary: Observed neutrino oscillations can be reproduced by a refractive neutrino mass-squared arising from interactions with ultralight scalar dark matter (ULDM). The wave behaviour of the scalar field gives rise to a fluctuating interference pattern, inducing spatial and temporal variations in the refractive mass that can distort neutrino oscillation probabilities. We simulate the interference patterns of the scalar field in the presence of self-interactions. Using results of these simulations, the oscillation probabilities for JUNO and T2K experiments are computed. We find that the refractive mass scenario remains viable for the complex scalar field without self-coupling for $m_φ\lesssim 10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$. For $m_φ\gtrsim10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$, repulsive self-interactions narrow the density distribution, reducing the deviation of the survival probability at the first minimum to $ΔP \approx 0.07$ for an appropriate self-interaction coupling.
items.author: Soham Sahasrabuddhe, Manibrata Sen, Alexei Y. Smirnov

items.title: Self-gravity depletes superradiant clouds
items.summary: Superradiant clouds of ultralight scalars around black holes are often modeled as free fields, whose levels grow independently and decay slowly through gravitational-wave emission. We show that this limit is never realized. The cloud's self-gravity redistributes particles between levels, just as in the case of axion self-interactions, and dominates over self-interactions for decay constants $f_a\gtrsim6\times10^{16}\,{\rm GeV}\,(α/0.1)$, with $α$ the gravitational fine-structure constant. Self-gravity depletes the cloud by orders of magnitude and feeds more extended levels, weakening all signals that rely on the existence of a large cloud mass. A binary companion, however, can partly offset the depletion. Any assessment of superradiant signals must therefore account for both self-gravity and the cloud's environment.
items.author: Mateja Bošković, Lucas Gathercole, Thomas F. M. Spieksma et al.

items.title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
items.summary: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no direct experimental validation is available, comparisons to physically motivated potentials are valuable for drawing insight. We distinguish static properties, which are thermally accessible, from emergent properties, which require work from an external fatigue stress to drive rare events, and compare the potentials on both. An EAM potential and the NequIP foundational potential both agree closely with reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an anomalously low intrinsic stacking fault energy ($\sim7$ times lower than EAM) and thus predicts far more plastic deformation under fatigue cycling of a nanoscale flaw modeled after the classical Griffith crack problem.
items.author: Jingye Tan, Benjamin A. Jasperson, Eric Rothchild et al.

items.title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias alone
items.summary: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits. We demonstrate a generic, fabrication-free alternative in which a standard commercial photodiode becomes a spectrometer through its electrical drive alone, requiring no modification of the device, no optical filter and no modulation of the light. The mechanism is bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion (OED): light of different wavelengths is absorbed at different depths, and a sinusoidal bias changes how carriers generated at each depth are collected, so that every spectrum is encoded in the shape of the photocurrent waveform over one bias period.
items.author: Roi Yozevitch, Shmuel Sternklar, Ziv Glasser

items.title: Full Kummer Beams: Skyrmionic textures in bichromatic light
items.summary: In this work, we introduce full Kummer beams, the bichromatic analog of full Poincaré beams. To this end, we define three parameters that characterize bichromatic states of polarization and span the Kummer shape, the bichromatic counterpart of the Poincaré sphere. We find that, under certain conditions, full Kummer beams can exhibit skyrmionic textures with a Skyrme number that depends not only on the topological charges but also on the frequencies. These beams can also exhibit emergent behavior upon propagation, including robust, higher-order-like structures and a propagation-invariant Skyrme number over a wide range of beam-waist selections.
items.author: Jefferson Delgado-Quesada, Miguel A. Alonso, Eileen Otte

items.title: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Finite Element Model Updating: Closed-Form Hyperelastic Strain Energies from Heterogeneous Experiments
items.summary: Calibrating a hyperelastic constitutive model for a soft material traditionally poses two problems: an expert must choose its functional form, and several homogeneous tests must determine its parameters. Neural constitutive models solve the first, but either remain black boxes or draw on a library of candidate terms fixed in advance. Full-field measurements, such as those from digital image correlation (DIC), promise to solve the second, replacing those tests by a single heterogeneous one. Two gaps remain: flexibility during training with interpretability afterwards, and a way to train such a model on one heterogeneous test. Here we close both. We embed a constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold network (CKAN) in finite element model updating (FEMU) and train it by minimizing the mismatch between the predicted and the measured kinematic fields and reaction forces.
items.author: Kian P. Abdolazizi, Kevin Linka, Christian J. Cyron

items.title: $Zγ$ production in gluon fusion at NLO+NLL
items.summary: We study the production of $Zγ$ in gluon fusion at hadron colliders at the next-to-leading-order (NLO) in QCD. At the $13.6$ TeV LHC, we find that these NLO corrections are found to enhance the leading-order (LO) cross section by about $83$\% and reduce the conventional seven-point scale uncertainty from $22.3$\% at LO to $15.2$\% at NLO. We further perform the threshold resummation at next-to-leading-logarithmic (NLL) accuracy and match to the fixed order NLO results. We have presented the production cross section for various center of mass energies at the LHC. We find that this NLL resummation enhances the NLO production cross section by about $23$\%.
items.author: Chinmoy Dey, Niraj Koirala, M. C. Kumar et al.

items.title: ACE-Brain-0.7: Learning Execution-Grounded Reasoning for Embodied Agents
items.summary: Reliable reasoning for long-horizon embodied tasks requires predictions grounded in the observed execution state. We present ACE-Brain-0.7, a 9B vision--language model that combines spatial grounding, task understanding, and progress estimation. To train the model, we curate 3.7 million question--answer pairs, drawing execution supervision from egocentric human videos, robot episodes, and simulation. These questions span different stages of an execution and connect task-level judgments with observed progress and outcomes. We then fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B on this collection together with additional task, spatial-grounding, and progress-estimation data. Across six public task-reasoning benchmarks, ACE-Brain-0.7 achieves an average score of 76.5, ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 72.7 and Claude Opus 5.5 at 73.5.
items.author: Yinhe Wang, Shijun Shi, Feng Pan et al.

items.title: JARVIS: An Agent That Designs, Builds, and Tests Circuit Boards on Its Own
items.summary: Power electronics is central to the energy transition, but developing new hardware still relies on human-led design, fabrication, testing, and iteration. We present JARVIS, an embodied AI agent that autonomously closes this loop for circuit boards. JARVIS maintains machine-specific capabilities and constraints, scans its workspace using a robot-mounted 3D scanner, and constructs an executable digital twin in which it rehearses robot motions, fabrication steps, and circuit behavior before consuming materials. A single text instruction initiates the physical experiment. Using unmodified desktop equipment, the agent coordinates a robot arm, a PCB printer that deposits conductive silver ink and solder paste, and a pick-and-place machine.
items.author: Shibo Zhou, Tianqi Hong, Zheng Yan et al.

items.title: Inhomogeneous Cutoff Regularization of Loops in Cosmological Correlators
items.summary: We revisit the use of cutoff regularization in computing loop corrections to cosmological correlators. We argue that a cutoff corresponding to a fixed physical scale must be defined with respect to the local background geometry. In the presence of superhorizon perturbations, this is naturally implemented within the separate universe picture, where different local patches are regulated at the same physical scale. Expanding this cutoff in the long-wavelength background generates a series of regulator-induced contributions to loop amplitudes, which admit a diagrammatic interpretation as long-mode insertions on the corresponding loop contractions. Our cutoff prescription preserves residual spatial dilatations and volume-preserving anisotropic rescalings.
items.author: Jacopo Fumagalli, Keisuke Inomata

items.title: An Open-Source ROS 2 Framework for Shared Control in Surgical Teleoperation: Integrating the Haply Inverse3 with the da Vinci Research Kit
items.summary: Surgical teleoperation deprives surgeons of touch, forcing visual inference of tissue forces; the commercial platforms now restoring force feedback remain closed, preventing open research on haptic shared control. This paper provides a system contribution: it presents an open-source, ROS 2-native framework that integrates the compact, three-degree-of-freedom (3-DOF) Haply Inverse3 haptic device with the da~Vinci Research Kit (dVRK). The framework includes a novel mapping strategy that combines 3-DOF translational device input with separately tracked VerseGrip orientation into 6-DOF patient-side manipulator commands. Two virtual-fixture-inspired guidance modes serve as reference implementations to evaluate the framework in a within-subjects user study on a teleoperated hot-wire benchmark task in simulation, and the architecture is further demonstrated on physical dVRK hardware.
items.author: Balint Varga, Sebastian Fritz, Gergely Kiss et al.

items.title: Two distinct notions of speed in antiferromagnets
items.summary: The terahertz resonance frequencies of antiferromagnets characterize their precessional dynamics but do not necessarily imply faster laser-induced quenching of magnetic order. Here, we investigate the distinct roles of magnetic compensation and electronic scattering phase space by comparing ultrafast demagnetization in the antiferromagnetic charge-transfer insulator NiO, the metallic antiferromagnet Mn2Au, and a ferromagnetic Ni reference. The extracted response in Mn2Au is approximately four times faster than in NiO and substantially faster than in Ni. These observations are consistent with exchange-mediated scattering between antiparallel sublattices enabling rapid loss of antiferromagnetic order without requiring net angular-momentum transfer to an external reservoir, provided sufficient electronic scattering phase space is available.
items.author: Paul Herrgen, Stephan Wust, Christin Schmitt et al.

items.title: Review of Pion and Nucleon Gluon Parton Distribution Functions from Lattice QCD
items.summary: Gluons play an essential role in the strong interaction that binds quarks into hadrons, as described by quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Understanding how the fundamental dynamics of QCD give rise to hadron structure remains one of the outstanding challenges in nuclear and particle physics. Parton distribution functions (PDFs) provide a successful framework for describing high-energy scattering processes involving hadrons. However, our knowledge of gluon PDFs remains comparatively limited because of the experimental challenges associated with directly constraining the gluon structure of hadrons. In recent years, a major breakthrough has enabled the calculation of the Bjorken-$x$ dependence of PDFs directly from lattice QCD.
items.author: William Good, Huey-Wen Lin

items.title: Future avenues for precision oscillation measurements with compact movable reactors
items.summary: No planned neutrino experiment is expected to surpass Daya Bay's precision on $\thone$. Doing so requires innovative strategies to reduce statistical and systematic uncertainties. In this study, we consider a futuristic program with a movable reactor antineutrino source placed within short distances ($L\lesssim 3\,\km$) from the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) detector. Due to the large fiducial mass of JUNO, even a relatively small reactor can produce a statistically significant number of events over a few years to probe the $\lesssim 8.7\% \,\nuebar$ disappearance set by $\thone$. We consider two possibilities: a $\mathcal{O}(20\mwth)$ microreactor in alcoves of the access tunnel to the underground laboratory, and a $\mathcal{O}(400 \mwth)$ unit on the surface.
items.author: Matheus Hostert, Stephan A. Meighen-Berger, Maxim Pospelov

items.title: Simulation-pretrained autoencoders versus PCA for compressing multimode fibre transmission matrices
items.summary: Multimode optical fibres can image through a thin, flexible probe once their transmission matrix (TM) has been measured, but a TM is large and must be re-measured whenever the fibre moves. A compact model of feasible TMs would make storing and re-estimating them cheaper, so we ask how compactly TMs can be represented, and from how few measured TMs. Here we benchmark a permutation-equivariant autoencoder, pretrained on simulated fibres and adapted to measured TMs, against principal component analysis (PCA). At 62x compression, adapting the pretrained autoencoder with just two measured TMs reconstructs the TM of a 50um fibre well enough to focus light at 98% of the ideal enhancement, and it stays accurate when the TMs are shifted by 25 pixels or zoomed by 10%, which quickly degrades a linear basis.
items.author: Callum J. Wilson, Terry Wright, Qing Yang et al.

items.title: A photon-number-conserving multimode framework for pulse propagation dynamics across zero nonlinearity: Kerr-Raman cooperation and competition
items.summary: Raman scattering in multimode fibers shifts pulse spectra to lower frequencies and transfers photons between spatial modes. When the nonlinear coefficient changes sign within the pulse spectrum, the ordinary generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) can give unphysical predictions. Existing photon-number-conserving formulations either treat a single mode or exclude Raman scattering. We develop a time-domain multimode GNLSE that conserves photon number, includes the full Raman response and remains well defined at the zero-nonlinearity frequency. For narrowband pulses with a constant positive nonlinear coefficient, the framework reduces to the standard multimode GNLSE with instantaneous Kerr and delayed Raman terms. We then apply the framework to three coherently excited modes whose spectra shift across the zero-nonlinearity frequency.
items.author: Chao Mei, Weiye Huang, Junhong Yang et al.

items.title: High-Power Short-Wavelength Frequency Comb from Coherent Radiation of Uncompressed Electron Beams
items.summary: High-power frequency combs at short wavelengths would open new opportunities for precision measurements and high-resolution spectroscopy. Here, we propose a frequency comb based on coherent undulator radiation from uncompressed electron bunches. An optical frequency comb serves as the seed, establishing a common phase reference for microbunching in successive electron bunches and transferring its phase coherence to short-wavelength harmonic radiation. By exploiting interference between distinct laser-induced microbunching pathways, we reduce the sensitivity of the harmonic bunching phase to electron-beam energy fluctuations, a major challenge for maintaining interpulse coherence. Start-to-end simulations demonstrate frequency comb generation in the vacuum-ultraviolet (148 nm) and soft X-ray regimes, yielding average radiation powers of approximately 1 W and 100 mW, respectively, with approximately 6 $μ$W and 100 nW concentrated in individual comb teeth.
items.author: Chenzhi Xu, Bingyang Yan, Hanxiang Yang et al.

items.title: Perfumer: A Large Language Model-based Agentic Framework Accelerating Structural Relaxation and Electronic Band Prediction for First-Principle Calculation
items.summary: First-principles structural relaxation and band calculations require substantial computation and expertise. Here we present Perfumer, a large language model-based agentic framework that couples Quantum ESPRESSO with two predictive models. Across tested structures, pre-relaxation with Perfumer-relax model followed by QE refinement yielded a 2.75-fold overall speedup over QE alone. Perfumer-band model combines a periodic graph neural network with a latent Hermitian spectral head returns 12 band energies at any requested wavevector, preserving reciprocal lattice periodicity and time-reversal symmetry without constructing Hamiltonian. Trained on 125,153 self-curated band structures, Perfumer-band model reaches a median per-material mean absolute error of 0.157 eV on 2,607 test materials, including lanthanide, actinide and magnetic compounds, from held-out composition families spanning 85 elements, taking about 97 ms per material on two consumer CPU cores.
items.author: Zhiwei Li, Yuhao Zhou, Yikai Yang et al.

items.title: Hybrid Plasmon-Phonon Eigenmodes and Vortex States in a Graphene Ring on a Silica Substrate
items.summary: We investigate hybrid plasmon-phonon eigenmodes and localized electromagnetic vortex states in a graphene ring supported by a dispersive silica substrate. The interaction between graphene plasmons and infrared-active optical phonons of the substrate gives rise to distinct spectral branches of surface polaritons, whose dispersion characteristics are established analytically and validated by full-wave numerical simulations. Geometric confinement of these hybrid surface excitations produces spectrally separated families of localized multipolar eigenmodes with corresponding azimuthal symmetries. Particular attention is devoted to quadrupolar eigenstates, which exhibit nearly identical normalized spatial field distributions despite their substantial spectral separation and different attenuation characteristics. We demonstrate that coherent superposition of orthogonal quadrupolar field patterns gives rise to localized vortex states with opposite azimuthal phase winding.
items.author: Yanxu Guo, Oleh Demianyk, Vladimir R. Tuz

items.title: New Cryptography-Inspired Method Finds Pulsars Faster Using NASA Data
items.summary: Scientists have developed a breakthrough method using open data from NASA's Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope to discover pulsars a million times faster than before. By adapting geometry and lattice algorithms traditionally used in cryptography, researchers turned complex multi-dimensional signal searches into manageable mathematical problems. This technique allowed a standard computer processor to find an isolated pulsar in just ten hours of equivalent computing time, bypassing traditional methods that would have taken centuries. The open-access nature of NASA's Fermi data enabled researchers outside the primary mission to apply these novel approaches, opening up possibilities for discovering many more elusive pulsars in the future.

items.title: Efficient calculation of the full Laguerre-Gaussian spectrum of entangled biphotons
items.summary: The spatial biphoton state generated by spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) enables applications in high-dimensional quantum information processing and is often described in Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) modes. However, calculating the full LG spectrum for arbitrary radial and orbital angular momentum (OAM) indices requires computationally demanding multidimensional integrations. We present a generating-function approach that analytically performs the four-dimensional transverse spatial integral without approximating the phase-matching function. The source geometry can be completely described by a few dimensionless parameters, which reduce to two parameters for wave-vector-degenerate photons with equal waists. Our derived expressions for the full LG spectrum allow for computationally efficient and numerically stable evaluation at high mode orders, addressing a crucial obstacle in previous works.
items.author: Jiabao Peng, Richard Bernecker, Stephan Fritzsche

items.title: Unusual increase in electrical and thermal conductivity of severely deformed CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy: Roles of disordering and nanostructuring in electron and phonon transport
items.summary: This work investigates how defect engineering and nanostructuring via severe plastic deformation influence electrical and thermal transport in the high-entropy alloy CrMnFeCoNi. High-pressure torsion (HPT) for up to N = 4 turns produces a hierarchical defect structure, including deformation twins at low strains, dislocations and Lomer-Cottrell locks at intermediate strains, and a high fraction of high-angle grain boundaries at large strains. While hardness naturally increases and saturates at ~520 Hv, both electrical and thermal conductivity exhibit an unusual increase upon HPT processing (from 0.953 MS m-1 and 10.3 W m-1 K-1 after homogenization to 1.003 +- 0.005 MS m-1 and 14.4 W m-1 K-1 after N = 4).
items.author: Jacqueline Hidalgo-Jiménez, Payam Edalati, Md Amirul Islam et al.

items.title: NASA Tests RS-25 Engine for Artemis Program
items.summary: NASA successfully conducted a developmental hot fire test of the RS-25 engine at the Stennis Space Center in Mississippi. Operators fired engine No. 10001 for 200 seconds on the Fred Haise Test Stand to capture performance and reliability data. Although this specific developmental unit will not fly, the tests support future Artemis missions, including the planned Artemis IV Moon landing. Four RS-25 engines provide up to 2 million pounds of combined thrust to launch the Space Launch System rocket for each Artemis flight.

items.title: Reward misalignment as an opportunity for materials discovery
items.summary: Reward misalignment is usually regarded as a failure of artificial intelligence. In materials discovery with generative AI models, however, disagreement between predefined rewards and expert judgment may reveal materials that the rewards overlook. We investigate this possibility using electronic flat bands as a prime example. Experts mostly agree with a numerical bandwidth score, but their disagreements are systematic and cannot be explained by an estimated 5% rate of mistaken labels. We learn the experts' preferences from pairwise comparisons and use them to guide a crystal diffusion model. The learned preferences and numerical score agree on the flattest bands but diverge elsewhere.
items.author: Ryotaro Okabe, Shoki Kishida, Abhijatmedhi Chotrattanapituk et al.

items.title: DUV (257 nm) LIDT of Anti-Reflective Coatings
items.summary: Laser-induced damage threshold in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) was used to perform tests on AR coated windows intended for industrial processes. The 257 nm wavelength was generated from Yb:YAG fundamental (1030 nm) and the long-term LIDT stability (up to 100000 shots) was selected as representative for minimal industrial qualification. Selected setup for the fourth harmonics generation consists of two stages, generation of second harmonic and subsequently the fourth harmonic with 13,4% conversation efficiency. In both 1-on-1 and S-on-1 experiments, the optics coated with Al2O3/SiO2 by ion beam sputtering technique demonstrated the highest LIDT value of 0.73 and 0.5 J/cm2 respectively.
items.author: Martin Mydlar, Hana Turcicova, Priyadarshani Narayanasamy et al.

items.title: Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day Distance From Earth After 49 Years
items.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft has reached a milestone of one light-day away from Earth, equivalent to roughly 16.1 billion miles, following more than 49 years of space travel. Operating since 1977 alongside its twin Voyager 2, the probe continues to explore interstellar space while relying on a diminishing nuclear battery. Mission engineers confirmed the milestone using the spacecraft's carrier signal and trajectory calculations while analyzing a temporary loss of science and engineering data. Radio signals now require a full 24 hours to travel in each direction between Earth and the distant probe.
items.author: Jessica Taveau

items.ai_title: Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day Distance From Earth After 49 Years
items.ai_summary: NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft has reached a milestone of one light-day away from Earth, equivalent to roughly 16.1 billion miles, following more than 49 years of space travel. Operating since 1977 alongside its twin Voyager 2, the probe continues to explore interstellar space while relying on a diminishing nuclear battery. Mission engineers confirmed the milestone using the spacecraft's carrier signal and trajectory calculations while analyzing a temporary loss of science and engineering data. Radio signals now require a full 24 hours to travel in each direction between Earth and the distant probe.

items.title: Sliding-ferroelectric control of dipolar and quadrupolar excitons in R-stacked WSe$_2$
items.summary: A fundamental property of interlayer excitons is their dipolar character, enabling electrical tunability, enhanced exciton-exciton interactions and extended lifetime. It is important for studying collective phenomena and realizing novel optoelectronic devices. However, in homo- or heterostructures based on two-dimensional semiconductors, the magnitude and orientation of the dipole moment are commonly locked due to spatially confined charges and nature of the band transition. Here, we use gate-dependent photoluminescence of few-layer R-WSe2 to harness sliding ferroelectricity for controlling the exciton dipole configuration of emerging layer-hybridised excitons. The sliding-ferroelectric control enables a pronounced on/off switching of the diffusive transport of hybrid dipolar excitons, while further facilitating gradual and abrupt dipole reconfigurations with emerging quadrupolar excitons.
items.author: Asmund Ottesen, Shun Feng, Edoardo Lopriore et al.

items.title: Study Uncovers Role of SUMOylation in Apoptotic Cell Clearance
items.summary: Research demonstrates that SUMO modifications play a crucial role in the clearance of apoptotic cells by regulating phagosomal degradation in C. elegans. Specifically, the SUMO E3 ligase GEI-17 modifies the GDP dissociation inhibitor GDI-1 at a specific site, which triggers phagosomal degradation. This modification allows GDI-1 to release GDP-bound RAB-1, which is subsequently converted into its active GTP-bound form with the help of the displacement factor PRAF-3. The converted RAB-1 then enables RAB-7 to bind and move from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi apparatus, promoting maturation and degradation activities. Without this targeted SUMOylation, GDI-1 traps RAB-1 in the cytoplasm, leading to impaired degradation. This regulatory mechanism is also conserved in mammals.
items.author: Lei Yuan, Peiyao Li, Aiying Ma et al.
items.original_title: GEI-17-mediated SUMOylation of GDP dissociation inhibitor GDI-1 regulates apoptotic cell clearance
items.original_summary: by Lei Yuan, Peiyao Li, Aiying Ma, Chao Li, Fuqiao Liu, Yunmin Xie, Qian Zheng, Hui Wang, Hui Xiao Apoptotic cell clearance represents the final stage of apoptosis and involves phagosome formation, maturation, and digestion. Here, we found that SUMO modifications participate in apoptotic cell clearance by influencing phagosomal degradation activity in C. elegans . The SUMO E3 ligase, GEI-17, SUMOylates GDP dissociation inhibitor (GDI-1) at K270 to trigger phagosomal degradation. Upon SUMOylation, GDI-1 facilitates release of GDP-bound RAB-1, which is subsequently converted to the GTP-bound form in a manner dependent on GDI displacement factor, PRAF-3. RAB-1 conversion enables binding and translocation of RAB-7 from the endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi to promote phagosome maturation and degradation activity.

items.title: High Altitude Hypoxia Blunted Varroa Mite Reproduction in Tibetan Bees
items.summary: Researchers investigating why beekeepers on the Tibetan Plateau rarely encounter Varroa mites discovered that high-altitude hypoxic conditions suppress the reproduction of these destructive parasites. Translocation experiments demonstrated that oxygen levels found at altitudes above 3,500 meters reduce mite fecundity and prevent offspring development, halting the persistence of local mite populations. Similar reproductive failures occurred when low-altitude honey bee colonies were subjected to comparable low-oxygen environments. This newly identified physiological vulnerability to reduced oxygen availability could inspire innovative, chemical-free methods for controlling mites in the beekeeping industry.
items.author: Ruike Wei, Shangning Yang, Xinlan Chen et al.
items.original_title: Altitude-induced hypoxia suppresses Varroa mite reproduction in Tibetan honey bees
items.original_summary: by Ruike Wei, Shangning Yang, Xinlan Chen, Yicheng Lu, Yao Liu, Fuliang Hu, Stephen J. Martin, Luo Zha, Huoqing Zheng Our reliance on honey bees ( Apis mellifera ) for pollination services and honey production continues to increase due to the global decline in other pollinators and rising demand for honey. The ectoparasitic mite ( Varroa destructor ) remains the biggest pest of honey bees forcing beekeepers into continual miticide use. Beekeepers on the Tibetan Plateau, however, report rarely seeing mites in their colonies, unlike all other areas of China. We conducted a series of translocation experiments to investigate this phenomenon.

items.title: Local Feedback Regulates Cell Fate and Tumor Stability
items.summary: Cell-state transitions within hierarchical tumors determine overall cellular composition, but the exact regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Using a Drosophila tumor model, researchers found that the differentiation of cancer stem cells into transit-amplifying progenitors depends directly on the proportion of immediate neighbors that are progenitors. This dynamic is governed by a local feedback transition rule that successfully predicts transition probabilities and replicates tumor growth patterns in 3D simulations. The feedback is driven by EGFR signaling from newly formed progenitors, which spreads differentiation across cell clusters. Furthermore, cell clustering shields the stem cell population from excessive depletion, showing that spatial architecture and lineage dynamics work together to maintain a stable stem cell fraction.
items.author: Emma Legait, Charlotte Rulquin, Lauranne Bouteille et al.
items.original_title: Local feedback governs cell fate transition to drive self-organized phenotypic equilibrium in hierarchical tumors
items.original_summary: by Emma Legait, Charlotte Rulquin, Lauranne Bouteille, Raphaël Clément, Cédric Maurange How cell-state transitions are regulated along a tumor lineage to determine its overall cellular composition remains unclear. Using a simple hierarchical tumor model in Drosophila , we show that differentiation of cancer stem cells (CSCs) into transit amplifying progenitors (TAPs) depends on the fraction of TAPs among their immediate neighbors. This relationship is captured by a local feedback transition rule that quantitatively predicts CSC transition probability. Implementing this rule in 3D growth simulations spontaneously recapitulates CSC clustering and the emergence of a stable CSC fraction within tumors. Mechanistically, the local feedback is mediated by EGFR signaling from newly produced TAPs, propagating differentiation across CSC clusters.

items.title: Mechanistic Study Reveals How AlphaFold 3 Infers Protein Structures
items.summary: AlphaFold 3 predicts protein structures and biomolecular assemblies with high accuracy, but the internal transformation of evolutionary data into three-dimensional models has remained unclear. Using mechanistic interpretability techniques, researchers analyzed the model's forward pass to understand its structural inference process. The findings indicate that the model does not rely strictly on raw sequences or maximum multiple-sequence alignment depth. Instead, a small set of phylogenetically diverse homologues is sufficient to reconstruct predicted structures. The pairformer component translates this evolutionary signal into a latent space where spatial distances, contacts, and confidence metrics become decodable, showing that AlphaFold 3 constrains its geometric predictions using sequence variations found in alignments.
items.author: Jonathan Feldman, Jeffrey Skolnick
items.original_title: AlphaInterp: Revealing how AlphaFold 3 processes structure, confidence, and evolutionary information
items.original_summary: by Jonathan Feldman, Jeffrey Skolnick How does evolutionary information become structural knowledge? AlphaFold 3 predicts protein structures and biomolecular assemblies with remarkable accuracy, yet how it transforms comparative sequence information into three-dimensional structure remains poorly understood. Here, we use mechanistic interpretability to follow this transformation through AlphaFold 3 and identify a computational principle underlying its structural inference. By extracting single- and pair-representations across the model’s forward pass and combining representational-geometry analysis, linear probing, activation patching, and perturbation of the multiple-sequence alignment (MSA) and its phylogenetic diversity, we show that AlphaFold 3 does not simply infer structure from raw sequence nor from MSA depth.

items.title: Gray Bats Balance Social Spacing and Obstacle Navigation
items.summary: Recent research investigates how gray bats navigate group flight while encountering environmental obstacles. By collecting stereoscopic video data from a wild colony of Myotis grisescens on their normal foraging paths, scientists observed that the bats stay close to walls but maintain distance from one another during group flight. An agent-based model developed from this data indicates that social repulsion behavior intensifies when the bats face novel navigational challenges and physical clutter.
items.author: Eighdi Aung, Nicole Abaid
items.original_title: Gray bats heighten their response to social cues when navigating group flight in environments with obstacles
items.original_summary: by Eighdi Aung, Nicole Abaid Bats are fast fliers with great maneuverability. Many species sense and communicate through echolocation, relying on acoustic signals in the environment. Bats also form large colonies, which necessitates that they fly in groups. When group size increases or obstacles are in their flight paths, the acoustic space can become cluttered, posing a non-trivial challenge for navigation. How do they interact with their environment and conspecifics, and how do they balance social and environmental cues? Recent research has uncovered individual adaptations to calling and flight patterns when flying in the groups or avoiding obstacles. Studies also suggest coordination when foraging, as well as strategies used by the group to mitigate acoustic clutter.

items.title: Gata2 Essential for Müllerian Duct Maintenance and Reproductive Tract Development
items.summary: Female embryos typically retain Müllerian ducts, the precursors to the reproductive tract, by default in the absence of anti-Müllerian hormone. However, whether active signaling is required to maintain these structures has remained unclear. Using mouse models, researchers found that the deletion of mesenchymal Gata2 causes selective regression of the cranial Müllerian duct, leading to conditions like uterine hypoplasia and vaginal atresia, while epithelial Gata2 is needed for uterine gland differentiation. This regression stems from the loss of region-specific signaling rather than ectopic hormone activity. Human data further support these findings, as patients with GATA2 deficiency exhibit similar reproductive tract anomalies, identifying Gata2 as a crucial regulator of female reproductive development.
items.author: Shuai Jia, Margaret Woodward, Allyssa Fogarty et al.
items.original_title: Müllerian duct maintenance is promoted by GATA2: Evidence from genetic mouse studies and two human cases of Müllerian duct agenesis
items.original_summary: by Shuai Jia, Margaret Woodward, Allyssa Fogarty, Jessica King, Janine R. Daub, Mary L. Fairbanks, Audrey M. Neale, Wenyan Bai, Emery H. Bresnick, Steven M. Holland, Veronica Gomez-Lobo, Fei Zhao The paradigm of sexual differentiation holds that female embryos retain the Müllerian ducts, the precursor of the female reproductive tract, by default in the absence of anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH). However, whether Müllerian duct maintenance requires active signaling remains unknown. Here, using mouse genetic models, we discover that deletion of mesenchymal Gata2 causes selective regression of the cranial Müllerian duct, the precursor of the oviduct. This regression is not driven by ectopic AMH signaling but may instead result from the loss of region-specific NRG1 signaling.

items.title: GPCR-Gaq Signaling Mediates Trametinib Resistance in Melanoma
items.summary: Oncogenic BRAF mutations drive MAPK signaling in various cancers, but resistance to MEK inhibitors like trametinib often limits their clinical success. To study how cells maintain MAPK activity during treatment, researchers utilized a Caenorhabditis elegans model mimicking oncogenic BRAF and identified high-dose trametinib resistance tied to increased egl-30 expression and EGL-30/Gaq-PLC-PKC signaling. In trametinib-resistant human melanoma cells, the gene F2RL1, which encodes the Gaq-coupled GPCR PAR2, was also upregulated. Inhibiting PAR2 or downstream Gaq signaling lowered ERK phosphorylation and reduced cell viability. Furthermore, combining MEK and Gaq-PLC-PKC inhibitors successfully suppressed tumor growth and restored drug sensitivity in xenograft models, highlighting a potential vulnerability in drug-resistant melanoma.
items.author: Jingyi Ke, Zi Wang, Zhengyang Guo et al.
items.original_title: GPCR-Gαq signaling drives adaptive resistance to MEK inhibition in BRAF-mutant melanoma
items.original_summary: by Jingyi Ke, Zi Wang, Zhengyang Guo, Guangshuo Ou, Wei Li Oncogenic BRAFV600E mutations drive constitutive MAPK signaling across various cancers; however, resistance to MEK inhibitors such as trametinib undermines clinical benefits, and the mechanisms sustaining MAPK activity under treatment remain unclear. We developed a lin-45(V627E) Caenorhabditis elegans model to mimic oncogenic BRAF signaling and found that these animals exhibited high-dose trametinib resistance, as assessed by brood size. Transcriptomic analysis revealed increased egl-30 expression in worms resistant to high-dose trametinib. Genetic and pharmacological analyses implicated EGL-30/Gαq-PLC-PKC signaling in this high-dose resistance phenotype. In trametinib-resistant A375 melanoma cells, F2RL1 , which encodes the Gαq-coupled GPCR PAR2, was upregulated compared with parental cells.

items.title: Genomic Analysis Reveals Antimalarial Resistance and Fitness Trade-Offs in Senegal
items.summary: Drug resistance in Plasmodium falciparum continues to threaten global malaria control efforts. Researchers analyzed whole-genome sequencing data from over 2,800 monogenomic parasite infections collected from patients in Senegal between 2006 and 2022. The results showed that wild-type, drug-sensitive alleles were rare, while known resistance-associated variants predominated across major loci. Laboratory cultures of clinical isolates demonstrated distinct drug and background-dependent effects on resistance profiles. Additionally, competitive growth assays revealed specific resistance-fitness trade-offs, where certain mutations reduced parasite competitive ability while others partially rescued it. These dynamics provide important insights into how parasite populations evolve in response to changing antimalarial treatments.

items.title: A Single Amino Acid in PilO Controls Helicobacter pylori Motility and Biofilms
items.summary: Helicobacter pylori bacteria possess complex flagellar motors, yet certain wild-type strains exhibit delayed migration in semisolid agar assays. Researchers identified that loss-of-function mutations in specific genes, particularly pilO, eliminate this delay and reduce early biofilm formation. Epistasis analysis positioned PilO as an upstream regulatory hub governing both motility and biofilms. Sequence comparisons across multiple wild-type strains revealed that a single varying amino acid in PilO dictates whether a strain displays immediate or delayed migration behavior. Furthermore, experiments demonstrated that the loss of pilO results in severe stomach colonization defects, indicating that PilO acts as a critical regulatory switch for both lifestyle transitions and infection.
items.author: Xiaolin Liu, Jiunn C. N. Fong, Eric H. L. Huang et al.
items.original_title: A single amino acid switch in PilO controls planktonic-sessile lifestyle in Helicobacter pylori
items.original_summary: by Xiaolin Liu, Jiunn C. N. Fong, Eric H. L. Huang, Karen M. Ottemann Helicobacter pylori and related Campylobacterota assemble high torque motors with many additional proteins compared to model bacteria. Despite these structural enhancements, some wild-type H. pylori strains have been previously reported to have delayed migration in the semisolid agar motility assay. The basis for this delay was characterized by identifying genetic suppressors that allowed H. pylori G27 wild type to migrate immediately. This analysis identified loss of function mutations in four genes ( pilO , fliL , hcpX , and alpA ) that restored migration. Targeted loss of any one of these genes resulted in strains that both migrated immediately in semisolid agar and displayed low early biofilm formation.

items.title: Correction Issued for Research on African Swine Fever Virus Protein pB318L
items.summary: A correction has been published for a study detailing how the African swine fever virus protein pB318L suppresses inflammatory responses through the inhibition of NF-κB activation and NLRP3 inflammasome formation. The notice addresses labeling errors in Fig 6D and corrects incorrect input Western blot panels and associated ratios in Fig 8C and Fig 8F. According to a member of the PLOS Pathogens Editorial Board, these replacements and corrections do not alter the validity of the original conclusions. The authors have formally apologized for the mistakes in the published work.

items.title: Deltacoronavirus Triggers circRNA Upregulation to Drive Viral Replication
items.summary: Research demonstrates that deltacoronavirus infection significantly increases the levels of a previously uncharacterized circular RNA, circC3. The virus induces the host RNA-binding protein muscleblind-like 1 (MBNL1), which binds to specific motifs within the C3 gene to promote exon skipping and enhance circC3 biogenesis. Functionally, circC3 acts to suppress MBNL1's antiviral activity by accelerating the decay of MBNL1 mRNA via direct interaction, ultimately aiding viral replication. This discovery uncovers a regulatory mechanism by which viral infections manipulate host circular RNA production to evade innate immune defenses.
items.author: Liuyang Du, Liping Wang, Lei Zhao et al.

items.original_summary: by Liuyang Du, Liping Wang, Lei Zhao, Juan Li, Yan Yan, Xiran Peng, Weiren Dong, Wei Wu, Jiyong Zhou, Jinyan Gu Circular RNAs (circRNAs) with diverse biological functions are frequently dysregulated upon viral infection, yet the mechanisms governing their differential expression and functional relevance during infection remain poorly defined. Here, we identify a previously uncharacterized circRNA, circC3 , that is robustly upregulated following virus infection. Host RNA binding protein muscleblind-like 1 (MBNL1) was markedly induced by deltacoronavirus (δ-CoV) infection, which recognizes YGCY motifs within intron 19 and intron 21 of the C3 gene and promotes skipping of exons 20 and 21 for C3 gene, thereby enhancing circC3 biogenesis.

items.title: RNA Modification and Glycolysis Link Immunity to Virus Infection in Shrimp
items.summary: Viral infections depend heavily on cellular glycolysis for energy and materials, but the role of post-transcriptional RNA modifications in regulating this process in invertebrates remains largely unstudied. New findings show that white spot syndrome virus infection in shrimp increases METTL3-mediated N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) mRNA. The m6A reader protein YTHDF3 recognizes this modification and recruits a translation initiation factor to stabilize mRNA and boost LDH translation. The resulting increase in LDH-derived lactate leads to histone lactylation, which directly stimulates mettl3 gene transcription from chromatin. This establishes a regulatory circuit connecting RNA epitranscriptomics, metabolic reprogramming, and innate immune responses during viral invasion.
items.author: Xumei Sun, Fan Xin, Siyuan Zhang
items.original_title: N6-methyladenosine dependent glycolysis enhances viral infection by histone lactylation in an arthropod
items.original_summary: by Xumei Sun, Fan Xin, Siyuan Zhang The glycolysis is crucial for the material and energy source of virus infection. However, the role of post-transcriptional modification, particularly N6-methyladenosine (m6A), in regulating virus-induced glycolysis in invertebrate remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that METTL3-mediated m6A modification of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) mRNA increased in shrimp upon white spot syndrome virus (WSSV) infection to promote glycolysis. An m6A site in the LDH mRNA is recognized by the m6A reader YTH domain family protein 3 (YTHDF3), which recruits translation initiation factor core subunit eIF4A to enhance LDH translation elongation and mRNA stability. LDH-derived lactate acts as a key metabolite responsible for lactylation of histone lysine residues that stimulates methyltransferase-like 3 ( mettl3 ) gene transcription from chromatin directly.

items.title: Low HLA-A Expression Associated with NK Cell Activity Linked to HIV Remission in Children
items.summary: Natural killer (NK) cells are vital for controlling HIV-1 in treatment-naive children and adults. By studying a cohort of 274 vertically infected children from KwaZulu-Natal, researchers evaluated the role of NK cell activity in post-treatment control following very early antiretroviral therapy. Results showed that low baseline total HIV-1 DNA load was linked to low HLA-A expression. At nine months of age, low viral DNA levels in virally suppressed infants correlated with reduced HLA-A expression alongside elevated levels of NKG2D and CD107a on specific NK cell subsets. Although female infants generally exhibited stronger NK responses, they frequently displayed higher total HIV-1 DNA loads—particularly those carrying protective HLA-B alleles with pro-inflammatory IL-17 pathway upregulation. These observations highlight an important connection between specialized NK cell phenotypes, low HLA-A expression, and HIV-1 remission in early-treated children.

items.title: Feasibility Study Evaluates Handheld Raman Spectroscopy for Cervical Lesion Assessment
items.summary: Current diagnostic procedures for cervical lesions are limited by processing time and molecular-level assessment constraints. To address this, a methodological feasibility study investigated the use of a handheld 785-nm Raman spectrometer for label-free molecular profiling of ex vivo tissue sections from 74 patients. After testing various parameters, researchers selected optimal working acquisition conditions of 128 mW laser power, a 4000 ms integration time, and approximately 1-mm-thick tissue sections. Exploratory evaluations yielded promising area-under-the-curve metrics for classifying invasive cancer and high-grade lesions versus noncancer or benign states. However, predictive performance declined substantially under rigorous patient-independent cross-validation. While the findings confirm the methodological feasibility of handheld Raman acquisition and indicate lesion-associated spectral variations, the approach remains exploratory and requires larger, multicenter cohorts before clinical adoption.
items.author: Yixuan Zhang, Huan Wang, Ying He et al.
items.original_title: Handheld Raman spectroscopy for ex vivo molecular assessment of cervical lesions: A methodological feasibility study
items.original_summary: by Yixuan Zhang, Huan Wang, Ying He, Siyuan Zhang, Pengyu Wang, Yimin Han Current diagnostic workflows for cervical lesions remain constrained by processing time, sampling representativeness, and limited molecular-level tissue assessment. Handheld Raman spectroscopy may provide label-free molecular profiling of ex vivo tissue specimens. In this methodological feasibility study, we evaluated a defined ex vivo acquisition workflow using a handheld 785-nm Raman spectrometer. We systematically evaluated laser power, integration time, and tissue thickness, and 128 mW laser power, 4000 ms integration time, and approximately 1-mm-thick tissue sections were selected as the working acquisition conditions for subsequent cervical measurements. The cervical cohort comprised 74 patients contributing 212 Raman spectra and was evaluated for two predefined primary binary classification tasks: invasive cervical cancer versus noncancer lesions (B1) and high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) versus benign lesions plus low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) (B2).

items.title: IntiCom-DB v2.0 Expands Inter-Tissue Communication Resource
items.summary: Researchers have introduced IntiCom-DB v2.0, an updated literature-derived database designed to document experimentally supported inter-tissue and inter-organ communication events. The new version expands its curated collection to 1,862 entries derived from 1,485 publications, encompassing 651 unique molecules across proteins, RNAs, and metabolites. It identifies 398 distinct communication routes linking 51 source tissues with 53 target tissues, with protein-mediated interactions forming the largest group. To aid functional analysis, the database integrates single-cell expression data, secretion characteristics, post-translational modification sites, and proteolytic details. A redesigned web interface offers advanced search, browsing, and visualization tools to help researchers explore complex communication patterns and identify key disease mediators. The resource is freely accessible online.
items.author: Qiong Zhou, Changxian Xiong, Linshu Wang et al.
items.original_title: IntiCom-DB v2.0: An expanded manually curated resource for inter-tissue/organ communications
items.original_summary: by Qiong Zhou, Changxian Xiong, Linshu Wang, Huai Pang, Rucong Liu, Jingkun Yi, Yu Han, Yuan Zhou Inter-tissue/organ communication (ITC) is essential for coordinating metabolism, immunity, development and disease progression. However, experimentally supported ITC events are dispersed across individual studies, hindering a systematic retrieval of their molecular mediators, source-to-target tissue routes and supporting evidence. Here, we present IntiCom-DB v2.0, an updated literature-derived database of experimentally supported ITC events. Compared with the previous version, IntiCom-DB v2.0 expands the curated collection to 1,862 entries from 1,485 publications, covering 651 unique ITC molecules across proteins, RNAs and metabolites. The updated database identifies 398 distinct communication routes between 51 source tissues and 53 target tissues, with protein-mediated events representing the largest category.

items.title: Maillard Reaction Precursors Enhance Composting at Extreme Ratios
items.summary: Agricultural waste management often faces challenges when combining spent mushroom substrate and pig manure at extreme mixing ratios, leading to nutrient loss and suppressed humification. A 120-day aerobic incubation study investigated the application of exogenous Maillard reaction precursors—specifically catechol, glucose, and glycine—to address these issues. The results showed that all three precursors improved overall compost maturity, enhanced nutrient retention, and promoted humus synthesis. Glucose accelerated phytotoxin degradation and aided humic acid synthesis in high-pig-manure systems, while glycine optimized nitrogen fixation and reduced degradation in high-substrate systems. Catechol assisted with ion chelation but yielded a slower humification rate. Spectroscopic and elemental analyses confirmed that these precursors improved the structural stability and aromatization of humic acid, offering targeted strategies for better agricultural waste recycling.
items.author: Ming Sun, Yanyan Liu, Baoyi Lu et al.
items.original_title: Regulatory effects of Maillard reaction precursors on humification during co-composting of spent mushroom substrate and pig manure at extreme mixing ratios
items.original_summary: by Ming Sun, Yanyan Liu, Baoyi Lu, Mingshuo Wang, Pingxin Liu Spent mushroom substrate (SMS) and pig manure (PM) represent two dominant types of agricultural organic waste. Co-composting of these two substrates at extreme mixing ratios—common in regions with a surplus of a single waste type—frequently suffers from C/N imbalance, suppressed humification, and substantial nutrient loss. Maillard reaction precursors (MRPs) are well-documented key regulators of humus (HS) formation, yet their regulatory mechanisms and efficacy in SMS–PM co-composting at extreme mixing ratios remain poorly understood. In this study, we performed a 120-day aerobic solid-state incubation experiment using two extreme SMS: PM mass ratios (9:1 for the high-SMS system, 1:9 for the high-PM system), with catechol (Cat), glucose (Glu), and glycine (Gly) applied as exogenous MRPs.

items.title: Comparing Platelet Function Tests for Aspirin Monitoring in Neuroendovascular Care
items.summary: Aspirin is commonly used for antiplatelet therapy during neuroendovascular procedures, but patient response variability presents clinical challenges. A retrospective review of 124 patients evaluated five platelet function tests across light transmission aggregometry using the CN-6000 device and the VerifyNow system. Assessments occurred prior to surgery, shortly after, and one month later, measuring parameters such as maximum aggregation induced by arachidonic acid, adenosine diphosphate, and collagen, alongside aspirin reaction units. Significant perioperative changes were detected exclusively through maximum aggregation induced by 1 millimolar arachidonic acid. While correlations between VerifyNow and aggregometry results were modest, the automated CN-6000 device offers a practical option for monitoring aspirin response, though further prospective studies are needed to confirm its clinical usefulness.
items.author: Tasuku Sakayori, Kenji Shoda, Ryosuke Nakanishi et al.
items.original_title: Assessment of aspirin response in patients undergoing neuroendovascular treatments: A comparison of five platelet function tests across two platforms
items.original_summary: by Tasuku Sakayori, Kenji Shoda, Ryosuke Nakanishi, Yoshihiko Ueno, Ayumu Kanbe, Aki Oka, Daisuke Mizutani, Miyu Kitagami, Keisuke Kitano, Ryosuke Kikuchi, Yukiko Enomoto Aspirin is widely used for periprocedural antiplatelet therapy in neuroendovascular procedures; however, variability in patient response poses clinical challenges. This study aimed to assess five platelet function tests on two different platforms: light transmission aggregometry (LTA) using the CN-6000 device and the VerifyNow system, which were utilized to assess patients undergoing neuroendovascular procedures. A total of 124 patients who underwent elective neuroendovascular procedures and received perioperative aspirin-based antiplatelet therapy between September 2020 and December 2023 were retrospectively reviewed.

items.title: Structural Reorganization of Elite Men's Water Polo Following 2025 Rule Changes
items.summary: Recent rule revisions by World Aquatics for men's water polo modified the field length, shot clock duration, and possession reset times to quicken offensive tempo. A quasi-experimental study compared performance indicators from the 2024 and 2025 World Championships to assess the initial impacts of these changes. Multivariate analyses revealed significant differences across offensive performance, goalkeeping, exclusions, and game management domains. While shooting and save rates remained stable, univariate findings showed changes in event frequency and distribution. Teams in 2025 averaged more possessions, action shot attempts, and exclusions, but fewer counterattack attempts. These findings demonstrate that the rule changes induced a structural reorganization of match performance rather than isolated improvements in technical efficiency.
items.author: Seung-Hun Lee
items.original_title: Structural reorganization of elite men’s water polo: A quasi-experimental multivariate analysis of the 2025 rule changes
items.original_summary: by Seung-Hun Lee The 2025 World Aquatics rule revisions for water polo aimed to accelerate offensive tempo and alter tactical decision-making by reducing the field length, shot clock duration, and possession reset times. This study used the 2024 and 2025 Men’s Water Polo World Championships as consecutive editions of the same elite international competition to provide an initial quasi-experimental assessment of performance changes associated with these revisions. Performance indicators across four domains (offensive performance, goalkeeping, exclusions, and game management) were analyzed using a multivariate analysis of variance. Notably, significant multivariate differences were observed between tournaments across all performance domains. Subsequent univariate analyses showed that these differences were primarily reflected in the frequency and distribution of match events.

items.title: Clinicopathological Factors Linked to Biochemical Recurrence After Prostate Surgery
items.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the relationship between clinicopathological characteristics and biochemical recurrence following robot-assisted radical prostatectomy. Researchers reviewed 16 cohort studies encompassing 6,409 prostate cancer patients from multiple medical databases up to March 2026. The findings identified several factors significantly linked to a heightened risk of biochemical recurrence, including preoperative prostate-specific antigen levels of 10 nanograms per milliliter or higher, a Gleason score of 8 or greater, pathological stage T3a, positive surgical margins, increased International Society of Urological Pathology grades, and positive lymph nodes. The study synthesizes existing prognostic evidence but does not establish or validate a formal clinical prediction model for individual patient outcomes.
items.author: Ting Li, Danhua Wu, Lujie Ye
items.original_title: Clinicopathological factors associated with biochemical recurrence after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: A systematic review and meta-analysis
items.original_summary: by Ting Li, Danhua Wu, Lujie Ye Background This study aimed to systematically review and quantify the associations between clinicopathological factors and biochemical recurrence (BCR) following robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP). Methods This study systematically searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science for observational studies on predictors of BCR following RARP. The search was conducted up to March 20, 2026. Included studies were required to report results of multivariate analyses and provide odds ratios (OR) with their 95% confidence intervals (CI). Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale (NOS) criteria, and data analysis was performed using Stata 15.

items.title: Correction Issued for Figures in High-Fat Diet Colitis Study
items.summary: The publishers of PLOS ONE have issued a correction for an article examining the role of the AMPK/PPARalpha pathway in high-fat diet-aggravated ulcerative colitis. The notice states that Figures 1 and 2 were uploaded incorrectly in the original publication. The revised figures provide accurate data regarding body weight loss percentage, disease activity index, colonic section staining, colon length comparisons, and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression levels in mice subjected to a normal versus high-fat diet during a seven-day period.

items.title: Comparing Long-Term Complications of Adult Craniopharyngioma Resection Approaches
items.summary: A retrospective cohort study evaluated long-term complications following transsphenoidal and transcranial surgical resection of adult craniopharyngiomas using the TriNetX network. Researchers analyzed patient data to compare outcomes across approaches. The study found that adults with craniopharyngiomas experience substantial long-term visual, endocrine, and treatment-related morbidities. While both methods offer distinct profiles, transsphenoidal resection generally showed lower rates of hydrocephalus, blindness, epilepsy, and diabetes insipidus, but carried higher rates of cerebrospinal fluid leaks and hypopituitarism compared to transcranial resection. These findings provide population-level estimates to help guide surgical counseling and postoperative patient monitoring.
items.author: William L. Zeng, Aman Singla, David J. Cote et al.
items.original_title: Long-term complication profiles following transsphenoidal and transcranial resection of adult craniopharyngioma: A retrospective cohort study
items.original_summary: by William L. Zeng, Aman Singla, David J. Cote, Sindhu Daggupati, Jonathan Dallas, Robert G. Briggs, Gabriel Zada Introduction Craniopharyngiomas arise in the sellar/suprasellar region and are managed with maximal safe resection via transsphenoidal (TSR) or transcranial (TCR) approaches. The optimal approach remains contested, as treatment must balance tumor control against long-term visual, endocrine, neurologic, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak–related morbidity. Longitudinal complication and morbidity profiles of craniopharyngioma resection in adults remain limited. We evaluated approach-specific long-term outcomes in a large multi-institutional adult cohort. Methods In a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX network, adult craniopharyngioma patients undergoing TSR or TCR were compared using unmatched analyses and propensity score matching (PSM).

items.title: Custom 3D-Printed Insoles Outperform Standard Care for Diabetic Foot Offloading
items.summary: Researchers evaluated whether novel 3D-printed custom accommodative insoles could improve plantar pressure offloading for individuals with diabetes compared to standard-of-care insoles and no insoles. Twenty-five adults with diabetes and high plantar pressure completed walking trials across different insole conditions. Peak plantar pressure and pressure-time integrals were measured across high-risk and adjacent areas, alongside participant comfort feedback. Results showed that all insoles significantly reduced peak plantar pressure and pressure-time integrals by over 14% in regions of interest compared to having no insole. The findings suggest that personalized, 3D-printed insoles represent a promising patient-centered approach to help prevent diabetic foot complications.
items.author: Brittney C. Muir, Kimberly A. Nickerson, Christina Carranza et al.
items.original_title: Improving offloading in diabetic feet: 3D-printed custom accommodative insoles outperform standard of care
items.original_summary: by Brittney C. Muir, Kimberly A. Nickerson, Christina Carranza, Mathew Sunil Varre, Avocet Nagle-Christensen, Dylan Heino, Ellen Y. Li, William R. Ledoux, Scott Telfer Introduction 3D-printed custom accommodative insoles may offer improved plantar pressure offloading compared to standard-of-care (total contact EVA base with a 4-mm Plastazote-PORON foam top layer) insoles for individuals with diabetes. We have developed two versions of 3D-printed accommodative insoles that have patient-specific geometries as well as patient-specific stiffnesses and structural behaviors. The purpose of this study is to determine if two styles of novel 3D printed accommodative insoles (pressure-based and finite element-based), with patient-specific geometries as well as local patient-specific stiffnesses, can provide greater reductions in plantar pressures for at-risk areas of the foot without increasing pressure in the regions adjacent compared to the standard-of-care and no insole, in individuals with diabetes.

items.title: Digital health tools for health education and information access in low and middle-income countries (LMICs) affected by humanitarian crises: A scoping review protocol
items.summary: by Niaz Ahmed, Elysée Nouvet, Saleema Allana, Anam Shahil-Feroz, Anushka Ataullahjan Humanitarian crises disrupt health services and access to reliable information in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Mobile-enabled digital tools may reach affected communities, but evidence on the technologies used, implementation contexts, and equitable access is dispersed. This scoping review will map empirical evidence on mobile-enabled digital tools used to deliver health education, health promotion, risk communication, or health information to crisis-affected populations in LMICs. The review will follow Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) scoping review guidance and will be reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR).
items.author: Niaz Ahmed, Elysée Nouvet, Saleema Allana et al.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy combined with palliative transarterial chemoembolization followed by targeted therapy and immunotherapy in patients with BCLC stage C hepatocellular carcinoma: Clinical trial protocol
items.summary: by Yang Fang, Songnan Zhang Background Interventional therapy combined with systemic treatment has demonstrated promising antitumor activity and an overall manageable safety profile in patients with advanced, unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, prospective evidence supporting the optimal combination strategy remains limited, and the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) characteristics underlying differential treatment responses have not been systematically elucidated. The present study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) combined with palliative transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), followed by sequential targeted-immunotherapy, in treatment-naïve patients with BCLC stage C HCC, while also exploring the TIME features associated with therapeutic response.
items.author: Yang Fang, Songnan Zhang

items.title: Data-driven clinical decision trees and generative topographic mapping to guide stroke rehabilitation program allocation
items.summary: by Dimitrios Sokratis Komaris, Panagiotis Anagnostou, Spiros Nikolopoulos, Dimitrios Tsaopoulos, Anna Guillen-Sola, Esther Duarte, Ryan A. A. Bellfield, Sandra Ortega-Martorell, Ivan Olier, Ioannis Kompatsiaris Background Early and timely admission to post-stroke rehabilitation remains a key determinant of optimal functional recovery. In this study, we present a structured framework for the development and evaluation of multivariable prediction models and Classification and Regression Tree (CART) decision-support tools to guide patient allocation across diverse subacute rehabilitation settings. Methods We have constructed a heterogeneous synthetic dataset of 700 stroke patients characterized by 49 demographic, clinical, and functional variables derived from multiple, literature-reported, statistical distributions of patient populations.
items.author: Dimitrios Sokratis Komaris, Panagiotis Anagnostou, Spiros Nikolopoulos et al.

items.title: Remimazolam for sedation in elderly patients undergoing gastrointestinal endoscopy: Protocol for a scoping review
items.summary: by Shuang Tao, Xiaoying Li, Zhongyuan Zhou, Hongbo Zhang Background Gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy is one of the most commonly performed procedures in older adults, who constitute an increasing proportion of the endoscopic population yet face a higher risk of sedation-related cardiorespiratory adverse events, delayed recovery, and postoperative neurocognitive disturbances. Remimazolam, an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine metabolised by tissue esterases independently of hepatic and renal function, is a candidate sedative of particular interest in this group. However, the extent and gaps of the available evidence specific to sedation with remimazolam in elderly patients undergoing GI endoscopy have not been systematically mapped. Objectives To systematically map the existing evidence on the use of remimazolam for procedural sedation in elderly patients (aged ≥65 years) undergoing GI endoscopy, characterising study design, reported outcomes, comparators, and dosing regimens, and identifying knowledge gaps.
items.author: Shuang Tao, Xiaoying Li, Zhongyuan Zhou et al.

items.title: Clinical features, first aid practices, and hospital management of snakebites in Northern Uganda: A multi-facility cross-sectional study
items.summary: by Solomon T. Wafula, Trophy Akello, Shakiim Mubiru, Richard K. Mugambe, John Bosco Isunju, John Bosco Ddamulira, David Musoke Snakebite envenoming is a neglected tropical disease with a disproportionate burden in sub-Saharan Africa, where weak surveillance, limited antivenom availability, and reliance on traditional remedies compound morbidity and mortality. Evidence on how snakebite cases are clinically managed in routine practice in Uganda remains scarce. We conducted a facility-based cross-sectional study with retrospective abstraction of records from four purposively selected health facilities in Gulu and Arua Districts of Northern Uganda. Snakebite case records from outpatient, inpatient, paediatric, and intensive-care service points covering the period 2017–2021 were reviewed using a standardised abstraction tool.
items.author: Solomon T. Wafula, Trophy Akello, Shakiim Mubiru et al.

items.title: Five-year trends in Malaria prevalence, Plasmodium species distribution, demographic patterns, and seasonal variation at Yejube health center, Baso Liben district, East Gojjam zone, Ethiopia, 2020–2024: Implications for Malaria elimination
items.summary: by Abebe Fenta, Tebelay Dilnessa, Adane Tilahun, Adane Adugna, Habtamu Belew, Bantayehu Addis Tegegne, Desalegn Abebaw Background Malaria remains a major global public health problem, with an estimated 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths in 2024, predominantly in the WHO African Region. Ethiopia continues to face substantial malaria transmission and has adopted an elimination strategy emphasizing surveillance, early diagnosis and treatment, and integrated vector control. Assessing local temporal, species-specific, demographic, and seasonal patterns is essential to guide targeted malaria elimination efforts. Objective To assess the five-year temporal trend of malaria prevalence, Plasmodium species distribution, demographic patterns, and seasonal variation among patients attending Yejube Health Center, Baso Liben District, East Gojjam Zone, Ethiopia.
items.author: Abebe Fenta, Tebelay Dilnessa, Adane Tilahun et al.

items.title: Inequities and determinants of cesarean section delivery in Malawi: A multilevel analysis of 2024 demographic and health survey
items.summary: by Habtu Kifle Negash Background Cesarean section (CS) is a life-saving surgical procedure for childbirth complications, but its use varies widely. Globally, CS rates have risen from 7% in 1990 to 21% in recent years, with disparities between high- and low-income countries. Sub-Saharan Africa, including Malawi, has some of the lowest CS coverage, despite high institutional delivery rates. Its use is influenced by individual and community factors, reflecting inequities in obstetric care. This study assessed the prevalence and determinants of CS among reproductive-age women in Malawi. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted using secondary data from the 2024 Malawi Demographic and Health Survey, including a weighted sample of 6,798 women aged 15–49 years.
items.author: Habtu Kifle Negash

items.title: A proximity‑based multi‑indicator framework for optimizing emergency shelter layout in a mountainous city: A case study of Dujiangyan, China
items.summary: by Gang Chen, Yanxi Chen, Jiangyue Fu, Yi Yang, Xinchuan Liu Emergency shelters play a vital role in protecting human life in disaster‑prone regions such as China. However, in many high‑risk cities, existing emergency shelter systems are often planned for single hazards and exhibit spatial layouts that are poorly aligned with population distribution, thereby undermining evacuation efficiency and post‑disaster resettlement capacity. To address these limitations, this study proposes a GIS‑based proximity‑driven framework for hazard exposure assessment and spatial optimization of emergency shelters, with Dujiangyan City, China, as a case study. First, a hazard exposure evaluation system was constructed using proximity‑to‑source indicators for major threats, including earthquakes, geological hazards (e.g., landslides and debris flows), floods, and secondary fires.

items.title: Effects of velocity-based strength training versus percentage-based strength training on technical error rates in collegiate lion dance athletes: A randomized controlled trial
items.summary: by Mu Yuan Yang Background Lion dance is a Chinese intangible cultural heritage that demands exceptional strength, explosive power, and movement precision. Velocity-based training has shown benefits for general athletic performance, but its effects on sport-specific technical performance in traditional sports remain unclear. Objective To compare the effects of velocity-based training and percentage-based training on technical error rates in collegiate lion dance athletes. Methods Thirty collegiate lion dance athletes were recruited and randomly assigned in fixed head–tail pairs to a velocity-based training group (VBT, n = 10), a percentage-based training group (PBT, n = 10), or a regular-training control group (CON, n = 10).
