items.title: Ethnic, religious, and occupational disparities in the prevalence of depression, anxiety, and stress among Ghanaian Nurses
items.summary: by Grace Arthur, Reginald Quansah, Prudence Tettey Background Mental health disorders constitute a significant component of the disease burden among nurses, given the demanding and stressful nature of the profession. This study assessed the prevalence of depression, anxiety, and stress among nurses and examined socio-cultural, demographic, lifestyle, and occupational factors associated with these conditions. Method A cross-sectional study involving 302 nurses was conducted at LEKMA Hospital. Socio-demographic information was collected using a structured questionnaire, and depression, anxiety, and stress were measured using the 21-item Depression Anxiety Stress Scales (DASS-21), with standard scoring and severity classification. Logistic regression analysis was employed to identify ethnic, religious, and occupational factors associated with these mental health disorders.
items.author: Grace Arthur, Reginald Quansah, Prudence Tettey

items.title: Hydroclimatic evolution under changing westerly–monsoon influences in northeastern China since the Late Glacial
items.summary: by Yi Huang, Hongwei Meng, Jianbo Zhu, Dongbo Wang, Zeyang Zhu, Jing Wu Hydroclimatic variability in the transition zone between the East Asian summer monsoon and mid-latitude westerlies reflects the combined influence of these two circulation systems. Understanding how their relative influences have changed over time is essential for interpreting long-term regional moisture variability. Here, we reconstructed regional hydroclimatic changes since 14.3 ka BP using a continuous lacustrine sequence from Aranji Nur, a closed lake on the southwestern margin of the Hulunbuir Grassland in northeastern China. Sediment grain-size distributions were analyzed and compared with regional paleoclimate and environmental records. Four major hydroclimatic stages were identified: relatively dry conditions during 14.3–9.2 ka BP, increased effective moisture during 9.2–4.8 ka BP, gradually declining moisture during 4.8–1.5 ka BP, and renewed aridification since 1.5 ka BP.
items.author: Yi Huang, Hongwei Meng, Jianbo Zhu et al.

items.title: The effect of YouTube video platform on the students’ English-speaking self-efficacy beliefs and motivation in a communicative English Skills II course: First year undergraduate students in focus
items.summary: by Mesfin Mekuria Dangore, Elias Woemego Bushisso, Kassa Mihiretie Woldeyes The major aim of this study was to examine the effects of the YouTube video platform on English speaking self-efficacy beliefs and motivation among first year undergraduate students at Wolaita Sodo University, Ethiopia. A quasi-experimental design involving two intact groups was employed. One group served as the treatment group (N = 52), while the other served as the comparison group (N = 52). To collect the data, pre- and post-intervention English speaking self-efficacy beliefs and motivation questionnaires were administered to both groups. To contextualize and complement the quantitative findings, qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews with six purposively selected students.
items.author: Mesfin Mekuria Dangore, Elias Woemego Bushisso, Kassa Mihiretie Woldeyes

items.title: Enhancing auto-segmentation accuracy and robustness through multiple deep learning systems
items.summary: by Ying Zhang, Mohammad Zarenia, Christina Sarosiek, Lulin Yuan, Eric Paulson, X. Sharon Qi Purpose Deep learning auto-segmentation (DLAS) can improve the efficiency and consistency of clinical contouring; however, no single DLAS system performs optimally across all cases, organs, and image slices, and each system may produce occasional poor-quality or outlier contours. Because multiple DLAS systems are available in some institutions, this proof-of-concept study evaluated a multi-system fusion framework designed to leverage their complementary strengths and generate more accurate and robust auto-contours, with potential extension to consensus generation from multiple manual contours. Methods Using 35 abdominal CT datasets from three institutions, contours of the stomach, duodenum, liver, and right kidney were generated by three commercial DLAS systems and one non-commercial research DLAS model.
items.author: Ying Zhang, Mohammad Zarenia, Christina Sarosiek et al.

items.title: Spatiotemporal analysis of COVID-19 in Japan: The twelve epidemic waves from 2020 to 2025
items.summary: by Shiho Sato, Masayoshi Matsumoto, Chihiro Wakabayashi, Izumi Oki, Yuri Matsubara, Daisuke Matsubara, Yui Nakaizumi, Yoshihisa Aiba, Yosikazu Nakamura, Hiroshi Yanagawa Since the first confirmed case of COVID-19 in Japan in January 2020, multiple epidemic waves have emerged under changing legal classifications and public health measures. Although nationwide surveillance data have been continuously available, integrated analyses of temporal and geographic patterns remain limited. This study described the spatiotemporal evolution of COVID-19 in Japan in relation to the timing of major policy, vaccination, variant, and surveillance changes. Weekly prefecture-level case counts from 2020 to 2025 were analyzed using official data from the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, and the epidemic period was divided into early epidemic, expansion, and plateau phases.
items.author: Shiho Sato, Masayoshi Matsumoto, Chihiro Wakabayashi et al.

items.title: Deformation response and energy evolution of slotted coal subjected to cyclic loading
items.summary: by Xiaoyan Sun, Ke Xu, Haolong Zheng, Hao Liu, Han Liu, Tengfei Ma Given the challenges posed by low gas permeability and complex hydraulic fracturing disturbance environments in deep low-permeability reservoirs, this study conducted cyclic loading and unloading tests with different cyclic amplitudes and fracture angles to investigate the deformation response and energy evolution of slotted coal under the effects of external disturbances and fracture angles. The results indicate that the peak strength and peak strain of the coal specimens decrease with increasing fracture angle, while the peak strain increases with increasing cyclic amplitude. During the low-stress loading phase, the modulus of the coal specimens first increase and then gradually stabilize.
items.author: Xiaoyan Sun, Ke Xu, Haolong Zheng et al.

items.title: Polarization dynamics in science and conspiratorial forums on Reddit: Cognitive, emotional, and identity narratives
items.summary: by Dandan Wang, Stephanie Jean Tsang, Yadong Zhou Polarization in online anonymous communities has become a prominent feature of contemporary digital interaction. This study examines its temporal dynamics in two structurally distinct Reddit communities, r/Askscience and r/Conspiracy, using longitudinal data from 2009–2022. Narrative-structure features related to cognition, emotion, and identity were extracted employing natural language processing, temporal network analysis, and large language model-assisted lexicon development. Weekly community-level polarization was operationalized as interaction-weighted evaluative dominance, measured by a signed index combining balance of positive and negative evaluations with interaction homogeneity, rather than directly measuring substantive stance divergence. ARIMA and ARIMAX models were used to examine temporal patterns and their associations with narrative features.
items.author: Dandan Wang, Stephanie Jean Tsang, Yadong Zhou

items.title: Seasonal cycles in basic human values: Evidence from over thirteen years of U.S. data on the Schwartz value survey
items.summary: by Radha Bazaz, Ian Hohm, Mark Schaller Previous research revealed a bimodal seasonal cycle in Americans’ endorsement of “binding” moral values (authority, loyalty, purity). We extended this work by examining seasonal patterns in human values more broadly, using Schwartz Value Survey data collected across more than 13 years from respondents in the United States (N = 31,981). Of the 10 values assessed, four values—pertaining to conformity, power, achievement, and benevolence—showed seasonal cycles that were consistent across years and robust across analytic strategies. These seasonal cycles were bimodal—characterized by two peaks (periods of strong endorsement) and two valleys (periods of lower endorsement) over the year—but the timing of those peaks and valleys differed across values.
items.author: Radha Bazaz, Ian Hohm, Mark Schaller

items.title: Wearable environmental sensing to forecast foot center of pressure and time of impact during level-ground-to-stair-ascent transitions
items.summary: by Michael D. Murray, James Tung, Richard W. Nuckols Objective Computer-vision has been used for environmental classification during gait and is often used to inform control in assistive systems; however, the ability to predict how the foot will contact a changing environment is underexplored. Methods We evaluated the feasibility of forecasting the anterior-posterior foot center-of-pressure (COP) and time-of-impact (TOI) prior to foot-strike on a level-ground-to-stair-ascent transition. Eight subjects wore a camera that supplied paired grayscale stereo frames on their right shank and instrumented insoles in their shoes while performing level-ground-to-stair-ascent transitions in a controlled laboratory setting (~90 trials each). We trained one CNN-RNN base model for COP and another for TOI, then fine-tuned both for each subject to generate continuous forecasts (16.67 ms temporal resolution) within a 250 ms window prior to foot-strike, termed the forecast horizon (FH).
items.author: Michael D. Murray, James Tung, Richard W. Nuckols

items.title: Photonic processors that carry their own unclonable fingerprint
items.summary: Physically unclonable functions (PUFs) derive cryptographic keys from uncontrollable fabrication disorder, removing the need to store secrets in vulnerable non-volatile memory. Programmable photonic processors are natural candidates for PUFs, because each of their many tunable interferometers carries its own fabrication imperfections. However, we show that the mesh topology itself funnels light along short paths, so that most of this disorder contributes little to the response. Here we introduce an isotropic ring routing scheme that steers light to the core of a hexagonal mesh and redistributes it uniformly towards the perimeter, suppressing a distance-dependent power decay of 14.7 dB and raising the mean Shannon entropy of the response from 1.95 to 3.48 bits by reprogramming alone.
items.author: Oxel Arnal Martínez, Pablo Martínez-Carrasco Romero, David Álvarez Outerelo et al.

items.title: Exceptional unidirectional radiation modes
items.summary: Singularities such as exceptional points (EPs) and bound states in the continuum (BICs) fundamentally reshape the spectral response of non-Hermitian open systems, unlocking exotic physical phenomena and unprecedented ways of wave manipulation. Nevertheless, the radiation behaviors of modes evolving around these singularities lack a unified picture. Here we show that a mode originating from a BIC can radiate unidirectionally, exhibiting a quality factor that continuously varies in parameter space from a near-infinite value (near the BIC) to a finite lower bound as it coalesces with the other (leaky) mode at an EP. The crossing of the unidirectional radiation mode and the EP in parameter space results in not only merged poles (resonant EP) but also merged zeros (absorbing EP) of the scattering matrix, along with a counterintuitive reversal of radiation direction decoupled from the coalesced eigenmodes under near-field excitation.

items.title: Captured Nebulas Showcased in Astronomy Picture
items.summary: A detailed astronomical image reveals the Horsehead and Flame Nebulas alongside surrounding cosmic structures. The bright triple star Alnitak anchors part of Orion's Belt, while the iconic dark Horsehead Nebula spans roughly five light-years and sits about 1,500 light-years away. Hydrogen gas ionized by the star Sigma Orionis creates a glowing red backdrop behind the dark dust and gas. Meanwhile, the neighboring Flame Nebula and the blue reflection nebula NGC 2023 complete the scene. Data for the celestial photograph were gathered over nearly six hours at the Utah Desert Remote Observatories using equipment controlled remotely from Illinois.

items.title: Rare Rains Transform the Atacama Desert Into a Vibrant Landscape
items.summary: Unusually heavy winter precipitation, driven by a strengthening El Niño and atmospheric river events, triggered a massive blooming desert phenomenon across northern Chile's Atacama Desert in spring 2026. The rainfall awakened dormant seeds, resulting in expansive displays of red-purple pata de guanaco and green-capped suspiros. Researchers utilized satellite data from Landsat 8 and 9, alongside field drones and digital cameras, to monitor the unprecedented biological event. Scientists note that this iteration stands out as the most extensive and significant blooming period of the satellite era in terms of duration and intensity.

items.title: Collagen-stimulating activity of a pentapeptide conjugate and self-assembly into micelles.
items.summary: We present a lipopeptide conjugate, farnesyl-mercapto(diethylene glycol)-KTTKS (FMdEG-KTTKS), designed to include the KTTKS collagen-stimulating sequence attached to a terpenoid branched lipid chain via a short hydrophilic spacer. This conjugate stimulates fibroblasts to produce greater than 200% more collagen per cell than conventional stimulants. This activity is observed at low concentration, well below a critical micelle concentration (CMC) determined by fluorescence probe measurements. Above the CMC, this molecule self-assembles into well-defined spherical micelles, as shown by cryogenic-transmission electron microscopy (cryo-TEM) and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS). The behaviour of this conjugate is contrasted with that of related lipopeptides: FMdEG-KTTKS forms micelles across a wide pH range, instead of nanotapes observed for C 16 -KTTKS (Matrixyl™).

items.title: NASA Schedules Cargo Resupply Mission to the International Space Station
items.summary: NASA, Northrop Grumman, and SpaceX are targeting November 29 for the launch of the CRS-25 mission to the International Space Station. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket will carry the Northrop Grumman Cygnus XL spacecraft, loaded with roughly 11,000 pounds of cargo and scientific investigations, from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. The mission includes experiments focused on cancer treatment, muscle loss, and food production. Astronauts aboard the station will capture the spacecraft using the Canadarm2 robotic arm on December 1 and attach it to the Unity module. Named after astronaut James A. Lovell, the spacecraft is scheduled to remain docked until May 2027 before returning with unneeded cargo to burn up during re-entry.

items.title: A Symmetry-Stratified Framework for Phase Transitions: Thermodynamic States, Critical Dynamics, and Spectral Mechanical Signatures
items.summary: Structural symmetry, thermodynamic phase stability, and elastic-wave response provide related but distinct descriptions of a transforming solid. We formulate a symmetry-stratified framework that connects these descriptions through a finite-dimensional internal state and a parent-invariant free energy. Stabilizers classify structural states, whereas free-energy comparisons and stability conditions determine equilibrium branches and dissipative evolution. Equivariance ensures that the frozen elastic tangent inherits the structural stabilizer. Equality requires additional identifiability conditions. Little-group representations and degenerate perturbation theory then determine whether an acoustic doublet splits and the first nonzero splitting order $p$. On a selected continuous branch with order-parameter exponent $β$, a regular, observable acoustic gap scales as $|t|^{pβ}$, provided critical self-energies and structural relaxation do not dominate the measurement.

items.title: Geometric control of diffusive relaxation: spectral design, transport bounds and transverse mode isolation
items.summary: Geometric confinement changes both thermal relaxation and heat throughput, but these effects need not be governed by the same conduction path. We establish a distinction between serial and parallel geometries for passive, homogeneous Fourier conductors at fixed material properties, volume and length. For a reduced variable-area conductor, two logarithmic shape harmonics independently tune two selected Bloch-rate pairs, and exact local transport level sets permit spectral redistribution at fixed effective diffusivity. A nonperturbative weighted Poincaré bound, however, requires the effective axial diffusivity to vanish if the first positive insulated rate tends to zero at fixed length. This obstruction is avoided by continuous parallel paths with weak transverse exchange.

items.title: Colloquium: Isotopes for medicine and fundamental physics
items.summary: Isotopes, variants of elements distinguished by their neutron number, have important applications for medicine and fundamental science. This review explores the historical challenges and new technologies for enriching and detecting isotopes. We motivate the work by challenges posed by three of history's greatest scientists: James Clerk Maxwell's thought experiment on thermodynamics, Ernest Rutherford's practical dilemma in radiochemistry, and Albert Einstein's questions about the probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics. The journey to meet these challenges has catalyzed the development of innovative techniques for isotope separation. These advancements can mitigate the worldwide crisis in the supply of enriched isotopes. We then explore the expected impact of these new technologies on medicine, which include radioisotopes for cancer therapy and stable isotopes as tracers for metabolism.
items.author: V. J. Ajith, Mark G. Raizen

items.title: Z-sight Unifies Robot Vision-Language-Action with Latent World Modeling
items.summary: Researchers introduced Z-sight, a robot foundation model that combines vision-language-action capabilities with generative latent world modeling. Unlike traditional models that incur heavy costs from pixel-level video generation or decouple feature spaces, Z-sight predicts future states directly within the visual token space used by its vision-language model. By pairing a foresight expert and a continuous action expert through a mixture-of-transformers architecture, the model jointly denoises future spatial tokens and actions without requiring pixel reconstruction or external encoders. Trained on human videos and robot trajectories, Z-sight achieves strong performance improvements across various manipulation tasks and benchmarks, maintaining an efficient processing speed of 110 milliseconds per chunk.
items.author: Junjie Ye, Yiqi Zhao, Muchen Xu et al.
items.original_title: $Z$-sight: Unifying Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling
items.original_summary: We introduce $Z$-sight, a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling. Video-based world action models (WAMs) show the value of joint future-and-action generation for control, yet inherit the heavy cost of video generators. Recent latent-space policies avoid pixel generation, yet typically align intermediate features or rely on frozen target encoders, decoupling future prediction from the VLM's native feature space. $Z$-sight instead predicts the future directly in the visual token space in which its VLM perceives the present. Coupling a foresight expert and a continuous action expert with the VLM in a mixture-of-transformers, $Z$-sight jointly denoises future spatial tokens and actions at inference without pixel reconstruction or external encoders.

items.title: Spherical Neural Networks Improve Primordial Gravitational Wave Inference
items.summary: A spherical graph convolutional network has been developed to infer the tensor-to-scalar ratio directly from multifrequency cosmic microwave background B-mode maps on the cut sky. Tested against simulated ground-based experiments featuring lensed CMB, noise, and Galactic dust and synchrotron emissions, the neural network outperforms traditional bandpower likelihood approaches. Working directly on the maps without requiring power-spectrum estimation or component separation, the network reduces the root-mean-square error by a factor of 1.3 and produces narrower, well-calibrated confidence intervals. Saliency mapping reveals that the network autonomously prioritizes the cleanest frequency channels and deepest sky regions. Although tied to its training foreground model, the network demonstrates generalization to alternative models, highlighting its potential for future cosmological analyses.
items.author: Anto I. Lonappan, Adrian E. Bayer, Brian Keating et al.
items.original_title: Map-Level Inference of Primordial Gravitational Waves from the CMB with Spherical Neural Networks
items.original_summary: We train a spherical graph convolutional network to infer the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ directly from multifrequency cosmic microwave background (CMB) $B$-mode maps on the cut sky. We test the network on simulations of a generic ground-based experiment including lensed CMB, inhomogeneous noise, and stochastic Galactic dust and synchrotron emission. We compare the network with a multifrequency bandpower likelihood built from the same 20,000 simulations used to train it. Working directly on the maps, with no power-spectrum estimation or component separation, the network reduces the root-mean-square error on $r$ by a factor of 1.3 and gives well-calibrated 68% intervals 1.2 times narrower than the likelihood with the same prior.

items.title: Phoenix Enhances Scene Structure Representations for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Researchers introduced Phoenix, a representation learning framework that improves scene structure understanding for world-action models in robotic manipulation. Phoenix utilizes an encoder that enriches DINOv3 visual semantics through dual-teacher geometric and spatiotemporal distillation, paired with a causal variational autoencoder that compresses features into generative latents while retaining spatial layouts. Trained on approximately 39,000 hours of egocentric and robot data, Phoenix jointly predicts scene evolution and actions. It achieves state-of-the-art performance across simulation and real-world benchmarks, exhibits high robustness to perturbations, and demonstrates strong few-shot adaptation when trained with limited downstream demonstrations.
items.author: Yupeng Zheng, Chaoyue Li, Linbo Wang et al.
items.original_title: Phoenix: Learning Scene Structure Representations for Generalizable World-Action Models
items.original_summary: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet reconstruction-oriented visual representations do not explicitly emphasize the spatial relationships and object-state changes needed for manipulation. We introduce Phoenix, which learns representations of scene structure for world-action modeling. Specifically, Phoenix Encoder enriches DINOv3's general visual semantics through dual-teacher distillation of geometric and spatiotemporal semantic knowledge. Next, CS-VAE causally aggregates and compresses Phoenix Encoder features into generative latents while preserving scene information and spatial layout. Finally, Phoenix jointly predicts these latents, complementary appearance latents, and robot actions, linking scene evolution with action generation. To study pretraining data efficiency, we curate approximately 39,000 hours of egocentric and robot manipulation data for representation learning and use the robot demonstration subset for WAM pretraining.

items.title: Managing Holiday Stress and Mental Well-Being
items.summary: The holiday season can introduce unique stressors, varying widely from person to person. Managing this period effectively involves acknowledging personal emotions, setting realistic expectations, and establishing a calendar and budget to avoid overcommitment. Experts recommend prioritizing self-care, maintaining regular sleep and eating habits, and scheduling time for breaks and fresh air. Individuals should focus on meaningful connections rather than anxiety-inducing activities. When feeling overwhelmed, taking moments alone to breathe or reaching out to trusted contacts, therapists, or support lines like 988 can help maintain emotional balance.

items.title: Metacognitive Calibration Defines Human Value in AI-Assisted Systems
items.summary: When humans collaborate with advanced AI models on decision-making, a reviewer's value depends primarily on metacognitive calibration, which is the alignment between their behavioral confidence and the actual correctness of their choices. Researchers propose a trait theory featuring five key claims regarding behavioral telemetry, expertise, and agent delegation. Analyzing a six-month production window of an AI-assisted accounting system with hundreds of reviewers, the study found that pure behavioral expertise metrics can invert ground truth by favoring overconfident groups over genuine experts. Furthermore, reviewer quality remains flat across tenure, indicating that this critical trait is not simply learned on the job. Applying proper calibration logic to both humans and the AI model effectively concentrates human effort onto genuine errors, though individual causal value cannot be identified under majority-vote aggregation.
items.author: Priyanka Sinha, Sugam Pandey
items.original_title: Knowing What You Know: A Trait Theory of Reviewer Value in Human-AI Cognitive Systems
items.original_summary: When a capable model and a human reviewer cooperate on the same decision, which human still adds value? We argue this is a question about a single cognitive trait, metacognitive calibration: the alignment between a reviewer's behavioral confidence and the actual correctness of their judgments. We develop a trait theory of reviewer value to make it precise.

items.title: Analyzing Residual Allan Stability Under Periodic Ramsey Sampling
items.summary: The timing of auxiliary Ramsey measurements significantly impacts frequency stability when dealing with drifting pulse shifts. Researchers derived exact residual covariance and Allan variance for periodic instantaneous observations of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck shift, comparing the results against a continuous Kalman reference model. The findings show that periodic estimation increases cycle-averaged estimation-error variance, decreases short-time residual Allan variance, and raises its long-time value. The team extended these calculations to include multiple independent modes and incorporated a three-level Ramsey model to illustrate how dark times affect scheduling choices.
items.author: Zhiqian Su
items.original_title: Residual Allan Stability under Periodic Auxiliary Ramsey Sampling
items.original_summary: The timing of auxiliary Ramsey measurements can change the frequency stability associated with a drifting pulse shift at a fixed nominal Fisher-information rate for a constant shift. For periodic instantaneous observations of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck shift with causal prediction between updates, we derive the exact residual covariance averaged over the update cycle and the corresponding Allan variance at arbitrary averaging times. Relative to a continuous Kalman reference at the same information rate, periodic estimation increases the cycle-averaged estimation-error variance, reduces the short-time residual Allan variance, and increases its long-time value. Its covariance decays more slowly at the origin and has a larger integral.

items.title: Mapping the AI Supply Chain and Ecosystem Dependencies
items.summary: Artificial intelligence systems rely on a complex network of organizations contributing models, data, compute, capital, and talent. Although the layers of the AI stack are generally recognized, relationships, dependencies, and potential chokepoints across these layers remain sparsely documented. Researchers have developed a data pipeline to systematically map the organizational AI supply chain, creating a large-scale, multilayered dataset that records actors, components, and their relationships. This publicly available resource aims to provide transparency into market concentration, power structures, and fragmented accountability within the industry. Illustrative analyses highlight central actors, network concentration, and critical chokepoints, though public records necessarily omit certain private deals and search-driven constraints.
items.author: Sarah H. Cen, Lindsey A. Gailmard, Joohan Kim et al.
items.original_title: Mapping the AI Supply Chain: Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Market Concentration in the AI Ecosystem
items.original_summary: AI systems are built across many organizations that contribute models, data, compute, capital, talent, and other assets. While the layers of the AI stack are relatively well understood, the relationships between actors and components across layers remains sparsely documented. In this work, we focus on the organizations that make up the AI supply chain: the complex network of actors that contribute to the development and deployment of AI. We motivate the examination of the organizational AI supply chain---highlighting concerns about concentration, power, chokepoints, cascading failures, fragmented accountability, and risk---then describe our pipeline for mapping the AI supply chain. Our pipeline yields our main contribution: a multilayered, large-scale dataset of actors and relationships in the AI ecosystem, annotated with dates, descriptions, types, tags, and more.

items.title: Grana: Vision-Language Model for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Robot reward modeling struggles with generalizing across different tasks and tracking progress during long-horizon manipulation. To resolve these issues, researchers introduced Grana, a vision-language robot reward model that identifies unfinished subtasks and estimates continuous progress utilizing open-vocabulary subtask descriptions. Traditional models often rely on inflexible action vocabularies or struggle with elapsed-time proxies that fail when task durations vary or errors reverse local progress. Grana bypasses this by using an annotation protocol that converts sparse subtask boundaries and action qualities into dense progress targets without requiring explicit numerical scoring. Pretraining across diverse short-horizon tasks allows the model to achieve zero-shot reward prediction on unseen tasks and enhances performance after adapting to multi-minute, long-horizon operations.
items.author: Zi-ang Cao, Kaiyuan Zheng, Yinzhen Xu et al.
items.original_title: Grana: Compositional Reward Modeling for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
items.original_summary: Robot reward modeling faces two challenges: generalizing across tasks and accurately tracking progress in long-horizon manipulation. General-purpose reward models demonstrate broad task transfer, but transfer from short-task pretraining to long-horizon tasks remains underexplored. Long-horizon progress models often rely on task-specific subtask classifiers or fixed action vocabularies, limiting the reuse of learned progress knowledge when adapting to new tasks. To address these challenges, we introduce Grana, a vision-language robot reward model that learns to identify unfinished subtasks and estimate their continuous progress using open-vocabulary subtask descriptions. We train a language-conditioned model to estimate progress in short-horizon tasks and individual subtasks of long-horizon tasks.

items.title: Doppel: An Embodiment-Agnostic Video World Model for Robotics
items.summary: Predicting the consequences of an agent's actions requires understanding both body motion and environmental responses. Most video world models attempt to learn both aspects strictly from numerical actions, even though geometry and kinematics already define intended movements. Researchers developed Doppel, an embodiment-agnostic video world model conditioned on camera-aligned renderings of future body configurations alongside numerical action trajectories. By explicitly providing the intended motion via renderings, the model focuses on predicting object movements and interaction-driven environmental shifts, while using rendered motion as a universal visual interface across various physical embodiments. Trained on hundreds of hours of video data spanning diverse human and robot embodiments without requiring explicit labels, Doppel improves prediction accuracy and object motion consistency over traditional action-only baseline models.
items.author: Yash Jangir, Karan Mirakhor, Renos Zabounidis et al.
items.original_title: Render the Robot, Generate the World: One Video World Model Across Embodiments
items.original_summary: Predicting the consequences of an agent's actions requires modeling both the body's motion and the environment's response. Most video world models attempt to learn both from numerical actions, even though geometry and kinematics already specify the intended motion. We introduce Doppel, an embodiment-agnostic video world model conditioned on camera-aligned renderings of future body configurations and numerical action trajectories. By explicitly providing the intended motion, Doppel can focus on predicting object motion and interaction-driven changes in the environment. Rendered motion also provides a common visual interface across different embodiments and action spaces. To train on robot datasets without camera extrinsics, we recover camera poses and align rendered trajectories with recorded observations.

items.title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta Improves AI Model Capability Alignment
items.summary: Real-world harness engineering often relies on narrow patches and benchmark-specific metrics, overlooking implicit user needs. To address this, researchers introduced Agentic Harness Engineering Beta (AHE-Beta), a requirement-centered loop. AHE-Beta operates via a three-step process: user-driven evaluation where simulated users raise issues over multiple turns, team-based modification to implement generalizable changes, and requirement-driven selection that merges changes only after verifying they pass review. Empirical tests show AHE-Beta increases pass@1 performance while consuming fewer tokens than baseline models, outperforming several existing systems. Blind human A/B tests confirmed that human users consistently prefer AHE-Beta and rate it higher across multiple dimensions. Furthermore, these performance gains transfer directly to other models like GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash without requiring further evolution, demonstrating a more general method for enhancing agent capabilities.
items.author: Jiahang Lin, Jiahao Chen, Yiding Wang et al.
items.original_title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
items.original_summary: Real-world harness engineering is driven by explicit and implicit user requirements, which guide development and validation. However, existing harness evolution methods often overlook implicit requirements and interaction needs, while using a single evolution agent to modify the harness and benchmark scores to select changes. This process often produces narrow patches and leads to benchmark-specific local optima. We introduce Agentic Harness Engineering Beta (AHE-Beta), a requirement-centered loop that brings real-world engineering practices into harness evolution. The loop consists of three steps: (1) User-driven evaluation lets simulated users raise their requirements as issues while they work with the harness over multiple turns.

items.title: Ultrafast Optical Modulation Achieved via Inverse-Designed Transparent Conducting Oxide Cavities
items.summary: Achieving strong and ultrafast optical modulation remains a major hurdle in time-varying photonics. Researchers theoretically demonstrate that combining inverse-designed cavities using transparent conducting oxides at the epsilon-near-zero point with boundaries supporting carrier transport can overcome this challenge. The method leverages enhanced optical absorption, electron heating, and interface-engineered carrier relaxation. A multilayer framework combined with a structural disorder-aware correction loop preserves robust resonant absorption in ultrathin films under realistic material conditions. Compared to conventional geometries, these structures exhibit stronger light confinement, greater electron temperature modulation, and faster recovery. Additionally, interfacial barrier engineering and adjacent-layer doping allow co-design of spectral and temporal dynamics, enabling richer oscillatory transmittance and supporting ultrafast optical responses.
items.author: Jae Ik Choi, Ludmila J. Prokopeva, Vahagn Mkhitaryan et al.
items.original_title: Strong Epsilon-Near-Zero Confinement and Interface-Controlled Dynamics in Inverse-Designed Transparent Conducting Oxide Cavities
items.original_summary: Achieving optical modulation that is both strong and ultrafast remains a central challenge in time-varying photonics. Here, we theoretically demonstrate that combining inverse-designed cavities that utilize transparent conducting oxides (TCOs) operating at the epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) point with boundaries that support carrier transport can meet this requirement. This is achieved by leveraging ENZ-enhanced optical absorption and electron heating with interface-engineered carrier relaxation. A multilayer inverse-design framework, combined with a structural disorder-aware correction loop, is developed to preserve robust resonant absorption in ultrathin TCO films under realistic material disorder. Relative to conventional TCO cavity geometries, the inverse-designed structures exhibit stronger light confinement, greater electron temperature modulation, and markedly faster recovery.

items.title: Locally Infrared-Finite Two-Loop Amplitudes for Multi-Higgs Production
items.summary: Researchers studied two-loop amplitudes for multi-Higgs production through a massive top-quark loop associated with one jet, focusing on the quark-antiquark channel with a final-state gluon. By utilizing non-local Ward identities in momentum space, they factorized longitudinal and gauge degrees of freedom via exact identities between Feynman graphs without relying on an infrared region. Within genuine two-loop topologies, replacing internal gluons with physical degrees of freedom rendered the resulting amplitude free of collinear singularities. The remaining infrared divergence consists solely of a soft singularity tied to changes in the reference gauge vector. Explicit soft counterterms were constructed to yield a locally infrared-finite representation. This approach eliminates the need for collinear counterterms and successfully reproduces remaining infrared poles.
items.author: Aniruddha Venkata
items.original_title: Locally infrared finite two-loop amplitudes for multi Higgs production in association with one jet
items.original_summary: We study the two-loop amplitudes for multi-Higgs production through a massive top-quark loop in association with one jet. We consider the quark-antiquark channel with a final-state gluon, $q\bar q\to g+nH$ although our construction applies to crossed channel as well. We utilize (non-local in momentum space) Ward identities to factorize longitudinal and gauge degrees of freedom through exact identities between Feynman graphs without reference to an infrared region. In the genuine two loop topologies, we replace the internal gluons by their physical degrees of freedom and show that the resulting amplitude is free of collinear singularities. The only remaining infrared divergence is a soft singularity that can be identified with a change of reference gauge vector.

items.title: A Nonsecular Quantum Master Equation with Detailed Balance and Error Bounds
items.summary: Developing effective theories for open quantum systems requires preserving detailed balance from microscopic reversibility while maintaining accuracy during relaxation. This is especially difficult in quantum many-body systems where dense spectra invalidate the secular approximation. Researchers constructed a nonsecular quantum master equation that satisfies time-reversal Kubo-Martin-Schwinger detailed balance. They proved a time-uniform error bound on the difference between predicted and exact reduced density matrices based on the system-bath coupling strength. The approach successfully completes the Redfield generator by enforcing detailed balance while matching dissipative and coherent coefficients at resonance. Benchmarking against exact dynamics of coupled oscillators showed the equation maintains high accuracy across both secular and nonsecular regimes, providing a systematic pathway to thermodynamically consistent open quantum dynamics.
items.author: Ji-Hui Pei, Jin-Fu Chen
items.original_title: A Nonsecular Quantum Master Equation with Detailed Balance and Second-order Error Bound
items.original_summary: An effective theory of open quantum systems should preserve the detailed balance structure inherited from microscopic reversibility and remain accurate throughout relaxation. Meeting both requirements is particularly challenging in quantum many-body systems, where dense spectra can invalidate the secular approximation even at weak coupling. Here we construct a nonsecular quantum master equation that satisfies time-reversal Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (TR-KMS) detailed balance. Under suitable conditions, we prove a time-uniform $O(λ^2)$ bound on the difference between the predicted and exact reduced density matrices, where $λ$ is the system-bath coupling strength. Our construction completes the Redfield generator by imposing detailed balance while matching its dissipative and coherent coefficients at resonance.
items.ai_title: A Nonsecular Quantum Master Equation with Detailed Balance and Error Bounds
items.ai_summary: Developing effective theories for open quantum systems requires preserving detailed balance from microscopic reversibility while maintaining accuracy during relaxation. This is especially difficult in quantum many-body systems where dense spectra invalidate the secular approximation. Researchers constructed a nonsecular quantum master equation that satisfies time-reversal Kubo-Martin-Schwinger detailed balance. They proved a time-uniform error bound on the difference between predicted and exact reduced density matrices based on the system-bath coupling strength. The approach successfully completes the Redfield generator by enforcing detailed balance while matching dissipative and coherent coefficients at resonance. Benchmarking against exact dynamics of coupled oscillators showed the equation maintains high accuracy across both secular and nonsecular regimes, providing a systematic pathway to thermodynamically consistent open quantum dynamics.

items.title: Dressed-State Quantum Information Processing Using Multilayer Ion Trap Chips
items.summary: Researchers demonstrated the experimental preparation, coherent operation, and selective readout of radio frequency (RF) dressed-state qubits using trapped 171Yb+ ions. They developed and characterized a microstructured multilayer ion trap chip featuring an integrated resonator. This integrated component generates a spatial gradient of the RF magnetic field amplitude along the axis of a linear ion crystal, enabling individual qubit addressing and qubit-qubit coupling within a two-ion Coulomb crystal. The system was experimentally evaluated using the electronic ground-state hyperfine states of laser-cooled ions driven by a global modulated RF field oscillating near 12.6 GHz. These developments establish a robust hardware foundation for advanced dressed-state quantum information processing.
items.author: Ivan A. Boldin, Elham Esteki, Bogdan Okhrimenko et al.
items.original_title: Dressed-State Quantum Information Processing Using a Multilayer Ion Trap Chip with an Integrated Radio Frequency Resonator
items.original_summary: We present the experimental preparation of a radio frequency (RF)-dressed-state qubit, the coherent operation of a single RF-dressed qubit, and the selective readout of RF-dressed hyperfine states of $^{171}$Yb${^+}$ ions trapped using a novel microstructured ion trap chip. We demonstrate the individual addressing of RF-dressed-state qubits in a two-ion Coulomb crystal. To this end, we developed, manufactured, and characterized a trap chip specifcally designed for quantum information processing with RF-dressed-state qubits. The chip consists of multiple layers, one of which includes an integrated resonator that creates a gradient of the RF magnetic field amplitude along the axis of a linear ion crystal.
items.ai_title: Dressed-State Quantum Information Processing Using Multilayer Ion Trap Chips
items.ai_summary: Researchers demonstrated the experimental preparation, coherent operation, and selective readout of radio frequency (RF) dressed-state qubits using trapped 171Yb+ ions. They developed and characterized a microstructured multilayer ion trap chip featuring an integrated resonator. This integrated component generates a spatial gradient of the RF magnetic field amplitude along the axis of a linear ion crystal, enabling individual qubit addressing and qubit-qubit coupling within a two-ion Coulomb crystal. The system was experimentally evaluated using the electronic ground-state hyperfine states of laser-cooled ions driven by a global modulated RF field oscillating near 12.6 GHz. These developments establish a robust hardware foundation for advanced dressed-state quantum information processing.

items.title: Prediction and Screening of $η$-carbide-type Nitrides for Ammonia Synthesis
items.summary: Synthesis of ammonia is of critical importance to applications in energy, industrial chemistry, and especially agriculture, and is accomplished industrially using the carbon- and energy-intensive Haber-Bosch process. η-carbide-type nitrides such as Co3Mo3N have gained attention in recent years as alternative ammonia synthesis catalysts with the potential to lower these energy demands. Co3Mo3N is experimentally observed to undergo a reversible phase transition from Co3Mo3N to Co6Mo6N, offering a chemical looping-based NH3 synthesis route that has not been fully explored. In this work, we present a first-principles exploration of phase change in the Co3Mo3N/Co6Mo6N system as a prototype η-carbide-type nitride and fit a cluster expansion to predict the energy of Co3Mo3Nx systems.
items.author: Luka H. Mikek, Nicholas D. Humphrey, Andrea Ambrosini et al.

items.title: Decomposing SGD Dynamics in Neural Networks: Teacher-Induced Spikes and Variance Inflation
items.summary: We study two-layer neural networks trained by stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on a multi-index teacher model, focusing on how first-layer parameters orthogonal to the teacher subspace affect generalization. We decompose the first-layer weights into a signal component aligned with the teacher and an orthogonal complement, and analyze their joint SGD dynamics together with the second layer in the proportional limit. We show that although SGD updates to the complement are initially isotropic, the training dynamics induce teacher-dependent spectral spikes in the complement Gram matrix. This emergent anisotropy provides a concrete mechanism by which representation variance is amplified, and generalization degrades.
items.author: Samet Demir, Zafer Dogan

items.title: New Observational Insights into Generalised Axion-Like Dark Energy
items.summary: We consider a quintessence model based on a generalised axion-like scalar field potential, originally introduced as a phenomenological framework to describe the late-time accelerated expansion of the Universe. The model exhibits a tracking regime that alleviates the coincidence problem and naturally leads to a phase of late-time acceleration driven by an effective cosmological constant, without requiring fine-tuning of the scalar field initial conditions. In this work, we confront the background cosmological evolution of this model with current observations by performing a parameter inference analysis using cosmic microwave background distance priors, baryon acoustic oscillation measurements, Type Ia supernovae, the SH0ES distance ladder, cosmic chronometers, and gamma-ray bursts.
items.author: Mariam Bouhmadi-López, Hsu-Wen Chiang, Carlos G. Boiza et al.

items.title: Beyond hidden zeros and uniqueness in Tr$(φ^3)$: Block and rod zeros in any Tr$(φ^m)$
items.summary: Hidden zeros have proven powerful tools for reconstructing amplitudes in Tr$(φ^3)$, a theory of colored scalars with cubic interactions. We show that these structures extend to any Tr$(φ^m)$ theory. For odd $m$, we construct \emph{block zeros} from orthogonal sums of consecutive momenta, generalizing the original cubic hidden zeros. For every $m\geq4$, including even $m$, we describe a second family of nonlinear \emph{rod zeros} through a rod packing problem. In Tr$(φ^4)$ this construction reduces to a simple rank-one condition on a matrix of momentum contractions. We connect this new zero to the classic threshold nullification zeros of Voloshin, where certain amplitudes in massive $φ^4$ theory vanish when all produced particles are at rest.
items.author: Laurentiu Rodina

items.title: Equivariant Modeling with Polynomial Features via Minimal Homogeneous Generators
items.summary: We present a general framework for modeling and learning equivariant functions between finite dimensional semisimple real group representations, unifying constructions developed across many application areas. Our model is a linear combination of equivariant polynomial features whose coefficients are arbitrary learnable functions of invariant polynomial features. We take as features minimal homogeneous generators for the invariant algebra and the covariant module over the invariant algebra, up to prescribed degrees. We provide a Python package that automatically computes these features and fits the resulting models to training data. The algorithm for feature computation requires explicit isotypic decompositions of the input and output representations, along with explicit Clebsch-Gordan decompositions of the tensor product of irreducible representations, and achieves speedups over alternative methods in computational algebra.
items.author: Michael Liaofan Liu, Joe Kileel

items.title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents
items.summary: User simulators offer a scalable way to evaluate interactive agents, but how to assess their quality remains underexplored. In particular, it is unclear whether existing user simulator evaluation frameworks reliably detect meaningful failures in simulated user behavior. This uncertainty makes it difficult to interpret simulator evaluation. To understand what a high benchmark score tells us about simulator quality, we (meta-)evaluate the metrics themselves. To instantiate this meta-evaluation, we deliberately perturb simulated replays to induce failures such as altered goals, omitted constraints, premature stopping, and acceptance of broken work, then test whether the metrics penalize these failures. Evaluation methods from three prior studies detect only 5-6 of the 10 perturbations; their combined scores even favor populations instructed to accept broken work over unmodified controls.
items.author: Hengguang Zhou, I-Hung Hsu, Li Chen et al.

items.title: Cap-and-Track: Optimizing LLM Inference Request Dispatch Across Shifting Capacity
items.summary: A fixed dispatch rate for LLM inference becomes stale as serving fleets resize and request sizes change. Generative output length is unknown at admission, and shared provider pools can lose capacity. We present Cap-and-Track, a design for asynchronous inference across provider capacity and internal GPUs. Meta's traffic shaper implements Cap-and-Track for post and live-video understanding. Refusals signal the backend's current admission ceiling. Durable priority queues hold excess work outside execution, including refused requests for retry. Cap is a fail-fast admission check at the saturated resource that refuses work before a long wait. Using only those refusals, the Track dispatcher probes upward and backs off.
items.author: Benjamin Novotny, Doug Szeto, Chang Wang et al.

items.title: Residual-Algebraic Design of Symmetry-Preserving Variational Quantum Circuits
items.summary: Symmetry-preserving (SP) variational quantum circuits restrict evolution to physically relevant sectors of Hilbert space, but symmetry preservation alone does not guarantee accessibility within those sectors. We show that a restricted generator set can possess a residual dynamical Lie algebra whose commutant further decomposes the target symmetry sector into invariant blocks. The associated block populations are conserved and impose a kinematic upper bound on the fidelity with a target state. We then invert this diagnostic into a circuit-design principle: candidate SP generators can be screened before variational optimization by asking whether they break the residual commutant, which invariant blocks they couple, and what adjoint module they generate under the residual algebra.
items.author: Sahinur Reja

items.title: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game
items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) now perform strongly on Alan Turing's 1950 Imitation Game, so we propose a harder challenge, the Personal Imitation Game, which asks whether a machine can replicate a specific individual in conversation rather than a generic human. Testing with 30 participants, we establish a human baseline and report the identity signals interrogators rely on: stylometric features, personality traits, and biographical facts. To demonstrate the framework, we design an LLM-based system that plays the game for one of the paper's authors, drawing on an autoethnographic dataset spanning ten years of personal digital communication. In a 20-person deception study, interrogators choose our system over the author's own friends in 7 of 10 rounds, and the author over our system in 13 of 20; neither rate is distinguishable from chance at this sample size.
items.author: Muhammad Rizky Wellyanto, Hajara-Yasmin Isa, Kexin Xue et al.

items.title: CREST: A Hardware-Aware GNN-Based Framework for High-Fidelity and Robust Superconducting Quantum Compilation
items.summary: Quantum compilation on superconducting processors requires selecting a connected execution region whose topology and calibrated properties suit the input circuit. This choice constrains subsequent routing and influences the noise encountered during execution, yet aggregate hardware-quality metrics alone may not reliably predict the execution fidelity of a given circuit. Calibration updates can also change region suitability and trigger the rebuilding of calibration-dependent resource structures. We present CREST, a graph neural network (GNN)-based framework that evaluates circuit-region compatibility before routing. It encodes gate dependencies and logical-qubit interactions alongside each candidate region's connectivity and current calibration attributes; bidirectional cross-graph attention relates the two representations, while real-device execution outcomes supervise candidate ranking.
items.author: Wenjie Sun, Xiaoyu Li, Zhigang Wang et al.

items.title: Quantum Simulation of First-Quantised Chemistry with a Sum-of-Squares Representation
items.summary: Calculating molecular energies is expected to be an important application of quantum computers, but the most efficient algorithms to achieve this typically have significant space requirements. Scaling quantum processors to thousands of logical qubits is a daunting engineering challenge, so developing algorithms that run with reduced qubit requirements is of particular importance. Moreover, most algorithms are benchmarked on active spaces with about as many orbitals as electrons, missing dynamical correlation which is necessary to describe real chemistry. Capturing this correlation requires several times more orbitals than electrons, even in compact atomic-orbital basis sets. This low-filling regime favours first quantisation, where each electron is represented by a number of qubits that grows only logarithmically with the number of orbitals.
items.author: Aleksei V. Ivanov, Christoph Sünderhauf, Jon Kunjummen et al.

items.title: Teleoperated Haircutting with Delay Compensation and Passivity-Based Control for Unilateral Internet Teleoperation under Real Communication Uncertainties
items.summary: Robotic haircutting requires accurate motion execution and reliable communication to safely reproduce the operator's commands. Internet-based teleoperation is a key enabling technology to remotely perform precise manipulation tasks such as haircutting. However, communication uncertainties, including variable transmission delays and packet jitter, degrade synchronization between the master and slave systems and affect tracking performance. This paper presents a unilateral Internet teleoperation framework for robotic haircutting that takes into account experimentally measured communication uncertainties. Three delay-compensation techniques, namely Zero-Order Hold (ZOH), First-Order Hold (FOH), and Low-Pass Filtering (LPF), are evaluated together with a classical proportional-derivative (PD) controller and a passivity-based synchronization controller.
items.author: Viridiana Luna-Zempoalteca, Zhendai Huang, Rosalba Galvan-Guerra et al.

items.title: Hurst Exponent Estimation with Quantum Wavelets
items.summary: How accurately can the Hurst exponent $H$ of fractional Brownian motion be estimated from repeated preparations of a single amplitude-encoded path, when every measurement interrogates the same realization? We extend the $ε$-decimated quantum nondecimated wavelet transform in three directions: we remove the endpoint jump of circular filtering, derive the sampling distribution of the estimator, and compare readouts at equal query budgets. A one-qubit mirror extension removes the jump and keeps every coefficient that straddles a fold of the same order as an interior coefficient, for any compactly supported filter and circular shift. The transform for any such filter is compiled from the paraunitary lattice of its filter bank, and the energy share of a level is the success probability of one multiply-controlled reflection, which is both the controlled unitary of a Hadamard test and the oracle of amplitude estimation.
items.author: Brani Vidakovic

items.title: Monoculture Robust Learning
items.summary: We introduce a notion of monoculture robustness in Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning, as a way to mitigate the problem of algorithmic monoculture (Kleinberg and Raghavan, 2021): the tendency of models sharing the same components (e.g., training data) to fail on the same inputs. Specifically, we ask whether a learner with access to a single dataset can output $k$ individually accurate hypotheses whose joint failure probability is comparable to training on $k$ independent datasets. We say that such a learning procedure achieves monoculture robustness, and we quantify this by bounding the conjunctive error that all $k$ hypotheses misclassify points in an individual sense.
items.author: Lee Cohen, Jon Kleinberg, Omer Reingold

items.title: Local AI Agents in Power Electronics Simulation: Deployment, Measurements and Costs
items.summary: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging in power electronics, where it drives the simulation loop that engineers used to close largely by hand. In this loop, a converter design, or a study of the network it connects to, is built, run, measured and revised until it satisfies its specification. Such an agent can be served from a cloud API or from an inference device on the premises. For organizations whose designs, customer data or export-controlled material cannot leave the site, and whose simulators are licensed there, local deployment is the natural choice. In such a deployment, the agent becomes an electrical load on the organization's own equipment, i.e., every run consumes power and energy on a local device, generates tokens and takes time.
items.author: Yuzhuo Li, Pasan Gunawardena, Yunwei Li

items.title: From geometric curvature to effective backgrounds: a dictionary for Dirac fermions in one, two and three spatial dimensions
items.summary: Dirac equation on curved backgrounds can be rewritten as a flat-space equation in which geometry appears as a tensorial Fermi velocity together with a set of background fields. We derive this correspondence from a single Clifford-algebra identity and follow it through one, two, and three spatial dimensions. Once the spin connection is written in terms of Ricci rotation coefficients, only two contractions can occur. The trace produces a term with the index structure of a vector potential in every dimensionality; it enters with an imaginary factor i and is precisely the term that keeps the operator Hermitian when the Fermi velocity depends on position.
items.author: David Valenzuela, Alfredo Raya

items.title: Auditing black-box clinical prediction models with a large language model through queries alone: a blinded test with planted flaws
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are used to explain clinical prediction models, on the promise that they can say what a model computes, find its faults and even reveal new knowledge in it. We tested the three promises where the answers could be checked. From the International Stroke Trial we trained four kinds of model (logistic regression, explainable boosting machine, gradient-boosted trees, neural network) for two outcomes on patients randomised earlier, planted one flaw in each of 24 copies (an under-predicted subgroup, a reversed risk factor or an implausible step) and mixed them with the 8 clean models. GPT-6 Astra audited each model three times, blind, through a tool that only returned the model's predictions; the judging rules were committed before any run and applied by program.
items.author: Zhiyu Liu, Xinyu Yang

items.title: Learning to Interact in Multi-Agent Self-Play for Controllable Autonomous Driving Scenario Generation
items.summary: Large-scale, multi-agent self-play trains robust driving policies effectively in simulation, but controlling these models to generate specific, safety-critical edge cases remains a key challenge. Existing goal-conditioned self-play frameworks rely primarily on static map-location goals and fail to reliably produce complex agent interactions such as aggressive tailgating or adversarial cut-offs. These agent interactions are necessary for rigorous autonomous vehicle (AV) testing. To address this, we present an extended multi-agent self-play framework that introduces agent-relative dynamic goals. By conditioning policies on this extended goal representation, our framework enables targeted, controllable scenario synthesis. We demonstrate that our approach successfully generates interactive driving behaviors that static-goal baselines cannot simulate, providing a flexible tool for long-tail scenario generation in AV testing.
items.author: Beyazit Yalcinkaya, Ethan Pronovost, Maximilian Naumann et al.

items.title: Rotating black hole thermodynamics at NNLO in higher-curvature gravity
items.summary: We investigate higher-curvature corrections to black-hole thermodynamics in quasitopological gravity using perturbative Euclidean-action methods. Static, spherically symmetric black holes provide a benchmark for the action expansion, while our main application concerns five-dimensional, asymptotically flat, rotating black holes with equal angular momenta. For Einstein gravity supplemented by Gauss--Bonnet and cubic quasitopological interactions, we compute the Gibbs free energy through next-to-next-to-leading order, retaining both quadratic and cubic corrections. The result retains the full dependence on the background spin parameter, without a slow-rotation expansion, and extends to arbitrary couplings of quadratic and cubic curvature invariants. We derive the corrected mass, entropy and angular momenta, and show how rotation affects the size and sign of the corrections.
items.author: Cristobal Laporte

items.title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
items.summary: Rules govern how player actions change interactive worlds. Different rules create distinct gameplay experiences within similar scenes and action spaces. For customizable gameplay, generative world models must follow user-defined rules beyond real-world behaviors. However, realizing user-defined rules presents two challenges: Rule-State Persistence and Rule-to-Visual Realization. The former requires preserving rule definitions, dependencies, and world states across saving and loading, so that restored worlds follow the established rules. The latter requires accurately realizing rule-induced changes on designated objects and attributes, particularly when affected objects are unseen. In this paper, we propose WorldRuler, which organizes rule definitions, dependencies, and object states in an executable 3D rule graph and connects rule execution, video generation, and perceptual feedback in a closed loop.
items.author: Mingliang Zhai, Chuanhao Li, Jiaming Tan et al.

items.title: Choosing What to Observe: Budget-Paired Counterfactual Audits for Credible Evaluation of Visual Agents
items.summary: Visual agents that read dense documents must ration a finite observation budget across candidate regions, yet answer accuracy conflates where an agent looks, how it adapts to the reads that remain, and how it an?swers once observation stops. We introduce budget-paired counterfactual audits, an evaluation protocol that holds public evidence and region bindings fixed while perturbing only the remaining budget or de?clared task parameters, and credits every acquired history with exact continuation values. The resulting accounting decomposes lost expected accuracy into stepwise acquisition loss and terminal decision loss, separating planning from fixed-role heuristics. Across forty paired routing anchors, five open-weight
items.author: Ruiqi Liu, Jinming Li, Mo Wang et al.

items.title: NereidVLA: Learning to Understand and Navigate the Underwater World
items.summary: Underwater navigation requires translating visual spatial cues into motion, yet marine vision-language datasets rarely include paired robot trajectories. We present NereidVLA, a vision-language-action model that transfers marine spatial knowledge to language-conditioned 3D navigation. We first train Sea2Know on approximately two million marine examples to learn target grounding, spatial relations, and scene structure without paired robot-motion supervision. We then adapt it using expert trajectories executed under simulated underwater vehicle dynamics. Given RGB histories and a language instruction, NereidVLA predicts discrete motion tokens that decode into local 3D trajectories for closed-loop tracking. Evaluation combines an independent six-dimensional underwater navigation understanding benchmark with offline prediction and closed-loop navigation.
items.author: Chenjie Zhao, Zhiliang Zhu, Quan Chen et al.

items.title: Time-Varying Medium from an Ensemble of Laser-Dressed Quantum Emitters
items.summary: We propose a minimal quantum-mechanical model of a frequency dispersive, time-modulated medium that explicitly incorporates the pumping mechanism. It consists of a homogeneous ensemble of quantum emitters dressed by a pump laser. We analyze their dispersive, time-varying response to a perturbative probe field by deriving the macroscopic polarizability of the ensemble, and then solving Maxwell's equations via the Floquet formalism. This yields a rich band structure that departs from conventional analyses in which the modulation source is neglected, arising from the interplay between the dispersive polaritonic and time-varying responses. These results shed light on the role of the modulation source in time-varying media and pave the way toward realizing dispersive time-varying media from driven quantum-mechanical systems.
items.author: Adrián Juan-Delgado, Diego Martín-Cano, Paloma A. Huidobro

items.title: Communications-free Collective Intelligence Via Allocentric Belief
items.summary: A team of skilled card players share no information amongst each other, and yet still are able to coordinate their play by watching the same players and reading the same tells. Autonomous systems have failed to exploit this logic, relying instead on explicit communication or complex state estimation schemes that can fail when it matters most. Without it, decentralized agents diverge in their world beliefs, and coordination collapses. Here we show that anchoring all agents to a single shared external actor, a common witness whose reactions encode team state, produces spontaneous, communication-free coordination. An allocentric belief network trained on witness behavior allows each agent to independently reconstruct full team state, keeping group beliefs consistent with no inter-agent exchange.
items.author: Cameron Mehlman, Arjun Mulchandani, Hovik Grigoryan et al.

items.title: Raman-induced Kerr effect and heating in diamond
items.summary: We fully characterize the polarization-dependent third-order nonlinear susceptibility in a diamond crystal using phase-sensitive nondegenerate pump-probe spectroscopy near 1~$μ$m wavelength. Measuring the frequency-domain phase shift and amplitude change of the probe pulse as a function of polarization and probe wavelength allows direct extraction of the full anisotropic $χ^{(3)}$ response, including the Raman contribution. We find that the polarization dependence of the two-beam coupling contribution for the Raman component differs from that predicted solely using one-beam selection rules. We measure a Kerr coefficient that is within the range of reported values in the literature, and our measured anisotropy parameters satisfy Kleinman symmetry, as expected.
items.author: C. D. Cruz, J. C. Stephenson, J. K. Wahlstrand

items.title: NASA Launches AMPERE Challenge for Mid-Power Electric Rocket Prototypes
items.summary: NASA has initiated the Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket (AMPERE) Challenge, inviting U.S. companies to develop prototypes of mid-power Hall effect thrusters. The competition offers a total of $500,000 split between two winning teams to advance propulsion systems critical for deep space operations and satellites. The challenge consists of three phases, beginning with concept design submissions, advancing to prototype development with NASA technology access, and concluding with no-cost testing at NASA Glenn. Registration for the challenge remains open until January 27, 2027.

items.title: Shedding Light on Quantum Non-Classicality: Witnessing Wigner Negativity with Free Electrons
items.summary: Certifying quantum non-classicality like Wigner negativity typically demands full optical state tomography. This work introduces a noise-resilient framework for witnessing optical Wigner negativity using phase-resolved quantum photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (QPINEM). By mapping electron coherences directly to symmetrically ordered optical characteristic functions within a coupling-limited phase-space region, the protocol bypasses full optical reconstruction. A post-measurement witness matrix is constructed via Bochner's theorem from recorded electron spectra, where negative eigenvalues certify non-classicality. To ensure reliability under realistic experimental conditions, a noise-aware selection procedure decouples discovery from statistical validation. Benchmarked across various optical preparations-including vacuum-Fock superpositions, odd cat states, and GKP states-the protocol provides a statistically bounded pathway for probing quantum features with free electrons.
items.author: Sunjun Hwang, Leong Chuan Kwek

items.title: Whitehead doubles and the failure of the AJ conjecture
items.summary: For marked Whitehead doubles of torus knots with coprime parameters $2\le r<s$, the AJ conjecture fails for both clasp signs, both companion chiralities, and every integer twist. The zero-framed signed unreduced colored Jones sequence has a nonzero rationally saturated annihilator. Every nonzero primitive representative specializes nontrivially at $t=-1$ with the meridian variable $M$ independent. With $L$ the longitude variable, the specialization contains the irreducible quadratic $E=L^2-(M^4-4M^2+1)L+M^4$ for the negative clasp and $M^4E(M^{-1},L)$ for the positive clasp. The corresponding quadratic is coprime to the full classical $A$-polynomial, including $L-1$, over $\mathbb{Q}(M)[L^{\pm1}]$, so the discrepancy persists when each irreducible factor is counted once.
items.author: Jinzheng Li, Yuqi Li, Hao-Yu Sun

items.title: Three-nucleon potentials and their matrix elements for $δ_{\mathrm{NS}}$ in superallowed $β$ decays
items.summary: We derive three-nucleon potentials for radiative corrections at order $\mathcal{O}(αε_χ^2)$ in chiral effective field theory where $α$ is the electromagnetic coupling and $ε_χ$ is the chiral expansion parameter. These corrections contribute to the nuclear-structure-dependent term $δ_\mathrm{NS}$ for determinations of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa matrix element $V_{ud}$ from superallowed nuclear $β$ decays. We compute matrix elements of three-nucleon contributions at orders $\mathcal{O}(α^2)$ and $\mathcal{O}(αε_χ^2)$ using quantum Monte Carlo methods. We find the matrix elements at order $\mathcal{O}(α^2)$ to be large and to have an effect on the extraction of $V_{ud}$ at the scale of $10^{-4}$. In the case of $^{10}$C, the matrix elements of $\mathcal{O}(αε_χ^2)$ three-nucleon operators provide a 2% correction to $δ_{\text{NS}}$, and are thus beyond the current precision goals.

items.title: Design and Modeling of Graded Base III-Nitride HBTs for High-Frequency Applications
items.summary: This work analyzes the high-frequency performance constraints of AlGaN/GaN heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) and proposes a novel band-engineered graded base N-polar AlGaN/GaN HBT and evaluates the RF performances. Unlike conventional p-GaN base designs, we propose a graded base in the N-polar orientation which offers polarization-induced hole accumulation with quasi-electric field-assisted minority carrier transport. The proposed design simultaneously mitigates the longstanding current crowding, Webster effect, and conventional base resistance limitations. Using well-calibrated two-dimensional TCAD simulations, the proposed compositionally graded base HBT projects peak f_T/f_{MAX} of 190/200 GHz with a power density (V_{BR}I_{MAX}/8 > 20 W/mm), offering a promising pathway toward simultaneous high-frequency and high-power GaN millimeter-wave electronics.
items.author: Md Saklain Morshed, Chandan Joishi, Ijaas Mohamed et al.

items.title: NASA Outlines Plans for Humanity's First Lunar Outpost
items.summary: NASA is developing humanity's first lunar outpost at the Moon's South Pole, where astronauts will live, work, and explore. Construction is split into three phases: initial robotic exploration and site selection from current years through 2028, establishing infrastructure and power systems from 2029 to 2032, and finally assembling a permanent habitable base. The lunar South Pole was chosen for its extreme environment, which includes areas of extended sunlight for solar power and permanently shadowed craters that may hold frozen water ice. Specialized equipment, such as the VIPER and PROMISE rovers, crewed lunar terrain vehicles, and propulsive drones, will map the treacherous terrain, avoid sharp regolith dust, and test technologies needed to prepare humanity for future missions to Mars.

items.title: Holography at finite resolution: zero-point length in AdS/CFT
items.summary: We explore the zero-point length $l_0$ of T-duality-inspired effective field theory in holography, distinguishing two readings. As a boundary resolution scale, $l_0$ filters the source of a bulk scalar in anti-de Sitter space and yields an exactly solvable boundary response that is ultraviolet finite without a hard cutoff and inherits the power-law tails of the zero-point-length kernel. We show that this filter is the source-normalized bulk-to-boundary transfer function of a $ν=1$ scalar evaluated at radial depth $z=l_0$. Anchoring Ryu-Takayanagi surfaces on the same radial surface gives finite entanglement entropies that retain the perimeter law and the universal sphere free energy.
items.author: Ankit Anand, Kimet Jusufi, Amir A. Khodahami et al.

items.title: 4D-TEMPO: Differentiable 4D-STEM ptychography via fast Physics Optimizers
items.summary: Electron ptychography recovers atomic structure from 4D-STEM data: diffraction patterns at multiple positions of a scanned probe. Current codes reconstruct an image and read atoms off it, or fit atoms under an $L_1$ loss; neither gives per-atom uncertainty. We propose 4D-TEMPO, a differentiable physical renderer that fits the atoms, the microscope, and the detector directly to the recorded electron counts under a Poisson likelihood. The output is a list of atoms, each a Gaussian primitive with a 3D position, a thermal width, and a model-conditional error bar from the Fisher information. The Fisher information also conditions the solver, gives the dose (electrons per Å$^2$) each parameter needs, and separates calibration from imaging.
items.author: Ramani Duraiswami, Yichao Zhang
