items.title: Characterizing adsorption thermodynamics in carbon capture materials: an efficient first-principles approach
items.summary: Porous materials offer a vast design space for CO$_2$ capture, whose exploration hinges on efficient and accurate first-principles predictions of the thermodynamics governing adsorption. However, simulating isotherms and heats of adsorption using grand canonical molecular simulations is extremely computationally expensive when combined with accurate ab initio treatments of the molecular interactions, limiting screening to low-pressure uptake encoded in the Henry constant. Identifying and designing the best CO$_2$ capture materials requires a strategy that can efficiently calculate their adsorption properties using ab initio potential energy surfaces such as those now available from foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs). Here we develop a neural classical density functional (cDFT) framework for carbon capture processes that allows direct calculation of adsorption isotherms from low to high loading limits of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) without grand canonical simulations.
items.author: Anna T. Bui, Grant M. Rotskoff, Thomas E. Markland

items.title: Grain-size distribution characterization from single-shot x-ray diffraction using hierarchical Bayesian multi-emitter analysis
items.summary: The distribution of grain sizes in a polycrystalline material can be determined from a 2D x-ray diffraction pattern by counting and characterizing diffraction spots, so long as the spots are discrete. This approach breaks down if there is substantial overlap of the reflections due to either a large number of grains in the scattering volume or crowding of spots caused by crystallographic texture. As a result, the spot-counting approach to grain size determination is infeasible for many situations of practical interest. We address this limitation by applying hierarchical probabilistic learning using a reversible-jump Markov chain Monte Carlo framework to jointly infer diffraction spot populations and their intensity distributions.
items.author: Hyun Sang Park, Gannon Murray, Rohit Berlia et al.

items.title: Atomic-scale assembly of sulfur vacancy complexes for tailored in-gap states in monolayer WS$_{2}$
items.summary: Atomic-scale defects in two-dimensional semiconductors are quasi-isolated quantum systems with promise for emerging technologies. Although their potential as spin qubits, quantum sensors and single-photon emitters has been demonstrated experimentally, creating them deterministically and identifying them chemically remains challenging, which limits control over their electronic states. In this work we assemble sulfur vacancies in monolayer WS$_{2}$ into complexes of different sizes and geometries using the tip of a scanning tunneling microscope. We study their electronic properties by a combination of scanning tunneling spectroscopy and density functional theory, revealing the intricate influences of geometry, underlying point group symmetries and spin-orbit coupling on hybridized states.
items.author: Daniel Jansen, Guangyao Miao, Jan-Heinrich Keienburg et al.

items.title: Computing $F$-Symbols from Modular Data
items.summary: We present a strategy for computing the $F$-symbols of unitary modular categories with a self-dual simple generator, starting from their modular data, which almost entirely avoids the non-linear solution of the pentagon equations. The algorithm climbs a ladder of braid group representations on successively more strands of the generator until enough $F$-symbols have been determined to propagate them to a complete solution. The strategy presented is successful in difficult cases through ranks 11 and 12, including $\operatorname{Z}(\mathrm{Haagerup}_3)$, and does not require the category to be multiplicity-free. Although the algorithm is implemented numerically, we describe a reliable means of recovering the exact $F$-symbols, assuming that in some gauge they lie in a given number field, and of certifying every pentagon and hexagon equation exactly.
items.author: Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez et al.

items.title: Learning the Anyon Atlas
items.summary: We extend our previous search for the modular data of topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions from 22 to 42 anyons, identifying 150,679 new modular data. We do so by adding to our algorithm three rejection gates, two of them based on logistic regression, that discard representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ unlikely to yield modular data. We estimate that roughly 80% of the modular data between ranks 23 and 42 has been identified after closing under known constructions. With this data, we find counterexamples to a conjecture of Geiko and Moore that the reality of the higher Gauss sums suffices for time-reversal symmetry in Chern-Simons theories, and propose a refined criterion.
items.author: Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez et al.

items.title: An Atiyah--Hirzebruch to Adams map and the hastened Adams spectral sequence for supercohomology
items.summary: We construct a map of filtered spectra inducing a map from the Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence (AHSS) to the Baker--Lazarev Adams spectral sequence of a $\mathit{ko}$-module $M$. Using this and a theorem of Bruner--Rognes, we construct a hastened Adams spectral sequence (HASS) for the Postnikov truncations of $\mathit{ko}$ and the connective Adams summand. Then, motivated by questions in quantum field theory, topological phases of matter, and tensor category theory, we apply the HASS to supercohomology, the cohomology theory $I_{\mathbb{C}^\times}(τ_{\le 2}\mathit{ko})$, and observe that in examples of interest it is easier to calculate with than either the AHSS or the usual Adams spectral sequence.
items.author: Arun Debray, Weicheng Ye, Matthew Yu

items.title: The Long and Winding Pore: Tuning Porosity in Templated Nanoporous Carbons
items.summary: Disordered materials pose a recurring challenge for molecular simulation: realistic structural models are often generated through thermal protocols in which several structural descriptors emerge simultaneously and cannot easily be varied independently. Nanoporous carbons constitute a particularly relevant example: pore size, wall order, curvature, and network tortuosity generally emerge as outcomes of the thermal preparation protocol, rather than being independently prescribed structural parameters. Moreover, for practical applications, models of porous materials should ideally exhibit a percolating pore network, capable of supporting end-to-end transport of adsorbed species through the material. To this end, here we introduce a hierarchy of templating strategies, built around a common melt-quench-anneal protocol driven by a machine-learned interatomic potential for carbon, that progressively separates these variables.
items.author: Zacharie Waysenson, Baptiste Barthe-Gold, Arthur France-Lanord et al.

items.title: Pole parameters of the $f_2(1270)$ and $f_2'(1525)$ from a coupled-channel analysis of the radiative $J/ψ$ multipoles
items.summary: We determine the pole parameters of $f_2(1270)$ and $f_2'(1525)$ from the combined fit to the isoscalar $D$-wave $ππ$ phase shift, the $ππ\to K\bar K$ modulus, and the BESIII $J/ψ\toγπ^0π^0$ and $γK_SK_S$ data: all three $2^{++}$ multipoles $E1$, $M2$ and $E3$, and the $M2$-$E1$ phases. The hadronic amplitude is a two-channel $K$-matrix with two poles and all parameters free, so that no resonance information is taken from the Particle Data Group. The radiative decay amplitudes are written as a coupled-channel Muskhelishvili-Omnès representation, with the Omnès matrix generated by that hadronic amplitude. The left-hand cuts, which carry the production dynamics, are approximated by a linear subtraction polynomial in the physical region.
items.author: Igor Danilkin, David Baron, Emilie Passemar et al.

items.title: On the cosmic window for neutrino self-interactions
items.summary: Neutrino self-interactions ($ν$SI) beyond the Standard Model have arisen as a promising probe of new physics in cosmology. In this Letter, we show that $ν$SI emerging in the low-energy limit of renormalizable theories implies resonant mediator behavior. We identify two regions for $ν$SI: (i) neutrinos become tightly coupled with background evolution; for the first time, we establish how this evolution modifies the Boltzmann hierarchy equations (BHEs), and (ii) resonant $ν$SI dominates the dynamics with negligible background evolution, relevant for mediator masses $\sim 10^{-6}-1$ MeV. In region (i), before matter-radiation equality, neutrino free-streaming is determined by the effective four-fermion interaction, known as the heavy-mediator limit (HML); we explore the impact of background evolution on this scenario, and from our modified BHEs, we show that self-interacting dark radiation scenarios require larger couplings than previously estimated to mimic $ν$SI.
items.author: Ivan Pérez-Castro, Jorge Venzor, Josue De-Santiago et al.

items.title: A New GUT
items.summary: We present a new class of 4-dimensional Grand Unified Theories where the gauge sectors of the standard model have a novel embedding in the unified group that does not factor through an $SU(5)$ subgroup. The smallest example has gauge algebra $\frak{su}(12)$ and an anomaly-free spectrum that produces the three standard model generations with no additional chiral matter. The embedding predicts the axion-photon anomaly ratio $E/N=2/3$ and the weak mixing angle $\sin^2θ_W=1/2$ at the unification scale. Gauge-mediated proton decay proceeds through flipped-$SU(5)$-like operators and the minimally charged smooth monopole carries two Dirac charge units. The global gauge group can be $SU(12)$ or $SU(12)/\mathbb{Z}_2$, with the former allowing color singlets of half-integer electric charge.

items.title: NASA Telescopes Observe Rare Stellar Merger in Andromeda Galaxy
items.summary: Researchers identified a rare stellar merger in the Andromeda galaxy involving a star slightly less massive than the Sun spiraling into and merging with a supergiant star. Nicknamed Bao, the newly single star was monitored by NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope and other observatories, providing an unprecedented look at a common envelope evolution. The primary star, a massive supergiant, engulfed its smaller companion over just seven orbits. Through updated simulations and multi-wavelength data, scientists reconstructed the event and estimated the mass of the demolished companion. This discovery paves the way for similar transient analyses using upcoming surveys from NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

items.title: Light fermions can trigger a Brout-Englert-Higgs effect
items.summary: The Brout-Englert-Higgs effect produces the masses of the Standard Model particles. However, the cause of this effect is unknown. Beyond-the-Standard-Model theories aim to find the source of this effect, for example using a composite Higgs and dynamically generating its vacuum expectation value. In this paper, we show evidence from lattice simulations with vectorially coupled fermions and without Yukawa couplings that the Brout-Englert-Higgs effect could be triggered by the light masses of fermions. This suggests that an explanation entirely within the Standard Model could be possible. Moreover, our results are consistent with weak couplings and fermions can only impact the Higgs potential at NNLO.
items.author: Axel Maas, Sofie Martins, Georg Wieland

items.title: Generation of neutron Bessel beams
items.summary: Matter waves can exhibit structured wavefields analogous to those of light, offering new means of controlling the spatial and angular-momentum degrees of freedom of massive particles. Bessel beams are a fundamental class of structured waves that exhibit non-diffracting propagation, self-healing, and well-defined orbital angular momentum (OAM). Here, we experimentally realize neutron Bessel beams by imprinting a nanoscale conical phase gradient onto a neutron wavefront. By incorporating azimuthal phase gradients, we generate zeroth-, third-, and sixth-order Bessel beams, demonstrating direct control of both the OAM and radial structure of a massive particle. We also propose a neutron Bessel-grating interferometer, complementary to established optical and electron interferometric methods, in which varying the radial grating period by approximately 100 nm yields a controlled Gouy phase shift of $π$.
items.author: Owen Lailey, Dusan Sarenac, Nir Emelianenko et al.

items.title: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA stochastic constraints on first-order phase transitions: A tale of priors
items.summary: We re-examine the methodology for constraining cosmological first-order phase transitions from gravitational-wave searches using Bayesian statistical analysis. Specifically, we use results from LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA searches for a stochastic gravitational wave background during observing runs O1--O4a. We explore multiple prior choices across three categories of fit parameters: geometrical parameters, thermodynamical parameters of phase transitions, and the parameters of an Abelian Higgs particle physics model. Our key finding is that the constraints on most parameters describing gravitational waves from a phase transition depend strongly on the prior. Consequently, the data do not yet allow to derive robust constraints on these parameters. Besides, even if a parameter is meaningfully constrained, the upper limit can vary significantly with the prior range.
items.author: S. AbdusSalam, J. Kersten, S. A. Ojaghi et al.

items.title: Reliable arithmetic circuits using less reliable (sub-digital) logic
items.summary: The frequent static failure of CMOS logic gates at ultra-low voltages has historically been perceived as a strict barrier to extreme voltage scaling: this paper introduces a statistical circuit law proving this intuition wrong. We discovered a universal power law connecting gate and circuit static failure probabilities, revealing that circuit failure requires the simultaneous breakdown of an entire gate cluster rather than a single component. Because the required cluster size increases rapidly as voltage drops, low-voltage \textit{sub-digital} logic exhibits surprising inherent resilience to static failure. This insight stems from new theoretical tools we developed to quantify static failure, extending well beyond conventional voltage-margin analysis.
items.author: Trevor McCourt, Ila R. Fiete, Neil Gershenfeld et al.

items.title: Orientation-Tunable Interfacial Thermal Conductance in Lateral MoSe2/MoS2 Heterostructures: A Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics Study
items.summary: Managing heat flow across interfaces in lateral 2D transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterostructures is a key challenge for next-generation nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices. To tackle this, we trained a deep learning interatomic potential (DLP) using DeePMD-kit on density functional theory (DFT) data, then paired it with non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) simulations to study interfacial thermal conductance (ITC) in lateral MoSe$_2$/MoS$_2$ heterostructures, considering both armchair and zigzag interface orientations. The potential we trained closely matches DFT energies, forces, and phonon dispersion relations, which confirms its reliability for thermal transport simulations. Examining cell lengths from 10 to 40 nm and extrapolating to infinite length, the armchair interface shows a higher ITC (473 MW/m$^2$K) than the zigzag interface (387 MW/m$^2$K), and the armchair interface remains higher at every length considered.
items.author: Shirin Sabokdast, Pedram Mirchi, Ali Rajabpour

items.title: Mid-Infrared Integrated Acousto-Optic Phase Modulation on GaAs/AlGaAs
items.summary: We demonstrate a mid-infrared (7.5-10 um) integrated acousto-optic phase modulator operating at 460MHz based on a GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure. The combination of broad mid-infrared transparency and piezoelectric properties of GaAs based structures allows monolithic integration of all the device functions (electro-acoustic transduction and acousto-optic interaction) on a single material platform. Addressing the challenge presented by comparable mid-infrared and acoustic wavelengths, simultaneous propagation and confinement of surface acoustic waves and guided light is achieved using a deep-etched sub-wavelength grating. We develop a comprehensive and quantitative simulation framework to design the modulator devices, characterize their acoustic properties in a heterodyne vibrometer and perform a full, quantitative analysis of the device performance by inserting them in an integrated Mach-Zehnder interferometer.
items.author: Thomas Gérodou, Mathilde Urbain, Luca Lucia et al.

items.title: Machine-learned potentials for iron oxides at extreme conditions
items.summary: Reliable phase stability requires accurate relative free energies, which small force errors alone do not guarantee. We develop atomic-cluster-expansion potentials for five iron oxides from Fe$_2$O to Fe$_2$O$_3$, covering crystalline and liquid states at 140--260\,GPa and 1000--11000\,K, with electronic and ionic temperatures matched. Force-dominated training leaves systematic energy offsets between structure families of up to 41\,meV/atom that persist despite additional training data. Stronger energy weighting and weaker regularization largely remove these offsets, while converged k-point sampling prevents further composition-dependent biases. The final potentials achieve held-out energy errors of 2.0--5.5\,meV/atom and first-order free-energy errors within 3.4\,meV/atom for liquids at 5000--9000\,K. However, an untrained NiAs-type FeO phase exhibits a free-energy error of 57\,meV/atom despite a low extrapolation grade.
items.author: S. Azadi, S. M. Vinko, T. D. Kühne et al.

items.title: First Implementation and Characterization of a Fiber Amplifier in a Gravitational Wave Detector
items.summary: Gravitational-wave detectors rely on large-scale interferometers operating at exquisite sensitivities, where the laser source plays a central and critical role. The sensitivity of these instruments is directly influenced by the power level and noise properties of the injected light. Fiber amplifiers are a promising technology that are currently considered for the next generation of detectors because of their potential in laser power scaling and their superior output beam quality. In the context of the Virgo gravitational wave detector, we report the first implementation of a fiber amplifier into Virgo's injection system as a high-power laser source. We demonstrate a 130 W output beam that fulfills the requirements in terms of frequency noise, power noise, and beam-pointing noise.
items.author: Margherita Turconi, Marina Trad Nery, Rémi Soulard et al.

items.title: Migration's Impact on Ungulate Evolution
items.summary: A new study published in PLOS Biology reveals that migration significantly influences the diversification dynamics of ungulates. By moving to more favorable areas to overcome resource limitations, these species drove changes in ecosystem properties and functioning.

items.title: Indirect Muscles Stabilize Insect Flight
items.summary: Flapping flight in Drosophila is inherently unstable, requiring rapid adjustments. While direct steering muscles control quick reflexes, recent connectome data show indirect steering muscles receive identical sensory synaptic inputs. Researchers demonstrated that indirect tergopleural muscles significantly contribute to flight stabilization, particularly during large pitch perturbations. When faced with large disturbances, flies alter wing pitch angles to harness extra lift and drag forces efficiently. Using optogenetics and control theory, the team found that the tergopleural muscle is activated by a proportional gain component to adjust the wing's rest angle. This highlights how insects select reflex strategies to maintain stability during time-critical behaviors.
items.author: Han Kheng Teoh, Debojyoti Biswas, Haoru Li et al.
items.original_title: An indirect wing steering muscle stabilizes flight by regulating wing pitch angle in Drosophila
items.original_summary: by Han Kheng Teoh, Debojyoti Biswas, Haoru Li, Abby Leung, B. Kemper Ludlow, Samuel C. Whitehead, Erica Ehrhardt, Michael Dickinson, Tsevi Beatus, Noah J. Cowan, Itai Cohen Flapping flight is inherently unstable, requiring Drosophila to fine-tune their wing motions on a milliseconds timescale. Pioneering studies have shown that the direct steering muscles, which attach to the wing hinge, are important for generating these rapid flight reflexes. Recent connectome data, however, reveal that indirect steering muscles or tension muscles, which alter the mechanics of the thorax, receive some of the same synaptic inputs from the sensory apparatus as the direct steering muscles.

items.title: New Statistical Tool Decodes Complex Gene Interactions
items.summary: Analyzing gene-gene interactions across multiple binary phenotypes is difficult due to sparse interaction matrices and low statistical power. To address this, researchers introduced GiMat, a statistical framework extending multivariate kernel regression to model gene interactions jointly across dichotomous phenotypes. GiMat successfully captures both homogeneous and heterogeneous effects while controlling type I error. When applied to UK Biobank data concerning type 2 diabetes and hypertension comorbidity, the framework uncovered four previously unknown gene-gene interaction pairs, demonstrating its potential for robust genetic discovery.
items.author: Siru Wang, Xuhui Zhu, Yu Li et al.
items.original_title: A statistical framework to identify gene-gene interactions underlying multiple dichotomous phenotypes from genotype data
items.original_summary: by Siru Wang, Xuhui Zhu, Yu Li, Gengjie Jia Identifying gene-gene (G × G) interactions across multiple dichotomous phenotypes is challenging due to the extreme sparsity of SNP-derived interaction matrices and the reduced statistical power associated with binary outcomes. Existing G × G association methods are restricted to either single or multiple continuous phenotypes. Here we introduce GiMat (Gene Interaction and Multiple-phenotype Association Test), a statistical framework that extends multivariate kernel regression to model G × G interactions jointly across dichotomous phenotypes, while explicitly capturing homogeneous and heterogeneous interaction effects. Extensive simulations demonstrate that GiMat controls type I error conservatively and adapts power flexibly to different types of relationships between interaction effects and phenotypes.

items.title: Calibrating Epigenetic Clocks for Longevity in Blue Zones
items.summary: Researchers investigated how biological aging differs from chronological age in the Nicoya blue zone of Costa Rica using DNA methylation data. By applying a machine learning ensemble approach called SuperLearner on a reference population of non-Nicoyan Costa Ricans, the team optimized predictive performance across existing epigenetic clocks. Initial estimates of Epigenetic Age Acceleration varied widely depending on the clock used. However, mean calibration aligned the results and revealed a modest biological age advantage for Nicoyan residents, which was primarily concentrated among the oldest participants.
items.author: Nolan Gunter, Andres Cardenas, Michael Kobor et al.
items.original_title: Aging out of the blue: Region-specific epigenetic clock calibration for a blue zone with the DNAm SuperLearner
items.original_summary: by Nolan Gunter, Andres Cardenas, Michael Kobor, Nicole Gladish, Julie MacIsaac, Kristy Dever, David Rehkopf, William Dow, Luis Rosero-Bixby, Alan Hubbard Epigenetic clocks estimate biological age from DNA methylation patterns at CpG sites, providing robust predictions of mortality and morbidity risk. “Blue zones,” regions of exceptional longevity, offer a unique opportunity to investigate how biological aging diverges from chronological age. However, standard clocks are typically trained on large, heterogeneous datasets, reflecting average population trends rather than region-specific dynamics. Using data from the Costa Rican Longevity and Healthy Aging Study (CRELES), we profiled DNA methylation from residents of the Nicoya blue zone ( n = 206) and a reference population in other parts of Costa Rica ( n = 875).
items.ai_title: Calibrating Epigenetic Clocks for Longevity in Blue Zones
items.ai_summary: Researchers investigated how biological aging differs from chronological age in the Nicoya blue zone of Costa Rica using DNA methylation data. By applying a machine learning ensemble approach called SuperLearner on a reference population of non-Nicoyan Costa Ricans, the team optimized predictive performance across existing epigenetic clocks. Initial estimates of Epigenetic Age Acceleration varied widely depending on the clock used. However, mean calibration aligned the results and revealed a modest biological age advantage for Nicoyan residents, which was primarily concentrated among the oldest participants.

items.title: Mathematical Models Reveal Role of Molecular Error Correction in Cell Memory
items.summary: Cells store biological information by attaching molecular marks to DNA and proteins, but random enzymatic activity normally causes these marks to degrade quickly within the timeframe of molecular turnover. Researchers used minimal mathematical models to study a cellular strategy called molecular error correction, which closely mirrors a theoretical mechanism proposed by Francis Crick. The analysis shows that Crick-like error correction significantly extends the lifetime of stored memories without requiring excessive molecular redundancy. However, ambient marking activity can generate false positives, revealing that optimal error correction operates at a moderate level rather than an unlimited maximum. Combining error correction with redundant encoding successfully produced stable memories lasting ten to one hundred times longer than normal turnover periods, providing fresh insights into noisy biological memory systems.
items.author: John J. Vastola, Tejas Ramdas, Samuel J. Gershman
items.original_title: Storing long-lived memories via molecular error correction: A minimal mathematical model of Crick’s memory switch
items.original_summary: by John J. Vastola, Tejas Ramdas, Samuel J. Gershman Cells store information in part by attaching molecular marks to proteins and DNA. But because marks can be randomly removed (e.g., due to ambient phosphatase activity) and added (e.g., due to ambient kinase activity), information encoding may be poor, and in the worst case marks may only store information on the time scale of molecular turnover. We identify a high-level strategy cells use to maintain encoding fidelity beyond the time scale of turnover—which we call molecular error correction—and find that it closely resembles an underexplored theoretical proposal by Francis Crick. To assess the effectiveness of molecular error correction, we construct and analyze several minimal mathematical models of molecular memory switches.

items.title: Mechanistic Modeling Improves Radiopharmaceutical Therapy for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Radiopharmaceutical therapy using [177Lu]Lu-PSMA is an approved treatment for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, but current clinical protocols rely on nonpersonalized, empirical fixed schedules. Researchers developed a patient-personalizable mathematical model to simulate tumor response and organ-at-risk toxicity during this treatment. By integrating tumor growth dynamics, radiobiological responses, and organ-resolved pharmacokinetics from imaging data, the model allows for simulations across virtual patient cohorts. Global sensitivity analysis highlighted tumor growth, drug uptake, and radiosensitivity as major drivers of differences between patients. In silico trials evaluating various dosing strategies demonstrated that consolidated regimens with fewer, higher-activity injections improved overall survival in simulations but increased kidney toxicity. These findings suggest that mechanistic modeling can effectively help design and personalize radiopharmaceutical dosing schedules.

items.original_title: Radiopharmaceutical therapy for metastatic prostate cancer: Insights from mechanistic modeling and in silico trials
items.original_summary: by Matteo Italia, Silvia Bordel-Vozmediano, José García Otero, Gabriel F. Calvo, Víctor M. Pérez-García Radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) has rapidly evolved into a key precision-oncology modality, with radioligands now approved or in late-stage development for multiple solid tumors, including neuroendocrine and prostate cancers. RPT with [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA (Prostate-Specific Membrane Antigen) has recently been approved as a life-prolonging treatment for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), but its clinical use still relies on nonpersonalized, empirically chosen fixed schedules. Here, we develop a mechanistic, patient-personalizable mathematical model simulating mCRPC response and organ-at-risk toxicity during [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA RPT. The model integrates tumor growth dynamics, radiobiological response, and organ-resolved pharmacokinetics inferred from mass data and standardized uptake values obtained from positron emission tomography studies.

items.title: IncD Protein Proven Essential for Chlamydia Infection and Host Interactions
items.summary: The bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis causes sexually transmitted infections and relies on a specialized intracellular compartment called an inclusion for replication. Within the inclusion membrane, bacterial proteins known as Inc proteins manipulate host pathways to acquire vital nutrients, particularly host sphingolipids delivered via CERT-dependent pathways. Because traditional methods disrupted vesicular and non-vesicular trafficking simultaneously, researchers engineered conditional and null incD mutants to study the specific role of the inclusion membrane protein IncD. Depleting IncD or mutating its CERT-binding region resulted in smaller inclusions, premature lysis, and fewer infectious progeny. A complete loss of IncD halted bacterial growth unless CERT was artificially redirected to the inclusion. Furthermore, tests in a mouse model confirmed that IncD is required for infection in vivo, establishing the IncD-CERT pathway as essential for Chlamydia development.
items.author: Samantha K. D’Spain, Haley E. Adcox, Lily P. Phan et al.
items.original_title: IncD is an essential type III effector that supports Chlamydia propagation
items.original_summary: by Samantha K. D’Spain, Haley E. Adcox, Lily P. Phan, Eleanor S. Steiner, Katerina Wolf, Kentaro Hanada, Isabelle Derré The obligate intracellular bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis is the most common bacterial cause of sexually transmitted infections worldwide. C. trachomatis replicates within a specialized intracellular compartment, the inclusion, whose membrane contains bacterial inclusion membrane (Inc) proteins, a family of type III secreted effectors that manipulate host pathways to support bacterial development and nutrient acquisition. Acquisition of host sphingolipids is essential for C. trachomatis development, but the relative contributions of the two CERT-dependent pathways that deliver sphingomyelin to the inclusion remain unclear. CERT mediates both vesicular trafficking from the Golgi and non-vesicular trafficking at endoplasmic reticulum-inclusion membrane contact sites through its interaction with the inclusion membrane protein IncD.

items.title: New Mycobacterial Protein Discovered Linking Cell Division and Envelope Integrity
items.summary: Mycobacterium tuberculosis and related species have evolved unique growth and division mechanisms that differ significantly from model bacteria like Escherichia coli. Researchers identified two novel DivIVA domain-containing proteins in mycobacteria, Msm0050 and Msm5083, thereby expanding the known repertoire of these structural elements. Detailed functional analysis of Msm5083 revealed its critical involvement in lipid biosynthesis and the maintenance of cell envelope integrity, leading to its designation as CidIVA. Subcellular localization and interactome studies showed that CidIVA targets the cell membrane and interacts with proteins involved in lipid metabolism, membrane synthesis, and transportation. Although its orthologue Rv1209 was found to be dispensable for in vitro growth, it is explicitly required for mycobacterial survival inside a living host, advancing overall understanding of bacterial cell biology.

items.original_title: CidIVA, a novel DivIVA domain-containing protein, is critical for cell envelope integrity and intracellular survival of mycobacteria
items.original_summary: by Yogita Kapoor, Debatri Dutta, K. S. Suhas, Arnab Chakraborty, Shalini Birua, Anshu Priya, Mehak Zahoor Khan, Harikrishna Adicherla, Archana Singh, Siddhesh S. Kamat, Neeraj Dhar, Amit Singh, Vinay Kumar Nandicoori Bacterial genomes encode a diverse array of proteins that function in a coordinated manner to orchestrate the highly dynamic process of cell division. Over the course of evolution, Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) and related mycobacterial species have diverged from the model bacterial species such as E. coli and B. subtilis and acquired distinct, poorly conserved proteins that underpin their distinct mechanisms of growth and division. However, the identity and functional roles of these molecular determinants remain largely elusive.

items.title: Leishmania Parasites Hijack Host ER Protein to Alter Macrophage Metabolism
items.summary: During Leishmania infections, interactions between the parasite's vacuole and the host cell endoplasmic reticulum are vital for replication. Researchers identified the endoplasmic reticulum-shaping protein CLIMP-63 as a key host factor that promotes infection by Leishmania. Following internalization, CLIMP-63 redistributes to the parasitophorous vacuoles, where it associates with VDAC2 at endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondria contact sites using the parasite virulence glycolipid lipophosphoglycan. Further investigation revealed that CLIMP-63 is necessary for Leishmania-induced mitochondrial DNA replication, cristae biogenesis, and heightened mitochondrial respiration, all of which assist the parasite in colonizing macrophages. These findings demonstrate how Leishmania exploits host structural proteins to reprogram cellular bioenergetics.
items.author: Charles-Antoine Boyer, Hamlet Acevedo Ospina, Albert Descoteaux
items.original_title: Leishmania exploits the macrophage endoplasmic reticulum-shaping protein CLIMP-63 to modulate mitochondrial biogenesis and bioenergetics
items.original_summary: by Charles-Antoine Boyer, Hamlet Acevedo Ospina, Albert Descoteaux In Leishmania -infected macrophages, interactions between parasitophorous vacuoles and the host cell endoplasmic reticulum are critical for parasite replication. Whether the complex architecture of this organelle influences these interactions remains unknown. Here, we identify the endoplasmic reticulum-shaping protein CLIMP-63 as a host factor promoting Leishmania infection. Following parasite internalization, we observed a redistribution of CLIMP-63 to parasitophorous vacuoles where it associates with VDAC2, a component of endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondria contact sites, in a process dependent on the virulence glycolipid lipophosphoglycan. Mechanistically, we found that CLIMP-63 is required for Leishmania -induced mitochondrial DNA replication, cristae biogenesis, and enhanced mitochondrial respiration, which collectively contribute to parasite colonization of macrophages.

items.title: Scoping Review Explores Vitamin D and Uterine Leiomyomas
items.summary: A scoping review examined clinical, molecular, and genetic evidence concerning the vitamin D-vitamin D receptor axis in uterine leiomyomas. Researchers searched major databases from January 2016 to December 2025, ultimately including 42 relevant studies. Most clinical findings indicated lower circulating vitamin D levels in women with uterine leiomyomas compared to controls, often showing inverse relationships with fibroid size and volume. Meanwhile, molecular studies highlighted reduced receptor expression and altered signaling pathways in leiomyoma tissue. The authors concluded that while existing data points to consistent associations, further prospective cohort studies with rigorous confounder adjustment are required to determine true causality and mechanisms.
items.author: Godfrey Katamba, Rogers Kajabwangu, Hamson Kanyesigye et al.
items.original_title: The vitamin D-vitamin D receptor axis in uterine leiomyomas: A scoping review of clinical, molecular, and genetic evidence
items.original_summary: by Godfrey Katamba, Rogers Kajabwangu, Hamson Kanyesigye, Mivule A. Kinene, David Collins Agaba, Ronald Ouma Omolo, Agnes Namaganda, Haruna Muwonge Uterine leiomyomas are the most common benign tumours of the female reproductive tract and a major cause of gynaecological morbidity worldwide. Observational and experimental studies have linked vitamin D and the vitamin D receptor (VDR) separately to uterine leiomyoma biology, including effects on cell proliferation and Wnt/β-catenin signalling in vitro; however, the breadth of this evidence has not been comprehensively mapped across clinical, molecular, and genetic domains. We conducted a scoping review following Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and reported using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR).

items.title: Examining Older Adults' Informal Social Support Networks in Slovenia
items.summary: Researchers analyzed the evolution of informal social support networks among older adults in Slovenia from 2002 to 2025 using cross-sectional survey data. The study identified several distinct network types, including family dependent, private restricted, local self-contained, locally integrated, and wider community networks. Findings revealed that the proportion of older adults reporting no informal social support rose sharply to 7.8% in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, but partially recovered to 4.4% by 2025. Despite this recovery, persistent inequalities remain, with older men showing a higher vulnerability to social isolation and pointing to a need for targeted public support services.

items.original_title: Social support networks of older adults before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
items.original_summary: by Marjan Cugmas, Anuška Ferligoj, Tina Kogovšek, Zenel Batagelj Societies are considerably challenged by population aging, especially when it comes to providing services and support for older adults. Although formal services such as home care and volunteering address some of these needs, the informal social support given by relatives, friends and neighbours is just as vital. In Slovenia, the share of older adults reporting they have no informal social support rose from around 1% in 2002 to 7.8% in 2020, coinciding with the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic. The article examines the prevalence and characteristics of social support network types relied on by older adults in Slovenia between 2002 and 2025, with a special focus on the post-pandemic recovery.

items.title: Systematic Review Details Musculoskeletal Injuries in African Football
items.summary: A systematic review synthesized existing evidence regarding the epidemiology of musculoskeletal injuries among football players across Africa. Researchers systematically searched multiple databases and assessed the methodological quality of eligible studies using established tools. Out of the reviewed literature, reported injury incidence varied widely from 2.2 to 289 injuries per 1,000 athlete-exposure hours, while prevalence estimates ranged from 4.1% to 81.6%. Lower-extremity injuries, particularly involving the ankle and knee, were the most prevalent, with sprains, strains, and contusions occurring most frequently. A history of previous injury was consistently identified as a primary risk factor. The authors emphasize the need for standardized injury surveillance to improve future research and prevention strategies.

items.original_title: Musculoskeletal injury epidemiology among football players in Africa: A systematic review of injury incidence, patterns and associated factors
items.original_summary: by Fadilulahi Adekilekun Jimoh, Adeola Medinat Adepoju, Samuel Timileyin Afolabi, Abass Mosebolatan Bolarinwa Background Football is widely played across Africa, yet evidence on the epidemiology of musculoskeletal injuries among African football players remains fragmented across countries, populations, and competitive settings. Differences in injury definitions, surveillance methods, and exposure measurement further limit comparison between studies. This systematic review synthesised the available evidence on musculoskeletal injury epidemiology in African football. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, the Cochrane Database, and Google Scholar were systematically searched from inception to the final search date, supplemented by backward citation searching. Studies investigating musculoskeletal injuries among football players in Africa were eligible for inclusion.

items.title: Biological and Genomic Analysis of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. sunkii
items.summary: Researchers analyzed the biological characteristics, morphology, and genetic functions of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. sunkii, a strain isolated from the vaginal secretions of pregnant women. Using mass spectrometry, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, electron microscopy, and whole-genome sequencing, the team examined the strain's structural and genetic properties. Laboratory assays tested its biochemical reactions, acid production, antimicrobial susceptibility, and antibacterial activity against specific pathogens. The findings indicate that the strain is a Gram-positive, facultative anaerobe that ferments sugars into acid, inhibits certain bacteria, and carries multiple antibiotic resistance genes. This research provides foundational knowledge regarding vaginal microbiota balance and potential probiotic development, though further animal studies are required to confirm its role in humans.

Elucidating its biological properties and genetic functions may provide a theoretical foundation for developing probiotic preparations to treat bacterial vaginosis. The strain was identified as L. delbrueckii subsp. sunkii using mass spectrometry and 16S ribosomal RNA (16S rRNA) gene sequencing. Colony morphology was observed, Gram staining characteristics were examined, and cellular ultrastructure was visualized via scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Whole-genome sequencing was performed using both second- and third-generation sequencing platforms, followed by comprehensive bioinformatics analysis.

items.title: Compact Microwave Metasurface Absorber Achieves High Absorption
items.summary: Scientists have developed a compact metasurface-based absorber designed for the microwave band to improve the performance of small aerial platforms such as unmanned aerial vehicles. Conventional absorbers often require specific thicknesses or active components, limiting practical use. By engineering dipole resonances to achieve impedance matching, the new design reaches a maximum absorptance of 99.6% at 10 GHz. The absorber maintains an absorptance above 50% for incidence angles from 0 to 70 degrees. Utilizing finite-element simulations, researchers confirmed the physical origin of absorption and evaluated structural parameters. With a thickness of only one-thirtieth of its operating wavelength, the device offers high design freedom and presents a practical approach for miniaturized microwave hardware.

At the same time, the absorber maintains an absorptance above 50% for incidence angles ranging from 0° to 70°.

items.title: Evaluation of Research Publication Practices Among African Academics
items.summary: A study investigating research publication practices among African university-based researchers highlights how systemic and structural challenges impact scientific output. Using an indigenous realist evaluation approach, data were gathered from interviews with participants in research capacity-strengthening workshops. The analysis reveals that institutional pressures, such as career growth tied to publications and the 'publish or perish' mindset, drive researchers to focus on publication quantity. Additionally, misconceptions surrounding journal impact factors and the perceived prestige of Western publications influence where academics choose to submit their work. When universities establish read-and-publish agreements with Western outlets while local journals lack visibility, researchers increasingly target international journals. The findings suggest that African institutions should reevaluate their career progression and publication policies through a decolonial lens.

items.original_summary: by Meshack Nzesei Mutua, Felix Otieno, Marthe Montcho, Ferdinand C. Mukumbang Understanding research publication practices among African academics is critical to promoting knowledge equity and addressing structural and systemic challenges that disproportionately affect them, thereby increasing the quantity and quality of scientific output and catalysing socio-economic development on the continent. By exploring research publication practices among university-based African researchers, this paper offers transferable insights into how and why initiatives can promote positive publication practices, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Using an Indigenous realist evaluation approach, data were collected from three distinct African research project teams that participated in research capacity-strengthening workshops to enhance their research publication skills.

items.title: Late-Pregnancy Food Insecurity Linked to Lower Newborn Birth Weights
items.summary: A facility-based cross-sectional study conducted in Northern Ethiopia evaluated the association between household food insecurity during late pregnancy and infant birth weight. Utilizing propensity score matching among 286 mother-newborn pairs, the study found that 38.1% of participating households experienced food insecurity. The prevalence of low birth weight was significantly higher among food-insecure mothers at 48.6%, compared to 11.3% among food-secure mothers. Statistical models revealed that newborns born to food-insecure mothers weighed an average of 204 grams less. These findings indicate a strong link between maternal food access and adverse birth outcomes, underscoring the need for nutritional assessments, targeted education, and social support interventions during antenatal care to improve maternal and child health.

items.title: Genomic and Cold-Stress Analysis of Soybean HD-ZIP IV Transcription Factors
items.summary: Homeodomain-leucine zipper transcription factors play vital roles in plant growth and environmental stress responses. This study characterized soybean HD-ZIP IV candidates through domain screening, genomic mapping, phylogenetic comparisons, and expression analyses. A domain audit identified 29 candidates with group IV patterns distributed across 15 chromosomes. Evolutionary analysis of candidate pairs revealed Ka/Ks ratios consistently below 1.0, pointing to purifying selection constraints. Co-expression networks and secondary cold-stress expression data further highlighted specific candidate genes responding to low temperatures. These insights establish a foundation for future functional studies on soybean cold tolerance and gene regulation mechanisms.

items.original_title: Genomic characterization, synteny, and cold-responsive expression of Soybean HD-ZIP IV transcription factor candidates
items.original_summary: by Kenzhen Zhao, Huilong Hong, Xiulin Liu, Xueyang Wang, Chunlei Zhang, Fengyi Zhang, Rongqiang Yuan, Sobhi F. Lamlom, Honglei Ren Homeodomain–leucine zipper (HD-ZIP) transcription factors regulate plant development and responses to environmental stress. This study characterized selected soybean ( Glycine max ) HD-ZIP IV candidates by integrating domain screening, genomic mapping, phylogenetic comparison, evolutionary analysis, general co-expression networks, and secondary analysis of cold-stress expression data. A broader domain audit recovered 95 loci with family-associated architectures, comprising 54 with I/II patterns, 12 with III patterns, and 29 with IV patterns. Comparison with a published 88-gene inventory established correspondences for 86 entries, of which 82 satisfied the joint-domain criteria; recovery therefore remained conditional rather than demonstrating completeness.
items.ai_title: Genomic and Cold-Stress Analysis of Soybean HD-ZIP IV Transcription Factors
items.ai_summary: Homeodomain-leucine zipper transcription factors play vital roles in plant growth and environmental stress responses. This study characterized soybean HD-ZIP IV candidates through domain screening, genomic mapping, phylogenetic comparisons, and expression analyses. A domain audit identified 29 candidates with group IV patterns distributed across 15 chromosomes. Evolutionary analysis of candidate pairs revealed Ka/Ks ratios consistently below 1.0, pointing to purifying selection constraints. Co-expression networks and secondary cold-stress expression data further highlighted specific candidate genes responding to low temperatures. These insights establish a foundation for future functional studies on soybean cold tolerance and gene regulation mechanisms.
flow: Perform domain screening and genomic mapping to identify soybean HD-ZIP gene candidates.
Conduct phylogenetic comparisons and evolutionary analyses, including Ka/Ks ratio calculations.
Construct co-expression networks and analyze secondary expression data under cold-stress conditions.

items.title: Novel risk models based on screening history results and timing of lung cancer diagnosis: Post hoc analysis of the National Lung Cancer Screening Trial
items.summary: by Sofia A. Haddan, Asim Waqas, Ghulam Rasool, Matthew B. Schabath Background Our group previously reported that lung cancer (LC) screening history results and subsequent timing of diagnosis are associated with significant differences in survival outcomes. As a follow-up study, we sought to develop novel personalized risk models that considered screening history for incidence cancers, interval LCs, and prevalence LCs. Methods Using data from the CT-arm of the NLST, four independent case-control analyses were conducted to develop parsimonious risk models. Controls (n = 26,038) were those never diagnosed with LC. The four LC case groups were 270 prevalence LCs, 44 interval LCs, 206 screen-detected LCs (SDLCs) that had a baseline positive screen, and 164 SDLCs that had a baseline negative screen.
items.author: Sofia A. Haddan, Asim Waqas, Ghulam Rasool et al.

items.title: Cluster analysis of high-cost patients in Japan: A longitudinal study using health insurance data
items.summary: by Yoko Matsuo, Keita Yamauchi This study aimed to identify distinct patterns of medical expenditure trajectories among high-cost patients in Japan and characterise the identified groups using diagnostic and health check-up data, including laboratory test results. This retrospective study analysed data from 190,190 high-cost patients (top 5% of annual medical expenditure in fiscal year 2021) in the Japanese JMDC Claims Database. Five-year healthcare expenditure trajectories were classified using K-means clustering. The resulting clusters were characterised according to demographic characteristics, disease patterns, hospitalisation rates, and health check-up data. Eighteen clusters were identified and further grouped into four descriptive types of expenditure trajectory.
items.author: Yoko Matsuo, Keita Yamauchi

items.title: National macro-surveillance of overweight and obesity in India, Bangladesh, and Nepal: A systematic review of global versus Asian BMI thresholds and associated factors
items.summary: by Rameshwor Parajuli, Wilna Oldewage-Theron, Surya Raj Niraula Introduction Evaluating how global versus Asian-specific body mass index (BMI) thresholds impact macro-level population surveillance is essential for addressing South Asia’s changing epidemiological landscape. We systematically synthesized the prevalence of overweight and obesity and identified significant associated factors across India, Bangladesh, and Nepal to compare the diagnostic impact of these distinct BMI criteria. Materials and methods Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched electronic databases including PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ), Google Scholar, and Index Medicus for the South-East Asia Region (IMSEAR) for peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2026 utilizing nationally representative datasets from 2011 onward.
items.author: Rameshwor Parajuli, Wilna Oldewage-Theron, Surya Raj Niraula

items.title: Neurodevelopment among children under five years with sickle cell disease in Eastern Uganda: A propensity score analysis
items.summary: by Bernard Maumbe, David Mukunya, Brendah Nambozo, Faith Oguttu, Julian Abeso, Sarah Mutonyi, Joel Okwir, Milton W. Musaba, Susan Lunyolo, Henry K. Nabudere, Lawrence Ssegawa, Deogratias Munube, Sarah Kiguli, Peter Olupot-Olupot Aim We compared neurodevelopment among children under-five years with and without sickle cell disease in eastern Uganda. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study between March and September 2025 at the pediatric sickle cell clinic of Mbale Regional Referral Hospital. We included 350 children under five years (117 with sickle cell disease and 233 without sickle cell disease). The primary outcome was neurodevelopment assessed using the Malawi Development Assessment Tool.
items.author: Bernard Maumbe, David Mukunya, Brendah Nambozo et al.

items.title: Assessing Condylar hyperplasia management outcomes using semi-automatic segmentation methods: A reliability study
items.summary: by Karla Carpio Horta, Nishant Kharidehal, Nathalia Carolina Fernandes Fagundes, Andreu Puigdollers Pérez, Rodrigo Fariña, Manuel Lagravère, Silvia Gianoni-Capenakas Objectives To assess the reliability of two condylar segmentation methods in patients with Unilateral Condylar Hyperplasia (UCH) treated with proportional condylectomy. Methods A sample of 10 patients with UCH who underwent proportional condylectomy was randomly selected from a private practice. Landmarks were defined and volumetric measurements were performed from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) from affected (n = 10) and non-affected sides (n = 10), as well as before and after proportional condylectomy. Condyles were segmented using two methods: method SN (sigmoid notch method) and method ML (mandibular lingula method).
items.author: Karla Carpio Horta, Nishant Kharidehal, Nathalia Carolina Fernandes Fagundes et al.

items.title: LightTeaNet: SeparableConv-based lightweight CNN with Grad-CAM explainability for tea leaf disease identification
items.summary: by Md Rifat Sarker, Jonayed Al-Faruk, Kaniz Fatema, Joyonta Das, Md. Shahabuddin Saju, Ozifatun Jannat Akhi Global tea production, valued at USD 25.6 billion in 2024, faces annual yield losses of approximately 20% due to foliar diseases, yet existing deep learning-based detection systems remain impractical for real-world deployment due to prohibitive computational requirements and limited interpretability. This paper presents a purpose-built lightweight convolutional neural network architecture for four-class tea leaf disease classification (Brown Blight, Red Rust, Red Spider Mite, and Healthy Leaves) that achieves an exceptional balance between classification accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed model leverages depthwise separable convolutions across four progressive feature extraction blocks, integrated with Batch Normalization, Global Average Pooling, and Dropout regularization to minimize parameter count while maintaining discriminative feature learning.
items.author: Md Rifat Sarker, Jonayed Al-Faruk, Kaniz Fatema et al.

items.title: Climate variability and dysentery morbidity in Gambella Region, Ethiopia: A retrospective ecological time-series analysis, 2012–2021
items.summary: by Geteneh Moges Assefa Background Evidence on meteorological variability and dysentery morbidity in Ethiopia remains limited. We examined associations between monthly temperature, rainfall, relative humidity and surveillance-reported dysentery in three Gambella woredas. Methods A separate 1992–2021 meteorological series provided descriptive climatic context. This retrospective ecological time-series study linked monthly surveillance and meteorological data from September 2012 to December 2021. Negative binomial candidate models evaluated exposures at lags of 0–2 months using a common dataset of 330 woreda-month observations. Models included a population offset, woreda fixed effects, month-of-year indicators and a smooth temporal trend. The selected model used natural cubic splines for same-month exposures.
items.author: Geteneh Moges Assefa

items.title: Preclinical safety evaluation of Vernolac, a commercially available polyherbal nutraceutical comprising Vernonia zeylanica, Nigella sativa, Hemidesmus indicus, Smilax glabra, and Leucas zeylanica, in Wistar rats
items.summary: by Shalini Kaushalya Wijerathne, Oshadi V. Epitawala Arachchige, Sandani De Vass Gunawardane, Ashein Kothalawala, Tharindu Lakmal Dissanayake, Gayani Ranaweera, Arumugam Murugananthan, Prasanna Galhena, Kanishka Senathilake, Sameera R. Samarakoon Vernolac is a commercially available polyherbal formulation comprising Vernonia zeylanica aerial parts, Nigella sativa seeds, Hemidesmus indicus roots, Smilax glabra rhizome, and Leucas zeylanica aerial parts. Although previous in vitro studies have demonstrated the anticancer potential of Vernolac and its active ingredients, safety data are available only for some of the plant ingredients of Vernolac. In the present study, acute and 28-day repeat-dose toxicity of Vernolac were evaluated in Wistar rats in accordance with OECD guidelines 420 and 407, respectively.
items.author: Shalini Kaushalya Wijerathne, Oshadi V. Epitawala Arachchige, Sandani De Vass Gunawardane et al.

items.title: Study on the rising trend of groundwater levels in Beijing and its impact on underground space
items.summary: by Hongli Mu, Yanlin Li, Shiqing Wang, Han Zhu Most large and medium-sized cities in China are water-deficient. Long-term overexploitation of groundwater has led to the deterioration of the urban geo-environment, whereas recent measures such as ecological water replenishment and groundwater abstraction control have substantially alleviated this trend. However, groundwater level rise may also cause damage to underground space and affect the development and utilization of underground space resources. Taking the Beijing Plain as an example, this study investigates the trend and patterns of urban groundwater level rise from 2019 to 2025, as well as its impact on the development and utilization of underground space.
items.author: Hongli Mu, Yanlin Li, Shiqing Wang et al.

items.title: A Multivariate Empirical (MVE) simulation approach to modeling sunflower yield risk and productivity under alternative farming practices in Tanzania
items.summary: by Ibrahim L. Kadigi, Lekumok Kironyi Increasing domestic sunflower ( Helianthus annuus L.) production is important to Tanzania’s efforts to reduce edible oil imports and improve smallholder livelihoods. Yet yields remain low and vary considerably among production systems. This study used a Multivariate Empirical (MVE) model within a Monte Carlo simulation framework to examine yield distributions and production risk under six combinations of seed and fertilizer use. We obtained nationally representative household data from the 2019/20 National Sample Census of Agriculture. The systems comprised local seed with no fertilizer (LS_F0), organic fertilizer (LS_F1), or inorganic fertilizer (LS_F2), and improved seed with no fertilizer (IMS_F0), organic fertilizer (IMS_F1), or inorganic fertilizer (IMS_F2).

items.title: Misinformation-based preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar: A cross-sectional study
items.summary: by Win Min Thit, Seung Chun Paek, Mark Stephan Felix, Francois Rene Lamy Widespread misinformation influenced public understanding of disease risk and preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in low-resource and conflict-affected settings such as Myanmar. Although preventive behaviors were generally protective, some actions driven by misinformation may have been ineffective or harmful. Evidence on determinants of misinformation-based preventive behaviors remained limited. This study aimed to examine associations between misinformation-based preventive behaviors (MPB) and sociodemographic characteristics, information sources, social media use, and health belief factors in Myanmar. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among adults residing in Myanmar, with data collected between March and May 2024.
items.author: Win Min Thit, Seung Chun Paek, Mark Stephan Felix et al.

items.title: A benchmark for elevator fault diagnosis: Multi-level tasks from perception to diagnostic reasoning
items.summary: by Xinda Wang, Haozhe Sun, Junjie Huang, Qiang Zhang Elevator fault diagnosis is a safety-critical problem that requires capabilities beyond isolated fault classification, including knowledge grounding and structured reasoning for maintenance support. In this work, we present a benchmark for elevator fault diagnosis and organize evaluation into three complementary task groups: (A) sensor-based fault detection and classification, (B) taxonomy-grounded fault classification and cause identification, and (C) reasoning with incomplete or constrained information. To enable reproducible comparison across heterogeneous model families, we standardize task definitions, input/output formats, and scoring protocols and report component-level predictive metrics. Experiments across representative language models show task-dependent performance: higher performance on one task does not necessarily transfer to another.
items.author: Xinda Wang, Haozhe Sun, Junjie Huang et al.

items.title: From keypoints to classifications: A SHAP-driven TabPFN framework for forward head posture screening
items.summary: by Siyu Liang, Ziyi Wang Forward Head Posture (FHP) is a prevalent postural abnormality among adolescents, linked to musculoskeletal imbalances and long-term health risks. To investigate its prevalence and develop a research-stage screening framework, we conducted a large-scale population study involving 1,577 Chinese adolescents, recruited for the screening and assessment of FHP. Building on this cohort, we propose an end-to-end predictive framework that integrates human pose estimation with tabular machine learning. RTMPose was used to extract key anatomical landmarks from side-view images, followed by the computational derivation of seven predefined, anatomy-informed posture features. A TabPFN classifier trained on these features achieved an F1 score of 82.46% and an AUC of 0.837.
items.author: Siyu Liang, Ziyi Wang

items.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of Jordanian mothers regarding acute gastroenteritis in children
items.summary: by Mahdi Ahmad Al-Shboul, Ali Mohammad Ahmad, Mohammad Tayseer Khashroom, Sara Najeh Almugheed, Abdulrahman Emad Alramahi, Zainab Maref Al-Zoubi, Dana Hasan Al-Essa, Razan Mathhar Namir Purpose This study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and reported practices of mothers living in Jordan regarding childhood acute gastroenteritis and to identify factors associated with poor knowledge, poor practice, lack of oral rehydration solution (ORS) awareness, and antibiotic use without medical consultation. Methods An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 730 mothers living in Jordan using a structured Arabic-language questionnaire. Participants were recruited through paediatric hospital settings and social media using convenience sampling.
items.author: Mahdi Ahmad Al-Shboul, Ali Mohammad Ahmad, Mohammad Tayseer Khashroom et al.

items.title: Evaluation and strategy provision to promote the indicators of Integrated Geriatric Care Program in Yazd County: A Participatory Action Research
items.summary: by Neda Sadat Nazaripanah, Haidar Nadrian, Neda Gilani, Mina Hashemiparast, Amirhossein Zebhi Background The growing aging population challenges healthcare systems worldwide, emphasizing the need for integrated geriatric care and continuous evaluation to improve key program indicators. This study aimed to evaluate and provide strategies to promote indicators of the Integrated Geriatric Care Program (IGCP) in Yazd County. Methods A Participatory Action Research (PAR) study with a concurrent mixed-methods design was conducted in Yazd, Iran, from January 2023 to August 2024. The study was carried out in six sequential steps within two action research cycles: (1) problem identification, (2) planning, (3) implementation of the Proposed Intervention Plan (PIP), 4) evaluating and revising the PIP, 5) implementation of the Modified Proposed Intervention Plan (MPIP), and 6) evaluation of the MPIP.
items.author: Neda Sadat Nazaripanah, Haidar Nadrian, Neda Gilani et al.

items.title: DTCN-RevIN: A Densely Temporal Causal Network with reversible instance normalization for enhanced weather forecasting via multi-scale feature integration
items.summary: by Xixiang Yin, Sheng Shu, Minglei Yuan Accurate weather forecasting is of paramount importance for disaster prevention, agriculture, and resource management, yet traditional Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) systems such as the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model face inherent limitations in temporal resolution and computational efficiency when capturing rapidly evolving atmospheric dynamics. Meanwhile, existing deep learning approaches—including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN), and Transformers—struggle with long-range temporal dependencies, distribution shift, and scalability. To address these challenges, this study proposes the Densely Temporal Causal Network with Reversible Instance Normalization (DTCN), a deep learning architecture that combines: (1) causal dilated convolutions for efficient temporal modeling, (2) dense inter-layer connections for enhanced feature propagation, (3) multi-scale feature integration, and critically, (4) RevIN standardization to address distribution shift in meteorological time series.
items.author: Xixiang Yin, Sheng Shu, Minglei Yuan

items.title: Multidisciplinary care models for managing pregnancies complicated with chronic diseases: A systematic review
items.summary: by Gayani Shashikala Amarasinghe, Sucharitha Rangi Weerasuriya, Christina Malatzky, Sanjeewa Kularatna, William Parsonage Multidisciplinary care is a key recommendation for the management of complicated pregnancies in contemporary obstetrics, but how to implement it in the real world remains unclear and poorly supported by research evidence. This systematic review describes the characteristics and outcomes of multidisciplinary care models for managing pregnancies complicated with chronic diseases. PubMed/Medline, Embase, and CINAHL databases were searched for relevant studies published between January 2013 and January 2026. Studies were included if they described a multidisciplinary care model in which multiple clinical disciplines interacted during pregnancy. Reporting quality was assessed with the TIDieR checklist.
items.author: Gayani Shashikala Amarasinghe, Sucharitha Rangi Weerasuriya, Christina Malatzky et al.

items.title: Exploring the impact of perceived value on cultural communication willingness during visits to folklore museums: An analysis based on LDA and fsQCA
items.summary: by Yu Wen, Kexin Xu, Xiaoxia Li The synergistic development of culture and tourism is an important driver of global economic growth. As key venues that bear collective memory and sustain cultural roots, folklore museums have assumed an increasingly prominent role in cultural communication and identity formation amid evolving social demands and a globalized context of national cultural identity. However, existing research has yet to fully elucidate the complex mechanisms by which perceived value in the folklore museum context shapes visitors’ willingness for cultural communication. Grounded in complexity theory, this study develops a configurational analysis framework linking perceived value, satisfaction, and cultural communication willingness.
items.author: Yu Wen, Kexin Xu, Xiaoxia Li

items.title: Calibration algorithm for hybrid solar-blind ultraviolet detectors for discharge detection of high-voltage electrical equipment
items.summary: by Shideng Zhu, Chuang Wang, Yuanjun Wang, Baolong Liu The solar-blind ultraviolet technology mainly utilizes the “solar-blind” characteristics of the mid ultraviolet region for detection, which is usually not affected by sunlight interference. However, the ultraviolet spectrum has a wide range and may overlap with other spectra such as near ultraviolet or visible light. The cross interference caused by spectral overlap reduces the accuracy of discharge detection for high-voltage electrical equipment. For this purpose, a hybrid solar-blind UV detector calibration algorithm was designed to optimize discharge detection results and improve detection accuracy.
items.author: Shideng Zhu, Chuang Wang, Yuanjun Wang et al.

items.title: Characterization of meningococcal disease outbreaks in the United States, 2014–2019
items.summary: by Gabrielle A. Cooper, Nicole E. Brown, Amy B. Rubis, How Yi Chang, Caelin Cubenas, Daya Marasini, Adam Retchless, Shalabh Sharma, Sarah Meyer, Lucy A. McNamara Background Meningococcal disease, caused by the bacterium Neisseria meningitidis , is a serious bacterial infection that can be fatal or leave survivors with permanent sequelae. Despite decades of declining incidence in the United States (U.S.), meningococcal disease outbreaks are still of public health concern. Methods Meningococcal disease cases reported through the National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System along with additional data provided by jurisdiction health departments were used to identify outbreak-associated cases and public health response measures during 2014–2019.

items.title: Nonideal Absorbers in Hot-Carrier and Hot-Absorber Solar Cells: Losses and Heat Recycling
items.summary: The hot carrier solar cell exhibits a photovoltaic conversion efficiency limit of 85.4%. Among the idealizations necessary to achieve this efficiency, it has traditionally been considered essential that the electrons absorbing sunlight do not end up transferring the captured energy to the crystal lattice. In this work, we argue that such a requirement is not necessary if the absorber is thermally insulated. In our analysis, we also consider the possibility of ohmic losses in the absorber due to finite electrical conductivity. We also demonstrate that such losses, delivered as heat, can be partially recycled into electrical work with an efficiency that is given by the Carnot factor.

items.title: Observation of room-temperature intrinsic antiferroelectricity in van der Waals NbOCl2
items.summary: In recent years, two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectricity has been extensively investigated across a wide range of 2D materials, while intrinsic 2D antiferroelectricity remains exceptionally rare, limiting its implementation in next-generation photonic and electronic devices. Here, we report the observation of room-temperature-stable antiferroelectricity in the layered transition metal oxyhalide NbOCl2, and demonstrate a reversible, stimuli-driven antiferroelectric-to-ferroelectric (AFE-to-FE) phase transition in this material. Second-harmonic generation (SHG) mapping reveals a well-defined stripe-like spatial distribution of SHG intensity across as-grown NbOCl2 flakes spanning thickness from few-layer to bulk-like configurations. This distinctive SHG signature originates from the existence of antiferroelectric phase and the coexistence of antiferroelectric and ferroelectric phases within individual crystals, as evidenced by a combined incident-angle-dependent SHG measurement and Raman spectroscopy.

items.title: Early Season Snowstorm Blankets Sierra Nevada Mountains
items.summary: An early-season storm brought heavy rain to lower elevations in Sacramento and roughly a foot of snow to the Sierra Nevada mountains on November 13, 2026. The severe weather disrupted travel, causing authorities to temporarily close Interstate 80 near Donner Pass and shut down several roads around Yosemite National Park. Ski areas like Mammoth Mountain also reported significant accumulations. NASA's Terra satellite captured imagery showing the stark contrast in snow cover before and after the storm. Following a brief lull, the National Weather Service issued additional winter storm warnings for mid-November, predicting further travel disruptions and potentially massive snow accumulations at higher elevations.

items.title: Materials representations organize transferable supervision for chemical extrapolation
items.summary: Materials discovery often requires chemical extrapolation beyond labeled data. When target compounds contain elements absent from training, which compounds of other elements provide transferable supervision remains unclear. Here we show that, without target-property labels, materials representations rank other elements by the supervision their compounds provide. Engineered descriptors rank them largely by elemental-property similarity, whereas a pretrained crystal-graph encoder ranks them by the geometry of its learned representation. At fixed training-set size, excluding the compounds of the encoder's six top-ranked elements raises formation-energy and bandgap errors by 100-110 meV per atom and 42-85 meV, versus little change for six lower-ranked elements.

items.title: Unpolarized Generalized Parton Distributions of the Nucleon in a Covariant Quark-Diquark Approach
items.summary: We study the unpolarized generalized parton distributions (GPDs) of the nucleon in a covariant quark-diquark approach, in which both scalar and axial-vector diquarks are treated as composite subsystems. Motivated by previous form factor studies, we introduce a vertex correction based on the pion cloud picture as a first exploratory treatment of pion cloud effects at the GPD level, in order to improve the description of $E^q(ξ, x, t)$ and related magnetic observables. At the model input scale, only valence quarks are included. With the vertex correction, the electromagnetic form factors $G_{E, M}$ and the mass form factor $A$ obtained from the Mellin moments of the GPDs agree well with those obtained from direct calculations.
items.author: Hao Zhang, Dongyan Fu, Jiaqi Wang et al.

items.title: Covering the Pauli Observables: Sampling Thresholds and the Design Effect of a Measurement Setting
items.summary: Quantum state tomography and shadow-based estimation rely on measuring Pauli observables. An experiment does not measure them one at a time: it chooses a measurement setting that assigns one of the bases X, Y or Z to each qubit, and a single run in that setting yields estimates of every Pauli observable compatible with it. We say that the setting covers those observables. We determine how many random settings cover a prescribed fraction of all Pauli observables. As the number of settings grows exponentially with the number of qubits, the covered fraction has a sharp threshold at a growth rate of $3^{3/4}$ per qubit, set by the rate-distortion function of covering at zero distortion.
items.author: Kausthubh Chandramouli, Noah Siekierski, Bojko N. Bakalov et al.

items.title: Observation of Exact Mobility-Edge Phases in Two-Dimensional Photonic Quasicrystals
items.summary: Mobility edges, separating localized and extended states in energy, are central to localization physics. While exact mobility edges have been established in several one-dimensional quasiperiodic models, their realization in two dimensions remains largely unexplored. Here, we uncover a general route to exact mobility edges in the two-dimensional Aubry-Andre quasicrystal by introducing auxiliary subsystems. Through isospectral reduction, we reveal a hidden self-dual structure that yields exact mobility-edge conditions, separating extended, localized, and partially localized states in the spectrum. Tailoring the auxiliary structures controls the effective couplings and resulting mobility edge configurations, while auxiliary resonances further support flat-band states. In a decorated Lieb-type quasicrystal, we experimentally realize these predicted phases in photonic waveguide lattices and probe their energy-dependent localization through site-selective quench dynamics.
