items.title: Stationary Quantum Time Series: Spectral Theory of Process Memory and Measurement Records
items.summary: Classical time series analysis converts temporal dependence into structure that can be learned from a single observed trajectory, through stationarity, ergodicity, spectral representation, and finite-memory models. Quantum experiments are naturally time series: every run is a sequence of interventions and outcomes, and the memory of an open system is written in its temporal statistics. However, the classical foundation cannot be translated directly: measuring a process and forgetting the outcome differs from not measuring at all, so no single family of joint probability distributions describes a quantum process. We develop a process-tensor framework for stationary quantum time series and establish its first structural theorems.
items.author: Hai Wang

items.title: Critical--localized reentry under periodic spacer control
items.summary: Tracking a fixed fraction of a quasiperiodic spectrum tests whether repeated critical--localized alternation extends over a nonzero spectral weight. We find such alternation in a matched-dimer chain by varying only the spacer on-site energies and following a fixed interval of integrated-density-of-states (IDS) labels. An exact Bloch-determinant identity links the physical transfer discriminant to the bands of a periodic reference operator. For the golden cell frequency, we prove that, on a common full-measure set of phases and for every finite value of the spacer control, the physical spectrum in the open reference bands is critical, with purely singular-continuous spectrum and zero Lyapunov exponent, while the spectrum strictly outside the bands is pure point, with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions.
items.author: Xin Wang, Pei-Jie Chang, Dong Ruan et al.

items.title: Spectral Engineering of Charge Localization and Work Reliability in Collective Quantum Batteries
items.summary: The performance of a quantum battery depends not only on how much energy it stores, but also on how rapidly useful charge can be restored after work extraction. We show how engineering the reservoir spectrum connects these properties in an interacting collective-spin battery. Interactions separate the Dicke transition frequencies, allowing frequency-selective pumping and loss to control where excitation accumulates and how populations move along the ladder. Analytical results relate the pump-to-loss ratio to charge localization, fluctuations, and extractable work. Two reservoirs producing the same mean charge can nevertheless exhibit markedly different localization and charging times. Under repeated extraction, finite-time recharging also generates correlations between successive work outputs.
items.author: He-Guang Xu, G. D. de Moraes Neto

items.title: QWeaver: Quantum Circuit Cut Workflow with MLIR-based Compiler, Runtime, and Weaver Hybrid Tasks
items.summary: Quantum computers available today are constrained by limited qubit counts and high noise levels, making the direct execution of large quantum circuits infeasible on a single device, and while quantum circuit cutting addresses this by partitioning a large circuit into smaller subcircuits for independent execution, orchestrating the full end-to-end workflow remains a significant programming challenge. In this paper, we present QWeaver, a task-graph-based programming and orchestration workflow framework for quantum circuit cutting that accepts OpenQASM quantum circuits as input and constructs a directed acyclic task graph. In this graph, the Multi-Level Intermediate Representation (MLIR)-based circuit cut is the first task, responsible for analyzing and partitioning the input circuit into executable fragment representations; the generated fragments are then handed to a set of quantum circuit execution tasks that depend on the cut task and can be dispatched concurrently across available quantum backends via the Quantum Intelligent Runtime System (Q-IRIS).
items.author: Narasinga Rao Miniskar, Elaine Wong, Vicente Leyton-Ortega et al.

items.title: Subsystem evolution in the history state formalism
items.summary: We present a relational framework for characterizing the evolution of quantum composite systems, based on the correlations within a history state describing the whole evolution relative to a quantum reference clock. While total system-clock entanglement entropy consistently measures the unitary evolution of the closed global system, a different picture emerges for the reduced state of an open subsystem, whose evolution is generally non-unitary due to environmental coupling. We introduce a general formalism that quantifies open-subsystem dynamics using a subsystem-clock mutual information derived from the history state. We demonstrate that this quantity serves as a consistent quantifier of subsystem evolution with respect to a given clock basis, can be applied to arbitrary dynamics, and reduces to system-time entanglement entropy in the global limit.

items.title: Addressable transversal CCZ gates on almost good quantum LDPC codes and nearly optimal magic state protocols
items.summary: Assuming uniform subfield product expansion, we construct quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes with distances $Ω_ε(N/\log^2N)$ and at least $N^{1-ε}$ individually addressable logical CCZ gates on pairwise disjoint triples of logical qubits, for every fixed $0<ε<1$. With all logical qubits outside these triples initialized to $|0\rangle$, any subset of the corresponding logical CCZ gates can be implemented with a transversal physical CCZ circuit. As applications, we obtain two nearly optimal magic state protocols: CCZ distillation with arbitrarily small overhead exponent $γ\rightarrow 0$ and error suppression of nearly linear order, and a magic state fountain that directly prepares $N^{1-ε}$ encoded CCZ magic states with nearly linear distance $Ω_ε(N/\log^2N)$.
items.author: Shi Jie Samuel Tan, Guanyu Zhu

items.title: Physics-Guided Crystal Structure Elucidation from Powder X-Ray Diffraction with Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
items.summary: Determining unique atomic coordinates from powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) remains challenging because peak overlap, weak scattering from light elements, limited scattering contrast between elements with similar atomic numbers, and experimental noise render the inverse problem underdetermined. Here, we present XCAPE (XRD-Constrained Accelerated Prediction Engine), a crystal structure prediction (CSP) framework that integrates experimentally derived composition, unit cell parameters, space group, and PXRD data into a symmetry-aware evolutionary search. XCAPE explores Wyckoff-site configurations using tailored mutation operations, evaluates candidates by both energetic stability and diffraction agreement, and accelerates geometry optimization using a universal machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP). The framework recovered 71 of 77 database-derived benchmark structures (92.2%) from simulated PXRD patterns and all 12 reference structures from experimental PXRD patterns.
items.author: Yunsung Lim, Seungwoo Hwang, Seungwu Han

items.title: Parity Push Post-Selection with Soft Parity Constraints for Quantum LDPC Codes
items.summary: Post-selection lowers the logical error rate of a quantum error-correcting code by rejecting unreliable shots. For a code with $K$ logical observables, the logical gap, a standard post-selection criterion, involves $2^K$ logical classes, and existing approximations to it suffer from a non-convergence error floor or a shielding effect. We introduce a decoder-agnostic post-selection strategy for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, called parity push post-selection (PPPS), which re-decodes a shot once per logical observable with a push toward the opposite parity. Each push adds one check node and one variable node to the Tanner graph of the detector error model, and we accept a shot only when every re-decoding returns a solution in the original logical class.
items.author: Hong Jun Kim, Gun Sik Min, Seok-Hyung Lee et al.

items.title: Charged Schrödinger blocks in $1+1$ dimensions from the quartic Casimir and endpoint equations
items.summary: We construct charge-two Schrödinger conformal blocks in one spatial dimension, independently of any dynamical realization. We consider ordered vacuum four-point functions of fundamental fields of dimension $1/2$, with homogeneous Schrödinger equations at the earliest and latest insertions and interactions allowed in the intermediate two-particle interval. For reduced blocks analytic in signed spatial coordinates and even under simultaneous spatial inversion, two functions of the time cross-ratio determine the full spatial dependence: the collinear value and a rescaled mixed spatial derivative. An exact Kummer lift, built from confluent hypergeometric functions, gives this reconstruction. An operator identity reduces the quartic Casimir equation, modulo the endpoint equations, to an equivalent coupled system for this pair.
items.author: Hirohiko Shimada

items.title: Gopakumar-Vafa invariants and Mordell-Weil lattices
items.summary: Let $X\to B$ be a Weierstrass fibration with integral fibers from a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold to a del Pezzo surface. For a smooth curve $D\subset B$ with smooth inverse image $Y$, we decompose the moduli fiber of stable sheaves with Euler characteristic one and projected cycle $D$. In fiber degree $k$, its components are indexed by all sections $C$ of $Y\to D$ with $\tfrac12\langle C,C\rangle\leq k$, where $\langle\, ,\,\rangle$ is the Mordell--Weil height pairing. For infinitesimally rigid sections we compute the GV contributions, recovering the $E_8$ theta product over a $(-1)$-curve. We formulate the corresponding conjecture for families of sections.
items.author: Lutian Zhao

items.title: XANES-Guided Molecular Structure Generation via Conditional Diffusion and Forward Spectral Prediction
items.summary: Reconstructing complete molecular structures from X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra remains challenging because the spectra primarily encode local chemical environments, with overlapping contributions from multiple absorbing sites. Here, we develop an inverse-forward framework combining XANES-conditioned diffusion-based molecular structure generation with forward spectral prediction for candidate selection. The inverse model generates atomic species, bond connectivity, and three-dimensional coordinates from C, N, and O K-edge XANES, given only the total atom count without molecular formulas or element-specific atom counts. Combining all three absorption edges substantially improves structural recovery, achieving a best-of-10 exact-match rate of 56.6% across 2,888 test molecules. The generated candidates also reproduce functional groups and structural motifs, achieving a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.951 across 21 categories.
items.author: Yu Fujikata, Teruyasu Mizoguchi

items.title: Fast closed-loop STEM navigation using vision-language models with typed decisions
items.summary: Closed-loop scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), in which each acquired image determines the next field of view and magnification, offers a route to autonomous atomic-scale materials analysis. Such a loop would automate navigation to defects and grain boundaries, a task that has long relied on operator judgment, and would enable systematic analysis of diverse local structures at scale. Realizing it hinges on the decision step, which must translate each acquired image into the next operation both quickly and correctly; yet which decision method can deliver both remains unclear. Here, we isolate this decision step. Using simulated atomic-resolution STEM images of a substitutional W dopant and a grain boundary in monolayer MoS$_2$, where the true target position is known and every method starts from identical conditions, we compared four vision-language models (VLMs) and three decision methods.
items.author: Shuichiro Ozawa, Izumi Takahara, Fumihiko Uesugi et al.

items.title: Structured Extraction of Diffraction Data from Covalent Organic Frameworks
items.summary: Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) is the primary structural evidence for covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and many other materials. Yet decades of measured patterns exist only as images in published figures. Automatic recovery is difficult, because PXRD figures vary widely in format, from a single curve to crowded stacks with labels, insets, and neighboring plots that challenge traditional computer vision. This work presents a pipeline in which a vision large language model (LLM) interprets the layout of each figure, locating the diffraction plot and its curves and sketching a coarse trace of each, while classical computer vision (CV) refines every trace to pixel-level accuracy.
items.author: Shenghan Gao, Zhiling Zheng

items.title: Simultaneous spectral measurement and programmable filtering on a universal silicon photonic chip
items.summary: Spectral measurement and spectral filtering are two fundamental operations in optics, yet they are conventionally implemented using separate optical systems, hindering their simultaneous and programmable operation on a common platform. Here, we demonstrate a universal silicon photonic chip that unifies spectral measurement and programmable filtering within a single integrated architecture. The chip comprises two 8 * 8 programmable unitary transformation circuits interconnected through optical intensity modulators, forming a universal linear optical circuit. In contrast to conventional universal circuits employing equal-length interconnections, we deliberately introduce different optical path lengths between the two unitary circuits. The resulting wavelength-dependent phase evolution provides spectral diversity while preserving the programmability of the universal circuit, enabling parallel spectral measurement and programmable filtering.
items.author: Yangyang Wan, Rui Tang, Kazuhiro Ikeda et al.

items.title: Contact-induced molecular reorganisation in a model Escherichia coli lipid membrane.
items.summary: The nanoscale composition, molecular organisation and mechanics of biological membranes underpins their function for cellular compartmentalisation, signalling, and mechanical integrity. Eukaryotic membranes can readjust their molecular content and structural organisation in response to specific interactions or changes in their environment, including through the formation of more ordered and solid-like nanodomains - lipid rafts. Recent studies have shown that bacterial membranes also possess significant lipid diversity and can form functional microdomains reminiscent of eukaryotic lipid rafts, despite lacking sterols and sphingolipids. In all cases, the role of biochemical interactions between lipids has long been recognized as determinant for the membrane molecular organisation and physical properties.
items.author: Tormena N, Pilizota T, Voïtchovsky K.

items.title: Molecular mechanisms of deposit control additive inhibition by biofuels.
items.summary: Blending biofuels into gasoline can have several environmental and performance benefits. However, high ethanol concentrations are known to reduce the effectiveness of deposit control additives (DCAs) that operate by adsorption onto deposit surfaces. The fundamental physicochemical difference between fossil fuels and biofuels is that the former are mostly non-polar hydrocarbons, while the latter are predominantly oxygen-containing polar species. Here, we use molecular modelling to reveal how the presence of ethanol molecules affects the binding strength of three DCAs with markedly different chemistries to a model carbonaceous deposit from surrogate fuel blends. For a zwitterionic DCA, ethanol forms a structured solvation shell around the charged head-group, which reduces its adsorption free energy on the model deposits by around 75%.
items.author: Corral-Casas C, Gattinoni C, Brewer M, Smith A, Dini D, Ewen JP.

items.title: Matrix materials as functional enablers in metabolite sensing: from mechanistic demands to translational potential.
items.summary: The performance of metabolite sensors is strongly shaped by the physicochemical properties of the matrix that governs analyte transport, interfacial stability, and signal coupling, yet the role of the matrix has largely been overlooked, often being viewed as a passive support rather than an active design parameter. This review analyses how matrix architecture controls sensing behaviour across polymeric, inorganic, carbon-based, and supramolecular material classes, examining mechanistic trade-offs between diffusion and binding, conductivity and biocompatibility, and structural stability and responsiveness in the context of electrochemical, optical, and electrical transduction modes. Particular emphasis is placed on operation in complex biological media, where protein adsorption, ionic fluctuations, mechanical mismatch, and dynamic metabolite flux impose constraints rarely captured in buffered laboratory systems.
items.author: Varga M, Risi G, Stepanova S, Nasehi M, Bahtiyar C, Rousakis E, Witthauer L.

items.title: A mesoporous electrode strategy for probing ions at the electrode-electrolyte interface using in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy.
items.summary: Electrolyte ions present at the electrode-electrolyte interface critically influence electrocatalytic reactions, yet direct, quantitative detection of interfacial ions under operating conditions remains challenging due to dominant bulk electrolyte signals. Here, we present an interface-sensitive soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) approach that enables quantitative tracking of interfacial ion behavior at electrified platinum (Pt) surfaces. Mesoporous Pt films with high surface-area-to-volume ratios were fabricated via soft-templated electrodeposition onto SiN x windows, strongly enhancing the relative contribution of the interfacial electrolyte within nanoscale pores while effectively attenuating signals from the bulk. Using Na + as a model cation, Na K-edge XAS measurements reveal pronounced dependencies of interfacial ion concentration on applied potential, electrolyte pH, and bulk concentration.
items.author: Rodriguez JSD, Larsson A, Deka N, Jorritsma R, Javed H, Kolmeijer K, Cuprija A, Liu W, Barber N, Squires AM, Teschner D, Ghafari A, Chuang CH, Mom RV.

items.title: First-principles prediction of the thermoelectric properties of Sn(S 0.2 Se 0.8 ) alloys.
items.summary: Thermoelectric power is an efficient and flexible technology for improving energy efficiency, but widespread applications require cost-effective and sustainable materials with a high figure of merit zT . Alloying is a common strategy for optimising zT , but predicting and understanding its impact on the material properties is made challenging by the structural disorder. In this work, we develop a practical and rigorous approach to predicting the zT of alloys, by combining first-principles electrical-transport and lattice thermal-conductivity calculations with approximate models for the electron and phonon scattering, and apply it to study the Sn(S 0.2 Se 0.8 ) alloy. We compare predictions obtained by averaging over the full set of unique configurations in a 32-atom supercell with those obtained from special quasi-random structure (SQS) structures with supercell sizes up to 256 atoms.

items.title: Optical Neural Networks Should Be Evaluated by Function, Not Only Physics
items.summary: Optical neural networks (ONNs) are attracting significant attention as alternative platforms for machine learning (ML). In an ONN, an optical module often takes over part of the computation inside a digital ML pipeline. How much of the task does the optical module itself perform, and how much does it contribute to any claimed system-level advantages, such as throughput or energy? This paper offers a simple, function-oriented evaluation methodology. Whatever its internal physics, the optical module appears to the surrounding digital pipeline as a mapping between real-valued tensors. We therefore evaluate it in three steps: (i) define its boundary in the pipeline, as real-valued tensors in and out; (ii) replace it with standard digital modules to identify those that match the optical system's performance on the same task and metric; and (iii) state system-level claims, such as speed or energy, per inference against the performance-matched digital module.
items.author: Shi-Yuan Ma, Xingjian Bai, Ryan Hamerly et al.

items.title: Retinal arterial velocity-proxy waveforms from differential spectral broadening in laser Doppler holography
items.summary: Laser Doppler holography (LDH) records pulsatile spectral broadening in retinal arteries. We compare vessel and local-background measurements to extract a signed differential-broadening waveform, $Δσ$. A minimal Gaussian convolution model motivates quadratic subtraction, and Doppler scaling relates the added width to a characteristic blood velocity. Real arteries show pulsatile waveforms, whereas identically processed imaginary arteries show only low-amplitude fluctuations around zero. We interpret the empirically scaled signal as a velocity proxy for waveform shape and within-vessel changes during a single acquisition under stable conditions.
items.author: Zacharie Auray, Yann Fischer, Olivier Martinache et al.

items.title: Comment on "Exact, nonsingular black holes from a phantom DBI field as primordial dark matter"
items.summary: We demonstrate that the metric and scalar configuration proposed in Ref.~[1] do not satisfy the complete set of field equations of the Dirac-Born-Infeld (DBI) field theory minimally coupled to general relativity on a radial domain containing the event horizon. The physical DBI branch for this gravitational setup terminates outside the event horizon. Thus, the proposed configuration does not describe a black hole solution of that theory.
items.author: Mustapha Azreg-Aïnou, Marco A. A. de Paula

items.title: Cold Magnetized Quark Matter under Compact-Star Conditions
items.summary: We investigate the phase structure of cold magnetized two-flavor quark matter under compact-star conditions within a nonlocal chiral quark model with separable interactions. Electric charge neutrality and beta equilibrium are imposed in order to describe matter under realistic neutron-star conditions, while nonlocality is implemented through a Gaussian form factor. We find that low and moderate magnetic fields reduce the critical chemical potential for chiral symmetry restoration, signaling inverse magnetic catalysis. For stronger magnetic fields, the critical chemical potential becomes nearly independent of the magnetic field strength, Compared with the isospin-symmetric case, the combined effects of charge neutrality and beta equilibrium shift the first-order chiral transition to slightly higher chemical potentials, indicating that compact-star constraints delay the onset of chiral symmetry restoration.
items.author: S. A. Ferraris, J. P. Carlomagno, G. A. Contrera et al.

items.title: Fuzzy Dark Matter as a diffractive barrier: Wave-optics Signatures of Ultralight Fields on Lensed Gravitational Waves
items.summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) propagate through the universe from sources at high redshift, experiencing the gravitational fields of the intervening matter distribution. Halos composed of ultralight dark matter (ULDM) contain strong density fluctuations, reflecting the interference pattern in the field distribution of the ultralight bosons. In the wave-optics regime, ULDM fluctuations act as a diffractive grating, imprinting frequency-dependent modulations of GWs, in addition to magnification and other gravitational lensing effects. Since lensing depends on the projected surface density, we derive its approximate probability distribution and show how it departs from a Gaussian distribution depending on the halo profile and coherence length.
items.author: Manish Tamta, Han Gil Choi, Diego Blas et al.

items.title: Perspective on Proton Transversity Distribution Functions
items.summary: Using available information on proton tensor charges and constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD), Ansaetze are introduced for hadron-scale in-proton valence-quark transversity distributions functions (DFs). The concept of a QCD effective charge, which defines an evolution scheme for collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions that is all-orders exact, is then used to deliver predictions for the $x$-dependence of these DFs at the scale $ζ_{2} = 2\,$GeV. Although the approach is largely algebraic, its predictions remain viable after comparisons with results obtained using computationally intensive methods. Thus, given the scarcity of data that can today be used for inference of proton transversity DFs, it may be worth using the results herein to inform and constrain related experiments and phenomenological fits.
items.author: Ke-Xin Zeng, Peng Cheng, Yang Yu et al.

items.title: Machine-learned acceleration of earthquake sequence simulations
items.summary: Earthquake sequence simulations involve slow interseismic processes and rapid dynamic ruptures. During interseismic periods, a numerical solver can take large time steps efficiently. During seismic periods, in contrast, the solver must drastically reduce the time step, and elastodynamic wave-mediated memory effects become significant; long-term simulations are therefore computationally expensive. We investigate the use of neural operators to accelerate earthquake sequence simulations. We train a Fourier neural operator (FNO) on data from high-fidelity, fully dynamic simulations to learn a jump map that advances the system state from before a seismic rupture to after it. We propose a hybrid modeling framework in which a conventional quasi-dynamic solver simulates the slow interseismic evolution, and the trained FNO replaces the solver during the computationally intensive seismic periods with wave-mediated inertial effects.
items.author: Reo Yanagi, Taeho Kim, Kaushik Bhattacharya et al.

items.title: NASA Launches Student Challenge on Space Nuclear Power
items.summary: NASA has initiated the Power to Explore Student Challenge, inviting students from kindergarten through 12th grade across the United States to explore space nuclear power systems. Participants are tasked with creating an original illustration depicting a nuclear-powered lunar base and writing a 200-word essay about a personal superpower that would help the mission. The competition aims to spark interest in STEM and showcase how nuclear energy can support sustainable lunar exploration by keeping instruments warm and enabling operations in shadowed polar regions. Submissions are open until March 1, 2027. Category winners will receive a trip to NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland, and all entrants will receive a digital certificate and an invitation to a virtual event with NASA experts.

items.title: Fe$^{2+}$:forsterite Qubit System
items.summary: Quantum Computing uses quantum mechanical phenomena, such as superposition and entanglement of quantum bits (qubits), to represent and manipulate information in multidimensional state spaces. This approach allows complex mathematical functions to be executed simultaneously rather than sequentially, making them much more efficient than classical computers. However, current quantum computers suffer from quantum decoherence, where small changes to their environment, such as thermal fluctuations and vibrations, affect the systems' fragile states. The goal of this study is to discuss the functionality of a proposed Fe$^{2+}$:forsterite qubit system by solving the unitary time-evolution of a quantum state vector for the system's Hamiltonian, using known axial and traverse anisotropy terms at temperatures up to 10 K.
items.author: Dishaanth S. Pillai, G. M. Wysin

items.title: Global NASA Space Apps Challenge Sets New Participation Records
items.summary: NASA's annual Space Apps Challenge achieved record-breaking participation, drawing 181,835 registered individuals across 593 global events. The two-day hackathon challenges participants to use NASA's open data and datasets from 17 international space agency partners to address real-world problems regarding Earth science and space exploration. Working in teams organized by local volunteers, participants develop projects and submit them before the deadline to compete for global awards. This year marked the fifth consecutive year of increased turnout, demonstrating the growing reach of the initiative since its inception in 2012.

items.title: Application of Pretrained Universal Machine Learning Force-Fields for Phase Transitions Prediction in ZrO2
items.summary: Pretrained universal machine-learning force fields can reduce the cost of finite-temperature molecular dynamics relative to density functional theory. However, most benchmarks test only static properties and do not assess whether these models reproduce the correct phase-transition sequence. Here, we benchmark ten open-source universal machine-learning force fields for zirconia (ZrO$_2$) using phonon dispersion calculations and variable-cell isothermal-isobaric molecular dynamics. Zirconia is a useful test because it has three thermodynamically stable crystalline phases prior to melting, following the sequence monoclinic-tetragonal-cubic. Four models reproduce this sequence: 7net-l3i5, MatterSim-v1.0.0-1M, MACE-mpa, and MACE-D3. Models with orthorhombic-tetragonal energy errors above about 10 meV/atom (7net-0, CHGNet, and MACE) instead produce an orthorhombic intermediate and predict monoclinic-orthorhombic-tetragonal-cubic-liquid upon heating.
items.author: Rajan Khadka, Axel van de Walle, Patrick Tepesch

items.title: The production of lepton pairs in heavy-ion collisions at SPS and RHIC energies
items.summary: We perform a quantitative study of dilepton production and elliptic flow in In+In collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=17.3$ GeV and isobar collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV, concentrating on the low and intermediate invariant mass regions. The medium evolution is simulated event-by-event with the multistage iEBE-MUSIC framework, and the electromagnetic emission combines for the first time quark-gluon plasma (QGP) emission calculated at next-to-leading order (NLO) in the strong coupling with in-medium radiation calculated with hadronic many-body theory. Freeze-out and surviving primordial $ρ$ decays are also included. The calculations are compared with the high-precision dimuon spectra measured by the NA60 Collaboration, and with STAR preliminary measurements of dielectron spectra and elliptic flow.
items.author: Xiang-Yu Wu, Han Gao, Charles Gale et al.

items.title: NASA Space Biology Program Launches Digital AVATAR Challenge
items.summary: NASA's Biological and Physical Sciences Division has introduced the BPS Digital AVATAR Challenge, offering $150,000 in total prizes. The challenge invites researchers to apply computational digital twin technologies to model how an astronaut bone marrow chip responds to spaceflight stressors. Following the recent return of organ-on-a-chip devices from the Artemis II mission, this new competition seeks innovative frameworks capable of processing multi-modal datasets to simulate personalized health outcomes, immune responses, and bone marrow reactions. Competitors must design models that distinguish individual crew member effects from shared responses and allow for continuous updates with new empirical data. Registration is open, and submissions close on February 12, 2027.

items.title: NASA's Chandra Observatory Converts Star Data Into Sound
items.summary: NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory and other space telescopes have released a new album of data turned into audio, known as sonifications, featuring active star-forming regions. By translating information captured by telescopes like Hubble and the James Webb Space Telescope into musical pitches, tones, and textures, astronomers offer a new way to explore stellar birth and the lifecycle of stars. The release highlights four distinct regions: the starburst galaxy Messier 82, the Orion Nebula, the Carina Nebula's Cosmic Cliffs, and the Rho Ophiuchi star-forming cloud. Each track maps different wavelengths of light—such as X-rays, optical, and infrared—to specific sounds to highlight elements like hot gas, dense dust, and energetic infant stars.

items.title: Quantum Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport in spacetime through spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and spatiotemporal states
items.summary: Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport is a mathematical framework that determines the most efficient way to transform one probability distribution into another while minimizing a given cost function. Its central constructions include the Wasserstein distances, which quantify the space of probability distributions, and dual formulations that link to convex analysis. Its standard quantum generalization replaces probability distributions with density operators and cost function with positive semidefinite cost operator, which should be regarded as spatial quantum optimal transport. In this work, we propose the quantum optimal transport problem in spacetime through the spatiotemporal phase-space Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distribution and spatiotemporal states and through spatiotemporal state.
items.author: Zhian Jia

items.title: Folded out-of-time-order correlators in double-scaled SYK
items.summary: Harlow and Zhao arXiv:2607.14215 have identified ``anti-scrambling'' as a characteristic signature of cosmological horizons in de Sitter space, and proposed that it can be realized in a quantum system with bounded energy by Euclidean time ``folding" of out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs). We implement this prescription in the DSSYK model. We use arXiv:2303.03474 to define an infinite-temperature ($β=0$) DSSYK OTOC that in the semiclassical limit of small values of the double-scaling parameter $λ$ reproduces the usual AdS eikonal shockwave behavior with its characteristic time delay, and then apply the Harlow-Zhao fold with the ``fake'' DSSYK inverse temperature $β_f$ playing the role of $β$.
items.author: Joseph D. Lykken, Madeline Mooney, Maria Spiropulu

items.title: Dynamics of a spinning body with scalar multipoles
items.summary: We construct an effective worldline action for a spinning compact object in theories of gravity with massless, non-minimally coupled scalar fields. To this end, we generalize the standard skeletonized approach used in General Relativity to model the stress-energy tensor of a small body in a background spacetime, dressing its multipolar structure with the scalar field. Within a pole-dipole approximation, we derive a modified set of Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations of motion for the spinning body, together with the field equations for the scalar field and the metric. We consider both parity-even and parity-odd scalars. We tailor this formalism to model the evolution of asymmetric binaries, such as Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs), by systematically expanding the relevant equations in powers of the binary mass ratio and deriving the dynamics up to first post-adiabatic (1PA) order, along with the self-force equations needed to determine the particle's acceleration.
items.author: Jacopo Lestingi, Thomas P. Sotiriou, Andrew Spiers et al.

items.title: SpaceX Dragon Prepares for Space Station Departure and Return to Earth
items.summary: A SpaceX Dragon spacecraft is scheduled to depart the International Space Station, carrying thousands of pounds of scientific research samples and hardware back to Earth. The mission includes returning specialized cargo such as a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel construct used for studying cardiovascular aging, frozen tumor organoids for cancer research, microbial samples, and a lighting system tested for supporting astronaut sleep. Following commands from ground controllers in California, the spacecraft is slated to undock from the Harmony module and target a splashdown off the coast of California, pending weather conditions.

items.title: ER=EPR and IMP wormholes in quantum gravity
items.summary: We analyze and refine the ER=EPR conjecture by studying IMP (Isenberg, Mazzeo and Pollack \cite{Isenberg:2001qe}) wormholes in QFT and quantum gravity, in the AdS/CFT context. IMP wormholes are solutions to the Einstein equations constructed from another general solution of Einstein's equations by gluing a handle on a Cauchy slice with a constant mean curvature, so that the initial data on the slice does not change in the regions away from the handle. This is made possible by using what is called the conformal method. This same method also enables one to recover a well defined perturbation theory in quantum gravity, and particularly for asymptotically AdS spacetimes \cite{Witten:2022xxp}.
items.author: Eyoab Bahiru

items.title: Twist-4 QCD Factorization for One-Point Correlators at Next-to-Leading Order in Electron-Ion Collisions
items.summary: Energy and charge correlators have emerged as powerful, infrared- and collinear-safe (IRC-safe) observables for probing QCD dynamics in the vacuum, established within the leading-twist factorization formalism. However, their IRC safety and factorization properties in a nuclear medium, where higher-twist contributions are critically enhanced, remain unproven. In this letter, we present the first proof of next-to-leading order QCD factorization for one-point energy and charge correlators (OPEC and OPCC) in electron-ion collisions at twist-4. Working within the higher-twist expansion framework, we calculate the twist-4 power corrections to the angular widths of the OPEC and OPCC, and explicitly demonstrate that the IRC singularities cancel and fragmentation-function dependence reduces to momentum and charge moments for final-state medium-enhanced observables in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering.
items.author: Omar Elgedawy, Zhong-Bo Kang, Hongxi Xing

items.title: Scalar/axion Wormholes and Boundary Conditions in Gravitational Path Integrals
items.summary: Recent work noted that whether or not a given class of spacetime wormholes contributes to the gravitational path integral can depend strongly on the choice of boundary conditions. In particular, for asymptotically-AdS scalar/axion wormholes with spherical boundaries it was suggested that there are regimes where the same wormhole contributes to a Euclidean low-energy effective field theory computation of the partition function $Z_N$ defined by imposing Neumann boundary conditions on the scalar/axion field, while it fails to contribute to a corresponding partition function $Z_D$ defined by imposing Dirichlet boundary conditions on this field. Here we investigate toy models of related wormholes associated with JT gravity coupled to a scalar field, asymptotically-AdS gravity coupled to an axion/scalar with toroidal boundary conditions, and asymptotically flat gravity coupled to an axion/scalar.
items.author: Jason Hallsten, Jesse Held, Zhenyu Heng et al.

items.title: Capturing Ultralight Dark Matter Around Black Holes
items.summary: Ultralight dark matter (DM) can form hydrogen-like bound states around black holes (BHs), that can be perturbatively described at small gravitational fine-structure constant alpha=G*M*mu<<1, where M and mu are the masses of the BH and the DM scalar, respectively. We show that self-interactions lead to the formation of a 2p-halo around a Schwarzschild BH, with the final cloud density as high as 10^5 times the background density. We also show that for the case of a Kerr BH with a superradiant cloud, the decay of the 211 state can populate the ground state faster than it decays into the BH.
items.author: Salvatore Bottaro, Viktor Firsov, Gilad Perez et al.

items.title: Collective Superconducting-Qubit Interfaces for Microwave-to-Optical Quantum Transduction
items.summary: Microwave-to-optical quantum transduction is essential for connecting superconducting quantum processors through optical networks. Mechanically mediated transducers, however, remain limited by weak electromechanical coupling, dissipation, and added noise. In this work, we study a transducer in which an ensemble of superconducting qubits couples collectively to a shared optomechanical resonator. For weak signals, we show that ensemble size and optical pump strength together set the conversion efficiency, added noise, and bandwidth, with pump heating limiting efficiency to a finite optimal pump strength. Near half excitation, the collective coupling grows nearly linearly with ensemble size, accelerating transfer of an excitation into the mechanics.
items.author: Nicolas Dirnegger, Matthew Guibord, William Munizzi et al.

items.title: Constructing Two-Dimensional Conformal Field Theories with Large Primary Gaps
items.summary: Researchers have built the first explicit examples of compact unitary bosonic full conformal field theories in two dimensions possessing a unique vacuum and an all-spin Virasoro-primary gap greater than two. By employing asymmetric orbifolds of lattice CFTs derived from even unimodular lattices, the team ensured that no charged state falls beneath the target gap. The methodology applies gauged symmetries combining orthogonal actions and independent sign reversals, which are proven to be anomaly-free. Analyzing untwisted spectra and twisted sectors allowed the exact calculation of gaps, yielding infinite families of models with specific gap sizes derived from ternary quadratic-residue codes and Barnes-Wall lattices.
items.author: Ziming Ji, Jiahua Tian
items.original_title: CFTs with Large Virasoro Primary Gaps
items.original_summary: We construct the first explicit examples of compact unitary bosonic full conformal field theories (CFTs) in two dimensions with a unique vacuum and an all-spin Virasoro-primary gap greater than two. Our constructions use asymmetric orbifolds of lattice CFTs built from even unimodular lattices of sufficiently large minimum norm, ensuring that no charged state lies below the desired gap. The gauged symmetries combine a common orthogonal action on the left- and right-moving currents with independent sign reversals; the latter project out the dimension-two scalar primary $\sum_i J_L^iJ_R^i$ that survives when the symmetry acts identically on both chiral halves. We prove that the gauging is anomaly-free and determine the exact gaps by analyzing the invariant untwisted spectrum and all twisted sectors.

items.title: Ambient SFT: Preventing Overfitting in Language Models via Temperature Matching
items.summary: Supervised fine-tuning of autoregressive language models is frequently limited by small dataset sizes, which can cause overfitting and catastrophic forgetting. To counter this, researchers developed Ambient SFT, a framework that uses a frozen pre-trained model as a noisy teacher. By requiring the post-training model's high-temperature conditional distributions to match those of the pre-trained model, the approach leverages imperfect predictions to augment the fine-tuning data. A temperature hyperparameter governs how much trust is placed in the pre-trained model. Experiments show that this technique improves performance across instruction-tuning, reasoning, and domain adaptation, achieving up to a 21 percent average relative improvement over standard fine-tuning methods.
items.author: Giannis Daras, Marios Papachristou, Adam Klivans et al.
items.original_title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
items.original_summary: Collecting large-scale, diverse, and high-quality post-training datasets for autoregressive language models is challenging. Consequently, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is typically applied to datasets significantly smaller than those used for pre-training, which leads to overfitting and the catastrophic forgetting of the tails of the data distribution. To prevent this collapse, we introduce Ambient SFT, a principled framework for leveraging imperfect predictions to augment the fine-tuning set. In our method, a "frozen" version of the pre-trained model serves as a noisy teacher that the fine-tuned model must match at a coarse level. In particular, we require that the high-temperature versions of the conditional distributions produced by the post-training model should match the high-temperature versions of the pre-training ones.

items.title: Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Applications such as visual accessibility agents and robotics require answering questions about recent video content promptly, over a bounded window of past frames (e.g., the last two minutes). Hybrid vision-language models (VLMs), which interleave attention with linear recurrent layers such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN), are attractive for this setting, but maintaining a sliding window is expensive. The reason is that recurrent layers combine all past frames into a shared state, so expiring old frames normally requires re-running the entire window through the model. We observe that the recurrent update is affine in the state with input-dependent coefficients, so the effect of each frame can be captured as a transformation that composes associatively.
items.author: Rui Ning, Om Chabra, Hari Balakrishnan

items.title: Expressivity of two-dimensional Gaussian fermion tensor network states
items.summary: Tensor network states (TNS) provide a family of efficiently compressed approximations to physically relevant many-body quantum states. An important quantity that characterizes the computational resources required by a TNS is its bond dimension. While in one dimension an area law for the Renyi-0 entropy guarantees an exact matrix product state representation with a bond dimension independent of the system size, an analogous statement does not hold for general states in two dimensions (2D). This leaves open the question of how the expressivity of 2D TNS is related to the entanglement properties of the states they represent. In this work, we focus on two families of 2D translation-invariant Gaussian fermionic states: single-band BCS superconductors and half-filled two-band insulators (including semimetals).
items.author: Pok Man Tam, William Musk, Zhehao Dai

items.title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
items.summary: We present StringQFT as a textbook collection for string constructions of quantum field theory and as infrastructure for AI-assisted theoretical physics. The collection comprises 18 volumes, 190 chapters and 3,795 pages, covering brane probes, brane webs, geometric engineering, F-theory constructions, wrapped M5-branes and exact worldsheet constructions. Its open-book benchmark inventory contains 1,073 items, including 499 with automatic finite-answer checking. For retrieval-augmented generation, it provides 1,371 section records linked to textbook sources and PDF locations, together with a local lexical retriever. Training-data preparation is illustrated by 21 private, source-linked examples. For agents, it exposes 19 calculation tools with specified inputs and finite domains, connecting tool use to textbook derivations.
items.author: Xingyang Yu

items.title: From nonlocal correlations to local symmetry breaking: Asymmetry dynamics of crosscap states
items.summary: Under unitary dynamics preserving a global symmetry, bipartite entanglement typically grows while an initially broken symmetry is locally restored. Here, we show that this conventional scenario can be reversed when symmetry-breaking coherence is initially encoded in long-range entanglement. We investigate this phenomenon in a family of charge deformed crosscap states, characterized by antipodal entangled pairs with tunable entanglement and symmetry breaking. We first characterize their static properties, finding a Page-like entanglement profile and an entanglement asymmetry that vanishes for subsystems smaller than half the system size, but grows logarithmically for larger subsystems. For symmetric subsystems, we also analyze the symmetry-resolved entanglement and investigate how it evolves as the subsystem is continuously deformed away from a symmetric partition.
items.author: Konstantinos Chalas, Pasquale Calabrese, Colin Rylands

items.title: An inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method for constrained convex finite-sum optimization
items.summary: In this paper, we study a class of constrained convex finite-sum optimization problems. In many practical applications, all or some of the constraints are hard constraints that represent imperative requirements. Consequently, any desirable approximate solution must (nearly) satisfy these constraints. Motivated by this, we focus on computing an $ε$-$surely\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ ($ε$-SFSO) solution, in which the constraint violation is deterministically bounded by $ε$, and the expected optimality gap is at most $ε$. While a recently proposed stochastic variance-reduced first-order penalty method can compute an $ε$-SFSO solution, there remains a significant gap between its first-order oracle complexity for computing an $ε$-SFSO solution and that for computing an $ε$-$expected\ feasible\ stochastic\ optimal$ solution, where both the expected constraint violation and the expected optimality gap are bounded by $ε$.
items.author: Zhaosong Lu, Yifeng Xiao

items.title: Complete Cosmological Collider Signatures from Right-handed Neutrino Loops
items.summary: We study the complete cosmological collider (CC) signatures from right-handed neutrino loops with chemical-potential enhancement. These CC signals are induced by the inflaton-right-handed-neutrino interaction and can be extracted in the collinear squeezed configuration, which allows the right-handed-neutrino triangle loop to be factorized into the hard and soft parts. We precisely compute the soft part of the fermion loop for the first time by using the complete mode functions and the full loop integral, and treat the hard part as a tree-level subdiagram. We subtract the large-momentum asymptotic terms of the soft loop integrand and retain their finite contributions to the oscillation.
items.author: Linghao Song, Jingtao You, Ming Cheng et al.

items.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
items.summary: LLM agents increasingly drive their own learning. Self-improvement methods delegate various components of model optimization to the models themselves. As models become more capable, this motivates a basic question: do these increasingly capable models still need us to specify how they should self-improve? In this paper we study an autonomous paradigm in which, given basic primitives, resources, and a general goal for self-improvement, agents construct their own self-learning algorithm for context-based optimization. Using the setting of gameplay as a testbed, a frozen LLM agent is given a compute budget and tools for collecting experience and updating text documents, and allowed to freely experiment without an externally imposed loop or access to real-world data.
items.author: Shobhita Sundaram, Cansu Sancaktar, Phillip Isola

items.title: What Does a Bias Head Measure? Non-Identifiability in Head-Level Bias Attribution
items.summary: Methods that localise social bias in large language models to individual attention heads and remove it by ablation are validated by their effect on a fairness metric, never by evidence that the statistic selecting the heads measures bias. We audit this on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The head map correlates at $ρ= -0.950$ and $-0.768$ with a label-blind response-length map, apparently identifying a surface confound. An intervention that breaks the length-label coupling rejects this reading: with the prompt held fixed, response length explains 1% of the statistic's variance. What does explain it is prompt identity, at 64% of variance, in an ordering that is not monotonic in length.
items.author: S. M Seefat Alam

items.title: Higher-Scoring Coding Models Did Not Get More Work Done
items.summary: New coding models advertise themselves on score improvements of coding benchmarks. Yet no study has tested if a model that scores higher on these benchmarks gets more real work done. On June 12, 2026, a U.S. export control directive banned access to Claude Fable 5 for 19 days, which forced users to switch to other models. During this time, most former Fable 5 users switched to Opus 4.8 (11 points lower on SWE-Bench Pro compared to Fable 5). We treat this suspension as a natural experiment, where the people and projects stayed the same and only the model changed, so we could isolate the effect of Fable 5 on user productivity.
items.author: Yining Hua

items.title: Feedback-Linearised Trajectory Tracking via Model-Informed Robust Geometric DDPC
items.summary: Data-driven predictive control (DDPC) predicts system responses from recorded trajectories, but nonlinear dynamics can limit the accuracy of fixed linear predictors. This paper studies geometric robust DDPC for trajectory tracking of a fully actuated manipulator using model-based feedback linearisation. A mechanical model maps virtual acceleration commands into joint torques, while recorded data capture residual dynamics arising from imperfect model parameters. The controller minimises worst-case prediction error over an open Grassmannian ball centred at the fitted trajectory subspace. Simulations on a planar 2R manipulator under gravity compare the proposed method with double-integrator model predictive control (MPC) and direct regularised data-enabled predictive control (DeePC).
items.author: Pranav Gupta, Deepan Muthirayan, Ravi Banavar

items.title: Modeling quantum information scrambling in realistic protein NMR experiments
items.summary: Out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) are important probes of operator spreading and information scrambling, and have recently been proposed as a means of extracting molecular structural information through nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). Realizing this potential requires accurate modeling of OTOCs in complex molecular environments within experimentally relevant settings. Here, we develop an end-to-end computational pipeline connecting molecular structures to OTOC dynamics in protein systems. Our framework incorporates molecular motion through molecular dynamics simulations, orientational averaging appropriate for powder samples, and spin-network truncation, using an experimentally realizable double-quantum effective Hamiltonian. We apply this framework to a dataset of over 350 carbon-carbon spin pairs across 10 protein systems, spanning interspin distances of 5-17 A.
items.author: Alec F. White, Joseph Haslehurst, Daniel R. Moberg et al.

items.title: Multimodal Masked Diffusion Autoencoder for Modeling Impaired Driving
items.summary: Human cognitive state (e.g., distraction, stress), gaze, and behavior interact with the driving environment in subtle ways that AI could use to assist drivers, but ground-truth labels for human cognitive state levels are costly to obtain at scale. We propose a multimodal masked-diffusion autoencoder, ID-MAE, that adds a self-supervised objective to impairment prediction: alongside predicting the impairment label as a masked token, it reconstructs masked gaze and trajectory. To probe the effects of different modalities and types of impairments on model inference, we introduce DIVERT, a driving-simulator dataset containing 103 hours of driving data (n = 109) with ten impairment inductions spanning cognitive, visual, and emotional states, recorded with gaze, vehicle state, and scene video.
items.author: John Gideon, Anshul Gupta, Megan Applegate-Kenton et al.

items.title: Distortion-Free Semantic Watermarks for Black-Box Generative Models
items.summary: We present a provably distortion-free semantic watermarking algorithm that requires only black-box sampling access to a generative model and black-box access to a semantic embedding. A watermark is called distortion-free if, averaged over its secret detection key, it leaves the generator's output distribution unchanged; this provides a formal guarantee that watermarking does not reduce output quality. Conventional such watermarks are often brittle to transformations. This is especially problematic for images, where benign operations such as compression, cropping, or resizing change the entire pixel representation. Semantic watermarks therefore require detection to be robust to content-preserving transformations. Previous methods combining these properties rely heavily on specific white-box properties of the underlying model: either to autoregressive text generation or to diffusion-specific access, such as control of the initial noise or diffusion inversion.
items.author: Aviv Yossef, Or Patashnik, Or Zamir

items.title: Local interference algorithms for observables in large random circuits
items.summary: In quantum dynamics, it is generally believed that interference effects lead to a sign problem for classical Monte Carlo sampling methods, rendering sampling ineffective. In this paper we show that this is generically not the case for the task of simulating the evolution of observables in random instances of circuit dynamics. Specifically, we consider two examples of observables which give large signals despite the randomness of the dynamics: first order out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) in unstructured random circuits without conservation laws and time-ordered charge-charge correlators (TOCs) in particle number-preserving random circuits. We show that these observables can be approximated by classical stochastic processes and that these approximations can be systematically improved with a series expansion that incorporates coherent corrections associated with clusters of gates.
items.author: Philippe Suchsland, Brayden Ware, Vladislav D. Kurilovich et al.

items.title: Reading Scene States: Uncovering Safety Failures in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) can provide harmful assistance by interpreting visual events, even without an explicit request for the underlying harmful objective. We identify this \textbf{scene-state safety vulnerability} and introduce \textbf{SceneSafetyBench}, comprising 375 image--question pairs spanning Initial, Medium, and Ultimate scene states and five visual presentations. Across eight VLMs, scene-state inputs elicit harmful assistance with attack success rates (ASRs) of 45.6--72.3\%. Comparative analysis across three VLMs shows that scene-state inputs most closely resemble QR-related images in their layer-wise safety-related signal profiles, while exhibiting lower average late-layer readouts and distinct signal dynamics during generation. To turn this vulnerability into a systematic attack, we propose \textbf{S3TA}, which translates harmful objectives into scene states, queries image--question pairs independently, and assembles the responses.
items.author: Tongxi Wu, Yuyang Cheng, Jiacheng Xian et al.

items.title: Fine-Tuning Gemma 4 Edge Models for MATLAB Signal-Processing Code with SFT and QLoRA on a Laptop iGPU
items.summary: Small language models that run on a laptop are attractive for writing signal-processing code offline, but they make systematic errors on digital signal processing (DSP) conventions. We apply supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to the Gemma 4 edge models E2B and E4B with 66 checked examples covering 11 signal-processing MATLAB subtasks, using low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and quantized LoRA (QLoRA) on the integrated GPU (iGPU) of a laptop, and deploy the 8-bit integer (int8) models with the adapters through OpenVINO. On held-out variants scored by deterministic checkers, the pass rate rises from 18/66 to 37/66 (LoRA) and 37/66 (QLoRA) for E2B and from 32/66 to 47/66 for E4B (QLoRA).
items.author: Mehmet Altan Toksöz

items.title: Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI): A Federated Identity, Trust, Attestation, and Accountability Architecture for Cross-Organization Autonomous AI Agents
items.summary: AI agents increasingly collaborate across organizational boundaries, invoking tools and interacting with agents operated by independent entities. Although existing agent frameworks support planning and coordination, they lack a common mechanism for verifying cross-organizational agent identity, execution integrity, and authorization. We propose the Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI), a framework-independent security architecture built on Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), and remote attestation. ATI establishes federated trust through peer organizational certificate authorities (AgentCAs), eliminating the need for a shared root authority. Before executing requests, ATI validates agent certificates, verifies approved model, tool, and system-prompt configurations, and enforces authorization through three policy checks.
items.author: Viet K. Nguyen, Mohammad I. Husain

items.title: A Universal Ratio Linking Cosmic Expansion and the Growth of Structure
items.summary: We identify a universal relation between the onset of cosmic acceleration ($z_t$) and the turnover ($z_{\rm pk}$) of the linear growth observable $fσ_{8}$. In a spatially flat $Λ$CDM Universe, these two redshifts obey $R \equiv (1+z_t)/(1+z_{\rm pk}) = 1.1596$, independent of the present matter fraction and the overall expansion and growth normalisations. This provides a new consistency test for $Λ$CDM, linking both background and growth dynamics. We further establish the conditions under which this extends to broader classes of dark energy and modified gravity theories.
items.author: Anjan A Sen, Purba Mukherjee

items.title: Learned versus Kinematic Trajectory Prediction under Reduced Observation Frequency
items.summary: Trajectory prediction models for automated driving are usually trained on data with a fixed sampling frequency, while positions received via vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication arrive at 1-10 Hz. We study whether a learned predictor that uses only the observation history keeps its advantage over constant velocity (CV) and constant acceleration (CA) models when the history frequency drops. On the Argoverse 2 motion forecasting dataset, the 5 s history of the focal agent was downsampled from 10 Hz to 5, 2, and 1 Hz, and the 6 s future was predicted without maps or neighboring agents. An LSTM-based recurrent neural network (RNN) trained for each frequency was compared with the same network trained at 10 Hz and applied to sparse histories after linear interpolation.
items.author: Nukhbala Gadzhiev, Alexander Morochko

items.title: Structure--Residual Inductive Biases for Language Model Pretraining
items.summary: Next-token prediction is relied upon to learn both predictive behavior and internal representations. We ask whether representation structure itself should be an explicit inductive bias. Motivated by the two-part coding view of Kolmogorov complexity, we study a structure--residual principle in which a representation separates structure from realization detail. We instantiate this principle in two complementary ways. Boundary Bottleneck Concept (BBC) routes information from token segments through boundary carriers while preserving local autoregressive computation. Continuous Concept (CC) regularizes representation geometry and induces a spectral decomposition into low-frequency structure and high-frequency residual. We derive coding bounds for both views and show that multiplicity-corrected boundary attention becomes exact as the within-segment path energy vanishes.
items.author: Hai Huang, Bartosz Żuk, Rassul Magauin et al.

items.title: Nonlinearity-preserving quantum simulation of flows in the early fault-tolerant regime
items.summary: Ensemble prediction of nonlinear dynamics propagates a probability density whose linear transport equation retains the nonlinear drift, but grid-dependent circuit costs leave end-to-end feasibility in early fault-tolerant quantum computing unresolved. We couple polynomial reduced-order models fitted by sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics to Walsh-synthesized Koopman-von Neumann (KvN) transport and surface-code resource estimation. At fixed model dimension and drift degree, per-step transport rotation counts scale polylogarithmically with cells per reduced coordinate. Balancing model accuracy against circuit costs makes reduced-model polynomial degree a design variable for early fault-tolerant quantum simulation. For a cylinder wake approaching saturation, preparation, propagation and sampling to 1% relative root-mean-square field error against the radial model are estimated to take 1.62 h on about 560,000 physical qubits.
items.author: Hansol Noh, Unam Oh, Sangkyu Baek et al.

items.title: Performance analysis of a Rydberg atom THz radiometer concept
items.summary: THz receiver technology lies between electronics and photonics; as such, its implementation is not as mature. This warrants investigation into alternative THz receivers such as Rydberg atom sensors, which are highly susceptible to electric fields. In particular, the conversion architecture has been demonstrated to coherently transduce thermal radiation. This system offers room-temperature operation and does not necessarily require a local oscillator at the frequency of the input signal. We provide an assessment of the feasibility of such sensors for THz radiometry within the context of Earth observation.
items.author: Richard J. Murchie, Petronilo Martin-Iglesias, Julian Hofmann et al.

items.title: WoRD: Diffusion-Based Posterior Inference for Online Goal Recognition
items.summary: Goal recognition is the task of inferring an agent's intended goal from its observed behavior. Most existing work focuses on high-level symbolic recognition, abstracting away the continuous motion through which agents reach their goal. Methods that do reason over continuous trajectories rely on an explicit dynamics model that is hard to acquire and rarely transfers across settings. Neither approach explicitly learns how agents move toward each candidate goal, limiting accuracy on ambiguous trajectory prefixes where such knowledge is most needed. We present WoRD (Waypoint Recognition with Diffusion), which uses a learned trajectory prior to infer the agent's goal from partial observations.
items.author: Almog Anschel, Sarah Keren

items.title: Quantum amplification with a linear quantum coupler
items.summary: Josephson parametric amplifiers (JPAs) are essential components for quantum-limited microwave measurement, but their dynamic range is often constrained by Kerr and other pump-induced nonlinear effects. In this work, we systematically study the performance of a parametric amplifier based on the linear inductive coupler (LINC). Starting from the driven-circuit Hamiltonian, we derive the effective three-wave-mixing amplifier model, including leading flux-driven nonlinear corrections relevant to realistic operation. We analyze the resulting gain response, saturation behavior, and intermodulation distortion, comparing them with representative state-of-the-art JPA designs. Our results show that the symmetry-protected structure of the LINC suppresses static Kerr nonlinearity. Moreover, suitable circuit-parameter optimization can further reduce the dressed-squeezing and driven-Kerr effects, leading to considerable improvements in power-handling metrics.
items.author: Changqing Wang, Yao Lu

items.title: Integral Tensor Isomorphism via Cubic Rings and Lattice Methods
items.summary: We prove that isomorphism of integral $2\times3\times3$ tensors under $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\times\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathbb{Z})\times\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ is decidable in bounded-error quantum polynomial time. For a tensor $T=(A,B)$ with nonzero determinant form $\det(xA-yB)$, we use the parametrization of Wood by balanced modules to reduce the isomorphism problem to principality tests for compatible lattices, and use the algorithms of Bley, Hofmann, and Johnston to solve this in BQP. When the determinant form vanishes identically, we get either an integral $2\times2\times2$ core, or a polynomial kernel vector of degree one or two. The linear-kernel case yields another compatible lattice problem, while the quadratic-kernel case reduces to a fixed system of polynomial congruences and unimodular lifting.
items.author: Thomas Huffstutler

items.title: Effect of superplastic deformation on the intergranular corrosion resistance of austenitic steel 321 with different types of UFG structure: A case of homogeneous and heterogeneous microstructure obtained by ECAP
items.summary: The effects of superplasticity (SP) on the structure, hardness, and intergranular corrosion (IGC) resistance of UFG 321L steel are reported. By increasing the number of the ECAP cycles (N) and varying the ECAP temperature, and annealing temperature, the degree of the microstructural heterogeneity was changed. Regardless of the microstructural homogeneity degree, UFG steels demonstrated the possibility of realizing the SP effect at temperatures below the onset temperature of dynamic recrystallization. The dependence of ductility of the UFG steel on the test temperature is non-monotonic with a minimum at 450-600C. The maximum elongation to failure (~250%) was achieved at a SP temperature of 800C.
items.author: A. V. Nokhrin, V. I. Kopylov, M. K. Chegurov et al.

items.title: The Pfaffian sector of $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ BPS cohomology: brane excitations, triality and fortuity
items.summary: We study the classical $\frac{1}{16}$-BPS cohomology of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory with gauge group $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ in the BMN sector, including the operators built with one $ε$-tensor. These operators are odd under the reflection in $\mathrm{O}(2N)$, carry the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ charge of a D3-brane wrapped on $\mathbb{RP}^3\subset\mathbb{RP}^5$, and form the Pfaffian sector. For $\mathrm{SO}(8)$ we determine this sector through level $j=18$, where the level is twice the total charge of an operator. All but one of its $106$ $\mathrm{SU}(3)_R$ multiplets are products of trace gravitons and excited Pfaffians. The exception is a singlet, represented by the singlet projection of the rank-four member of a four-term family of $ε$-tensor operators.
items.author: Zheng Miao, Yuezhang Tang

items.title: An Effective Theory for Hot Lines
items.summary: We develop a high-temperature effective theory for spatial conformal line defects in theories with thermal screening. The defect partition function admits a local geometric expansion, whose leading terms describe the effective tension and bending response of the line. Using a convergent bulk OPE for heavy-state defect matrix elements, we derive asymptotic relations for averaged products of defect one-point coefficients and bulk OPE coefficients in the regime $1 \ll Δ_χ\ll Δ^{1/d}$. We compute the leading EFT coefficients for a twisted free scalar and for the magnetic line at the $\mathrm{O}(N)$ Wilson-Fisher fixed point, large-$N$ Gross--Neveu model and $\mathcal N = 2$ Chern-Simons-matter theory.
items.author: Julien Barrat, Alessio Miscioscia, Fedor K. Popov

items.title: Dynamics of a Single-Domain Dissipative Magnetic Gyroscope in Electric and Magnetic Fields
items.summary: We formulate the coupled spin--rotation dynamics of a single-domain symmetric top ferromagnetic needle (a magnetic gyroscope) in static magnetic and electric fields. The conservative Hamiltonian contains the rotational kinetic energy, the magnetocrystalline and shape anisotropy, the Zeeman energy, the electrostatic energy of the dipole induced in the conducting needle, the linear magnetoelectric coupling, and the relativistic motional (spin-orbit) coupling. Gilbert damping is introduced, and in an electric field, Debye relaxation of the induced electric dipole of the conducting needle also results in dissipation. We give the equations of motion in the laboratory and body-fixed frames, with singularity-free quaternion kinematics.
items.author: Y. B. Band, Igor Kuzmenko

items.title: NASA's NICER X-ray Telescope Concludes Operations on Space Station
items.summary: NASA’s Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer (NICER) telescope has officially ended science operations on the International Space Station after operating for more than six years past its initial mission timeline. Launched in 2017, the X-ray instrument provided groundbreaking measurements of neutron stars, advanced our understanding of black holes, and demonstrated pulsar-based deep space navigation. Although operations were initially paused due to an unresolvable internal motor failure that restricted the telescope's tracking ability, the mission's legacy includes numerous scientific papers and spinoff applications for Earth technologies, such as prototype portable CT scanners.
items.author: Jeanette Kazmierczak

items.summary: A magnitude 4.5 earthquake was recorded approximately 26 kilometers northwest of Port-Vila, Vanuatu, at a depth of 10 kilometers. The seismic event occurred on November 17, 2026, with at least one individual reporting feeling the tremor.
