items.title: Benchmarking memory and nonlinear processing capacity of quantum recurrent neural networks for time series prediction
items.summary: Quantum machine learning has emerged as a promising approach to time series prediction. While quantum reservoir computing has been widely explored for this setting, variational quantum models tailored to sequential data remain comparatively understudied, largely because they are difficult to train. In this work, we present a rigorous benchmark of variational quantum recurrent neural networks (QRNNs) on time series prediction tasks, focusing on two key capabilities: memory and nonlinear processing. We introduce a task-driven methodology that quantifies model capacity, enabling an intuitive and fair comparison across architectures, including classical recurrent baselines. We evaluate the proposed framework on two generic benchmark tasks and on a synthetic dataset describing a chaotic system.
items.author: José Daniel Viqueira, Andrés Gómez, David Mera

items.title: Axioms for relative entropy
items.summary: For normal states of arbitrary von Neumann algebras, we characterize positive finite multiples of Araki relative entropy among non-degenerate divergences. The axioms are monotonicity under normal unital completely positive maps, tensor additivity, superadditivity for product second states, and separate lower semicontinuity in the predual norm. Alternatively, a conditional-expectation identity replaces the two tensor assumptions. The proof uses order bounds and asymptotic estimates on tensor powers. An appendix proves the known analytic estimates needed here, using standard modular theory and Haagerup L^p spaces. We also obtain the corresponding characterization in the C* algebraic setting.
items.author: Roberto Longo

items.title: TRACE: Topological Representations for Anomaly detection through Contrastive Embeddings
items.summary: Intrusion detectors must recognize evolving malicious behavior even when confirmed attack labels are scarce or incomplete. We present TRACE, a topology-aware graph contrastive learning framework for label-efficient intrusion detection. TRACE learns from benign system-activity graphs by combining message-passing and topological representations, then assigns anomaly scores in the same projected embedding space optimized by the contrastive objective. This design captures both local interactions and graph-scale structural deviations without using attack labels during representation learning. A labeled validation set containing benign and malicious graphs is used only to calibrate the anomaly threshold. We evaluate TRACE on StreamSpot, GraSec-IoT, and Unicorn Wget against a supervised graph neural network and the benign-only GraphCL baseline.
items.author: Sydney Johns

items.title: The speed limit of gravitational entanglement and the cost of noise
items.summary: Is gravity quantum? A proposed test lets two small masses, each in a superposition of two places, become entangled through their mutual gravity. Gravity is weak, so the masses must stay coherent for seconds while random forces disturb them. Here we ask how fast gravity can entangle two masses, and what noise costs. Without noise we find the maximum rate exactly: it falls as the inverse cube of the separation, and two positions per mass achieve it. Above a noise level set by the masses and their separation, gravity's leading pull can be imitated by classical signals, and every strategy is limited to a rate falling at least as the inverse fourth power.
items.author: Ekta Panwar, Anubhav Chaturvedi

items.title: Right Reason, Wrong Advice: Evaluating Recourse in LLM Explanations of Denied Requests
items.summary: Language models increasingly write the explanations people receive when a rule system denies their request. If several rules deny the request independently, an explanation can name a true reason and still leave the person denied after they fix it. We call the missing property recourse validity: changing what the explanation cites, without changing what was asked for, can flip the decision. We compute it exactly, and a hitting-set argument predicts from the policy alone when a correct reason fails. In six of seven rule systems ported from access control and US benefit eligibility, a single correct reason almost never gives recourse when several reasons apply.
items.author: Arunkumar V

items.title: The Skyrme-Dilaton and Nucleon Observables
items.summary: We extend the Skyrme model by incorporating the $σ/f_0(500)$-meson as a dilaton. The motivation is twofold: the $σ$-meson is the lightest scalar resonance in QCD and is therefore the natural extensions to the pions of the classical Skyrme model, while its interpretation as a pseudo-Goldstone boson of spontaneously broken scale symmetry is supported by recent studies of gravitational form factors and related developments. Although the $σ$-meson is a broad resonance, for static observables it can be treated as real particle since its line-shape is not expected to be essential. A combined fit to static nucleon observables yields $χ^2/\mathrm{dof} $ close to unity, with substantial improvement over the original Skyrme model, while simultaneously reproducing the physical value of $F_π$, the overall scale of the model.
items.author: Thomas Fischbacher, Roman Zwicky

items.title: Lazy-MOSAIC: Accelerating Skill-Centric Manipulation Planning with Learned Skill-Effect World Models
items.summary: Long-horizon manipulation tasks require a robot to perform a sequence of physical interactions with its environment, typically combining several different skills. Planning such behaviors efficiently is challenging: given a library of parameterized skills, solutions lie in a vast hybrid space of skill sequences and their parameters, and evaluating each candidate skill's feasibility and effect with a high-fidelity world model such as a physics simulator is computationally expensive. MOSAIC, a recent skill-centric approach, lets the skills guide a non-sequential search toward the regions of this space where they are likely to succeed; however, it pays the full cost of simulation for every parameterized skill it considers.
items.author: Itamar Mishani, Mukund Krishnakumar, Oren Salzman et al.

items.title: GHySSeg: Real-Time Geometric Ground and Road Segmentation for Hybrid Solid-State LiDAR
items.summary: Hybrid solid-state LiDAR sensors are making their way into production vehicles, yet the data they produce differs structurally from that of the established spinning mechanical sensors behind today's autonomous-driving datasets: it is ring-free, dense, cluttered, and concentrated in a frontal field of view. The classical geometric methods that autonomous vehicles rely on for drivable space computation and navigation assume the ordered ring-and-column structure of a 360-degree spinning LiDAR and degrade or fail on this data, while learned alternatives are computationally heavy, hard to certify, and trained almost exclusively on spinning-LiDAR data. We demonstrate that the same dense, per-curve geometry is instead an opportunity to close the divide between the industry's preferred sensors and autonomous-driving research.
items.author: Martín Palos, Fernando García

items.title: Learning from Duality in Neural Network Field Theories
items.summary: We develop neural realizations of positive-level Wess-Zumino-Witten models using bosonic Wakimoto and fermionic Fourier-Berezin fields. Level-rank duality connects the charged sectors of the fermionic construction, where explicit neural observables recover conformal block data and enable the transfer of information about unknown correlators between paired theories. We also show that distinct neural presentations of the same continuum current algebra exhibit different finite-width behavior, with approximation accuracy depending on architecture, regulator, and parameter distribution. These results connect the exact mathematical structure of conformal field theory with the expressive and computational properties of neural field theories.
items.author: Pietro Capuozzo, Brandon Robinson, Benjamin Suzzoni

items.title: Spectral integral method for reflection and transmission by one-dimensional periodic arrays of penetrable cylinders
items.summary: The spectral integral method (SIM) is extended from a single cylinder to an infinite one-dimensional (1-D) periodic array (a grating) of identical, homogeneous, arbitrarily shaped smooth cylinders. The cylinders may be dielectric or metallic with complex electrical permittivity. Interactions among all members of the array are carried exactly by the 1-D quasi-periodic Green's function, Gp, in the exterior boundary integral equation, so only the boundary of one reference cylinder is discretized. Gp is written as the free-space Green's function plus a regular part that is infinitely differentiable on the reference cylinder whenever the cylinders do not touch. The regular part and its gradient are evaluated with Ewald's method.
items.author: Ergun Simsek

items.title: Exponential Quantum Memory Advantage for Late-Graph Smoothness and Spectral Estimation
items.summary: Graph signal processing tests how smoothly the decisions of next-generation massive sensor networks with $N$ nodes vary over their neighbour graph. Memory becomes the bottleneck when the neighbour graph arrives only after data erasure, a late-graph setting motivated by dispersed sensor networks and telemetry. We analyse three collection scenarios, reliable rounds, continuous broadcast and ordered capture, and test the Dirichlet energy $\mathcal E_G=\mathbf z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf L\mathbf z/N$ of the fused decision map $\mathbf z\in\{\pm1\}^N$, with late-graph Laplacian $\mathbf L$, against two thresholds. Hidden Matching uses $O(\log N)$ qubits on fused bits, but in reliable rounds and continuous broadcast, where nodes report $b$ sub-bits separately, a classical record buffer before it uses $O(N b)$ bits; classical methods need $Ω(\sqrt N)$ bits in the worst case.
items.author: Burhan Gülbahar

items.title: Unraveling QCD dynamics via charm-tagged jets with ALICE at the LHC
items.summary: The study of jet substructure provides tests of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and offers differential ways to study hadronization mechanisms. QCD predicts that jet radiation patterns depend on the mass and color charge of the initiating parton. Parton showers are sensitive to the different Casimir factors of quarks and gluons, and to the parton mass through the dead-cone effect. In this talk, we present three sets of $\textrm{D}^0$-meson-tagged jet measurements. First, we present the first measurement of the Energy-Energy Correlator (EEC) for $\textrm{D}^0$-meson-tagged jets. This observable reveals the detailed structure of QCD radiation from heavy quarks, allowing for a distinction between perturbative and non-perturbative effects in charm-quark showers.
items.author: Emma Yeats

items.title: Entanglement distillation, nonlocal magic, and state sharing in an isospectral non-Hermitian bipartite model
items.summary: An invertible nonunitary similarity deformation leaves a two-qubit Hamiltonian's spectrum unchanged while varying a selected normalized right eigenstate in the fixed physical inner product. We embed this state in a two-parameter maximally correlated family that includes local dephasing and noisy circuit preparation. Hashing and a matching diagonal relative-entropy bound give the exact distillable entanglement and the PPT comparison distances at every finite tensor power. Correlated PPT catalysts cannot improve the Bell-pair distillation rate. The optimized CHSH value is \(2\sqrt{1+t^2}\): every state with nonzero coherence violates CHSH, while complete dephasing is separable. A calibrated finite-sample bound and two equal-fidelity preparations clarify which noise parameters determine the rate.
items.author: Chenhuan Wu

items.title: Windowed Singularity Subtraction for the Spectral Integral Method
items.summary: In 2004, the spectral integral method (SIM) was proposed to solve TM$_z$ scattering by homogeneous two-dimensional dielectric objects and perfect electrical conductors with smooth boundaries. Its error decreases exponentially as the number of boundary points increases linearly. Plasmonic resonances, however, require TE$_z$ polarization and permittivities with a negative real part. The extension of SIM to this case shows that the original global singularity subtraction suffers catastrophic cancellation, with a round-off floor that grows exponentially with the attenuation accumulated across the object. To resolve this issue, this work introduces a windowed singularity subtraction that limits this cancellation amplification to an exponential factor that the user can set independently of the object size, provided the window is adequately resolved.
items.author: Ergun Simsek

items.title: Controlling Mode-Locking in Liquid Light
items.summary: Mode-locking is the process by which the phases of many cavity modes organize collectively into a stationary state. In lasers, mode-locking originates from the interplay of gain, loss, dispersion and nonlinearities, most commonly resulting in the emission of short pulses. However, pulse formation is prevented when the gain recovery is fast enough to suppress amplitude fluctuations. Mode-locking then produces an extended state of nearly constant intensity, whose dynamics is governed by the phase. Yet, a general framework for designing the phase of such extended photonic states remains lacking. Here we introduce a hydrodynamic approach to designing extended photonic states, in which the phase dynamics are understood and controlled as a flow of liquid-like light.
items.author: Diego Piciocchi, Francesco Fortuna, Bahareh Marzban et al.

items.title: A Reinforcement Learning Method to Navigate SMEFT Operator Space
items.summary: In particle physics, discrepancies between experimental measurements and Standard Model (SM) predictions are commonly interpreted within new theoretical models. In this context, the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) provides a general framework encompassing a broad class of models. However, exploring the enormous space of possible SMEFT operators rapidly becomes a challenging combinatorial problem: many operators can contribute simultaneously to different observables, their effects are correlated, and distinct operator combinations can provide comparably good descriptions of the data. In this work, we formulate the exploration of the SMEFT operator space as a sequential decision-making problem using reinforcement learning (RL). Our RL agent employs a lightweight actor-critic architecture with approximately 40K trainable parameters in total.
items.author: Jacky Kumar

items.title: Geometry of squeezed states. The phase-space metric, relative vacua and cosmology
items.summary: Geometry enters quantum theory in two places. The space of quantum states carries a symplectic form, which generates unitary evolution, and a metric, which governs uncertainties and transition probabilities. The classical phase space acquires a metric of its own when a vacuum is chosen: quantizing a linear system amounts to choosing a compatible complex structure, equivalently a compatible metric $g$. We take this second metric as the primary object and show that it plays, on phase space, the role that the quantum metric plays on the space of states: fluctuations of linear observables are $g$-norms of Hamiltonian vector fields, and along coherent states $g/2\hbar$ \emph{is} the quantum metric.
items.author: Alejandro Corichi, Jerónimo Cortez

items.title: Shared-State Inverse Synthesis of Dual-Mode Conformal Metasurfaces for Low Scattering and Telemetry
items.summary: A conformal surface that alternates between sectoral low scattering and directive telemetry poses a shared-hardware inverse problem when both modes must use one finite passive impedance alphabet, although their spatial codebooks may differ. This paper formulates and solves that mixed continuous--discrete problem at the effective impedance-boundary level. Reference-centered Tikhonov preimages prescribe restricted radiation data; inverse-source null-space freedom then moves each current within its data-equivalent class toward impedance profiles quantizable by the same alphabet. A line-searched Gauss--Newton update, common-state assignment and projected-centroid updates, and exact forward refinement determine the currents, two codebooks, and one passive library. Data invariance, the current-to-impedance differential, the optimal state update, monotonic mismatch reduction, and a forward perturbation bound are derived.
items.author: Mohamed R. Khodja, Ghala A. Alomar

items.title: Non-Canonical Q-balls in Polyattractor Inflation Models
items.summary: We show that Q-balls can exist in supergravity-based polyattractor inflation models that interpolate between $α$-attractor T-models and polynomial attractor models. We consider both the original polyattractor potential and a natural generalisation. We find that Q-balls solutions exist when the model deviates significantly from the T-model $α$-attractor, whereas in the T-model limit no Q-balls exist. These are non-canonical Q-balls due to the non-canonical kinetic term of the complex inflaton field. Such Q-balls could have significant cosmological consequences if they are produced at the end of inflation. In particular, if the global $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry of the supergravity-based polyattractor model is unbroken, the Q-balls can be absolutely stable and could account for dark matter.
items.author: Kimberley Siret, Rhys Abercromby, Kit Lloyd-Stubbs et al.

items.title: Atomistic Insights into the All-Optical Switching of GdCo Alloys with Minimal Gd Concentration
items.summary: Single-pulse all-optical helicity-independent switching (AO-HIS) is most commonly observed in Gd-based ferrimagnets near magnetization compensation. Recent experiments, however, demonstrated switching in Pt/Co/Pt-based heterostructures containing only a small amount of Gd at a Co/Pt interface. Here, we use atomistic spin-dynamics simulations to test an effective interfacial GdCo-alloy picture and to determine how species-dependent spin-bath coupling controls the minimum Gd concentration required for reversal. We compare a three-monolayer Co film with Gd confined to the surface layer and a three-dimensional uniformly alloyed GdCo model. Within the present uniform-heating model, robust transient toggle-like reversal is obtained far from compensation when the Gd coupling to the thermal bath is substantially weaker than that of Co; for λCo = 0.02 and λCo = 0.001, reversal occurs down to 1.5 at.
items.author: Paul-Iulian Gavriloaea, Jackson L. Ross, Richard F. L. Evans et al.

items.title: Self-attention is a Dyson equation for many-body machine learning
items.summary: Why does symmetric sum-pooling (DeepSets) predict ground-state potentials to sub-meV accuracy, yet fail for correlated wavefunctions and excited states? Sum-pooling is a mean-field (Hartree) model: its $O(1/N)$ off-diagonal Jacobian suffices for nearsighted ground-state energies, but erases nonlocal two-body correlations. We show that self-attention is a real-space Dyson iteration whose Boltzmann (softmax) kernel acts as a two-body self-energy. Because physical Hamiltonians act pairwise, Löwdin's 2-RDM theorem and the Galitskii--Migdal relation guarantee that iterating a two-body propagator captures the full energetics of correlated matter. When fitting a fractal backflow determinant, DeepSets blurs the nodal surface onto a mean-field envelope, whereas self-attention recovers the fractal attractor.
items.author: Jarvist Moore Frost

items.title: Multilevel AlScN Ferroelectric Diode Crossbar Arrays with Sub-200 nm Cells for Selector-Free Nonvolatile Memory
items.summary: Passive crossbar arrays are a leading route to high-density nonvolatile memory and in-memory computing, but without a selector the memory element itself must supply the nonlinearity that suppresses sneak-path currents. Here we scale aluminum scandium nitride (AlScN) ferroelectric diodes (FeDs) in both dimensions that matter - the ferroelectric is thinned to 10 nm and the junction diameter is reduced to 100 nm. We further integrate 200 nm cells into a 2-kilobyte (128 * 128) passive crossbar. At a junction area of 0.0314 um2 this is a ~625 reduction in cell area, at equal array capacity, relative to kilobyte-scale AlScN FeD crossbars built on 5 μm cells.
items.author: Kwan-Ho Kim, Zekun Hu, Krishna Karthikeya Chemudupati et al.

items.title: Heavy double-gluon quarkonium and $\overline{b}ggc$ mesons
items.summary: We investigate heavy double-gluon hybrid mesons, built from a heavy quark-antiquark pair and two valence gluons, using the two-point QCD sum rule method. The charmonium-like $\bar{c}GGc$ and bottomonium-like $\bar{b}GGb$ states are considered with $J^{PC}=0^{\pm\pm}$ and $1^{\pm\pm}$, whereas the open-flavor $\bar{b}GGc$ states are classified by $J^{P}=0^{\pm}$ and $1^{\pm}$. The currents with $J^{PC}=0^{+-}, 0^{--}, 1^{++}$, and $1^{-+}$ vanish identically, so sum rules are derived for the remaining four channels. The operator product expansion is carried out up to dimension twelve, and the Borel parameter and continuum threshold are fixed so that the pole contribution dominates and the OPE converges. The resulting masses lie in the ranges $M\simeq 6.2$--$6.7$~GeV for $\bar{c}GGc$, $M\simeq 12.0$--$12.2$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGb$, and $M\simeq 9.2$--$9.6$~GeV for $\bar{b}GGc$, and the current couplings are obtained for all channels.
items.author: G. Daylan Esmer, B. Barsbay, K. Azizi et al.

items.title: Data-Driven Predictive Control for Autonomous Vehicle Racing under Varying Friction
items.summary: Data-driven predictive control (DPC) predicts future outputs by combining recorded input-output trajectory data such that the combined trajectory approximately matches a measured initial trajectory and tracks a provided reference. This paper investigates to what extent and under which conditions DPC using data pooled across operating conditions retains the prediction accuracy of DPC using data from the current operating condition. In autonomous vehicle racing, the tire-road friction varies between racetrack sections and tire sets. If the initial trajectory and the recorded data originate from different frictions, prediction accuracy of DPC degrades. Ensuring the frictions match requires knowing the friction during recording and estimating the current friction explicitly.
items.author: Julius Beerwerth, Julius Tischbein, Bassam Alrifaee

items.title: Inclusive Heavy Quarkonium Production in Lepton-Hadron Scattering in a Joint QCD+QED Factorization Approach
items.summary: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will provide an opportunity for precision studies of heavy quarkonium production in electron-proton ($ep$) and electron-nucleus ($eA$) collisions. Comparing production in $ep$ and $eA$ collisions provides a clean, well-controlled experimental environment to study interactions between a heavy quark pair and nuclear matter and the formation of quarkonia in a nuclear medium. In this talk, we present the first calculation of heavy quarkonium production in both $ep$ and $eA$ collisions at EIC energies using a joint QCD+QED factorization framework that treats collision-induced QCD and QED radiation on equal footing, and discuss the role of the nuclear medium in exploring how a physical quarkonium is emerged from a produced heavy quark pair.
items.author: Jian-Wei Qiu, Kazuhiro Watanabe, Jia-Yue Zhang

items.title: Accessing Electrode Edges: Upright Mounting for Site-Specific Cryogenic Atom Probe Tomography of Lithium-Ion Batteries
items.summary: Cryogenic atom probe tomography (cryo-APT) is increasingly being used to map the three-dimensional distribution of highly reactive species in heterogeneous materials, including those found in battery systems. However, site-specific preparation of localised features and liquid-solid interfaces remains challenging, particularly when regions of interest (ROIs) are concentrated along electrode edges that are difficult to access using conventional mounting geometries. Here, we present a cryo-APT workflow incorporating an upright-mounting procedure that enables targeted specimen preparation of localised regions using plasma focused ion beam (PFIB) microscopy and milling under cryogenic conditions. We first demonstrate the approach using an electrolyte-wetted graphite electrode, successfully preparing and analysing a specimen containing both an edge-localised electrolyte deposit and the underlying graphite and Cu current collector.
items.author: Syeda Ramin Jannat, James O. Douglas, Neil Mulcahy et al.

items.title: A Free Energy Approach to Modelling Disordered Hyperuniform Patterns
items.summary: We present a free-energy-based approach for modelling disordered hyperuniform patterns. Specifically, we devise a phase-field crystal model with a correlation kernel that simultaneously selects for a continuous range of degenerate wave modes. At small wave vectors, we construct the correlation function by inverting the Ornstein-Zernike relation to approximate the structure factor of a hyperuniform pattern. Our model demonstrates a crossover between liquid, crystalline, quasicrystalline, and long-lived disordered states depending on the specified free energy parameter and driving force. We show that, for a fixed driving force, the specific structures and wave vectors selected by the density field can be controlled by modulating the width of the correlation kernel.
items.author: Alex Mamaev, Enno Igel, Axel Voigt et al.

items.title: AMRT Framework Improves Generalizable Neural Decoding for Brain Activity
items.summary: Brain activity encodes motor information across multiple temporal scales, but existing neural decoding methods are typically limited to specific subjects and tasks. To overcome these constraints, researchers introduced AMRT, a shared neural decoding framework that supports heterogeneous electrode configurations and movement paradigms. AMRT uses a two-stage design that first anchors local motion through velocity estimation and then refines trajectories over longer horizons. This approach encourages the reuse of local motion tendencies across different subjects and tasks. Evaluated across three datasets, AMRT successfully generalizes to unseen trials and subjects while demonstrating strong transfer potential across diverse neural recordings and movement paradigms. The findings highlight the promise of shared neural representations and anchor-and-refine decoding strategies for achieving robust, continuous neural control.
items.author: Fanqi Shen, Junru Chen, Surui Cheng et al.
items.original_title: Anchoring Motion, Refining Trajectories: Generalizable Continuous Neural Decoding
items.original_summary: Brain activity encodes motor information across multiple temporal scales, enabling continuous neural control beyond discrete action recognition. However, existing methods are typically tailored to specific subjects and tasks, with direct neural-to-kinematic mappings that can entangle subject-specific neural variability with task-dependent motion patterns, limiting generalization. To address these limitations, we introduce AMRT, a shared neural decoding framework for heterogeneous electrode configurations and movement paradigms. Motivated by cortical encoding of movement direction and speed, AMRT adopts a two-stage design that anchors local motion through velocity estimation and refines the resulting trajectories over longer horizons, encouraging reuse of local motion tendencies across subjects and tasks.

items.title: Wavelet-Energy-Driven Dynamic Patching Enhances Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: Patch-based transformers traditionally use fixed-size windows, restricting models to a single temporal resolution despite the multi-scale nature of real signals. While discrete wavelet transforms offer a multi-scale alternative, researchers often couple them with learnable filters, making it difficult to isolate the source of forecasting improvements. A new forecaster addresses this by converting a learnable-DWT per-scale energy map into variable-length patches through the merging of adjacent windows sharing a dominant scale. Testing reveals that multi-resolution structure and variable-length patches drive most performance gains, outperforming fixed grids across numerous settings. In contrast, learning the filter yields marginal benefits only on select datasets. Consequently, researchers suggest starting with any valid wavelet, caching patch boundaries once, and treating filter training as a situational decision rather than a default requirement.
items.author: Syed Hafiz Bin Salim Alsree, Stephen Roberts, Stefan Zohren
items.original_title: Wavelet-Energy-Driven Dynamic Patching for Time Series Forecasting
items.original_summary: Patch-based transformers tokenise a time series into fixed-size, uniform windows, which commits the model to a single temporal resolution even though real signals are multi-scale. The discrete wavelet transform (DWT) is a natural alternative because it decomposes a signal across scales. A growing body of work makes the wavelet filter learnable, on the assumption that a more flexible wavelet forecasts better. That assumption has rarely been tested in isolation, because a single reported improvement usually credits three things at once. These are the use of any multi-resolution decomposition, the choice of wavelet and training the filter. We introduce a forecaster that turns a learnable-DWT per-scale energy map into variable-length patches by merging adjacent windows that share a dominant scale.

items.title: Training-Free Weight Baking Optimizes Latent Space Geometry in Language Models
items.summary: Researchers explore whether an analyst model can improve a trained language model's latent space organization by analyzing its topological geometry without gradient training. The analyst model reads a fixed-size digest of topological descriptors from a frozen target model's layers and suggests a transformation. Closed-form ridge regression then writes this transformation directly into the feed-forward weights. Experiments using lightweight models across 126 runs demonstrate that category purity increases on unseen text while benchmark accuracy remains stable. Furthermore, a five-model round robin approach showed that many model pairs successfully enhanced category purity. These results establish a solid baseline for future research on LLM-guided, training-free model editing that avoids the manipulation of raw weights.
items.author: Amin Golnari, Saeid Sanei
items.original_title: Can AI Mature a Model's Geometry? Training-Free Weight Baking in LLMs
items.original_summary: Can an AI make a trained language model more mature, in the sense of a better organized latent space, by looking only at the geometry of that space? An analyst model reads a fixed-size digest of topological descriptors of the layers of a frozen target and proposes a transformation, which closed-form ridge regression writes into the feed-forward weights without gradient training. Using lightweight models, 126 runs show that category purity rose on unseen words and sentences, benchmark accuracy stayed within sampling error, and the analyst matched a category-aware heuristic with gentler edits. In a five-model round robin approach, 16 pairs raised purity and four left the target unchanged.

items.title: Safe Physical Interaction of All-Electric Heavy-Duty Robotic Manipulators via Control Barrier Functions and Variable Impedance Control
items.summary: All-electric heavy-duty robotic manipulators are increasingly expected to operate close to tunnel walls, equipment, and other structures while retaining the force capability required for large-payload tasks. Accurate motion control alone does not address the resulting safety and interaction requirements. This paper develops a safety-aware physical-interaction architecture that combines variable impedance control (VIC) with control barrier functions (CBFs) on top of an established virtual decomposition control (VDC) framework for electromechanical linear actuator (EMLA)-driven manipulators. VIC continuously adapts the task-space stiffness and damping according to predicted proximity and contact risk, whereas a joint-velocity CBF filter enforces Cartesian workspace boundaries and the physical stroke limits induced by the closed-chain lift and tilt mechanisms.
items.author: Amir Hossein Barjini, Mohammad Bahari, Jouni Mattila

items.title: Programmable Semantic Interventions Enable Causal Abstraction Without Counterfactual Datasets
items.summary: Causal abstraction explains frozen neural networks by aligning their activations with simpler, interpretable models, a process traditionally requiring extensive counterfactual datasets and executable algorithms. Researchers introduce Programmable Semantic Interventions (PSI) and semantic programs, allowing investigators to directly define relationships between variable answers and expected intervention outputs. This low-rank activation subspace learns to alter model outputs according to the program, relying on answers read directly from the frozen model itself. On the MIB benchmark, PSI matches supervised alignment performance without requiring curated pairs or ground-truth labels. Additionally, on withheld natural science questions, it tracks model answers more effectively than subspaces trained on gold labels, while supporting donor-free steering for precise behavioral control.
items.author: Paolo Muratore, Mackenzie Weygandt Mathis
items.original_title: Programmable Semantic Interventions: Learning Causal Carriers from Behavioral Programs
items.original_summary: Causal abstraction explains a frozen network by aligning its activations with the variables of a simpler, interpretable model, and checking that interventions on the two agree. Finding such an alignment currently requires a counterfactual dataset: for every pair of prompts, the answer the network ought to give once the variable has been changed. In practice, those labels are produced by an executable algorithm for the behavior, written before studying the model supposed to implement it. However, the criterion these methods optimize only leverages the answer an intervention should produce. Here, we develop an approach that lets the investigator define that relationship directly: the answers the variable can produce, and which of them an intervention should yield.

items.title: Accelerated Convergence in Hamiltonian Monte Carlo via Uniform Mixing
items.summary: Recent research establishes simultaneous acceleration in both condition number and dimension for critically damped Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin with persistent uniforms. By examining target measures featuring specific convex and Lipschitz potentials, the study proves that this method achieves high-accuracy mixing in total variation using a quantified number of gradient evaluations. The proof introduces a novel coupling technology for general Markov chains, leveraging a weak maximal inequality derived from Hopf's ergodic theorem. This uncovers a stability mechanism within high-probability domains that supports fast local equilibration and naturally integrates framework concepts like Dobrushin and Wasserstein contractions.
items.author: Stefan Oberdörster
items.original_title: High-probability Uniform Mixing via Dobrushin Contraction and Accelerated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
items.original_summary: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, since its invention and subsequent rise to widespread use, has been motivated by its ability to accelerate convergence to equilibrium compared to diffusive methods, both in terms of dependence on condition number and dimension. In the present work, we establish this acceleration simultaneously in both aspects for critically damped Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin with persistent uniforms. More precisely, for target measures $μ(dx)\propto e^{-U(x)}dx$ with $m$-strongly convex, $L$-gradient Lipschitz, and $L_H$-Frobenius Hessian Lipschitz potentials, we show that the method mixes to $\varepsilon$-accuracy in total variation using $\mathcal O\bigl((κ^{1/2}+L_H^{1/2}m^{-3/4})\,d^{1/4}\bigr)$ gradient evaluations up to logarithmic factors, both uniformly over starting points in domains of high equilibrium probability and from warm starts.

items.title: Déjà-Events: Multi-view 3D Geometry with Event Cameras via Sparsity-Aware Adaptive Gating
items.summary: Event cameras keep capturing structure where conventional cameras blur or saturate, which makes them attractive for 3D perception in fast or poorly lit scenes. Event datasets with dense 3D ground truth, however, are far smaller and less diverse than the image collections behind feed-forward 3D reconstruction models. We present Déjà-Events, an event-only model that predicts depth, camera pose and pointmaps from multiple views in a single forward pass. Rather than relying on scarce 3D labels, we distil it from Déjà View, a feed-forward RGB model that refines its tokens by repeatedly applying one shared transformer block. On paired RGB and event recordings, the event student learns to reproduce the frozen teacher's final tokens, which requires no depth or pose ground truth and trains only about 1% of its parameters.
items.author: Arda Cinar Demirtas, Pablo Varela Bernal, Marc Pollefeys et al.

items.title: Physics-Infused Lecture Notes Bridge Classical Machine Learning and Modern LLMs
items.summary: Designed for third- and fourth-year students, a new set of introductory lecture notes on deep learning uses physical intuition instead of heavy mathematical formalism to explain complex concepts. Developed by a physicist at Queen Mary University of London, the curriculum starts with fundamental machine learning principles such as linear regression, gradient descent, and backpropagation. It progressively advances to more complex topics including regularization, convolutional methods, and neural network normalization. The second half of the material addresses modern natural language processing and large language models, covering transformers, attention mechanisms, reinforcement learning from human feedback, and chain-of-thought reasoning. The notes require minimal prerequisites, aiming to provide a clear and intuitive pathway into modern machine learning for students and independent learners with backgrounds in physics or mathematics.
items.author: Masanori Hanada
items.original_title: Deep Learning for Physicists: From Linear Regression to Reasoning Models
items.original_summary: These lecture notes are based on an introductory course on neural networks and deep learning that the author taught in the School of Mathematical Sciences at Queen Mary University of London in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The author, however, is a physicist, and it shows: wherever possible, ideas are explained with physical intuition rather than heavy formalism. Readers with a background in physics or mathematics who want a self-contained, introductory route into modern machine learning may therefore find these notes particularly friendly. The notes start from maximum likelihood, least squares, linear regression and (stochastic) gradient descent. They then cover neural networks, backpropagation, the vanishing gradient problem, batch and layer normalization, overfitting and regularization, adversarial examples, and the kernel method.

items.title: Generalized transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions of a photon and orbital angular momentum
items.summary: The coefficients of generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) that encode the canonical fermion orbital angular momentum and spin--orbit correlation do not contribute to the direct transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) and generalized-parton-distribution (GPD) projections. We present, to our knowledge, the first explicit calculation of the leading-twist, time-even, chiral-even fermion GTMDs of an on-shell real photon at zero skewness and order $α$. The coefficients $\mathcal{F}_A$ and $\mathcal{G}_A$, which multiply the $k_\perp\timesΔ_\perp$ structure, yield the fermion orbital angular momentum $\ell_z^f$ and spin--orbit correlation $\mathcal{C}_z^f$. For photon helicity $+1$, both are obtained in closed form in the leading fermion--antifermion sector and obey $\mathcal{C}_z^f=-\ell_z^f/2$ for a common transverse regulator independent of $x$, because the channel with the active fermion's spin anti-aligned with its orbital motion carries three times the integrated weight of the aligned channel.
items.author: Sujit Jana, Asmita Mukherjee, Sreeraj Nair

items.title: Low-Dimensional Data Sketches Improve Neural Posterior Estimation Efficiency
items.summary: Neural posterior estimation is a popular simulation-based inference approach that uses neural networks to approximate parameter posteriors based on simulated data. For high-dimensional observations, standard methods either rely on hand-crafted summary statistics, which require extensive scientific effort, or learn summaries from massive datasets, which can be computationally prohibitive. To overcome these challenges, researchers propose approximating parameter conditional density using low-dimensional data sketches instead of full datasets or complex summaries. The study demonstrates that for a model with a multi-dimensional parameter, a minimal number of random sketches are sufficient to achieve posterior consistency. Comparative evaluations show that this sketching method matches the performance of state-of-the-art embedding networks while significantly boosting computational efficiency.
items.author: Michael Wieck-Sosa, Cosma Rohilla Shalizi
items.original_title: Compressed Simulation-Based Inference: Neural Posterior Estimation for Massive Data via Low-Dimensional Sketches
items.original_summary: Neural posterior estimation (NPE) is a popular Bayesian simulation-based inference (SBI) approach that uses neural networks trained on simulated data--parameter pairs to approximate the posterior given a user-chosen prior. For high-dimensional observations, NPE methods typically approximate the conditional density of the parameter given a user-chosen or learned summary statistic, rather than the entire dataset, due to the curse of dimensionality. However, both approaches face challenges: hand-crafting good summaries for complex models requires considerable effort from scientists, while learning them from massive datasets can be prohibitively computationally expensive. To address these challenges, we propose approximating the conditional density of a parameter given low-dimensional sketches of the data.

items.title: Evaluating Parallel Sampling Depth and Reconstruction Thresholds in Planned Decoders
items.summary: Masked diffusion models typically sample token rounds independently, whereas planned decoders generate a coarse plan before filling in tokens in parallel. Researchers investigated when and how effectively plans save computational rounds by studying broadcast trees where token dependencies are dictated by edge correlations. Findings indicate that decoders lacking a plan require significantly more rounds below the reconstruction threshold, while planned decoders can achieve logarithmic depth. Analysis reveals that a plan provides the greatest advantage near the reconstruction threshold, provided its structural units are kept small. Exact divergence calculations within a Gaussian model further confirm these theoretical lower bounds and exponents.
items.author: Chuling Wen, Weijie Liang, Jian Lu
items.original_title: The Price of Not Planning: Parallel Sampling Depth Peaks at the Reconstruction Threshold
items.original_summary: Masked diffusion models sample the tokens of one round independently. Planned decoders first generate a coarse plan, then fill in the tokens in parallel. We ask when a plan saves rounds, how many it saves, and how fine it must be. We study this on broadcast trees: the leaves are the tokens, the internal nodes are the plan, and the edge correlation $θ$ sets how strongly tokens depend on the plan. Errors are measured by the forward Kullback-Leibler divergence $\varepsilon$, and the lower bounds hold for every deterministic value-adaptive rule, also with learned conditionals. We show that a decoder without the plan needs of order $\min\{n,(n/\varepsilon)^α\}$ rounds below the reconstruction threshold, where $α=\log b/(4\log(1/θ))$ rises to $1/2$ at the threshold, and that the exponent stays below $1/2$ above it (binary channel: $0.02\leθ\le0.98$).

items.title: A database of optical and thermal-radiative behaviour of materials under solar radiation
items.summary: Solar-matter interactions are important in many scientific and engineering applications. Modeling them needs consistent optical and thermal-radiative properties over the full solar spectrum. Here we present SpaderOptics, a database for 21 materials: metals, oxides, semiconductors, polymers, ceramics, and carbon. It compiles wavelength-dependent refractive indices and extinction coefficients from the literature. Each literature source is kept separate, together with its original conditions. One physics-based calculation chain turns these data into reflectivity, transmissivity, absorptivity, and emissivity for different incidence angles, slab thicknesses, and temperatures. Combined with the Air Mass Zero (AM0) solar spectrum, the properties give absorbed, reflected, and transmitted solar flux for concentrated sunlight.
items.author: Vasiliki E. Alexopoulou, Nikolaos Karalis, Konstantinos Asimakopoulos et al.

items.title: Pulsar Timing Correlations Induced by Stochastic Spin-2 Ultralight Dark Matter
items.summary: Ultralight dark matter (ULDM) can generate time-dependent gravitational perturbations, providing a potential signal for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). In Galactic halos, the velocity dispersion of ULDM gives rise to finite spatial coherence, which influences the correlations between pulsar timing signals. In this work, we derive the timing-residual cross-correlations induced by rapid metric oscillations of spin-2 ULDM, allowing for general polarization statistics. Under equipartition among the five polarization modes, the intrinsic angular kernel contains monopole and quadrupole components and exhibits an angular profile closely resembling that of spin-1 ULDM, suggesting a potential degeneracy between the two ULDM candidates in PTA observations.
items.author: Hao-Xuan Shi, Yu-Mei Wu, Chang Liu

items.title: Mono-Z Signatures of Vector Dark Matter Detection at Future Electron-Positron Colliders: FCC-ee and ILC
items.summary: We investigate the mono-$Z$ signature of a vector dark matter (VDM) model at future electron-positron colliders. In this model, a stable vector boson, arising from an extended $U(1)$ gauge symmetry, serves as a viable DM candidate that interacts with the Standard Model (SM) through a Higgs portal. We perform a detailed cut-based analysis for the mono-$Z$ channel at the FCC-ee (with $\sqrt{s}=240$ and $365$ GeV) and the ILC (with $\sqrt{s}=1$ TeV), considering both leptonic and hadronic decays of the $Z$ boson. Signal significances are evaluated for benchmark points using fast event simulation with MadGraph5, PYTHIA8, and Delphes3. Our results demonstrate that future $e^+e^-$ colliders provide excellent sensitivity to Higgs-portal VDM, with the ILC's beam polarization offering an additional handle to suppress SM backgrounds.
items.author: Seyed Yaser Ayazi, Saeid Paktinat Mehdiabadi, Rouzbeh Rouzbehi

items.title: Hybrid Optimization-Generative Motion Planning for Multiagent Affine Formations
items.summary: Formation maneuver control enables a multiagent system to cooperatively navigate through constrained environments in collective motion. While various formation controllers exist, they rely heavily on high-quality and dynamically feasible reference trajectories provided a priori, making formation motion planning (FMP) essential. To address the computational challenges for high-dimensional joint trajectories faced by conventional constrained optimization-based solutions, this paper introduces a hybrid optimization-generative framework with a focus on affine formations, which provide the necessary spatial flexibility. By formulating the planning task as a constrained Maximum-a-Posteriori estimation, we decouple multiagent objectives to leverage pre-trained single-agent diffusion priors for dynamic feasibility, obstacle avoidance, and smoothness.
items.author: Zhonggang Li, Hongyu Zhou, Raj Thilak Rajan

items.title: A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth
items.summary: We present a transferable Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB) model for bismuth with explicit spin-orbit coupling that enables exploration of the structural degrees of freedom governing topological properties with minimal computational resources. We have used our DFTB model to run high-throughput calculations at a scale that would be significantly more expensive with standard Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) to determine a strain-buckling map of electronic and topological properties for bismuthene, where we identify regions of band gap closure and band inversion as a function of structural parameters. We show that our approach yields an accurate band structure for the rhombohedral phase, where small band gaps exist at or near time-reversal-invariant momentum (TRIM) points.
items.author: Nir Goldman, Ben Hourahine

items.title: A boson representation of the electronic structure calculation based on the quantum Krylov subspace algorithm
items.summary: Quantum calculations are expected to broaden the range of strongly correlated phenomena in solids accessible to first-principles calculations. The quantum Krylov diagonalization method, or in a broader sense, the quantum subspace expansion method (QSE) offers an advantage over other variational methods in terms of numerical stability. In this work, we propose a boson representation of electronic systems with the aim of reducing QSE quantum circuit depth, where electron-hole pair bosons serve as the fundamental degrees of freedom. We benchmark the boson representation in comparison with a corresponding fermionic QSE and CCSD for an equidistant and a dimerized configuration of a periodic hydrogen chain \ce{(H2)_n}.
items.author: Hiroki Katow, Hisao Nakamura

items.title: Jim Mirandy Transitions from Contractor to Civil Servant at NASA Stennis
items.summary: Jim Mirandy has transitioned from a long-term contractor to a civil servant at NASA's Stennis Space Center in Mississippi. Hired under a workforce directive to restore core competencies, Mirandy serves as a quality assurance specialist and close call investigator. Growing up with a father who worked in the aerospace industry, Mirandy developed an early interest in fixing things and problem-solving. After starting his career hands-on as a mechanic working on the Space Shuttle External Tank, he shifted his focus toward safety and quality operations. At NASA Stennis, he contributes to institutional safety through employee committees, training programs, and rigorous testing oversight that supports missions like the Artemis program.
items.author: LaToya Dean
items.original_title: Contractor to Civil Servant: NASA Welcomes Jim Mirandy
items.original_summary: The rumble of a rocket engine might be considered a soundtrack for Jim Mirandy’s life. Mirandy has grown up with NASA as a constant presence, and his path to becoming a civil servant at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, has been decades in the making. Hired under the agency’s workforce directive […]

items.title: Immersive virtual reality in learning physics: a systematic review of opportunities and challenges
items.summary: Immersive virtual reality (IVR) can heighten presence and enable active, embodied interaction in realistic 3D environments, which has been associated with potential benefits in physics education. This article presents a comprehensive review of IVR implementation in physics education at both school and university levels. The analysis included 34 studies indexed in Scopus and ERIC, published between 1 January 2018 and 1 June 2025. Methodologically, this review followed a preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses approach. IVR implementations for physics learning were assessed, topic-aligned activity types were summarized, and associated opportunities and challenges were documented. Findings indicate that IVR can support physics learning by providing complementary visualizations, optimizing cognitive load, enabling haptic learning, saving time, and fostering collaborative inquiry.
items.author: Andrej Vidak, Iva Movre Šapić, Vjeran Gomzi et al.

items.title: Deterministic nonlinear domain engineering algorithm with variable sub-coherence-length domains
items.summary: We present a new and improved deterministic algorithm that calculates the poling domains for the implementation of arbitrary phase-matching functions (PMF) in quasi-phase-matched nonlinear crystals for parametric down-conversion photon sources. In contrast to previous work, the algorithm presented here makes full use of the limits of the fabrication process, such as the minimum feature size and resolution of the lithographic process underpinning the poling procedure. This minimizes the tracking error to the target electric field and improves the accuracy in reaching the desired PMF. We give a tutorial on how to calculate the target function for arbitrary PMFs and run the algorithm.
items.author: Michael Schlosser, Tommaso Faleo, Gregor Weihs et al.

items.title: Allosteric Inhibition Reverses Hydrocephalus Caused by Shp2 Mutation in Mice
items.summary: Researchers discovered that the catalytically inactive Shp2 C459S mutation leads to communicating hydrocephalus in mice by impairing ciliary development and motility, differing from mutations that alter neurogenesis. Brain tissues from mutant mice exhibited elevated GAB1 and AKT phosphorylation, pointing to dysregulated PI3K-AKT signaling as the underlying cause. The study revealed that pharmacological inhibition of PI3K successfully rescues ciliogenesis defects and alleviates hydrocephalus. Furthermore, using the allosteric SHP2 inhibitor SHP099 increased the thermal stability of the mutant protein and reduced hydrocephalus symptoms. These insights demonstrate that the condition is driven by structural conformational changes rather than catalytic activity, highlighting the therapeutic potential of conformation-specific allosteric inhibitors.
items.author: Neoklis Makrides, Emily Sun, Hilal Mir et al.
items.original_title: Allosteric inhibition rescues hydrocephalus caused by catalytically inactive Shp2 in mice
items.original_summary: by Neoklis Makrides, Emily Sun, Hilal Mir, Jen-Zen Chuang, Ziyuan Jiang, Yihua Wu, Carlos Serra, John Peregrin, Qian Wang, Wellington V. Cardoso, Ching-Hwa Sung, Neel H. Shah, Xin Zhang SHP2, a protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) crucial in Ras-MAPK signaling, is associated with various human congenital diseases and cancers. Here, we show that the catalytically inactive Shp2 C459S mutation results in communicating hydrocephalus, similar to the catalytically activating Shp2 E76K and Mek1 DD mutants. Unlike previous mutants, however, Shp2 C459S/+ mutation uniquely affects ciliary development rather than neurogenesis, leading to structural abnormalities in cilia and impaired ciliary motility. Differential scanning fluorimetry suggested that SHP2 C459S , SHP2 E76K , and SHP2 C459S/E76K mutations all induce an open SHP2 conformation, but only SHP2 C459S leads to aberrant GAB1 phosphorylation in cells expressing wild-type SHP2.

items.title: Dendritic Depolarization Block Enables Single Neurons to Perform XOR Computation
items.summary: Using biologically realistic modeling, researchers demonstrated that single neurons can perform complex exclusive-or logic computations through dendritic depolarization block rather than relying solely on multilayer networks. Voltage-gated calcium channels facilitate a non-monotonic input-output relationship where moderate asynchronous drive generates spikes, but excessive drive causes a sustained plateau that suppresses output. This XOR-like computation is strictly governed by the temporal distribution of synaptic inputs rather than their spatial arrangement. The process remains robust across various dendritic configurations but fails under synchronous activation. Cross-morphological validation confirms that this frequency-synapse-count trade-off serves as a generalized biophysical mechanism for neural information processing.
items.author: Yanheng Li, Xiaojuan Sun, Yunliang Zang
items.original_title: Neuronal XOR computation requires temporally activated synaptic information
items.original_summary: by Yanheng Li, Xiaojuan Sun, Yunliang Zang Single neurons can perform complex exclusive-or (XOR) computation which is conventionally thought to need multilayer networks, yet the biophysical mechanisms and the robustness of such computations under stochastic synaptic drive remain unclear. Using biologically realistic modeling, we demonstrate that dendritic depolarization block provides a universal and robust mechanism for XOR-like computation. Voltage-gated calcium channels enable a non-monotonic input-output relationship: moderate asynchronous drive evokes spiking, whereas excessive drive induces a sustained plateau that suppresses output, naturally implementing XOR logic computation. This computation is strictly gated by temporal distribution of synaptic inputs rather than spatial distribution; the XOR-like response is robust across diverse dendritic configurations but collapses under synchronous activation.

items.title: New Framework Improves Epidemic Control Despite Incomplete Observation Data
items.summary: Incomplete reporting, testing limits, and asymptomatic infections often distort epidemic-control policies. To address this, researchers developed a three-stage computational epidemiology framework combining observation modeling, state reconstruction, and policy optimization. The approach extends a metapopulation SEIQR model and introduces ODE-DynNet, a hybrid model that uses mobility-coupled epidemic dynamics and graph-temporal learning to infer hidden infection states. Coordinated testing and isolation are then framed as a multi-agent reinforcement learning problem. Testing the pipeline with community mobility data from Shenzhen, China, demonstrated an 88% reduction in infection costs compared to decoupled policies using raw proxy data, showing that explicit state reconstruction effectively supports epidemic control under surveillance gaps.
items.author: Shang Wang, Yuxiao Luo, Yunduan Cui et al.
items.original_title: Epidemic control under incomplete observations through mechanistic state reconstruction and multi-agent learning
items.original_summary: by Shang Wang, Yuxiao Luo, Yunduan Cui, Meng Zhang, Min Kang, Ling Yin Epidemic-control policies are usually optimized from reported infection states, but these reports are often incomplete because testing capacity, reporting behavior, delays, and asymptomatic infections vary across regions and time. Such observation gaps can distort the state used by the controller and lead to suboptimal testing and isolation decisions. We develop a three-stage computational epidemiology framework that links observation modeling, state reconstruction, and policy optimization. First, we extend a metapopulation SEIQR model to represent fully observable, steady partially observable, and non-steady partially observable surveillance regimes. Second, we introduce ODE-DynNet, a hybrid reconstruction model that combines mobility-coupled epidemic dynamics with graph-temporal learning to infer hidden infection states from distorted observations.

items.title: New Agent-Based Framework Evaluates Pneumococcal Vaccine Strategies
items.summary: Streptococcus pneumoniae remains a major global pathogen responsible for severe pneumonia and invasive bacterial diseases. Although pneumococcal conjugate vaccines have been widely deployed, their long-term effectiveness has often been undermined by serotype replacement, prompting the development of broader-coverage vaccines with lower individual immunogenicity. To assess the long-term effects of these newer formulations, researchers have introduced a flexible agent-based modeling framework that incorporates immunity, carriage, and clinical models. Unlike older paradigms that group serotypes strictly by vaccine type, this novel approach tracks individual serotype dynamics over time. The model's versatility was validated through a retrospective analysis tracking the sequential introduction of 7- and 13-valent pneumococcal vaccines in Australia.
items.author: Nefel Tellioglu, David J. Price, Xinghui Chen et al.
items.original_title: A flexible agent-based modelling framework of multi-serotype pneumococcal carriage to evaluate vaccine strategies in large populations
items.original_summary: by Nefel Tellioglu, David J. Price, Xinghui Chen, Violeta Spirkoska, Cyan Yingying Wang, Robert Moss, Natalie Carvalho, Kylie S. Carville, Patricia Therese Campbell, Jodie McVernon Streptococcus pneumoniae is a multi-serotype pathogen causing a substantial global burden of pneumonia and invasive bacterial disease. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines have been implemented worldwide, protecting against colonisation and disease from selected high-burden serotypes, but in many settings short-term effectiveness has been eroded by serotype replacement. Vaccines with broader serotype coverage have been developed, at the cost of immunogenicity against single serotypes. To determine the longer-term impact of these new formulations, we propose a novel modelling framework that evaluates the relationship between serotype-specific vaccine immunogenicity and effectiveness, comprising immunity, carriage and clinical models.
