items.title: Microstate-specific functional connectivity in alcohol use disorder using resting-state EEG.
items.summary: Introduction Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) is often described as a "disconnection syndrome", reflecting neural dysfunction associated with chronic alcohol use. However, previous studies on functional connectivity of resting-state EEG (rsEEG) in AUD have reported inconsistent findings, possibly due to overlooking the brain's dynamic nature. Methods We examined rsEEG in 26 young adults with AUD and 35 healthy controls (HC), using microstate analysis to characterise transient brain states and to estimate functional connectivity within each state. Results Although microstate map topologies were comparable between the two groups, the temporal dynamics of the AUD group were biased towards microstates C and D.
items.author: Park H, Yoo SY, Lee H, Park M, Choi JS, Chung D.

items.title: Label-free multi-metric pipeline for reproducible clustering of single-cell RNA-seq cell types.
items.summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing has transformed our ability to identify cell types and explore cellular diversity. However, determining whether apparent cell subtypes represent true biological populations or artifacts of data analysis remains a major challenge. To address this issue, we developed scClustBench, an open-source benchmarking framework that evaluates cluster quality, stability, and reproducibility across multiple analytical approaches. Rather than relying on a single clustering method, scClustBench tests whether proposed cell subtypes can be consistently recovered. We applied scClustBench to a mouse retinal dataset containing bipolar cells, which are known to exhibit subtype diversity, and rod photoreceptors, for which subtype classification remains controversial.
items.author: Yousef Z, Simone J, Klein D, Bhuyan A, Cho HJ, Bhatt P, Wu J, Wang H, Cai L.

items.title: MHC class II deficiency in Algeria: Delineating the clinical, immunological, and genetic spectrum.
items.summary: MHC class II deficiency is the most frequent combined immunodeficiency (CID) in the Maghreb, yet its phenotypic and molecular spectrum remains incompletely defined. Herein, we characterized 46 Algerian patients at the clinical, immunologic, and molecular levels. Disease onset was typically early, with a median age of 4.5 mo, while the clinical course was highly heterogeneous, ranging from severe, rapidly progressive disease to milder phenotypes with survival into adulthood. Recurrent infections were a universal feature, with protracted diarrhea (80.4%), recurrent pneumonia (71.7%), and oral candidiasis (54.3%) being the most common manifestations. CD4 lymphopenia occurred in 87% of patients, although lymphocyte profiles ranged from near-normal to SCID-like.
items.author: Tahiat A, Cuollo L, Buta Panov S, Hakem S, Touri S, Saad-Djaballah A, Bendahmane C, Ketfi A, Yagoubi A, Belbouab R, Smati L, Boukari R, Rosenzweig SD, Notarangelo LD, Benakli M, Bogunovic D, Djenouhat K.

items.title: Familial Ovarian Teratoma With Neural Tissue Expression and Anti-NMDAR Encephalitis.
items.summary: Objectives Anti-N-methyl-d-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) encephalitis is frequently associated with ovarian teratoma. We report an extremely rare parent-child occurrence of teratoma-associated anti-NMDAR encephalitis, with pathologic findings and human leukocyte antigen (HLA) typing. Methods Ovarian teratoma specimens were examined for GluN1 and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) by immunohistochemistry, and HLA typing was performed using next-generation sequencing . Results The mother and daughter developed anti-NMDAR encephalitis at 29 and 12 years of age, respectively, with ovarian teratomas. Both were positive for CSF anti-NMDAR antibodies, and teratomatous neural tissue was GluN1-positive. In addition, the daughter was positive for serum MOG antibody. Early immunotherapy and tumor resection led to favorable neurologic recovery.
items.author: Maeda K, Kimoto Y, Kojima K, Mori N, Mori K, Hidaka N, Miyamoto M, Fujisaki M, Hirata T, Moriguchi S, Chong PF, Sakai Y, Moritake H.

items.title: Transcriptional repression of central spindle genes marks the transition to endomitosis in the C. elegans intestine.
items.summary: During development, many cell types transition from canonical to noncanonical cell cycles, such as endomitosis and endoreplication, in which they duplicate their DNA but do not divide, giving rise to polyploidy. Little is known about the regulation of endomitosis, where cells enter M phase but do not perform cytokinesis. Here, we investigate how cells initiate and execute endomitosis in the Caenorhabditis elegans intestine and find that endomitotic cells fail to assemble a central spindle or initiate cytokinetic furrowing. We find that endomitotic cells transcriptionally repress multiple cytokinesis regulators, especially the central spindle factors ZEN-4MKLP1, CYK-4RACGAP1, and SPD-1PRC1. Intestinal cells lose the capacity to perform cytokinesis in late embryogenesis, and we find that the conserved DREAM (DP, RB-related, E2F, and MuvB) complex is involved in the repression of central spindle genes.
items.author: Barrull-Mascaró R, Veltkamp S, Boutaibi S, van Rijnberk LM, Lippmann R, Galli M.

items.title: Novel CYBB variant causing exon 5 skipping in a patient with X-linked chronic granulomatous disease.
items.summary: We report a novel hemizygous CYBB variant (c.483G>C) in a 4-year-old boy with X-linked chronic granulomatous disease. The variant affects the last nucleotide of exon 5 and causes exon 5 skipping, confirmed by cDNA analysis. Dihydrorhodamine assay showed absent neutrophil oxidative burst. These findings establish the variant as pathogenic and expand the spectrum of splicing defects in CGD.
items.author: Aleksenko M, Varlamova T, Lodoeva O, Kieva A, Raykina E.

items.title: Pain Pathophysiology and Assessment in Pediatric Critical Care.
items.summary: Pain is pervasive and affects upwards of 59% of critically ill children. Consequences of severe pain include worsened health related quality of life and longer lengths of stay. Evaluating pain in non-verbal critically ill children is a unique challenge due to difficulties with communication and the wide variety of developmental stages. The purpose of our review is to examine the underlying pathophysiology of pain, the current landscape in pain assessment of non-verbal critically ill children and pain assessment tools for non-verbal critically ill children. We performed literature searches from April 25, 2023 to November 20, 2025; we performed literature searches using PubMed and EMBASE with a combination of keywords that included "pain", "pathophysiology", "pediatric", "comfort-behavioral", "FLACC", "P-CPOT", "ventilated", "PICU".
items.author: Leong AY, Alladin-Karan A, Niven DJ, Doig CJ.

items.title: A Narrative Review on Medicinal Plants of Gilgit-Baltistan: Phytochemical Evidence, Environmental Variation, and Conservation Priorities.
items.summary: Medicinal plant traditions are promoted in the various alpine habitats of Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan; however, local use is often discussed in relation to the pharmacological results obtained from other places. This narrative review explores the role of identity, provenance, extraction, and environmental diversity in the understanding and translation of evidence. A focused literature update was performed on October 11, 2026, using web-assisted searches of PubMed, PubMed Central, and publisher websites, citation tracing, and valid taxonomic data. In all, 60 focal and contextual taxa are evaluated; this purposeful set is not a floristic inventory. Evidence was grouped by study design, with safety and conservation evaluated separately.
items.author: Ismail M, Abbas Q, Khan S, Law D, Malik FA, Naqvi STA.

items.title: Genotype and Medium Interactions Controlling Androgenic Callus Induction, Somatic Embryogenesis, and Shoot Regeneration in Stevia rebaudiana (Bertoni).
items.summary: Stevia rebaudiana (Bertoni) is an economically important medicinal plant, yet efficient androgenesis protocols remain highly genotype- and medium-dependent. This study evaluated androgenic response, callus induction, somatic embryogenesis, and plant regeneration of three cultivars (Levent 93, Turgut 82, and Tütüncü) across seven culture media and determined the ploidy status of regenerated plants. Anthers were incubated in darkness for 10 days to induce embryogenesis. Levent 93 exhibited the highest callus induction (47.43%) and embryo production (3.38 embryos per anther). Medium T4 (Murashige and Skoog (MS) + 2.0 mg L -1 1-naphthaleneacetic acid (NAA) + 0.5 mg L -1 6-benzylaminopurine (BAP)) was most effective, followed by T2 and T3.
items.author: Nasir N, Turgut K.

items.title: Limited Yield Response of Potato to Foliar Nanosilicon Under Water Deficit.
items.summary: Silicon dioxide nanoparticles (SiO 2 -NPs) have been proposed as a foliar treatment to support crop performance under limited water availability, but their effects on potato yield require evaluation across doses and genotypes. We tested 0, 25, and 50 mg L -1 SiO 2 -NPs in three potato genotypes (Agria, Javid, and Rona) under a well-watered control and two water-deficit regimes in a greenhouse experiment with three blocks and 81 pots. The experiment ran from 25 April to 22 July 2025. Because original substrate moisture-retention calibration and target pot-mass records were unavailable for independent verification, the water regimes nominally designated as -0.30 and -0.60 MPa are reported as protocol labels rather than verified matric potentials.
items.author: Mahmoodabad RZ, Tobeh A, Sheikhzadeh P, Hassanpanah D, Jahanbakhsh S.

items.title: Shared frontal E/I imbalance but selective alpha oscillatory collapse in depression comorbid with chronic pain.
items.author: Chen H, Ju P, Hu Z, Chen Y, Gao H, Cheng J, Meng S, Ling Y, Xu J, Yan J, Li C, Gao J, Xia Q, Zhu C.

items.title: Lower serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels are associated with greater fracture complexity in adult orthopaedic trauma patients: an OTA/AO classification-based cross-sectional study.
items.summary: Background Vitamin D deficiency is common among orthopaedic trauma patients, but its relationship with fracture morphology remains unclear, particularly in Latin American adult trauma populations. Methods The authors conducted an analytical cross-sectional study at 2 tertiary hospitals in Quito, Ecuador, from March 2023 to May 2025. Among 400 consecutive fracture patients, serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] was available in 136; after excluding patients younger than 18 years, 126 adults were analyzed. Fracture complexity was classified using the main OTA/AO morphological groups as an ordinal outcome: type A, simple; type B, wedge; and type C, multifragmentary/complex. Serum 25(OH)D was analyzed continuously and categorized descriptively as deficient, insufficient, or sufficient.
items.author: Barros Castro AX, Barros Prieto E, Ballesteros Ponce C, Noboa Freile CE, Peñaherrera C, Endara F.

items.title: Early deep infection after operatively managed low-velocity tibial gunshot fractures is associated with older age, temporary external fixation, and longer time to definitive fixation.
items.summary: Objectives The aim of this study was to determine postoperative infection rates and identify factors associated with deep infection in low-velocity tibial gunshot wound (GSW) fractures managed operatively. Design This is a retrospective cohort study. Setting The setting includes a Level 1 urban trauma center. Patients/participants The participants in this study are adult patients with operatively managed tibial fractures resulting from low-velocity GSWs treated between 2015 and 2024. Inclusion required operative fixation, 48 hours of postoperative intravenous antibiotics, and a minimum of 3 months of follow-up. A total of 113 patients with 116 tibial fractures met the inclusion criteria. Intervention Intervention included operative fixation of tibial GSW fractures with a uniform 48-hour postoperative intravenous antibiotic regimen.
items.author: Boutany M, Abdelnour D, Jandali D, Tobia J, Elmenini H, Nasr K, Vaidya R.

items.title: A Phase 1, Dose Escalation Study of Lenalidomide and Ibrutinib for Relapsed/Refractory Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia.
items.summary: Introduction BTK inhibitors have transformed the treatment of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL), but strategies to deepen and prolong response are needed. Lenalidomide is active in CLL/SLL through a non-overlapping mechanism but is limited by toxicity. We evaluated lenalidomide combined with ibrutinib in relapsed/refractory (R/R) CLL/SLL. Methods In this multicenter, phase 1, 3+3 dose-escalation study, patients with R/R CLL/SLL after ≥ 1 prior therapy received a 28-day ibrutinib run-in (420 mg daily), then added lenalidomide with intra-patient escalation to a cohort-assigned maximum of 2.5, 5, 7.5, or 10 mg daily. Lenalidomide was stopped after 12 cycles; ibrutinib continued until progression or intolerance.
items.author: Bair SM, Byrd JC, Gutman J, Phelps M, Johnson AJ, Fakhri B, Rogers KA, Woyach JA, Grever MR, Kamdar M, Coutre SE, Pollyea DA.

items.title: Perioperative antiplatelet use is not associated with increased risk of mortality among older adults undergoing operative hip fracture repair.
items.summary: Objectives To assess whether perioperative antiplatelet use increases mortality risk among older adults undergoing operative hip fracture repair. Methods Design Retrospective study. Setting Level 1 trauma center. Patient selection criteria A total of 965 patients 65 years or older who underwent surgical fixation for hip fractures (OTA/OA 31A, 31B and 31C) between 2018 and 2023. Outcome measures and comparisons The primary outcome was mortality at 365 days after discharge. Secondary outcomes were mortality at 30 days and 90 days, length of stay (LOS) > 7 days, need for blood transfusion, and 30-day readmission. Statistical methods Multivariate Cox proportional hazards models assessed the association between antiplatelet use and mortality.
items.author: Akodu M, Rajesh D, Steele A, Aung N, Zhang C, McTague M, DesRoches C, Wixted J, Agarwal-Harding K, Appleton P, Rodriguez E, Olveczky D, Chahal K.

items.title: Potential Association Between Antibiotics and Atrial Fibrillation: A Review of Current Evidence and Mechanistic Insights.
items.summary: Antibiotic-associated cardiotoxicity has traditionally been discussed in relation to QT prolongation and torsade de pointes. A possible association between antibiotic exposure and atrial fibrillation (AF) has also been reported, but infection itself is an established AF trigger. This review distinguishes observational epidemiology, pharmacovigilance analyses, clinical case reports, and experimental studies when considering antibiotic classes and proposed mechanisms. Pharmacovigilance findings include AF reporting associations for macrolides, whereas much of the cardiovascular evidence for fluoroquinolones concerns QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmias. AF-specific clinical evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Proposed pathways include electrolyte disturbances, autonomic effects, drug interactions, inflammatory or allergic reactions, myocardial injury, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and gut dysbiosis.
items.author: Ono K.

items.title: Impact of Center Volume on Access to Pancreas Transplantation and Waiting List Mortality: A 25-y Eurotransplant Experience.
items.summary: Background Pancreas transplantation remains among the few treatments able to restore sustained insulin independence in selected patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus, yet annual transplant numbers have declined across the Eurotransplant region. Previous work has linked center volume to posttransplant graft and patient survival, but its influence on access to transplantation and waiting list mortality remains incompletely characterized. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study of 6672 patients listed for vascularized pancreas transplantation within Eurotransplant between 2000 and 2024. Centers were classified each year by tertile of annual transplant volume into low-, medium-, and high-volume categories. Cumulative incidence functions for transplantation and waiting list mortality were estimated using the Aalen-Johansen estimator.
items.author: Filipe MD, van Bruchem M, Arbogast H, de Buijzer E, Gillard P, Györi G, Jadrijevic S, Jens A, Jacobs-Tulleneers-Thevissen D, Kahl A, Ludwig B, Moers C, Petric M, Poljak M, Schnitzbauer A, Stiegler P, Szakaly P, Tautenhahn HM, Telkes G, Tomazic A, Vogel T, Huurman V, Öllinger R.

items.title: Transplant Access, Waitlist Outcomes, and Survival Among Candidates With Lung-Liver Listing Intent Before and After Continuous Distribution.
items.summary: Background Continuous distribution using the Composite Allocation Score (CAS) was implemented to broaden access in lung allocation, but its effects on candidates with lung-liver listing intent remain incompletely defined. Methods We studied adult lung candidates listed January 1, 2018, through March 31, 2026, using Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network/United Network for Organ Sharing thoracic Standard Transplant Analysis and Research data. The primary waitlist outcomes were transplantation and death or removal for being too sick, analyzed as competing events using Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence functions and Fine-Gray models. One-year posttransplant survival was assessed among recipients with verified candidate-to-recipient linkage and complete survival data, using transplant center-clustered Cox models.
items.author: Kadir S, Sasidharan S, Shahmohammadi A, Al-Bayati S, Rozenbaum G, Tran S, Belli E, Pelaez A.

items.title: Current Status of Pain-Related Patient-Reported Outcomes and Perioperative Pain Management among 40,785 Patients: A Prospective Multicenter Study.
items.summary: This study analyzed self-reported pain-related outcomes of 40,785 surgical patients from 125 centers collected by CAPOPS (China Acute Postoperative Pain Study) between September 2019 and August 2023, to characterize the current status of acute postoperative pain management protocols and pain prognoses in Chinese medical institutions. Every participant completed the International Pain Outcome Questionnaire on the first postoperative day. Patient self-reported pain outcomes were assessed across the domains of pain severity, interference with activities and emotional well-being, adverse events, and perception of care. Outcome differences across geographic regions, time periods, and surgical types were analyzed. Risk factors associated with severe pain (score ≥ 7 on a 0-10 scale) were also evaluated with logistic regression.
items.author: Liu Y, Lv X, Li H, Yang H, Hou A, Han S, Wang J, Li L, Wu J, Hou D, Li F, Zhang Z, Diao Y, Han Y, Yang JJ, Zhang J, Mi W.

items.title: Ambient temperature and the global sewage resistome: shifts in clinically relevant bacterial genera.
items.summary: Objectives Temperature has been proposed as a driver of antimicrobial resistance, but global analyses have not separated it from socioeconomic conditions or determined how it acts. We tested its association with the sewage resistome and whether this operates through bacterial community composition. Methods We analysed 1084 sewage metagenomes from 337 cities in 104 countries (2016-2021), with 30-day mean air temperature before collection as the exposure. Resistome composition was compared using PERMANOVA, adjusted for WHO region, sampling year and seven socioeconomic and healthcare covariates. We assessed mediation by bacterial community composition, examined 12 genera on the 2024 WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List, and tested within-city consistency over time in five European cities.
items.author: Khurana MP, Scheidwasser N, Pust N, Duchêne DA, Bhatt S.

items.title: An interpretable physics-informed graph neural network for forecasting longitudinal tau progression in Alzheimer's disease.
items.summary: Forecasting the progression of tau pathology by modeling its spatiotemporal dynamics is critical for characterizing Alzheimer's disease (AD), where tau is a key driver of disease progression. Tau is an important prognostic biomarker for AD and is a primary endpoint for many ongoing clinical therapeutic trials. Tau burden can be quantified in vivo using positron emission tomography (PET), while its propagation is hypothesized to follow the structural connectome derived from diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), providing a framework for modeling network-driven tau spread. Deep learning approaches, particularly graph neural networks (GNNs), enable data-driven learning of regional changes in tau burden by leveraging brain connectivity.
items.author: Balaji V, Song TA, Yang F, Wang Z, Dutta J.

items.title: Development of subunit-based vaccine against Mpox and evaluation of immune response.
items.summary: Mpox, endemic to Central and West Africa, has recently seen a rise in cases in non-endemic regions, emphasizing the need for specific vaccines. The Mpox virus (MPXV) produces two infectious virions: intracellular mature virions (IMvs) and extracellular enveloped virions (EEvs). IMVs mediate host-to-host transmission, while EEvs facilitate viral dissemination within tissues. This study aimed to develop and evaluate recombinant protein-based vaccine formulations targeting MPXV A29L (IMV), A30L (IMV), and A35R (EEV) proteins to enhance immune responses. Four alum-adjuvanted recombinant protein vaccine formulations containing A29L, A30L and A35R antigens were developed based on the high sequence homology of MPXV with variola and vaccinia viruses.
items.author: Soydam S, Varan G, Turegun Atasoy B, Tavukcuoglu E.

items.title: An alternative approach may offer protection against serious pneumococcal infections: a plain language summary of preclinical studies.
items.author: Stevenson TC, Burke H, Roggensack SE, Pratt A, Hossain A, Ghosh P, Besin G, Lu Y, Zhang F, Malley R, Srokowski C, Willer DO, Sebastian S.

items.title: Revising the imposter phenomenon: a social perspective on the development and manifestation of the imposter phenomenon among medical students.
items.summary: Imposter Phenomenon (IP) describes the internal experience of perceived intellectual insincerity, marked by fear of exposure as an intellectual fraud. Research underscores a high prevalence amongst medical students. To date, IP has largely been recognised as an internal, psychological experience. This study expands this perspective by exploring the complex social environments that shape the development, manifestation, and perpetuation of IP. It offers a novel dimension to understanding IP within the context of medical education. A mixed methods approach was employed, combining quantitative data from 315 survey respondents with qualitative insights from focus group discussions. 71.7% of respondents experienced clinically significant IP (CIPS ≥ 62), with female students reporting higher median scores (73.00) than males (66.50, p = .003).
items.author: Pallett W, Black E, Thewlis D.

items.title: Noninvasive inference of presymptomatic abiotic stress in Solanum Lycopersicum from latent electrophysiological dynamics via action potential-based model.
items.summary: Early detection of abiotic stress in Solanum lycopersicum is critical for yield protection, yet current methods rely on visible symptoms that manifest only after irreversible physiological damage. Plant action potentials (APs), which directly reflect ion channel activity across the plasma membrane, represent an underexplored avenue for presymptomatic, noninvasive stress detection. We hypothesized that stress-induced alterations in ion channel activity would produce measurable changes in AP waveform morphology before visible symptoms appeared. One hundred sixty S. lycopersicum cv. Moneymaker plants, spanning two prospectively defined cohorts (80 for classifier development, 80 for detection-window quantification), were assigned to control, salinity (100 mM NaCl), osmotic (PEG-6000, -0.4 MPa), or K⁺/N deficiency groups.
items.author: Wu J, Pachori R, Kwon Y.

items.title: Engineering the β-cell microenvironment: a critical strategy for insulin-producing cell survival and therapeutic applications.
items.summary: Insulin-producing cells (IPCs) generated from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) are a promising cell source for β-cell replacement therapy in patients with diabetes. Despite substantial advances, optimizing IPC differentiation efficiency and maturation, as well as long-term functional stability after transplantation, remains challenging. One strategy to enhance IPC function and survival is to utilize native extracellular matrix (ECM) components present within the pancreatic islet niche. ECM components activate intracellular signaling pathways essential for cell adhesion, survival, and insulin gene expression. Researchers have developed various scaffolds to reconstitute these components in vitro . This review integrates current insights into ECM-IPC interactions, focusing on scaffold composition, physical properties, and bioactive modifications that enhance IPC viability and function and discusses how these scaffold properties could improve the outcomes of β-cell replacement therapy in diabetes.
items.author: Rezaei-Larijani M, Larijani B, Tahamtani Y, Aghayan HR, Kazemi Ashtiani M.

items.title: Severe mixed avian pox outbreak with atypically extensive cutaneous lesions in commercial free-range layer pullets with a reported fowlpox vaccination history.
items.summary: Avian pox is a globally distributed viral disease of domestic and wild birds that typically presents as cutaneous or diphtheritic lesions and is commonly controlled through vaccination. However, severe or atypical outbreaks in vaccinated flocks remain incompletely characterized, particularly under semi-intensive management and low-biosecurity conditions. Here, we describe a severe mixed form of avian pox with atypically extensive cutaneous involvement in a commercial free-range layer pullet flock with a reported fowlpox vaccination history in northeastern Brazil. Of the 180 birds in the flock, approximately 40% developed disseminated nodular cutaneous lesions affecting both feathered and non-feathered skin, while 20% exhibited conjunctivitis and respiratory signs.
items.author: Sousa RT, Barbosa FMS, Silva MLCR, Tavares Linhares M, Eloy LRC, Araújo Júnior JP, Dantas Malossi C, Sequetin Cunha M, Carvalho LRRA, Lucena RB.

items.title: Comment on: "Motivation and barriers to physicians' academic career in gastroenterology in France".
items.author: McCanny A.

items.title: Heart rate variability and calcium economy in sarcoidosis: the role of parathyroid hormone.
items.summary: Background Sarcoidosis (SA) dysregulates calcium metabolism, causing relatively suppressed/low normal parathyroid hormone (PTH). Autonomic dysfunction, assessed by heart rate variability (HRV), occurs in SA-related cardiac/neurological involvement. Their relationship in SA remains uncharacterized. Methods Cross-sectional analysis of 373 SA patients, having 24-h HRV and calcium measurements. Spearman correlations were computed for 11 HRV indices against 5 calcium parameters (PTH, serum calcium, urinary calcium, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (1,25(OH) 2 D), and 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D)). Multivariable linear regression models were constructed, adjusting for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), cardiac involvement, corticosteroid use, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus. Results The short-term fractal scaling exponent of detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA1) ( r = -0.202, p = 0.0001, q = 0.005, n = 370), low-frequency (LF) power ( r = -0.165, q = 0.027) and the LF-to-high-frequency ratio (LF/HF) ( r = -0.140, q = 0.042) were inversely correlated with PTH.
items.author: Giallafos E, Katsarou O, Oikonomou E, Tryfou E, Kolilekas L, Lama N, Katsanos S, Seitaridi G, Zisimos K, Tomos G, Drakopanagiotakis F, Steiropoulos P, Manali E, Siasos G, Ilias I.

items.title: Fecal microbiota transplantation for pediatric Clostridioides difficile infection: efficacy, challenges, and the path to next-generation microbiome therapies.
items.summary: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is an increasing cause of morbidity in children, with recurrent disease posing substantial therapeutic challenges. Antibiotic therapy remains the cornerstone of initial management; however, up to 30% of children experience recurrence, and those with underlying comorbidities face recurrence rates as high as 65%. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) has demonstrated superior efficacy over antibiotics for recurrent CDI (rCDI) in adults and has emerged as the most effective available intervention for pediatric rCDI. In this review, we synthesize current evidence on FMT efficacy, microbiome changes, and safety in children with CDI. Data from large multicenter cohort studies demonstrate cure rates exceeding 80%, with comparable efficacy observed in high-risk subpopulations, including those with inflammatory bowel disease and immunocompromising conditions.
items.author: Nicholson MR, Conrad MA, Diaz De Leon S, Strength R, Kelsen JR, Kahn SA, Hourigan SK.

items.title: Analysis of a recent human parvovirus B19 outbreak using a new genomic surveillance system.
items.summary: Human parvovirus B19 is the causative agent of various clinical diseases like erythema infectiosum, transient aplastic crisis, fetal hydrops, reactive arthritis, and rarely potentially fatal organ diseases. The worldwide seroprevalence of parvovirus B19 has been assessed to be about 40-60%. It has been shown that parvoviruses can also infect new host species, adapt, and co-evolve. A comprehensive genomic surveillance is essential to gain a better insight in the adaptation, evolution, and also epidemics of parvoviruses. In the scope of the large parvovirus B19 epidemic 2023/24 following the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, we developed a rapid and convenient system to analyze parvovirus B19 genomes directly from patient samples by next-generation sequencing.
items.author: Cordsmeier A, Steininger P, Albrecht JC, Korn K, Ensser A.

items.title: Genetically modified (GM) crop use 1996-2024: environmental impacts associated with pesticide use change.
items.summary: This paper assesses the environmental impacts associated with changes in pesticide use with GM crops at a global level. The main technologies impacting on pesticide use have been crops modified to be tolerant to specific herbicides to facilitate improved weed control and crops resistant to a range of crop insect pests that otherwise damage crops or typically require the application of insecticides to control them. Over the period examined of 1996 to 2024, the widespread use of GM insect-resistant and herbicide-tolerant seed technology has reduced pesticide application by 866.9 million kg (-6.5%) of active ingredient and, as a result, decreased the environmental impact associated with insecticide and herbicide use on these crops (as measured by the indicator, the Environmental Impact Quotient (EIQ)) by a larger 15.3% between 1996 and 2024.
items.author: Brookes G.

items.title: Association of Planetary Health Diet with decreased risk of cardiometabolic diseases, multimorbidity, and its progression: a prospective cohort study.
items.summary: Background Lifestyle factors account for most of cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs) and progression to cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM). Yet, whether adherence to the Planetary Health Diet (PHD) is related to a lower risk of CMDs, CMM, and CMD progression is less known. Methods We used large cohort data that included over 100,000 participants. Adherence to the PHD was measured by the Planetary Health Diet Index (PHDI) and CMDs were ascertained by linkage to national registries through 1 September 2023. Cox proportional hazards models or weighted Cox regression models were employed to analyse the relationship between the PHD and the risk of CMDs.
items.author: Li X, Liu M, Yang W, Liu J.

items.title: Changes in full vaccination coverage and in the gap between poor and non-poor households among children aged 12-23 months in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2013-14 to 2023-24: a comparison of two Demographic and Health surveys.
items.summary: Background Immunisation coverage in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is far below global targets, and poorer children are less often vaccinated. Expanded outreach since 2013-14 could have narrowed this gap; COVID-19, outbreaks and conflict could have widened it. Objectives To estimate full vaccination, BCG and DPT3 coverage in 2013-14 and 2023-24, the change in the poor-non-poor gap in full vaccination (primary outcome), and its provincial variation. Methods Repeated cross-sectional analysis of the 2013-14 and 2023-24 Demographic and Health Surveys (3,443 and 4,208 children aged 12-23 months). Poor: poorest 40% by household wealth index. Weighted linear probability models with a poor-by-survey interaction estimated the change in the percentage-point gap; a provincial interaction model assessed heterogeneity.
items.author: Tsala Dimbuene Z, Mabanza Matondo S, Muleka Ilunga B, Sampasa-Kanyinga H.

items.title: Label-free Raman spectroscopy for cancer therapy response: from methodological framework to clinical translation.
items.summary: The early detection of therapy-induced biomolecular changes and the prediction of therapeutic response remain major challenges in oncology. Current clinical methods often assess treatment response through macroscopic or morphological endpoints, whereas molecular alterations associated with sensitivity, resistance, or recurrence may arise earlier and remain undetected. Raman spectroscopy offers a label-free and non-destructive approach to probe the intrinsic biochemical composition of cells, tissues, and biofluids, providing spectral and spatial information that can support therapy response prediction and longitudinal monitoring. This review discusses Raman-based technologies for cancer therapy assessment, from preclinical models to emerging clinical applications. We first outline the clinical need for rapid, non-destructive, and molecularly informative tools, considering tumor heterogeneity, therapy resistance, the tumor microenvironment, and current standards for response evaluation.
items.author: Alcolea-Rodriguez V, Bresci A, Mühlig A, Agrimi C, Morasso C, Polli D, Guntinas-Lichius O, Vanna R.

items.title: A plant-based diet attenuates hypertension-induced renal and hepatic stress: an exploratory study.
items.summary: Hypertension drives progressive renal dysfunction and hepatic injury. In this secondary analysis, we investigated whether a plant-based diet (PBD) could prevent and/or reverse hypertension-induced renal and hepatic insult. Four-week-old female spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) consumed a refined control diet or PBD comprising 28% fruits, vegetables, nuts and legumes, while normotensive Wistar-Kyoto rats consumed the control diet. After 24 weeks, a subset of control-fed SHRs switched to PBD for 12 weeks. Despite sustained hypertension, exploratory analyses indicated that PBD may reduce serum urea during prevention (3.84 ± 1.12 vs. 3.03 ± 0.80 mmol L -1 ; P = 0.0263) and treatment (4.37 ± 1.80 vs.
items.author: Najjar RS, Jarrell ZR, McCarthy C, Lu W, Lim G, Go YM, Ziegler TR, Wang S, Feresin RG, Wainford RD, Gewirtz AT.

items.title: 5-Hydroxy-2(5 H )-furanone (HFO) - a versatile and bio-based platform chemical.
items.summary: The transition toward sustainable chemistry requires a fundamental rethinking of chemical building blocks beyond fossil-derived systems. While conventional petrochemical platform chemicals are industrially indispensable, they suffer from reliance on finite resources, environmental persistence, and restricted structural diversity. In contrast, bio-based and renewable platform chemicals offer major new opportunities, particularly when exploiting the inherent functionality and structural diversity of natural metabolites through bottom-up design strategies. This review highlights 5-hydroxy-2(5 H )-furanone (5-hydroxybutenolide, HFO), a chiral maleic anhydride analogue, as a promising yet underexplored bio-based platform chemical. It critically assesses its synthetic accessibility from renewable furanic feedstocks and examines key transformation strategies that enable the generation of structurally diverse and enantioenriched derivatives.
items.author: Meijer JT, Kleybolte MM, Jensma A, Kaniraj JP, Freese T, Feringa BL.

items.title: Identical-location electron microscopy for the discovery of heterogeneous catalysts' dynamics at the single-particle level.
items.summary: Understanding how heterogeneous catalysts evolve at the single-particle level is central to advancing modern industrial chemistry and energy conversion technologies. However, conventional characterisation techniques provide only ensemble-averaged information, obscuring the structural diversity and dynamic behaviour that govern catalytic performance. In particular, individual nanoparticles can follow distinct evolution pathways under reaction conditions, making it challenging to establish clear structure-property relationships. Identical-location electron microscopy (IL-EM) has emerged as a powerful approach to overcome these limitations by enabling the direct tracking of the same catalyst particle across different stages of a reaction. By preserving spatiotemporal continuity, IL-EM provides particle-resolved insights into single-particle events such as coalescence, dissolution, restructuring, and compositional changes, while avoiding radiolysis damage during the reaction stage.
items.author: Chen Y, Alves Fernandes J, Khlobystov AN.

items.title: New approach methodologies in nanomedicine: bridging the gap between in silico , in vitro , and in vivo systems.
items.summary: The rise of nanomedicine has led to the regulatory approval of more than 80 nanoparticle (NP)-based therapeutics over the past two decades. Further advancement in the field requires a deeper understanding of the nano-bio interface of NPs, including their uptake, delivery, efficacy, toxicity, and adverse effects. Despite the heavy reliance on conventional cell cultures for NP screening, these models do not recapitulate the in vivo microenvironment, complexity, and physiological responses; hence, follow-up animal studies are required. Nonetheless, because of species-specific differences and ethical concerns around animal studies, developing alternative platforms has become critical. To address these issues, 3D cell culture models such as organoids, spheroids, and organ-on-chip systems have emerged to bridge the gap between in vitro and in vivo systems.
items.author: Radwan Y, Rebolledo LP, Skelly E, Grabarnik E, Jain S, Halman M, Chammas R, Zakharov AV, Dobrovolskaia MA, Afonin KA.

items.title: A Unified Framework for Self-Recognition Across Monkeys, Infants, and Robots
items.summary: Self-recognition is a basic cognitive ability that indicates self-consciousness in humans. However, whether non-human agents such as monkeys and robots can possess a similar sense of self remains debated. Here, we develop a multi-scenario apparatus to examine self-recognition from different perspectives across macaque monkeys, human infants, and simulated robots. Monkeys trained for mirror-perspective (MP) self-face recognition were able to spontaneously recognize themselves when viewing video images of their back from a third-person perspective (3PP); however, this generalization required a few minutes of "exploration". In contrast, monkeys trained for 3PP self-back recognition spontaneously demonstrated MP self-recognition within seconds. Meanwhile, first-person-perspective (1PP) self-hand recognition represented a more basic ability that naive monkeys could achieve naturally.
items.author: Zhang, W., Chen, K., Zhang, T. et al.

items.title: Emerging transient dynamics at finite observation scales
items.summary: Biogeochemical, ecological, and astronomical systems are transient. Yet, predicting dynamical shifts remains challenging because of inferential uncertainties in datasets and the limitations of asymptotic-dependent theories. To address this problem, we developed a theoretical framework that builds on the finite nature of observations. This framework assesses the relative importance of processes, defined as the mechanisms that contribute to the rate of change of the system's dynamic variables; this allows prediction of switching thresholds, that is, the values of the dynamic variables at which a process becomes relevant or irrelevant, switching the dynamics into a new dynamic regime. The framework predicts that the number of possible observable dynamic regimes increases exponentially with the number of processes.
items.author: Cobo-Lopez, S., Carbajal, L. J., Witt, M. et al.

items.title: The key role of oxidation state and flake size in the ecotoxicological impact of industrial graphene oxide nanoflakes
items.summary: Graphene oxide (GO) is a widely used nanomaterial across various scientific and technological fields. Environmental exposure to GO and consequent ecotoxicological effects have been largely reported. Despite the significant efforts and illuminating conclusions, establishing fair pairwise correlations between material and toxicity descriptors remains challenging and controversial. Key drawbacks in GO ecotoxicological studies to date include a lack of standardized materials, poorly defined descriptors, and insufficient material variants. Here, we establish the first comprehensive framework to tackle the multidimensional ecotoxicology of GO. We perform thorough material characterization to derive descriptors that precisely define four key GO variants used in industrial scale-up, with differing flake granularity and oxidation extent.
items.author: Subrati, A., Bigini, P., De Luigi, A. et al.

items.title: Distinct changes in brain and peripheral oxygen levels induced by synthetic opioids of the nitazene family
items.summary: Nitazenes are a category of synthetic opioids, some of which have high analgesic potential but also high toxicity, which has historically prevented their development as therapeutic drugs. Like fentanyl, nitazenes induce respiratory depression, a primary factor in their toxicity. Recently, a nitazene derivative called N-desethyl-fluornitrazene (DFNZ) was shown to have high analgesic properties with weak hypoxic effects. To better characterize the hypoxic effects of DFNZ relative to its parent, fluornitrazene (FNZ) and the prototypical nitazene etonitazene, we used amperometric oxygen sensors in freely moving rats to examine oxygen dynamics in the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and the subcutaneous space, using fentanyl as a comparison.
items.author: Arce, A., Nguyen, N., Gomez, J. L. et al.

items.title: The activation-deactivation cycle of human PIEZO1
items.summary: PIEZO1 is a cation channel that is primarily activated through mechanical force, and activation has been shown to be influenced by membrane curvature. PIEZO1 is ubiquitously expressed and plays critical roles in various patho-/physiological processes such as inflammatory diseases or red blood cell volume regulation. Here we combine coarse-grained and atomistic simulations in which human PIEZO1 is embedded in a curved membrane and subjected to simulations under controlled membrane tension and a physiological transmembrane potential, allowing the gating cycle to be reconstructed at atomic resolution. Systematic pressure adaptation identifies an activation regime in which the channel flattens progressively, and ion permeation quantitatively reproduces the experimental conductance of 36 pS.
items.author: Massa, J., Frieg, B., Tyrchan, C. et al.

items.title: Insulin signaling in pericytes is a master regulator of endocrine and vascular niches in pancreatic islets
items.summary: Insulin plays a crucial role in lowering glycemia, but it is also a powerful anabolic hormone with potent effects on the vasculature. Most studies on insulin vascular actions have focused on endothelial cells. Much less is known about its effects on the mural cells of the microvasculature known as pericytes. This gap in knowledge is particularly relevant for the pancreatic islet microvasculature which is exposed to high insulin levels and relies on local pericytes to efficiently deliver its glucoregulatory hormones. To investigate how insulin affects islet pericyte function and the impact on glucose homeostasis, we generated mice that lack insulin receptors in pericytes (PerIRKO).
items.author: Barboza, C., Goncalves, L., Diaz Cruz, R. et al.

items.title: Cerebellar transcranial AC stimulation produces frequency and phase-dependent changes in Purkinje cell complex spike waveform
items.summary: Cerebellar transcranial alternating current stimulation (ctACS) can improve motor learning and may speed rehabilitation. The mechanisms by which ctACS induces long-term changes in brain function that underlie these effects are not known, and knowledge of them could greatly improve the application of ctACS. One potential mechanism is alteration of Purkinje cell (PC) complex spike (CS) activity, as CS activity is a key regulator of cerebellar synaptic plasticity. Thus, we investigated how ctACS modifies CS firing rates and waveform. Extracellular recordings were obtained from cerebellar PCs in anesthetized adult rats while ctACS (250 A) was applied across a range of frequencies (0.5 - 50 Hz).
items.author: Mourra, D., Sloane, J., Sahin, M. et al.

items.title: Variable penetrance of schizophrenia in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome is associated with impaired, but reversible, neuronal mitophagy.
items.summary: The 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22qDS) is a major genetic risk factor for schizophrenia (Sz). We found that iPSC-derived neurons (iNeurons) from 22qDS +Sz individuals exhibit weaker mitochondrial energetics, whereas iNeurons from individuals with the same deletion but no psychosis (22qDS -Sz) upregulate expression of mitochondrial biogenesis-related genes. Here, we investigated why the +Sz group fails to undergo this compensation, finding that 22qDS +Sz iNeurons have older and more depolarized mitochondria than 22qDS -Sz or controls. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed downregulation of mitophagy-related pathways, and live imaging revealed elevated lysosomal pH. Restoring lysosomal acidity with acidifying nanoparticles improved mitophagy and, remarkably, increased the expression of mitochondrial biogenesis-related transcription factors in the +Sz neurons.
items.author: Stronati, E., Rossano, A. J., Li, J. et al.

items.title: Early visual experience contributes to the calibration of higher-order body representations
items.summary: Higher-order body representations, including representations of body shape and size, play an important role in maintaining perceptual constancy in touch. However, whether the development of these representations depends on early visual experience remains unclear. Here, we investigated tactile distance perception in congenitally blind, late-blind, and sighted individuals. A given tactile distance is typically perceived as longer on the finger than on the forearm, reflecting distortions in cortical topography that is partially rescaled by higher-order representations of body size and shape. Congenitally blind participants showed a greater tendency to perceive identical tactile distances on the index finger as longer than those on the forearm.
items.author: Liu, Y., Wang, Y., Ma, Y.

items.title: Partially shared representational space for vision and language across objects, scenes, and visual events
items.summary: Deep neural networks (DNNs) and behavioural similarity judgements of visual stimuli predict neural responses in visual cortex. Recent work shows that large language model (LLM) embeddings and similarity judgements of language descriptions also predict visual brain activity. These predictors were examined separately across modalities (vision vs language) and types (models vs human behaviour). It remains unclear to what extent these predictors explain shared or unique aspects of visual brain responses, how these contributions vary along the visual hierarchy and category-selective regions, and whether vision-language convergence depends on the stimulus type. We used three fMRI datasets progressing toward naturalistic visual experience, from objects (THINGS) to scenes (NSD) to dynamic events (BMD).
items.author: Zou, Q., Jozwik, K.

items.title: Distal inhibition is recruited for action but not sensation in the primate superior colliculus
items.summary: Sensorimotor transformation requires neural circuits to coordinate excitation and inhibition, but how and whether this organization changes as the circuit transitions from processing sensation to action remain unresolved. We recorded laminar local field potentials across superior colliculus (SC) layers in four male macaques and computed current source density to resolve transmembrane currents during saccades to a target at one of eight isoradial directions. During the visual response, excitation was spatially confined to the receptive field, with little modulation at distant sites. During saccade generation, local excitation remained strongest for movements toward the receptive field, while inhibition extended across the SC map, including locations where spiking remained at baseline.
items.author: Bourrelly, C., Yang, F., Gandhi, N. J.

items.title: Hormone therapy attenuates menopause-related impairments in motor cortical spike-timing-dependent plasticity
items.summary: The menopause marks the permanent cessation of menstruation via a decline in endogenous hormone production. This transition influences brain health, yet its effects on motor cortical excitability and spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) are poorly understood. Across two sites, 46 females were categorised as pre-menopausal (PRE, age 28{+/-}7 years), perimenopausal (PERI, 50{+/-}3 years), post-menopausal (POST, 60{+/-}8 years), or combined continuous hormone therapy users (HT, 52{+/-}3 years). Transcranial magnetic stimulation was used to measure corticospinal excitability (MEP/Mmax), short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI), and intracortical facilitation (ICF) before, then 10 and 30 min after a paired associative stimulation (PAS) protocol (25-ms interstimulus interval). Serum hormone concentrations were quantified from venous blood.
items.author: Ansdell, P., Spillane, P., Nedelec, E. et al.

items.title: Chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy targeting CD94 for cytotoxic T/NK cell malignancies
items.summary: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy against pan-B-cell antigens is highly effective, but analogous approaches for T-cell lymphomas risk prolonged T-cell aplasia. We developed a CAR-T therapy targeting a post-thymic antigen, CD94, a receptor with restricted expression in normal tissues and immune cells but enriched in cytotoxic T/NK-cell malignancies. Second generation CD94 CAR T cells generated using a specific and high-affinity anti-CD94 monoclonal antibody showed potent and selective cytotoxicity against CD94-positive tumor cells in vitro and completely eradicated NK-cell leukemia xenografts and patient-derived xenograft models of hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma and NK/T-cell lymphoma in vivo. Incorporation of truncated B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) as a safety switch enabled rapid elimination of CAR T cells using anti-BCMA T-cell engagers or anti-BCMA antibody-drug conjugate.
items.author: Le, C. C., Weng, J., Liu, J. et al.

items.title: Computational identification and in vitro evaluation of astragaloside II as an inhibitor of dengue virus NS1-induced endothelial hyperpermeability
items.summary: Background Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease in which severe cases are marked by leakage of plasma from blood vessels. The secreted nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) of dengue virus damages the endothelial barrier and is a drug target, but no approved antiviral exists. We aimed to identify compounds that target NS1 and to test whether the selected compound, astragaloside II (ASII), counteracts NS1-induced endothelial hyperpermeability. Methodology/Principal findings We built a deep learning model that predicts compound-target binding from chemical fingerprints and protein sequences, and used it to prescreen 177 natural compounds against NS1 of the four dengue virus serotypes. The model outperformed the DeepConv-DTI baseline in recall and F1-score on a BindingDB holdout set and on two independent test sets.
items.author: Jantrachotechatchawan, C., Chawnawa, W., Leephatarakit, N. et al.

items.title: Long-term Epstein-Barr virus persistence in immunocompetent, primate-related Chinese tree shrews and inducible lytic reactivation in species-matched epithelial cultures
items.summary: Experimental models combining long-term Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection in immunocompetent animals with species-matched cellular systems for studying viral regulation remain limited. Chinese tree shrews combine evolutionary proximity to primates with small-animal practicality and native immunocompetence, offering a complementary nonrodent model. We serially monitored blood and oral specimens from six animals inoculated with Akata EBV. Five were followed for approximately two years, including two beyond two years, and the sixth underwent tissue collection at approximately six months. Intermittent EBV DNA detection included blood positivity beyond two years in one animal. Viral RNA localized to liver, lung, and spleen at six months and to liver and spleen of another animal near two years, supporting persistent infection.
items.author: Avilala, J., Dochi, H., Wekselblatt, J. et al.

items.title: In vitro reduction of mineral oil hydrocarbons by Lacticaseibacillus casei DSM 20011
items.summary: Mineral oil hydrocarbons (MOH) are food contaminants of increasing concern due to their widespread occurrence in food and potential health risks. Although various physicochemical and biological strategies have been investigated to reduce chemical contaminants in food, the ability of lactic acid bacteria (LAB) to remove MOH has not previously been explored. The present study aimed to evaluate the in vitro removal of MOH by Lacticaseibacillus casei DSM 20011 under incubation 0for 4 h with shaking at 100 rpm. Following the screening of different LAB strains, L. casei DSM 20011 was selected for in vitro evaluation of MOH removal using a representative mineral oil mixture, followed by the determination of MOH by on-line LC GC-FID.
items.author: Miklavcic Visnjevec, A., Pellegrini, M., Conchione, C. et al.

items.title: TRIDENT (Taxonomic Resolution and IDentification using Environmental dNa Traces): An Optimized Algorithm for Vertebrate Taxonomic Assignments in eDNA Metabarcoding, Integrating Molecular, Taxonomic, and Ecological Criteria
items.summary: Environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding has become a powerful approach for large-scale biodiversity assessment, yet taxonomic assignment remains one of its most critical error-prone steps. Current bioinformatic pipelines rely on molecular similarity searches against reference databases, but assignment accuracy is constrained not only by short marker length and database incompleteness, but also by fundamental limitations, including recent species radiations, incomplete lineage sorting, introgression, NUMTs, and the imperfect correspondence between genetic variation and species boundaries. Here, we present TRIDENT (Taxonomic Resolution and IDentification using Environmental dNa Traces), an automated and simple protocol designed to improve taxonomic assignments in eDNA metabarcoding. Developed for marine vertebrates, TRIDENT may be used with any barcode and integrates three complementary sources of evidence: molecular similarity (NCBI/GenBank and BOLD), curated taxonomic information (WoRMS), and ecological plausibility derived from biogeographic occurrence data (GBIF).
items.author: Haderle, R., Jung, G., Riou, M. et al.

items.title: IFT20 mediates trafficking of ciliary proteins to support mammalian motile ciliogenesis in testicular efferent ductules and respiratory tract.
items.summary: Cilia are antenna-like organelles that extend from the apical cell membrane and are broadly present in eukaryotes. They are classified as primary and motile types; the later including sperm flagellum and somatic multiciliated cells present within the reproductive and respiratory systems. Intraflagellar transport (IFT) provides delivery of cargo for cilia assembly and maintenance. Of the multiple protein components, IFT20, a component of the intraflagellar transport-B (IFT-B) complex, is required for cargo delivery anterograde during primary cilia and mouse sperm flagellum formation, and is also known to link the Golgi with the primary cilia; however, its role in motile cilia from somatic cells is so far unknown.
items.author: Li, T., Schmitt, A., Pan, J. et al.

items.title: Artifact-guided restoration improves visualization of cellular ultrastructure in cryo-FIB-SEM volumes
items.summary: Cryogenic focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (cryo-FIB-SEM) enables volumetric imaging of vitrified specimens, but charging artifacts, high noise and weak membrane contrast hinder the interpretation of biological features. Here we present a two-stage deep-learning-based framework that translates cryo-FIB-SEM images toward the domain of conventional room-temperature FIB-SEM (RT-FIB-SEM), suppressing large-scale charging artifacts and enhancing local membrane signal. Held-out synthetic tests show improved agreement with constructed reference targets, while results on four experimental cryo-FIB-SEM datasets show reduced visible artifacts and clearer membrane features. Processed cryo-FIB-SEM volumes from our two-stage model can be directly analyzed by tools designed for RT-FIB-SEM, and an existing pretrained segmentation model is applied to our model output, yielding extensive predictions of membrane structures.
items.author: Zhang, N., Joubert, L.-M., Wu, G.-H. et al.

items.title: Pleckstrin Homology-based proximity-labeling reveal lipid-associated interactomes
items.summary: Phosphoinositides (PIPs) organize membrane-associated signaling, but the proteins associated with specific PIPs and their regulation remain poorly characterized. Here, we establish a lipid-binding domain-based proximity-labeling approach to map PIP-associated proteomes in vivo, and applied it to plant cells. We identify distinct protein networks associated with PI4P and PI(4,5)P2, linking these lipids to membrane signaling, transport, and organization. Using molecular dynamics simulations and in vivo validation we further reveal how two previously uncharacterized PIP effectors, ALTERED RESPONSE TO GRAVITY-LIKE1 (ARL1) and HYPERSENSITIVE RESPONSE 1 (HIR1), engage with PIPs to regulate their membrane localization and nanodomain organization. Finally, we outline how PIP-associated proteomes change in response to prominent abiotic stress conditions, including salt and heat, in Arabidopsis.
items.author: Noack, L. C., Vogel, P., Neubergerova, M. et al.

items.title: Endogenous cAMP production within tissue fibroblasts is required for spontaneous fibrosis resolution
items.summary: Pathologic myofibroblasts (MFs) are pivotal effector cells in the development of persistent tissue fibrosis following parenchymal injury, and their activation and accumulation has been linked to a failure to phenotypically dedifferentiate and thus to resist apoptosis. The second messenger cyclic AMP (cAMP) has been shown to induce MF dedifferentiation and restore their sensitivity to apoptosis in vitro, but its endogenous role within MFs during fibrosis resolution in vivo has not been explored. To test the hypothesis that cAMP generation and signaling within fibroblasts is essential for fibrosis resolution, we leveraged the spontaneously resolving nature of the single-dose intrapulmonary and subcutaneous bleomycin models in mice with an inducible and fibroblast-specific abrogation of cAMP generation owing to deletion of the stimulatory G protein (Gs).
items.author: Fortier, S. M., Speth, J., Walker, N. M. et al.

items.title: Polarized Canine Liver Organoid Monolayers Capture Features of Western Diet-Induced Hepatic Metabolic Reprogramming Across Transcriptomic, Lipidomic, and Biogenic Amine Signatures
items.summary: Liver responses to Western-diet (WD) exposure remain incompletely defined, partly because conventional rodent models and immortalized hepatic cell lines incompletely recapitulate species-specific features of liver biology. Here, we established polarized epithelial monolayers from canine liver organoids derived from healthy beagles and beagles exposed to a WD for 8 weeks. We then used this platform to characterize diet-induced hepatic reprogramming and to explore differential responses to two SGLT2 inhibitors, dapagliflozin and bexagliflozin. The monolayers developed reproducible apical-basal polarity, with transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) values of 123-335 {Omega} cm2, enabling compartment-resolved sampling. Bulk transcriptomics, lipidomics, and biogenic amine profiling each independently separated WD-derived from healthy monolayers.
items.author: Giebelhaus, R. T., Zdyrski, C., de la Mata, A. P. et al.

items.title: COPS5 maintains spermatogenesis gene expression and piRNA-mediated transposon silencing
items.summary: COPS5 (CSN5/JAB1), a multifunctional subunit of the COP9 signalosome, is required for male germ cell survival, but how it acts is unclear. We combined a germ cell specific Cops5 conditional knockout (cKO) mouse model with transcriptomic, proteomic and small RNA analysis of P16 testes. Cops5 loss caused progressive spermatogenic arrest after postnatal day 16. At both the mRNA and protein levels, 59 genes were downregulated, including piRNA biogenesis factors such as PIWIL1/MIWI, PIWIL2/MILI, Tudor domain proteins, DDX4, MAEL and MOV10L1. In Cops5 cKO testes, pachytene piRNAs decreased in abundance and diversity, falling from about 56% to 18~30% of total small RNAs, while the 1U bias was retained.
items.author: Huang, J., Huang, Q., Zheng, C. et al.

items.title: Granger-causal inference to study crosstalk between two actin regulators in live cell imaging
items.summary: Dynamic actin filament assembly at the cell membrane drives cell migration. Its regulation is governed by functionally overlapping actin regulators and complex feedback loops that hinder conventional perturbation-approaches from dissecting actin regulatory pathways. Here we present an extended, perturbation-free statistical framework based on Granger causality (GC). The framework rests on statistical models that capture the interdependence among subcellular fluctuations of molecular and cell morphodynamic activities extracted from three-channel live-cell imaging. Applied to the inference of cause-effect relationships among actin, its regulators and cell-edge movement, the GC analysis identifies distinct regulatory hierarchies of the actin regulators Arp2/3, VASP and mDia1 on actin dynamics and cell edge movement.
items.author: Godana, A., Isogai, T., Bhatt, K. et al.

items.title: Re-evaluating donor-cell identity after hiPSC-RGC transplantation in mouse models of optic neuropathy
items.summary: Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by permanent visual field loss caused by the death of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs). Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. We investigated the potential of transplanting human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived RGCs (hiPSC-RGCs) in two mouse models of optic nerve degeneration: N-Methyl-D-Aspartate (NMDA) and optic nerve crush (ONC), and characterized their ability to survive, integrate, and form synaptic connections in a degenerated retina. Follow-up studies, including immunohistochemistry and patch-clamping experiments, one year after intravitreal injections, determined the location, identity, and function of the donor GFP+ve fluorescent cells within the mouse retinas and their similarity to native RGCs.
items.author: Vrathasha, V., Nikonov, S., Bell, B. et al.

items.title: Cold acclimation and diapause independently improve egg cold tolerance and act through distinct mechanisms in the invasive mosquito Aedes albopictus
items.summary: 1. Phenotypic plasticity is an important mechanism by which organisms can cope with environmental change. However, there is growing recognition that phenotypic plasticity is not a single phenomenon but instead encompasses a range of responses that vary in reversibility and are predicted to evolve under different conditions. Nevertheless, few studies have disentangled the fitness effects and mechanisms of different forms of plasticity, making it difficult to predict their respective roles in promoting population persistence in the face of climate change. 2. In our study, we assessed plasticity of egg cold tolerance in the vector mosquito Aedes albopictus, considering both irreversible plasticity caused by photoperiodically-mediated diapause and reversible plasticity caused by cold acclimation.
items.author: Sturiale, S. L., Kostal, V., Moos, M. et al.

items.title: Forecasting viral antigenic evolution from phylogenetic trees
items.summary: Forecasting the evolution of viral proteins can help inform pandemic preparedness and guide the development of interventions. Phylogenetic trees provide historical records of pathogen evolution, which are key for retrospective analysis, but using them to predict future genotypic changes remains challenging. We introduce antiGen, a machine learning model that learns from the evolutionary past of viruses to forecast the evolutionary future. antiGen achieves state-of-the-art performance in forecasting SARS-CoV-2 spike protein mutations according to a variety of metrics, including the prediction of mutations in the receptor binding domain, mutations never previously seen, and mutations with high prevalence. Most experimentally tested antiGen-forecasted spike variants retain pseudoviral infectivity in vitro, supporting their functional plausibility.
items.author: Specht, I., Park, S., Vermani, A. et al.

items.title: Evaluating Temporal Genomic Data for Detecting and Characterizing Balancing Selection
items.summary: Balancing selection encompasses a diverse set of evolutionary mechanisms that maintain genetic polymorphism within populations. However, both detecting balancing selection and distinguishing among its underlying mechanisms remain challenging. Recent advances in the generation of temporal genetic data and the application of machine learning offer new opportunities to address these challenges. In this study, we tested whether temporal genetic data improve the detection of balancing selection and the discrimination between two major balancing selection mechanisms, overdominance and negative frequency-dependent selection. Using forward simulations, we summarized temporal genetic data with features derived from a diverse set of population genetic summary statistics and trained support vector machine and random forest classifiers.
items.author: Taskent, O., Kocaaydin, N., Kilinc, G. M. et al.

items.title: Phylogenetic insights into the origin of piroplasmid infection in endemic carnivores of Madagascar
items.summary: Piroplasmids (order Piroplasmida), including the genera Babesia, Theileria, and Cytauxzoon, are tick-borne protozoan parasites of medical, veterinary, and economic importance. Understanding the diversity and evolutionary history of piroplasmids infecting endangered wildlife can provide insights into their origins, natural hosts, and potential to cause severe disease. Using nuclear 18S rRNA and mitochondrial cytb gene sequences, we characterized piroplasmid parasites infecting wild carnivorans across two protected areas in Madagascar. We detected piroplasmid infections in 91.5% of sampled individuals (n = 106; 95% CI: 84.6 - 95.4%) across three endemic carnivoran species, with infections associated with distinct, potentially host-associated Babesia sp. and Cytauxzoon sp.
items.author: Rasambainarivo, F. T., Evans, K. J., Rasolofoniaina, O. A. et al.

items.title: Kin selection for cooperation in the honey bee microbiome
items.summary: Bacteria engage in many cooperative behaviours which provide benefits to other cells in the population. Lab experiments have suggested that these costly behaviours can be favoured by kin selection due to the benefits they provide to closely related cells. However, we know much less about the role of kin selection in natural populations. Here, we used two complementary methods to measure and compare kin selected signatures of cooperation in 19 species of bacteria found in the guts of honey bees. We used bioinformatic tools to count the number (and proportion) of genes for cooperative traits in a genome, and used molecular population genetics to measure how natural selection is acting on those genes.
