items.title: Adhesive and Antibacterial Bio-Based Hydrogel for Human Voice Recognition and Osteoarthritis Recovery Monitoring.
items.summary: Conductive hydrogels derived from natural polysaccharides hold great promise for next generation wearable electronics owing to their intrinsic biocompatibility, adhesiveness, and tunable mechanical properties. However, realizing amylum-based hydrogels with simultaneously high stretchability, sensitivity, strong adhesion and antibacterial performance remains a significant challenge. Herein, a multifunctional ionic hydrogel, marked as PAPC 4 hydrogel, composed of polyacrylamide (PAAm), amylum and phenol-modified chitosan is developed via a one-pot synthesis strategy. The hydrogel exhibits exceptional stretchability (up to 1605%), short response time (16.1 ms), high optical transparency (96%), strong adhesion (43.2 kPa on PVC) and pronounced antibacterial activity. Cytotoxicity assays, live/dead staining, and subcutaneous implantation supported its biocompatibility under the tested conditions, while bacterial assays demonstrated activity against Escherichia coli .
items.author: He Q, Zhu T, Cheng Y, Song Y, Wen F, Huang J, Matičić D, Zhang Y, Lai Y, Zhang C, Li H.

items.title: The gut microbiome is associated with structural and functional brain alterations in adolescents with social anxiety disorder.
items.summary: Background Social anxiety disorder (SAD) commonly emerges in childhood or early adolescence and is associated with persistent impairments in social and emotional functioning. Although structural and functional brain abnormalities have been reported in SAD, the potential involvement of the microbiota-gut-brain axis in adolescent SAD remains poorly understood. Aims To investigate gut microbiota composition, predicted microbial functional pathways and multimodal brain alterations in adolescents with SAD, and to examine microbiome-brain associations and their exploratory discriminative value. Methods This cross-sectional study included 48 adolescents (31 with SAD and 17 healthy controls [HCs]) with complete clinical, faecal and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data.
items.author: Sun Y, Li Q, Ju P, Cheng W, Yang Z, Chen J.

items.title: Ocular Safety of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: A Comprehensive Review.
items.summary: Background Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) provide substantial glycemic and cardiometabolic benefits, but concerns regarding diabetic retinopathy (DR) progression and nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) have raised questions about their ocular safety. This review critically evaluates current evidence and its clinical implications. Methods A structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus was conducted from inception through July 2026. Evidence from randomized trials, observational studies, meta-analyses, pharmacovigilance investigations, clinical guidelines, and regulatory documents was narratively synthesized. Results In SUSTAIN-6, semaglutide increased DR complications compared with placebo (3.0% vs. 1.8%; hazard ratio 1.76, 95% confidence interval 1.11-2.78), predominantly among patients with pre-existing retinopathy and substantial early glycemic improvement.
items.author: Hanna E, Karam C, Aad S, Ali A, Farah J, Azzi AS.

items.title: Patient- and family-reported satisfaction in child and adolescent psychiatric inpatient care: An exploratory descriptive survey.
items.summary: Aim To describe and compare patient- and family-reported satisfaction with child and adolescent psychiatric inpatient care in a Japanese inpatient unit. Methods Patients aged 8-15 years discharged from a single Japanese inpatient unit and their families completed an anonymous web questionnaire with separate patient and family versions. Overall satisfaction was rated on a 10-point scale, and respondents who reported interaction rated the usefulness of five professional groups. Because responses were unlinked, 10 probable patient-family pairs identified from submission times were used in sensitivity analyses. Results Invitations were handed to 61 patients and their families at discharge; 52 family members (85.2%) and 26 patients (42.6%) responded.
items.author: Yamamoto K, Usami M.

items.title: Neurophysiological changes following intensive Naikan therapy in a patient with recurrent depressive episodes later diagnosed with bipolar II disorder: A case report.
items.summary: Background Intensive Naikan therapy is a structured Japanese psychotherapy involving systematic reflection on interpersonal relationships; however, its neurophysiological correlates remain unclear. We herein report changes in resting-state electroencephalography (EEG), the P300 event-related potential, and standardized low-resolution brain electromagnetic tomography (sLORETA)-estimated source activity after intensive Naikan therapy. Case presentation A 29-year-old man with recurrent depressive episodes and anxiety about family relationships and future employment underwent 7 days of inpatient intensive Naikan therapy. He was later diagnosed with bipolar II disorder after a hypomanic episode during the follow-up. Assessments were performed before and after the intervention. Anxiety decreased on State-Trait Anxiety Inventory state and trait scores (42 to 20 and 30 to 20, respectively), and depressive symptoms remained minimal on the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale and Beck Depression Inventory (4 to 3 and 0 to 0, respectively).
items.author: Furuichi A, Higuchi Y, Kaneko N, Takahashi T.

items.title: From Observational Biology to Functional and Computable Models of Living Systems.
items.summary: The proposed framework moves from fragmented biological evidence toward testable, computable life functions that describe how biological states evolve over time. A stepwise experimental approach progresses from molecular processes to unicellular and multicellular models, with tumor systems serving as models of pathological state transitions. The graphical image was Created with BioRender.com (Ji L. 2026; https://BioRender.com/zaxq2dd).
items.author: Ji L, Qian H.

items.title: Advances in natural product inhibitors targeting the type III secretion system 1 of Salmonella .
items.summary: Salmonella is an important foodborne pathogen that poses significant threats to human health, animal production, and food safety. Increasing antimicrobial resistance and limitations of conventional control strategies have promoted the development of anti-virulence approaches targeting bacterial virulence factors. The type III secretion system 1 (T3SS-1) mediates Salmonella invasion into host cells and effector protein translocation, yet is dispensable for bacterial survival, rendering it a promising anti-virulence target. This review summarizes recent advances in natural product-derived T3SS-1 inhibitors, classifies relevant inhibitors based on chemical structural characteristics and, from a mechanistic perspective, distinguishes direct protein binding mode with well-defined molecular interactions from indirect regulation mode that exert modulatory effects.
items.author: Hu C, Yang Z, Zhang H, Wu D, Shao D, He J, Liu Y, Wang L, Abula S, Ziyawudong B, Hao B, Wang S.

items.title: E2F4 gene therapy reverses established synaptic and cognitive deficits and remodels learning-associated signaling in Alzheimer's disease mice
items.summary: Alzheimer's disease (AD) causes progressive synaptic dysfunction, neurodegeneration, and cognitive decline, yet strategies capable of reversing established deficits remain limited. Here, we show that neuronal expression of a p38MAPK phosphorylation-resistant human E2F4 variant (hE2F4DN), delivered by adeno-associated virus, restores hippocampal long-term potentiation and memory in homozygous 5xFAD mice after functional impairment is established. Treatment also reduces amyloid-{beta} and phospho-tau pathology and prevents hippocampal neuronal loss. Integrated proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses reveal remodeling of metabolic, redox, neuroimmune, synaptic-vesicle, and GSK3{beta}-associated signaling pathways. Following contextual fear conditioning, hE2F4DN-treated mice exhibit broader learning-associated synaptic proteomic signatures and distinct phosphoregulatory responses involving synaptic machinery.
items.author: Sanchez-Puelles, C., Hernandez-Vivanco, A., Grieco, A. et al.

items.title: Magnetic nanoparticle enrichment reveals conserved nitric oxide burst responses in Arabidopsis and wheat
items.summary: Rapid nitric oxide bursts are a conserved response to environmental stimuli, but their effects on cellular S-nitrosylation remain poorly understood. We developed a fluorinated magnetic nanoparticle method for rapid, efficient profiling of S-nitrosylation. Using Arabidopsis and wheat, we treated plant tissues with S-nitrosoglutathione (GSNO) to simulate a rapid nitric oxide surge. The method was then employed to capture S-nitrosylation dynamics within 24 h after treatment. Our analysis revealed sequence-dependent preferences for cysteines near basic or hydrophobic residues. Proteins showing rapid S-nitrosylation increases were predominantly associated with oxidative stress responses and energy metabolism, consistent with our metabolomic data. Functional studies using wheat TaGR1 mutants identified glutathione reductase 1 as a key regulated target.
items.author: Ji, R., Yang, N., Yu, L. et al.

items.title: N-Hydroxypipecolic Acid Triggers Systemic Acquired Resistance Against Leaf Rust (Puccinia triticina) in Wheat
items.summary: Systemic acquired resistance (SAR) represents a conserved immune strategy enabling plants to mount long-lasting, whole-plant protection following localized pathogen challenge. In Arabidopsis thaliana, SAR is orchestrated by the mobile immune regulator N-hydroxypipecolic acid (NHP); however, the extent to which NHP defines systemic immune states in polyploid crops remains unclear. Here, we establish NHP as an inducer of systemic immunity in hexaploid wheat (Triticum aestivum) during infection by the obligate biotrophic fungus Puccinia triticina. Local NHP application conferred robust disease suppression in distal leaves and elicited a temporally structured oxidative response characterized by a distal, biphasic reactive oxygen species (ROS) wave linking local and systemic tissues.
items.author: Sun, S., Formby, S., Craven, C. et al.

items.title: Is the Bitter Lesson coming to genomic prediction? An untuned tabular foundation model matches or beats specialized methods
items.summary: Genomic prediction (GP) is dominated by models designed around assumptions about how genetic variation affects phenotypes. Here we asked how well a general-purpose pretrained tabular foundation model called TabPFN-3.5 does with no genetics-specific modeling and no tuning when given marker genotypes directly. We benchmarked TabPFN-3.5 using a published comparison of 18 GP methods on 18 traits in six plant species. Against the published means, TabPFN-3.5 ranked first on 11 of 18 traits and had the best median rank. Because the published benchmark did not identify its test sets, we reran GBLUP, RKHS and elastic-net models on the same splits as TabPFN-3.5.
items.author: Flagel, L.

items.title: Endogenous Osteoblast-Osteocyte-Osteoclast Signaling Enables Bone Remodeling, Drug Response, and Cancer Invasion in a Nanoscale Calcified Bone-on-a-Chip
items.summary: Bone homeostasis depends on spatially orchestrated interactions among osteoclasts, osteoblasts, and osteocytes within a unique microenvironment characterized by an extracellular matrix that is mineralized on the nanoscale. Reconstructing these interactions to enable autonomous cell differentiation and tissue remodeling remains a significant challenge in faithfully modeling bone physiology and disease in-vitro. Here, we present an engineered bone-on-a-chip platform that recapitulates the spatial organization of bone-resident cells, the differentiation of immune cells into osteoclasts, and calcified tissue resorption. We demonstrate that nanoscale mineralization of cell-laden collagen hydrogels is associated with ossification- and matrix-associated transcriptional changes and an osteocyte-like phenotype in osteoblast-lineage cells, while establishing a multicellular microenvironment associated with pro-osteoclastogenic RANKL/OPG signaling and supporting osteoclastogenesis and remodeling without the need for exogenous growth factors.
items.author: Sousa, M. G. C., Athirasala, A., Hosseini, M. et al.

items.title: Engineering the Lr67-associated G144R substitution by prime editing enhances leaf rust resistance in wheat
items.summary: Wheat rust diseases threaten global wheat production, highlighting the need for durable sources of resistance. The Lr67-associated G144R substitution in the sugar transport protein gene TaSTP13-D1 confers broad-spectrum resistance to multiple fungal pathogens. Here, we used an enhanced prime-editing system (ePPEplus) to introduce this resistance-associated substitution into the three TaSTP13 homoeologs in hexaploid wheat. Using the wheat-compatible JWPE1 vector, we achieved editing frequencies of 84 to 92% across the A, B, and D genomes in regenerated T0 plants. Homozygous edits were recovered in all three homoeologs, including one line carrying homozygous edits across all three genomes. Disease assays showed that edited lines had reduced leaf rust severity and fungal biomass compared with susceptible controls.
items.author: Waites, J., Venado, R. E., Syombua, E. D. et al.

items.title: Primate Saccade Rhythmicity
items.summary: Rhythmic sampling is a hallmark of many sensory systems across diverse organisms. In primate vision, rapid foveating eye movements repetitively sample the visual environment at a rate of approximately 4 Hz. Yet, the observed inter-saccadic interval distributions might equally well be produced by a non-rhythmic stochastic process as by a - putatively variable- rhythmic generator. This raises the fundamental question whether primate visual sampling differs from the numerous examples of rhythmic sampling strategies exhibited across sensory modalities and species. Here, using experiments in humans, macaques, and a marmoset, as well as statistical approaches adopted from studies of temporal structure in neuronal spiking patterns, we show that primate saccade generation is unambiguously rooted in a rhythmic source.
items.author: Näher, T., Zhang, Y., Spadacenta, S. et al.

items.title: EPHB2 promotes long-range axon extension and its variants cause callosal dysgenesis
items.summary: The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest fibre tract connecting the cerebral hemispheres, essential for integrating neural activity across large-scale brain networks. Accordingly, abnormal CC development is associated with diverse neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders. Callosal projection neurons (CPNs) of the cortex form the CC by extending long-range axons to the contralateral hemisphere; however, the mechanisms that sustain axon elongation over such remarkable distances remain poorly understood. Here we show that variants in the human gene EPHB2, which encodes a tyrosine kinase receptor regulating nervous system development and implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders, cause CC dysgenesis. We characterise variant- specific effects on EPHB2 signalling and demonstrate that variants identified in individuals with distinct CC morphologies differentially alter CPN axon outgrowth and integration in vivo.
items.author: Park, S. S., Nagy, G. N., Perez Ferrer, I. et al.

items.title: Do altered neural responses during self-reflection converge across psychiatric disorders? A systematic review and meta-analysis of neuroimaging studies
items.summary: Altered neural responses during self-reflection have been reported across psychiatric disorders, but it is unknown whether there exist common brain regions across studies. To fill the gap, we conducted a systematic review and coordinate-based activation likelihood estimation (ALE) meta-analysis of task-based neuroimaging studies. Through systematic literature search and article screening, we identified 36 studies across 8 diagnostic categories, of which 25 studies were eligible for the ALE meta-analysis. Qualitatively, these studies revealed altered neural response among psychiatric disorders in brain regions include cortical midline and lateral association regions. ALE analyses were conducted separately for self-versus other and self-versus control contrasts, the former identified convergence in the right anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), and the latter found converged activation in the left middle frontal gyrus (MFG).
items.author: Zhu, S., Yan, W.-J., Chuan-Peng, H.

items.title: Mathematical model for visual cortical development based on molecular mechanisms underlying the generation and elimination of dendritic spines
items.summary: In the developing brain, neural circuits are elaborated by the activity-dependent rewiring of synaptic connections. The current view of synaptic rewiring in early development is that filopodia spontaneously generated along dendrites transform into spines by establishing contacts with neighboring axonal boutons to form synapses whereas spines of inappropriate synapses are eliminated in an activity-dependent manner. In this theoretical study, we mainly focus on the processes of spine generation, maturation, and elimination to build a mathematical model of synaptic rewiring, incorporating experimental findings on actin polymerization and depolymerization under the activation of Rho-GTPases mediated by the binding of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) to neurotrophin receptors such as tropomyosin kinase receptor B (TrkB) and the low-affinity-nerve growth factor receptor (p75NTR).
items.author: Tanaka, S., Miyashita, M.

items.title: GradeBins: quality control of bins from synthetic and real metagenomes
items.summary: Genomes reconstructed from metagenomes support studies of microbial diversity and function, but their interpretation depends on how much DNA is recovered and whether foreign sequence is included. Quality can be measured in benchmarks, where contig origins are known, but must be estimated in routine analyses. Here we present GradeBins, which assesses individual bins (contigs assigned to one candidate genome) and summarizes the complete bin set from an assembly. For 6,374 simulated bins, its measurements agreed with AMBER and independent calculations within rounding. In control bins built from 20 kb fragments of reference genomes, GradeBins had lower observed completeness error than CheckM1 and CheckM2 and the highest observed F1 (the harmonic mean of precision and recall) for bin selection.
items.author: Bushnell, B., Bowers, R. M., Villada, J. C.

items.title: Unravelling the hidden diversity of the monkfish Lophius gastrophysus using integrative taxonomy
items.summary: The monkfish Lophius gastrophysus is a commercially exploited demersal species distributed along the continental shelf and slope of the western Atlantic Ocean. Like other anglerfish species, L. gastrophysus has a pelagic larval stage that can facilitate dispersal by oceanic currents (Farina et al., 2008). It is considered the most widely distributed species in the genus, spanning more than 10,000 km of the western Atlantic Coast, from North Carolina to Argentina. Previous morphological analyses based on a limited set of traits suggested that L. gastrophysus may comprise two distinct species. We tested this hypothesis by combining molecular and morphometric data. Sequence data were obtained from 38 L.
items.author: D'Elia, A. K. P., Soares, L. M. M., Henning, F. et al.

items.title: Centromere divergence and allopolyploidy reshape carnivorous sundew genomes
items.summary: Centromeres are essential for chromosome function, yet how contrasting centromere architectures shape polyploid genome evolution and plant diversification remains unresolved. In monocentric chromosomes, centromeric activity is restricted to one chromosomal region; in holocentric chromosomes, it is distributed along the chromosome length. Hybridization followed by genome doubling can place chromosome sets with different centromeres, repeat complements, and rearrangement histories in the same nucleus. We examined whether such genomic mergers are associated with later chromosome restructuring in carnivorous Caryophyllales, focusing on chromosome-scale assemblies of putatively holocentric Drosera regia and monocentric D. capensis. The two sundews retain broad syntenic continuity and related polyploid ancestry, but their present genomes differ sharply.
items.author: Avila Robledillo, L., Fukushima, K., Salojarvi, J. et al.

items.title: CLASSIFICATION OF PROKARYOTIC DNA METHYLTRANSFERASES BY CATALYTIC DOMAIN TOPOLOGY
items.summary: Prokaryotic DNA methyltransferases (MTases) are essential enzymes that play a crucial role in restriction-modification systems, preventing the degradation of self DNA by restriction enzymes. In addition, they contribute to the regulation of gene expression, DNA repair, DNA replication, and other processes. Here, we propose a novel classification of prokaryotic MTases based on the 3D topology of the catalytic domain, which addresses the limitations of the previous scheme developed by Malone and Bujnicki. The latter, which grouped MTases into categories such as , {beta}, {gamma}, etc., has been in use for over 20 years. We identified seven structural classes (A-G) of MTases by analyzing 38 experimentally determined 3D structures and several AlphaFold-predicted models, and validated the classification against all reviewed DNA MTases from Swiss-Prot.
items.author: Samokhina, M.

items.title: Restriction Enzyme activity under Force determined with autonomous DNA Origami Force Clamps via Gel Electrophoresis
items.summary: Investigating force-depending behaviour in biological systems is a challenging task, with most techniques requiring complex experimental equipment while also often being limited in scalability. We designed a facile force spectroscopy technique using DNA origami-based force clamps that apply forces up to ~40 pN. We validated the approach by using type II endonucleases that have been previously studied quantitatively by single-molecule measurements. Using ensemble measurements based on ubiquitously used agarose gel electrophoresis, we qualitatively observed force-dependent behaviour for EcoRV and force-independent behaviour for BamHI, replicating previous data for these enzymes. Interestingly, we also observed force-dependent behaviour for EcoRI, whose restriction behaviour has been previously described as force-independent.
items.author: Ermatov, A., Matthies, M., Sulc, P. et al.

items.title: Biomolecular design through latent reasoning with RFD4-Proteina
items.summary: Biomolecular design requires finding chemically and geometrically compatible arrangements of interacting atoms and molecules. The complexity of problems which can be tackled by deep learning design models is limited by both the molecular landscape they encompass and their ability to explore that landscape effectively. Here we introduce RFD4-Proteina, which addresses these limitations through intrinsic and extrinsic reasoning within a shared chemical and conformational latent space. The latent space encompasses standard and modified amino acids, sugars, DNA, and RNA, with force-field supervision favoring physically plausible atomic reconstructions. Within this space, intrinsic reasoning uses recurrent refinement to adaptively allocate computation, while extrinsic reasoning guides search with arbitrary constraints such as energetic or geometric criteria.
items.author: Corley, N., Didi, K., Kazman, M. W. et al.

items.title: ISdetector: precise mapping of insertion sequences and associated structural variations from short-read sequencing data
items.summary: Motivation. Repetitive insertion sequences (ISs) and adjacent structural variants (SVs) complicate precise mapping from bacte-rial short reads. Accurate insertion coordinates are important for studying genome evolution and tracking transmission. Results. ISdetector constructs IS-specific references with target copies removed and clusters soft-clipped reads to pinpoint insertion sites. On simulated genomes, it had higher recall and F1 score than ISMapper and MGEFinder. On 19 Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes, it achieved the highest high-confidence F1 score (0.86). On five Shigella sonnei genomes, it performed comparably to ISMapper (F1 score 0.85). It detected 81 of 105 IS6110 copies with associated SVs or complex events, versus 41 (ISMapper) and 12 (MGEFinder).
items.author: Zhou, Y., Lu, B., Zhao, Y.

items.title: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc
items.summary: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. Recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from these multicellular measurements requires two steps: explicit identification of individual cells and accurate estimation of per-gene expression. While existing methods have demonstrated the feasibility of recovering single-cell expression profiles, accurately estimating gene-level expression for individual cells remains an important challenge. To address this challenge, we propose st2sc (Spatial Transcriptomics to Single-Cell), an end-to-end framework for inferring single-cell gene profiles from multicellular ST data. st2sc introduces a novel Attention Gradient Flow Tracking (AGFT) algorithm that extracts attention maps from a Vision-Gene Transformer to identify candidate cell instances without predefined background constraints.
items.author: Lee, Y. J., Shah, S., Mantrala, S. et al.

items.title: DNA methylation assigns sequencing reads to closely related bacterial strains when their sequence cannot
items.summary: Clinical and public-health questions often concern strains rather than species, yet co-resident strains of one species can be so closely related that a single long read carries no sequence difference between them. We measured how often this happens in 639 pairs of isolates of Enterococcus faecium, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Listeria monocytogenes and Staphylococcus aureus sequenced on one nanopore platform. Among the 297 pairs above 99% average nucleotide identity (ANI), 40.37% of read placements (a read counted against one strain's genome) carried no sequence difference between the two strains, and above 99.9% ANI about three quarters did. Strains of one species also differ in the DNA motifs they methylate.
items.author: Kakabra, K., Claesson, M. J.

items.title: Point mutations in the FimH lectin domain: predicted folding stability versus conformational dynamics for R60P, Q133K and Y137A
items.summary: Background. The adhesin FimH attaches uropathogenic Escherichia coli to the urinary epithelium through a force-regulated catch-bond that single lectin-domain substitutions can modulate. How such substitutions reshape the dynamics of the isolated lectin domain, and whether stability predictors anticipate them, is unclear. Methods. We compared the wild-type (WT) lectin domain (PDB 4XO8, apo) with R60P, Y137A and Q133K, using three 500 ns molecular dynamics (MD) replicates per system (6 microseconds total) and three folding-stability predictors (FoldX, a Cartesian-ddG-type Rosetta protocol, ERIS-2). The replicate was the unit of analysis (n = 3), with 95% confidence intervals and a WT replicate-to-replicate control. Results.
items.author: Navas Passos, J. A., Pereira Tapia, A., Velez Duncan, C. et al.

items.title: A Rare Constitutional Centromeric Expansion of Chromosome 1 in a Phenotypically Normal Individual: A Comprehensive Cytogenetic Study
items.summary: Constitutional centromeric heteromorphisms are uncommon chromosomal variants that may complicate cytogenetic interpretation. We report a constitutional enlargement of the centromeric region of one chromosome 1 homologue identified incidentally during biological dose estimation in a suspected occupationally exposed individual. Conventional cytogenetics, pancentromeric fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and multiplex FISH confirmed the variant and excluded cryptic chromosomal rearrangements. Analysis of 500 metaphases revealed no dicentric chromosomes. Quantitative assessment demonstrated a centromere to chromosome length ratio of 0.314 plus/minus 0.019 for the enlarged homologue compared with 0.169 plus/minus 0.019 for the unaffected homologue and 0.161 to 0.186 in controls, representing an approximately 1.86 fold increase (t = 28.4, p < 0.0001).
items.author: Shirsath, K. B., Desai, U. N., Notnani, A. et al.

items.title: Fast and background-suppressed DNA-PAINT
items.summary: The speed and resolution of DNA-PAINT imaging is partly limited by the background fluorescence at high imager-strand concentrations. Here, we combine the photoactivatable fluorophore-quencher-DNA probes with the photoactivation, diffusion, and excitation strategy on a spinning disk confocal microscope, decoupling background fluorescence from the imager-strand concentration. This method yields >7-fold faster DNA-PAINT imaging in cells, a ~15 nm localization precision in hydrogels, without using specialized or speed-optimized imager strands.
items.author: Sun, T., Liu, S., Zhang, X. et al.

items.title: Tycholyzer: NanoTemper NT.6 Tycho Analysis Tool
items.summary: NanoTemper Tycho NT.6 is a nano differential scanning fluorimetry (nanoDSF) instrument that enables rapid measurement of apparent protein melting temperatures. Thermal shift assays are widely used to assess protein stability under different conditions, including screening for protein-ligand interactions. These experiments often involve multiple samples, conditions, and replicates collected across several instrument runs, generating datasets that can be cumbersome to organize, compare, and analyze quantitatively. Here, we introduce Tycholyzer, a user-friendly software application that streamlines processing and analysis of Tycho nanoDSF data. Tycholyzer allows users to combine data from multiple runs, inspect and select individual fluorescence traces, and normalize and group replicate profiles for comparison across experimental conditions.
items.author: Ghani, V. G., Boudker, O.

items.title: Minor intron splicing restricts E2F transcription factor activity in RB-deregulated prostate cancer
items.summary: Castration-resistant prostate cancer with neuroendocrine differentiation (CRPC-NE) arises in RB1-mutated lineage plastic cells in response to androgen receptor (AR)-targeted therapies. RB1 loss leads to constitutive E2F activation and cylin-dependent kinase (CDK) inhibitor resistance, making it challenging to restrict E2F activity. A post-transcriptional node is that typical E2Fs contain a rare but highly conserved minor intron, processed by the minor spliceosome (MiS). In an in vivo CRISPR screen, we nominate the MiS as the strongest dependency, and U6atac correlates strongest with E2F transcriptional programs in a clinical CRPC cohort. U6atac depletion led to mis-splicing of typical E2Fs, cell cycle arrest, and translation of a minor intron-containing E2F1 isoform (E2F1-MIRI) as a pharmacodynamic biomarker.
items.author: Thienger, P., Paassen, I., Maier, B. et al.

items.title: EcoToxFred: A knowledge-graph-grounded conversational agent for exploring ecotoxicological monitoring and hazard data
items.summary: Assessing chemical risks to aquatic ecosystems requires the joint interpretation of monitoring data, ecotoxicity data, and derived risk indicators, yet such integrated data are rarely accessible to users without database expertise. We present EcoToxFred, an open-source conversational agent that provides natural language access to a curated knowledge graph of chemical monitoring and hazard data for European surface waters. EcoToxFred couples a large language model (LLM) with a Neo4j graph database in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architecture. An agent interprets user questions, selects tools, translates questions into graph queries, and returns answers as text, tables, or interactive maps, together with the executed query for reproducibility.
items.author: Scheibe, P., Schmid, T. S., Schor, J.

items.title: Ultrasensitive Regulation in the Tryptophan System in Escherichia coli Provides Effective Noise Mitigation
items.summary: The tryptophan system in Escherichia coli maintains intracellular concentration of tryptophan in a narrow band regardless of the nutritional status and uncertainty in its environment. The system is characterized by three distinct regulations namely, genetic regulation, mRNA attenuation and enzyme inhibition, that use the tryptophan concentration as a feedback signal. It has been shown previously, that the multiple feedback loop design is responsible for rapid synthesis of tryptophan when faced with starvation. It is well known that a design with rapid response to external signals also implies poorer noise mitigation properties. This work investigates the design elements that limit the adverse impact of the multiple feedback loop architecture on noise propagation in the tryptophan system using a frequency response analysis.
items.author: Bavdekar, V., Bhartiya, S., Venkatesh, K. V.

items.title: Combination of in vitro and ex vivo infection models highlights the role of NAD-dependent ADP-ribosylation in Influenza A virus infection.
items.summary: Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a major public health concern, causing an estimated 650 000 deaths annually. Although vaccines are available, vaccination coverage is limited and must be repeated annually due to the genetic variability of these viruses. Furthermore, although direct acting antivirals are available, they must be administered as early as possible after infection to be effective. In this context, understanding the metabolic alterations associated with the replication and pathogenesis of IAV could contribute to the development of treatments that promote virus clearance and patient recovery. In this study, we identified the intracellular level of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) as a key factor in the replication of IAV.
items.author: Jacolin, F., Aublin-Gex, A., Vellet, M. et al.

items.title: Azospirillum brasilense and cytidine as combination treatment to enhance drought resilience of peas
items.summary: Aims: This study tested the efficacy of two combination treatments on drought resilience of peas; Azospirillum brasilense Sp7 with the chemoattractant seedling exudate compound cytidine or pea seedling exudate. Methods and Results: Phenotypic characterization revealed that drought tolerance of peas treated with ACyt was 68.9% higher than that of peas treated with the inoculant alone (A). Dry shoot weight of ACyt Drought plants was 30.7% higher than that of plants from the untreated control group NB Drought, drought recovery of ACyt plants was 21.6% better. The treatment with seedling exudate (AEx) was less effective. 16S rDNA analysis revealed that increase in drought tolerance was accompanied by modulation of the rhizosphere.
